AI/深度学习」方向，具体聚焦于抗体CDR（互补决定区）的序列建模。与AlphaFold等结构预测方法不同，本文提出一种仅依赖抗体和抗原一级序列的掩码语言模型（LangAAI），无需3D结构、对接姿态或表位注释，实现抗原条件化的CDR序列生成与优化。该工作处于抗体语言模型（如AntiBERTa、IgLM）与结构-based逆折叠模型（如ESM-IF）之间的生态位，试图以序列-only方式达到结构-based方法的性能。 02 一句话总结 本文提出LangAAI，一个仅以抗体和抗原一级序列为输入的掩码语言模型，通过抗原序列条件化实现CDR3区域的抗原感知建模，在序列恢复率上超越现有抗体语言模型，并在亲和力排序任务上达到与结构-based逆折叠模型相当的性能，从而为缺乏抗原-抗体复合物结构的靶点提供结构无关的抗体优化方案。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：如何在不依赖抗原3D结构、对接姿态或表位注释的前提下，实现对抗体CDR区域的抗原条件化建模与序列设计？ 为什么重要 ：抗体的CDR区域决定抗原特异性，CDR设计应条件于靶抗原。然而，大多数现有方法依赖抗原的3D结构，而实验获取抗原-抗体复合物结构困难且耗时。序列-only模型虽规避此需求，但通常在不含抗原上下文的情况下训练，导致模型无法学习抗原-抗体相互作用的决定因素。 现有方法为何不足 ： 结构-based方法（如逆折叠模型）需要抗原-抗体复合物或至少抗原的3D结构，应用范围受限。 现有抗体语言模型（如AntiBERTa、IgLM）仅以抗体序列为输入，缺乏抗原上下文，无法实现真正的抗原条件化生成。 简单地将抗原序列拼接输入并不保证模型学习到相互作用决定因素（作者明确指出"exposure to antigen sequences alone does not necessarily entail learning the underlying interaction determinants"）。 精确研究问题 ：Can a masked language model conditioned exclusively on antibody and antigen primary sequences achieve antigen-aware CDR modeling comparable to structure-based methods, without requiring 3D structures or epitope annotations? 04 背景与发展脉络 注：此脉络基于本文摘要及该领域公开知识构建，标注为「经外部核验」部分基于领域常识，但具体方法细节仅依据本文摘要。 阶段 代表性方法 优点 局限 本文位置 结构-based CDR建模 optimization" Abstract 最后一句 06 核心思想 1) 表面方法 LangAAI是一个掩码语言模型（masked language model），输入为抗体和抗原的一级序列（primary sequences），通过掩码重建任务训练，输出为CDR区域的序列预测/恢复。模型不依赖任何3D结构信息、对接姿态或表位注释。 2) 核心洞察 抗原条件化的验证机制 ：作者设计了一个关键实验——将同源抗原替换为非结合诱饵（non-binding decoy），观察模型行为变化。抗原无关模型对此替换不敏感，而LangAAI表现出序列恢复率的显著下降，且该下降集中在高变CDR3环。这一设计巧妙地将"是否真正条件于抗原"从"能否生成序列"中分离出来，提供了可操作的验证协议。 序列中隐含相互作用信息 ：尽管仅使用一级序列，模型仍能学习到抗原-抗体相互作用的决定因素，表明序列层面存在足够的信号供模型捕捉结合特异性。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] 条件化验证协议 ：对于任何声称"条件于某输入"的生成模型，替换该输入为阴性对照并观察输出变化，是一种通用且严格的验证方法。此协议可迁移至其他蛋白质设计任务（如酶-底物、受体-配体）。 序列-only的边界 ：本文表明，在抗体-抗原场景中，序列-only方法可达到与结构-based方法相当的性能，提示在某些预测任务中，序列信息可能已编码足够的结构-功能关系，无需显式3D结构。 CDR3作为特异性热点 ：抗原替换导致的序列恢复率下降集中在CDR3，验证了CDR3是抗体特异性的主要决定区域，这为设计实验提供了先验指导。 07 方法总览 输入 ：抗体序列 + 抗原序列（均为一级氨基酸序列） 输出 ：CDR区域（特别是CDR3）的掩码位置氨基酸预测/恢复 模型架构 ：掩码语言模型（masked language model），具体架构细节未在摘要中提供 训练任务 ：掩码重建（masked token prediction），即在抗体-抗原序列上随机掩码部分位置，训练模型预测被掩码的氨基酸 关键设计 ： 同时输入抗体和抗原序列，使模型可学习跨序列的相互作用模式 无需3D结构、对接姿态、表位注释 验证边界 ：抗原替换实验证明了模型对抗原输入的敏感性，但未提供该效应的定量规模（如恢复率下降的具体百分比）和统计显著性。 对比公平性 ：与结构-based方法的比较是在"各自协议下"进行的，非统一基准，因此"性能相当"的结论需谨慎解读——不同评测协议可能对某些方法有利。 端到端状态 ：模型输出为CDR序列预测，未涉及下游实验验证（如表达量、亲和力实验测量），"抗体优化"的结论基于计算指标推断。 算力与数据依赖 ：未提供训练数据规模、计算资源需求、训练时间等信息。 最难点 ：CDR3是抗原替换后受影响最大的区域，表明模型对CDR3的预测最依赖抗原上下文，但这也意味着对于CDR3的从头设计，模型可能对输入抗原序列高度敏感。 不确定性 ：未提供置信区间、误差棒、多次运行的标准差等不确定性度量。 有边界的复述 ：在仅使用抗体和抗原一级序列的条件下，LangAAI在CDR区域氨基酸恢复率上优于现有抗体语言模型，并在各自评测协议下达到与结构-based逆折叠模型相当的性能；抗原替换实验表明该模型确实利用了抗原信息，且该利用集中在CDR3区域。 12 作者自认局限 在提供的材料（仅摘要）中，未发现作者明确承认的局限。作者未在摘要中讨论方法的局限性、失败案例或适用边界。 作者提及的相关约束 boundary Claims and evidence presented in the abstract; no methods, figures, tables, or supplementary material were provided for evaluation Shared manuscript claim summary The authors introduce LangAAI, a masked language model that conditions on antibody and antigen primary sequences only, without requiring 3D structures, docking poses, or epitope annotations. They claim that LangAAI exhibits genuine antigen conditioning, as demonstrated by reduced sequence recovery when the cognate antigen is replaced with a non-binding decoy, with the effect concentrated in CDR3. They further claim improved amino-acid recovery relative to existing antibody language models, parity with structure-based methods under their respective protocols, and comparable ranking of experimentally measured variants by affinity relative to inverse-folding models using backbone coordinates. Visible evidence base Abstract text only. No figures, tables, methods descriptions, benchmark definitions, dataset specifications, or statistical details were provided. Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, methods section, benchmark protocols, dataset descriptions, baseline model specifications, decoy antigen construction details, statistical significance measures, and all quantitative results. The absence of these materials severely limits the ability to verify the central claims. Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially valuable contribution to antibody modeling, addressing a real gap in the field by proposing a sequence-only approach to antigen-conditioned CDR design. The concept of using decoy antigens to probe genuine antigen conditioning is methodologically interesting. However, the abstract alone provides insufficient evidence to evaluate the validity, robustness, or generalizability of the claims. The central claims of improved recovery, parity with structure-based methods, and affinity ranking comparability are stated without quantitative support. The manuscript cannot be assessed for technical soundness from the supplied material. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in computational antibody design, protein language models, and therapeutic antibody development would be interested. The work addresses a practical bottleneck in antibody engineering, namely the dependence on experimentally determined antigen structures. A sequence-only approach that demonstrably conditions on antigen information could enable broader application of computational design to targets lacking structural data. The decoy-based evaluation strategy may also be of methodological interest to the protein language model community. Major strengths The problem addressed is well-motivated and practically relevant. The proposed approach, if validated, would remove a significant barrier in antibody design. The decoy antigen substitution strategy is a thoughtful and potentially rigorous way to test whether the model genuinely uses antigen information rather than ignoring it. The claim of concentrating antigen sensitivity in CDR3 is biologically plausible and, if confirmed, would support the model's relevance to antigen specificity. Why it matters This is the central evidence for the claim of genuine antigen conditioning. Without quantitative details and a clear description of the decoy construction and evaluation protocol, the reader cannot assess whether the effect is robust, specific, or an artifact of the specific decoy set or evaluation metric. Show that the effect is consistent across multiple decoy antigens and is not explained by trivial sequence properties of the decoys. 01 基本信息 标题 ：UnibindMD: An Integrated AI and Molecular Dynamics Platform for De Novo Peptide Binder Design 作者与单位 ：Wu X; Huang A; Fu C; Wang Z; Fu W（单位未提供） 期刊/预印本平台 ：bioRxiv（预印本） 年份 ：2026-10-23 论文类型 ：方法学/平台论文（含案例研究） 领域 ：蛋白质-肽结合物设计 × AI + 分子动力学（MD）验证 关键词 ：de novo peptide binder design, BindCraft, AlphaFold3/Boltz-2, PRODIGY, ADMET-AI, GROMACS, Andes virus, molecular dynamics validation DOI/arXiv 号 ：10.64898/2026.10.20.760329 代码 ：未提供 数据 ：未提供（仅提及 PDB 结构 6Q99、2XIR 作为靶点结构） 阅读日期 ：2026-10-23 在该方向中的位置 ：本文属于「AI 驱动的蛋白质-肽结合物设计 + 物理模拟验证」的集成平台类工作。其核心主张是：单一 AI 设计工具的置信度指标（ipTM/pLDDT）是自洽但非独立的，必须通过独立的结构预测、亲和力预测、ADMET 评估和全原子 MD 模拟进行交叉验证，才能获得物理上稳定的候选分子。该工作位于「结构预测（AlphaFold 类）→ 结合物设计（BindCraft）→ 物理验证（MD）」这一流水线的集成端，强调工作流而非单一算法创新。 02 一句话总结 本文构建了一个五阶段集成平台 UnibindMD（BindCraft 设计 → Boltz-2 结构预测 → PRODIGY 亲和力预测 → ADMET-AI 成药性评估 → GROMACS MD 验证），在 Andes virus 三个靶点上产出 464 个候选肽结合物，其中 3 个先导物经 PRODIGY 预测 Kd 为 8 nM–0.2 μM，并在 100 ns 无约束 MD 中保持稳定结合（受体 Cα RMSD ≤ 2.6 Å，≥ 99.5% 帧保留 > 50% 初始界面接触）。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：如何将单次 AI 预测的肽结合物设计转化为经过独立交叉验证和动力学测试的可靠候选物？ 为什么重要 ：现有 AI 设计工具（如 BindCraft）的置信度指标（ipTM、pLDDT）是模型自洽的，但并非独立于模型本身的验证。一个被预测为高置信度的设计可能在物理上不稳定（如肽段折叠不稳定、界面接触松散、在 MD 中迅速解离）。在 Andes virus（致死率近 40%，2026 年 MV Hondius 游轮爆发 13 例 3 死，无获批治疗药物）等紧急场景下，需要快速且可靠的候选物。 现有方法为何不足 ：单一方法（仅 AI 设计、仅结构预测或仅 MD）各自存在盲区：AI 设计缺乏物理验证；结构预测的置信度指标自洽但不独立；MD 模拟需要初始候选物且计算成本高。没有集成平台将这些正交方法串联成可扩展的工作流。 精确研究问题 ：Can a five-stage integrated pipeline (AI design → independent structure prediction → affinity prediction → developability profiling → MD validation) convert single-prediction peptide-binder designs into physically stable, validated leads across multiple protein targets? 04 背景与发展脉络 注：以下脉络基于本文框架，标注为「仅本文框架」；未提供外部综述性引用。 阶段一：AI 驱动的结合物设计（BindCraft 类） - 代表性方法：BindCraft（深度学习，基于序列/结构生成肽结合物） - 优点：高通量、可扩展、无需先验实验数据 - 局限：输出为统计预测，缺乏物理稳定性保证；置信度指标（ipTM/pLDDT）自洽但不独立 - 本文位置：作为流水线第一站，生成候选池 阶段二：独立结构预测与置信度评估（AlphaFold3 类 / Boltz-2） - 代表性方法：AlphaFold3、Boltz-2 - 优点：高精度结构预测，提供 ipTM/pLDT 等置信度指标 - 局限：预测基于训练数据分布，对全新设计（de novo）可能过度自信；不评估动力学稳定性 - 本文位置：作为独立于 BindCraft 的第二验证层 阶段三：结合亲和力预测（PRODIGY） - 代表性方法：PRODIGY（基于接触界面的结合自由能预测） - 优点：快速、无需模拟 - 局限：基于经验/统计势，不捕捉构象动态 - 本文位置：提供热力学排序 阶段四：成药性评估（ADMET-AI） - 代表性方法：ADMET-AI（吸收、分布、代谢、排泄、毒性预测） - 优点：快速筛选类药性 - 局限：对肽类分子的口服生物利用度预测保守 - 本文位置：过滤不可开发候选 阶段五：全原子 MD 验证（GROMACS/CHARMM36m） - 代表性方法：GROMACS + CHARMM36m 力场 - 优点：物理真实性最高，可评估结合稳定性、构象保持、界面接触持久性 - 局限：计算成本高，需要初始候选物 - presented in the abstract; no full text, figures, tables, or supplementary material were provided Shared manuscript claim summary The authors present UnibindMD, an integrated computational platform combining five stages (BindCraft, Boltz-2, PRODIGY, ADMET-AI, GROMACS/CHARMM36m) for de novo peptide binder design. They report application to three Andes virus targets, with 464 accepted binders from 4,475 trajectories, top candidates at ipTM = 0.94 and pLDDT = 0.94, predicted binding free energies of -9.1 to -11.1 kcal mol-1, and stable 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations for three selected leads. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no figures, tables, methods, or supplementary data provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, methods details, simulation parameters, trajectory analyses, target structure preparation protocols, and supplementary data Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract describes a potentially useful integrated pipeline for peptide binder design, addressing a legitimate concern about over-reliance on self-consistent confidence metrics. However, the evidence presented in the abstract is insufficient to evaluate the technical soundness of the platform, the validity of the reported metrics, or the generalizability claims. Several quantitative claims lack methodological context, and the biological relevance of the three targets is asserted but not demonstrated with functional validation. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational biologists and protein design researchers interested in integrated pipelines that combine deep learning with physics-based validation. Structural biologists working on viral entry mechanisms, particularly arenaviruses, may find the application to Andes virus relevant. Drug discovery scientists seeking practical workflows for peptide binder development could benefit if the platform is shown to be robust and generalizable. Major strengths The platform addresses a real limitation in current AI-based protein design, namely the circularity of self-consistent confidence metrics. The multi-stage design is logical and each component is well-established in the field. The choice of Andes virus targets is timely and clinically motivated, given the high case fatality rate and lack of approved therapeutics. Major Concerns The abstract reports quantitative results without sufficient methodological context to assess their validity. The acceptance rate range of 2.3-67.6% is extremely broad and unexplained. The molecular dynamics metrics are presented as evidence of stability but the criteria for "stable" are not justified. The claim of generalizability is unsupported by the single-target-family demonstration. No functional or experimental validation is presented. no full text, figures, tables, or supplementary materials were provided for review Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report that small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) with contrast matching, using biosynthetically deuterated bacterial cellulose, reveals a distinct conformational state of the processive cellulase Trichoderma reesei Cel7A when bound to crystalline cellulose under catalytically favorable conditions. Molecular dynamics simulations of the free enzyme did not reproduce the bound-state structural features. The authors conclude that the linker and carbohydrate-binding module modulate interfacial positioning of the catalytic domain dynamically rather than acting as a rigid mechanical unit. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no experimental details, scattering profiles, fit parameters, simulation protocols, or statistical analyses are visible Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, experimental methods, simulation parameters, data analysis details, and supplementary information Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially interesting application of neutron contrast matching to study a cellulase enzyme at a solid-liquid interface, a technically demanding and relatively uncommon approach. The central claim, that cellulose-bound Cel7A adopts a conformationally distinct state under productive catalytic conditions, is plausible and would be of interest to the biocatalysis and glycoside hydrolase communities. However, the abstract alone provides insufficient detail to evaluate the rigor of the SANS analysis, the statistical significance of the observed differences, or the validity of the simulation comparisons. The conclusion regarding the dynamic role of the linker and carbohydrate-binding module is presented as strongly supported, but the evidence base visible here is too thin to assess whether this interpretation is uniquely supported or merely consistent with the data. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers studying enzymatic degradation of insoluble polysaccharides, particularly cellulases and other processive glycoside hydrolases, would find these results relevant to ongoing debates about how linker regions and carbohydrate-binding modules contribute to processive catalysis. The methodological demonstration of using deuterated substrates with neutron contrast variation to isolate protein scattering at an interface could also interest structural biologists working on solid-liquid interfacial systems. Those developing kinetic or mechanistic models of cellulase action on crystalline cellulose would need to account for the proposed interface-selected conformational state. Major strengths The use of biosynthetically deuterated bacterial cellulose with SANS contrast matching is an elegant experimental strategy to isolate the scattering contribution of the bound enzyme from that of the substrate. The comparison between catalytically favorable and unfavorable conditions provides an internal control that strengthens the interpretation that the observed conformational change is functionally relevant. The combination of experimental scattering with molecular dynamics simulations represents a complementary approach that could provide mechanistic insight beyond what either method alone would yield. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "SANS measurements performed under conditions supporting high or low catalytic activity revealed distinct differences between the free and cellulose-bound enzyme. Under poorly active conditions, the conformational distributions of free and bound Cel7A were similar. In contrast, catalytically favorable conditions produced an additional interdomain correlation in the bound enzyme" Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Concern The abstract reports a difference in scattering between free and bound Cel7A under active conditions, described as "an additional interdomain correlation," but provides no quantitative information about the magnitude of this effect, the signal-to-noise ratio of the SANS data, the contrast matching quality, or the statistical significance of the observed differences. No Guinier analysis, pair-distance distribution functions, or model fitting results are described. Without these details, it is impossible to assess whether the reported conformational difference is robust or could arise from incomplete contrast matching, residual background scattering, or analysis artifacts. Why it matters The central conclusion of the paper rests entirely on the reliability of the SANS contrast matching and the interpretation of scattering differences as conformational reorganization. If the contrast matching is imperfect or the difference is within experimental noise, the entire interpretive framework collapses. SANS experiments at solid-liquid interfaces are technically challenging, and the abstract does not demonstrate that the authors have addressed known pitfalls such as substrate polydispersity, surface roughness effects, or incomplete deuteration. Resolution test The full manuscript must provide SANS profiles with error bars, contrast matching validation data, quantitative comparison of scattering curves under different conditions (for example, with appropriate statistical tests), and model fits with residuals. The "additional interdomain correlation" should be identified through explicit structural modeling with confidence intervals, not merely inferred from qualitative differences in scattering curves. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "Molecular dynamics simulations showed that free Cel7A samples can assume compact, intermediate, and extended conformations, but these solution-state ensembles did not reproduce the structural features of cellulose-bound Cel7A" Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Concern The abstract states that MD simulations of free Cel7A did not reproduce the bound-state structural features, but provides no information about the simulation length, force field, starting structures, sampling methodology, or how the comparison between simulated ensembles and experimental scattering was performed. It is unclear whether the simulations were intended to sample the full conformational space of the free enzyme or to predict the bound-state conformation. The conclusion that the bound state is "structurally distinct" from anything sampled in solution depends critically on the adequacy of the conformational sampling, which cannot be evaluated from the abstract. Why it matters The claim that the bound state represents a "structurally distinct" conformation not present in the solution ensemble is a strong negative claim. If the simulations undersampled the conformational space, the absence of bound-like conformations in the simulated ensemble would be uninformative. Conversely, if the simulations did sample such conformations but with low probability, the interpretation would shift from "structurally distinct state" to "conformational selection from a pre-existing ensemble." These are mechanistically different models with different implications. Resolution test The full manuscript must provide simulation details including total simulation time, number of replicas, force field parameters, convergence metrics, and a quantitative comparison between simulated ensembles and experimental scattering data. The authors should demonstrate that the simulations adequately sample the conformational space of the free enzyme and that the absence of bound-like conformations is not a sampling artifact. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Scientific importance Claim pointer "These results identify productive cellulose engagement as a structurally distinct state of the Cel7A holoenzyme and support a dynamic model in which the linker and carbohydrate-binding module modulate interfacial positioning of the catalytic domain rather than functioning as a rigid mechanical unit during processive hydrolysis" Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Concern The abstract presents a mechanistic model of linker and CBM function as "modulating interfacial positioning" rather than acting as a "rigid mechanical unit," but the SANS data as described provide only a low-resolution view of the overall conformational envelope of the enzyme. It is not clear how such data can distinguish between a dynamic modulatory role and alternative models, such as a hinged but still mechanically coupled mechanism, or a model in which the CBM simply anchors the enzyme while the linker provides entropic flexibility. The abstract does not describe any experiments that directly test the proposed mechanism, such as mutations in the linker or CBM, or measurements under different substrate loadings. Why it matters The mechanistic conclusion is the primary conceptual contribution of the paper. If the data can only show that the bound conformation differs from the free conformation, this is consistent with many mechanistic models. The specific claim about the linker and CBM functioning as dynamic modulators rather than rigid mechanical units requires additional evidence or at least a more explicit argument for why the observed conformational change rules out alternative models. Resolution test The full manuscript should either provide direct experimental tests of the proposed mechanism or present a more carefully reasoned argument, with supporting data, for why the observed conformational reorganization specifically supports the dynamic modulation model over alternatives. If the data are only consistent with but not uniquely supportive of the proposed mechanism, this should be stated explicitly. Scientific importance: The question of how processive enzymes engage insoluble substrates is of genuine significance for understanding biomass deconstruction, but the conceptual advance claimed here, that interfacial binding selects a distinct conformational state, is incremental over existing models that already recognize the importance of linker flexibility and CBM dynamics. Interdisciplinary readership: The work bridges enzymology, structural biology, and biophysics, and the methodological demonstration could attract interest from neutron scattering practitioners, but the abstract does not currently frame the findings in a way that would compel a broad general science audience. Technical soundness: Cannot be adequately assessed from the abstract alone. The SANS methodology is demanding and the abstract does not provide sufficient detail to evaluate data quality, contrast matching effectiveness, or analysis rigor. The abstract presents an interesting approach and a plausible hypothesis, but the evidence base visible here is insufficient to evaluate the technical soundness of the SANS experiments, the adequacy of the simulations, or the strength of the mechanistic conclusions. A full manuscript with detailed methods, quantitative results, and statistical analyses would be required to assess whether the claims are supported. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that the bound enzyme exhibits "an additional interdomain correlation" under active conditions is unsupported without quantitative scattering data and statistical analysis. The claim that MD simulations of free Cel7A did not reproduce bound-state features is unverifiable without simulation details and convergence metrics. The mechanistic conclusion that the linker and CBM "modulate interfacial positioning" rather than acting as a "rigid mechanical unit" is not uniquely supported by the described data. The broader generalization to "heterogeneous biocatalysis" is not supported by evidence from a single enzyme system. The statement that the bound state is "structurally distinct" from solution states is a strong claim that requires demonstration that the observed difference exceeds experimental uncertainty and is not an artifact of the contrast matching procedure.

：softmax 将 logits 映射到概率时，低概率氨基酸的梯度被 Jacobian 压缩，导致这些氨基酸在早期被抑制后几乎无法恢复。PGD 直接更新概率，梯度不受此衰减影响。 概率空间的直接更新允许「重新进入」 ：被抑制的氨基酸在 PGD 中可以因后续梯度方向变化而重新获得概率质量，增加序列空间探索能力。 更少迭代 + 筛选 = 更高吞吐 ：短轨迹 PGD 配合候选筛选，在相同 GPU Softmax 重参数化（对照方法） $$p_i = \frac{\exp(l_i)}{\sum_{j=1}^{20} \exp(l_j)}$$ $p_i$：位置上的第 $i$ 个氨基酸概率 $l_i$：对应的 logit 用途 ：将 logits 映射到概率 simplex 直觉 ：softmax 的 Jacobian $\partial p_i / \partial l_j = p_i(\delta_{ij} - p_j)$，当 $p_i \to 0$ 时梯度 $\to 0$，即梯度衰减 来源 ：本文引言/方法（未提供节号） 2. They report that PGD minimises design loss in fewer iterations, produces designs with higher predicted interface confidence, improves in silico hit rates on six of ten targets with no significant degradation, yields more structurally diverse designs, and increases in silico hits per GPU-hour by 29% when paired with candidate screening. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no figures, tables, methods, or supplementary data were supplied Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, methods description, all figures and tables, supplementary information, code repository contents, and design data are not available for assessment Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially useful methodological contribution to the protein binder design community, addressing a practical gap in optimiser selection for gradient-based hallucination. The claims are specific and quantitative, which is commendable. However, the evidence base provided is insufficient to evaluate the technical soundness of the approach, the statistical rigour of the comparisons, or the generalisability of the findings. Several claims require detailed methodological and statistical support that is not visible in the abstract alone. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational protein designers, particularly those working on binder design and de novo protein hallucination. Researchers developing optimisation methods for sequence design in continuous relaxation spaces would also find the comparison between PGD and softmax-based approaches relevant. The efficiency gains in GPU-hours may interest practitioners running large-scale in silico screening campaigns. Major strengths The work addresses a specific and under-evaluated component of the hallucination pipeline, namely the optimiser choice. The proposed method is conceptually simple and likely easy to implement, which lowers the barrier to adoption. The evaluation includes multiple targets and a practical metric (hits per GPU-hour) that reflects real campaign constraints. The inclusion of structural diversity as an outcome measure is a useful addition beyond loss minimisation. Major Concerns The abstract alone does not provide sufficient detail to assess the validity of the reported improvements. Key methodological choices, statistical tests, and baseline configurations are not described. The claim of "no significant degradation on any" target requires knowledge of the statistical power and test used. The 29% improvement in hits per GPU-hour depends on unspecified screening thresholds and trajectory lengths. The mechanism by which PGD allows suppressed amino acids to re-enter the design is stated but not demonstrated. Minor Comments The abstract would benefit from specifying the number of independent runs or seeds used. The choice of ESMFold2 as the structure predictor and its potential influence on the results is not discussed. The relationship between predicted interface confidence and experimentally validated binding is not addressed. The public availability of code and data is noted but the contents are not described. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established The statistical methodology for comparing PGD against the softmax baseline is not described. The definition of "in silico hit" and the ipSAE threshold used are not provided. The computational cost comparison appears to conflate optimisation iterations with wall-clock time, which may be misleading if per-iteration costs differ between methods. The diversity metric is not defined. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: moderate. The application of PGD to hallucination-based design is a reasonable incremental contribution, but the core idea of projected gradient methods in probability simplices is well established in optimisation literature. Scientific importance: potentially relevant to a specialised community, but the abstract does not demonstrate broad biological or methodological significance beyond an incremental improvement. Interdisciplinary readership: limited; the work is primarily of interest to computational protein designers and optimisation researchers. Technical soundness: not assessable from the abstract; the absence of methodological detail precludes evaluation of the statistical and computational claims. Readability for nonspecialists: the abstract is reasonably clear for a technical audience but assumes familiarity with hallucination-based design, ipSAE, and sequence logit reparameterisation. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Methodological clarity Claim pointer "PGD avoids softmax-induced gradient attenuation and allows amino acids suppressed early in optimisation to re-enter the design" Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The mechanism by which PGD enables re-entry of suppressed amino acids is stated as a property of the method, but no evidence is presented to demonstrate that this occurs in practice or that it contributes to the observed improvements. The gradient attenuation argument is plausible but requires formal or empirical support. Why it matters The proposed advantage of PGD over the softmax baseline is central to the motivation of the work. If the mechanism is not demonstrated, the improvement could be attributed to other factors, such as different effective learning rates or update scales. Resolution test Provide a formal argument or empirical demonstration that PGD allows recovery of suppressed amino acids, and show that this property is linked to the observed performance gains, for example through ablation or trajectory analysis. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Computational cost comparison Claim pointer "pairing shorter PGD runs with candidate screening raises the total number of in silico hits per GPU-hour by 29% relative to default-length trajectories" Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The 29% improvement in hits per GPU-hour depends on the definition of "shorter" runs, the screening threshold, and the baseline trajectory length. The abstract does not specify these parameters, nor does it clarify whether the comparison accounts for the computational cost of screening itself. Why it matters The efficiency claim is a practical selling point of the method. If the comparison is not apples-to-apples, or if the screening cost is excluded, the reported improvement may be misleading. Resolution test Specify the trajectory lengths compared, the screening protocol and its computational cost, and the exact calculation of hits per GPU-hour. Without definitions, the claims cannot be reproduced or compared with other work. Why it matters The practical value of the method depends on whether the reported improvements in predicted confidence and diversity translate to better experimental outcomes. If the metrics are poorly chosen or defined, the claims may not be meaningful. Assessment boundary Claims and conclusions as stated in the abstract; no methods, figures, tables, or supplementary material were provided Shared manuscript claim summary The authors used comparative molecular dynamics simulations with three force field/water model combinations to study the flexibility of the N-terminal alpha-helix of human TRMT10C, comparing it with two designed helices and three additional Trm10 family helices. They report a stable alpha-helical segment (residues 132-139) embedded in flexible regions, a rigidity-flexibility pattern conserved across Trm10 family members, force-field-dependent behavior for a polyalanine control, and a functional interpretation linking local rigidity to tRNA presentation and overall flexibility to conformational adaptation. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no simulation protocols, convergence metrics, structural analyses, or quantitative results are visible Missing materials affecting confidence Full methods, force field parameters, system setup details, simulation convergence data, structural analysis figures, quantitative flexibility measures, sequence alignments, and any statistical treatment of the five replicas Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a plausible and potentially interesting computational study of a biologically relevant RNA-binding helix. The central observation of a conserved rigid segment within a flexible helix is intriguing and could have functional implications for tRNA processing. However, the abstract alone provides insufficient evidence to evaluate the technical quality of the simulations, the robustness of the flexibility rankings, or the strength of the functional interpretation. The claim of family-wide generalizability rests on a small number of homologues and is not supported by quantitative data in the visible material. The functional conclusion, while reasonable as a hypothesis, is presented with more certainty than the evidence described can justify. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers studying mitochondrial tRNA maturation and RNA modification enzymes, computational biochemists interested in force field effects on helical peptide dynamics, and structural biologists examining protein-RNA recognition mechanisms. The force field comparison aspect may also interest method developers in the molecular dynamics community. Major strengths The study addresses a biologically relevant question about the dynamic behavior of a functionally important helix. The use of multiple force fields and water models is a commendable approach to assess robustness. The inclusion of designed control helices and family homologues provides a comparative framework. The five-replica design for each system suggests attention to statistical sampling. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The abstract claims that "five independent 1-mus simulations were performed for each system" and that the flexibility rankings are robust across force fields for the AEEEKRK repeat helix and TRMT10C helix. Evidence pointer Abstract only; no methods or figures provided Concern The abstract provides no information about simulation convergence, equilibration protocols, temperature and pressure coupling schemes, or how the five replicas were analyzed and combined. Without convergence assessment, 1-microsecond simulations may not be sufficient to sample the conformational space of a 41-residue helix, particularly for the charged and flexible regions. The claim of robustness across force fields cannot be evaluated without quantitative comparison metrics. Why it matters Molecular dynamics results are only meaningful if the simulations are converged and the analysis methods are appropriate. The central conclusion about rigidity and flexibility patterns depends entirely on the reliability of the sampling and the force field behavior. Without this information, the technical foundation of the study cannot be assessed. Resolution test Provide convergence metrics (e.g., RMSD time series, cluster analysis, block averaging), detailed simulation protocols, and quantitative flexibility measures (e.g., per-residue RMSF, dihedral angle distributions) with error estimates across replicas. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Scientific importance Claim pointer The abstract states that "simulations of the N-terminal helices of other TRMT10C homologues revealed similar flexibility profiles, suggesting that the observed trends are generalizable across the family." Evidence pointer Abstract only; no sequence alignment or comparative data provided Concern The claim of family-wide generalizability is based on an unspecified number of homologues ("three additional helices belonging to the Trm10 family" plus "other TRMT10C homologues"). The abstract does not state how many homologues were simulated, their sequence identity to human TRMT10C, or the quantitative similarity of their flexibility profiles. Three to six homologues from one family is a limited sample for a generalizability claim. Why it matters The generalizability claim substantially strengthens the biological significance of the study. If the pattern is not robust across a diverse set of homologues, the conclusion is weakened. The current evidence base is insufficient to support this broad claim. Resolution test Specify the number and identity of homologues studied, provide sequence conservation data, and show quantitative comparison of flexibility profiles across all homologues with statistical significance testing. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Scientific importance Claim pointer The abstract concludes that "the human TRMT10C helix is tuned to combine localized rigidity to provide localized structural support that helps present the fragile mitochondrial tRNA to the maturation enzymes with overall flexibility for conformational adaptation, facilitating tRNA positioning and efficient catalysis." Evidence pointer Abstract only; no functional assays or structural data connecting dynamics to function Concern The functional interpretation is presented as a conclusion ("is tuned to combine") rather than as a hypothesis. The abstract describes a correlation between a rigid segment and a tRNA-interacting region, but correlation does not establish functional tuning. No experimental or additional computational evidence links the observed dynamics to catalytic efficiency or tRNA presentation. Why it matters The functional claim elevates the study from a descriptive dynamics analysis to a mechanistic proposal. If the authors intend this as a hypothesis, it should be framed as such. If presented as a conclusion, it requires additional supporting evidence beyond the simulation data described. Resolution test Reframe the functional statement as a hypothesis, or provide additional evidence such as mutation studies, enhanced sampling connecting dynamics to binding, or experimental validation of the predicted rigid segment's role. Required correction Add one sentence of biological context, such as the role of TRMT10C in mitochondrial tRNA processing and any disease associations. The phrase "overall flexibility ranking" is vague and does not specify which metric was ranked or how agreement was quantified. Required correction Specify the flexibility metric used (e.g., per-residue RMSF, helix unwinding rates) and provide a quantitative measure of agreement across force fields (e.g., correlation coefficients, rank-order statistics). Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Interdisciplinary readership Affected element Abstract text Evidence pointer Abstract, rigid segment description Issue The description of the rigid segment (residues 132-139) as "more hydrophobic" and the surrounding region as "enriched in charged residues" is presented without structural context. Nonspecialist readers may not understand why this pattern is mechanistically significant. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1 (simulation convergence and protocol transparency) and R1-M2 (insufficient evidence for generalizability claim) must be addressed. R1-M3 requires reframing or additional evidence. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality The approach of comparing a biologically relevant helix with designed controls and family homologues across multiple force fields is not entirely novel but is a reasonable application of existing methodology. The specific finding of a conserved rigid segment within a flexible helix may offer new insight. Scientific importance The biological question is relevant to mitochondrial biology and RNA modification, but the abstract does not establish the broader significance of TRMT10C dynamics beyond a descriptive observation. The functional interpretation, if validated, would increase importance. Interdisciplinary readership The topic bridges computational chemistry and RNA biology, which could attract readers from both communities. However, the abstract assumes familiarity with molecular dynamics terminology and mitochondrial tRNA processing, limiting accessibility. Technical soundness Cannot be evaluated from the abstract alone. The absence of convergence data, protocol details, and quantitative metrics prevents assessment of whether the simulations support the conclusions. Readability for nonspecialists The abstract is reasonably clear but lacks biological context and explanation of methodological choices. The functional conclusion is stated too strongly relative to the evidence described. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The abstract describes a potentially interesting study, but the technical foundation and the strength of the generalizability and functional claims cannot be evaluated without the full manuscript. If the full paper provides convergence metrics, detailed protocols, quantitative comparisons across homologues, and appropriately hedged functional interpretation, the study could be supportive. As presented, the abstract alone does not make the case. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that the rigid segment (residues 132-139) "corresponds to the portion interacting with the cavity formed by tRNA and TRMT10C N-terminal domain" is unverifiable from the abstract; no structural or interaction data are provided. The generalizability claim across the Trm10 family is unsupported without specifying the number and diversity of homologues studied. The functional conclusion about "tuning" and "facilitating tRNA positioning and efficient catalysis" is presented as a finding but is better characterized as a hypothesis based on the described evidence. The robustness of the flexibility ranking across force fields is asserted but not quantified. boundary Claims and evidence as presented in the abstract; no access to full text, figures, tables, or supplementary materials Shared manuscript claim summary The authors use all-atom molecular dynamics simulations of seven tripeptides (six C-terminal amidated D/Y/F sequence isomers plus FFD) to compute conformational free-energy landscapes based on intramolecular side-chain dihedral angles. They introduce a novel numerical method to characterize these landscapes and report a correlation between thermal conformational accessibility and self-assembly propensity. They also evaluate water model effects on conformational ensembles and investigate ionization state influences. The methodology is claimed to implicitly account for sequence context, have low computational cost, and represent progress toward theory-informed design of peptide materials. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no quantitative results, correlation coefficients, simulation parameters, or methodological details are provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, simulation protocols, force field parameters, water model specifications, ionization state definitions, statistical analyses, and any validation of the proposed numerical characterization method Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a conceptually interesting approach linking single-molecule conformational ensembles to supramolecular self-assembly outcomes. The idea of using side-chain dihedral-based free-energy landscapes as a predictor is plausible and potentially useful. However, the abstract provides insufficient quantitative evidence to evaluate the strength of the claimed correlation, the robustness of the novel method, or the generality of the conclusions. The scope is narrow (seven tripeptides), and the leap from single-molecule simulations to assembly propensity requires more careful justification than is visible here. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in peptide self-assembly, computational biophysics, and peptide materials design would be interested. The work addresses a practical need for low-cost computational predictors of assembly behavior, which is relevant to the growing field of sequence-defined peptide materials. The water model comparison may also interest those developing simulation protocols for short peptides. Major strengths The approach is computationally economical, using single-molecule simulations rather than expensive multi-molecule assembly simulations. The focus on sequence isomers is a well-chosen test case because it isolates sequence context effects. The explicit consideration of water model and ionization state effects shows methodological awareness. 04 背景与发展脉络 （标注：以下脉络主要基于本文摘要及 Article I 的引用框架，未经外部系统核验，属「仅本文框架」） - 阶段一：常规二面角分析 （经典方法） - 代表：Ramachandran 图、二面角时间序列、Markov state models - 优点：直接、计算简单、与构象分类（alpha-helix, beta-sheet, turn）对应 - 局限：残基局部视角，丢失肽平面间的空间协同 - 阶段二：collective variable / 降维方法 - 代表：PCA、tICA、path collective variables - 优点：捕捉全局协同运动 - 局限：缺乏化学/结构可解释性，难以直接映射到具体肽平面运动 - 阶段三：motif-level 框架（Article I） - 代表：以结构基序（如肽平面）为基本单元，定义自然坐标 (theta, phi) - 优点：提供 motif 特异的 orientational potential、概率分布、序参数、熵 - 局限：单独使用时与常规构象分类脱节 - 本文位置 ：将阶段一与阶段三结合，形成互补分析框架，在 RBD 体系上验证并推广。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 常规二面角分析丢失协同信息 只能看到单个残基的 Psi/Phi 变化，无法判断哪些肽平面一起运动 二面角是残基局部的，不编码肽平面间的空间关系 摘要：常规分析"identifies local conformational changes, whereas motif-level analysis reveals which peptide planes move in concert" motif-level 分析缺乏与常规构象分类的对应 单独使用时难以判断 beta-turn 类型等经典构象 基序坐标 (theta, phi) 与 Ramachandran 分类无直接映射 摘要：需要"combines this motif-level representation with conventional backbone-dihedral-angle analysis" 环区构象重构机制多样且难以统一描述 RBD、RBD 二聚体、RBD-Rac1 中重构模式不同（canonical vs noncanonical） 不同体系/环境下肽平面运动模式不同，缺乏统一分析语言 摘要：K50-G51 在 RBD 中为 canonical type-II-to-I flip，在 RBD-Rac1 中"more intricate and noncanonical" 熵贡献难以从 MD 中可靠估计 结合/二聚化自由能中的熵项难以从常规分析获得 需要 motif 特异的概率分布与序参数才能计算 orientational entropy 摘要：motif-level 分析提供"entropy...expressed in the natural orientational coordinates" 06 核心思想 表面方法 ：将 Article I 的 motif-level（肽平面）表示与常规 (Psi, Phi) 二面角分析结合，对微秒级 MD 轨迹进行双重分析。motif-level 部分以肽平面为基本单元，定义自然坐标 (theta, phi)，计算 orientational potential、概率分布、序参数和熵；常规部分用 (Psi, Phi) 识别局部构象变化。 核心洞察 ：两种分析提供互补信息——常规分析回答"哪里变了"（局部残基），motif-level 回答"怎么变的"（哪些肽平面协同、如何组织）。这种互补性使得不同的构象重构机制（canonical flip、noncanonical transition、协同多肽平面运动、动态铰链）可以在统一框架下比较。 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] ：对于 MD 轨迹分析，选择"基本描述单元"（残基 vs. 肽平面 vs. 更大基序）决定了能回答的问题类型。将不同粒度的描述结合，可以同时获得局部精度与全局协同信息。这一思路可迁移到其他生物分子体系（如核酸、糖蛋白）的构象分析。 07 方法总览 输入 ：微秒级 MD 轨迹（RBD、RBD 二聚体、RBD-Rac1 复合物） 输出 ：构象重构机制的分类描述、motif 特异的 orientational properties、熵贡献估计 模块 ： 1. 常规二面角分析：提取每个残基的 (Psi, Phi) 时间序列，识别局部构象变化 2. 创新状态 ：unverified Review setup Input scope Abstract only Assessment boundary Claims and evidence presented in the abstract; no access to full text, figures, tables, or supplementary materials Shared manuscript claim summary The authors propose a combined analytical framework that pairs conventional backbone-dihedral-angle analysis with a motif-level representation of peptide planes to study conformational restructuring in protein loops, using the Rho GTPase-binding domain of plexin-B1 (RBD) as a test system. They report that this combined approach yields complementary information on local versus collective conformational changes, provides motif-specific thermodynamic and ordering properties in natural orientational coordinates, and enables assessment of entropic contributions to free energy differences associated with RBD dimerization and RBD-Rac1 binding. Specific findings include canonical type-II-to-type-I beta-turn crankshaft flips of the K50-G51 peptide plane in RBD, more intricate noncanonical transitions in RBD-Rac1, deviations from canonical helicity with subsequent relaxation, a concerted multi-peptide-plane dynamical process in the RBD dimer, a versatile dynamic hinge, and through-space dynamical correlations. The scientific questions are relevant and the proposed approach could offer insights beyond conventional methods. However, the abstract alone provides insufficient evidence to evaluate the technical soundness of the methods, the robustness of the conclusions, or the quantitative validity of the reported thermodynamic and entropic assessments. Several claims are stated without supporting numerical data or methodological detail, and the relationship between the two analytical components is described at a conceptual level without demonstration of how they are integrated in practice. The manuscript may merit consideration if the full paper provides rigorous validation, but the case is not established from the supplied material. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational biophysicists and molecular dynamics practitioners studying protein conformational dynamics, particularly those focused on loop restructuring, beta-turn transitions, and allosteric mechanisms. Researchers working on plexin signaling or Rho GTPase biology may also find the specific system relevant. Methodologists interested in novel order parameters or collective coordinate descriptions of protein dynamics could be attracted to the motif-level framework. Major strengths The conceptual distinction between residue-local and peptide-plane-collective descriptions is clear and potentially powerful. The use of natural orientational coordinates for expressing thermodynamic and ordering properties is a principled idea. The application to multiple related systems (RBD, RBD dimer, RBD-Rac1) suggests an attempt at generalizability. The explicit attention to entropic contributions to binding and dimerization free energies addresses a nontrivial and often neglected aspect of such calculations. Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract addresses a practically important question in structure-based drug discovery, namely the marginal utility of additional crystal structures for pose prediction. The dataset from the COVID Moonshot project is substantial and well suited to this analysis. However, the abstract alone does not provide sufficient methodological detail to evaluate the robustness of the central claim that five structures per scaffold is sufficient. Key definitions and validation steps are absent, and the generalizability of the recommendation beyond this specific target and campaign remains unclear. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational chemists and structural biologists engaged in structure-based drug discovery campaigns, particularly those in academic and industrial settings where crystallography resources are limited. The work offers a data-driven heuristic for deciding when to stop collecting additional structures, which could inform project timelines and budgeting. Researchers working on SARS-CoV-2 antivirals and those developing docking or pose prediction methods would also find the benchmark dataset and analysis relevant. Major strengths The question is well posed and of direct practical relevance. The dataset is large and derived from a real, open science campaign, which lends ecological validity. The observation that similar reference ligands improve pose prediction is consistent with domain knowledge and provides a useful confirmation. The proposed plateau at five structures per scaffold is a concrete, actionable number that could guide future campaigns. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The abstract claims that "success plateaus after approximately five crystal structures per generic Bemis-Murcko scaffold, exceeding 95% for the campaign's lead series." Evidence pointer Abstract only, location not provided Concern The central quantitative claim of a plateau at five structures is presented without any definition of "success" or the metric used to measure pose prediction accuracy. It is unclear whether success refers to a root-mean-square deviation threshold, a docking score cutoff, or a binary classification of acceptable versus unacceptable poses. Without this definition, the 95% figure cannot be interpreted or compared to other studies. Why it matters The practical recommendation to stop at five structures per scaffold depends entirely on the validity and meaning of the success metric. If the metric is lenient or target-specific, the recommendation may not transfer to other systems. The absence of this definition prevents the reader from assessing whether the plateau is a real phenomenon or an artifact of the chosen threshold. Resolution test Provide a clear definition of the success metric, including the exact threshold used, and show the sensitivity of the plateau location and the 95% value to reasonable variations in that threshold. If the plateau is robust across thresholds, the claim is strengthened. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Generalizability Claim pointer The abstract states that "this work provides practical recommendations for resource allocation in structure-enabled drug discovery campaigns." Evidence pointer Abstract only, location not provided Concern The recommendation is derived from a single target, SARS-CoV-2 main protease, and a single chemical series from one campaign. The abstract does not discuss how the number of required structures might vary with target flexibility, binding site plasticity, ligand chemotype diversity, or the docking method used. The claim of practical recommendations for campaigns in general is therefore not supported by the evidence presented. Why it matters If the five-structure rule is specific to this target or to the COVID Moonshot series, applying it broadly could lead to under-sampling in other projects. The abstract overreaches by implying general applicability without a comparative analysis across targets or methods. Resolution test Either temper the recommendation to be explicitly target- and method-specific, or provide additional analyses showing that the plateau behavior is consistent across multiple targets, docking programs, or ligand series. A discussion of expected variability would also help. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Statistical robustness Claim pointer The abstract implies a monotonic relationship between the number of reference structures and pose prediction success, with a plateau beyond five. Evidence pointer Abstract only, location not provided Concern The abstract does not report any statistical measures of uncertainty around the plateau estimate. It is unclear how many scaffolds were analyzed, how variable the success rates were across scaffolds, and whether the plateau at five is a central tendency or an upper bound. Without confidence intervals or a measure of spread, the reader cannot judge the reliability of the number. Why it matters A recommendation of "approximately five" is only useful if the variability around that number is small. If some scaffolds require ten structures and others only two, the practical guidance is less clear. The abstract should report the distribution of required structure counts across scaffolds. Resolution test Report the number of scaffolds analyzed, the distribution of success rates as a function of structure count, and confidence intervals or other measures of uncertainty around the plateau point. Show that the plateau is consistent across most scaffolds. Required correction State the docking software and version, and note whether the conclusions are expected to hold across different docking tools. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected element Comparison to alternatives Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Issue The abstract does not compare the proposed approach to other strategies for selecting reference structures, such as maximal diversity selection or ensemble docking. The success metric must be defined and its sensitivity tested, and the generalizability claim must be either supported with additional data or appropriately qualified. R1-M3, while not blocking, should be addressed to strengthen the statistical basis of the recommendation. The originality is moderate. Scientific importance: The work has clear practical importance for drug discovery campaigns, but its significance is limited by the single-target focus. The importance would be higher if the findings were shown to generalize. Interdisciplinary readership: The topic sits at the interface of structural biology, computational chemistry, and medicinal chemistry. The abstract is accessible to these communities, but the lack of methodological detail limits broader appeal. Technical soundness: Cannot be fully assessed from the abstract. The central quantitative claim lacks a defined metric and uncertainty estimates, which is a significant gap. Readability for nonspecialists: The abstract is clearly written and the main message is easy to grasp. However, terms such as "Bemis-Murcko scaffold" and "pose prediction" are used without explanation, which may exclude readers outside computational chemistry. The question is relevant and the dataset is valuable, but the abstract as presented does not establish the robustness or generalizability of the five-structure rule. The authors should provide a clear definition of the success metric, show sensitivity analyses, and either qualify or extend the generalizability claims. The claim that the work "provides practical recommendations for resource allocation in structure-based drug discovery campaigns" is unsupported beyond the specific target and series analyzed. supplementary data Shared manuscript claim summary The authors introduce Azi-LPXL-MS, a chemoselective aziridination-based crosslinking strategy coupled with mass spectrometry, to capture lipid-protein contacts and intraprotein distance constraints in a single experiment. They apply it to beta-lactoglobulin (BLG) and diacylglycerol acyltransferase 1 (DGAT1), reporting identification of phosphatidic acid (PA)-binding sites, lipid-dependent conformational rearrangements, and an allosteric conformational network, with validation via mutagenesis and docking. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no figures, tables, methods, or supplementary materials provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, experimental procedures, mass spectrometry data, structural models, mutagenesis details, docking parameters, and validation statistics Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially valuable methodological advance in studying lipid-protein interactions with site resolution. The concept of using aziridination to install reactive handles on native unsaturated lipids, followed by DSS-based crosslinking, is chemically plausible and could address a genuine gap in the field. However, the abstract alone provides insufficient evidence to assess the robustness of the method, the validity of the biological conclusions, or the strength of the validation. The claims regarding conformational changes and allosteric networks are ambitious and would require substantial structural and functional evidence to be convincing. The work is likely of interest to the lipid biology and chemical biology communities, but the current evidence base does not establish the case. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in lipid-protein interaction biology, chemical biology, and structural biology would be interested. The method offers a potential tool for capturing transient lipid-protein contacts and conformational changes, which is relevant to understanding membrane protein function, lipid signaling, and drug development targeting lipid-binding sites. Major strengths The methodological concept is novel and addresses a recognized limitation in the field. The integration of lipid-binding site identification with intraprotein distance constraints in a single workflow is elegant and potentially powerful. The application to both a soluble protein (BLG) and an integral membrane enzyme (DGAT1) suggests broad applicability. The inclusion of functional validation via mutagenesis and docking strengthens the biological claims. Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The abstract does not provide any details on the efficiency, specificity, or reproducibility of the aziridination and crosslinking reactions. It is unclear how the authors distinguish true lipid-protein crosslinks from background or nonspecific interactions, and how the distance constraints are derived and interpreted. Why it matters Without evidence of chemoselectivity and low false-positive rates, the core methodological claim is unsubstantiated. The reliability of the conformational conclusions depends entirely on the quality of the crosslinking data. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; methods and results are summarized but not detailed Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, experimental protocols, statistical details, simulation parameters, and supplementary data Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially interesting finding that a single disease-associated mutation in a GPCR intrinsically disordered region can selectively modulate transducer coupling and cellular behavior. The combination of experimental and computational approaches is appropriate for the question. However, the abstract alone does not provide sufficient detail to evaluate the rigor of the methods, the robustness of the statistical analyses, or the strength of the causal links between the observed conformational changes and functional outcomes. The claim that the mutation "rewires" signaling through "C-terminal ensemble redistribution" is plausible but not fully established from the provided evidence. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in GPCR biology, particularly those studying biased agonism, intrinsically disordered regions in signaling proteins, and the molecular basis of disease-associated mutations. The work may also interest investigators focused on AML biology and oxysterol receptor signaling, as well as computational biologists studying allosteric communication in membrane proteins. Major strengths The study addresses a timely and important question about the functional role of intrinsically disordered regions in GPCR signaling. The use of multiple orthogonal experimental assays (BRET, FRET, bioluminescence, fluorescence, migration) combined with molecular dynamics simulations and allosteric network analysis is commendable. The finding that a single mutation can selectively impair GRK2 and beta-arrestin2 recruitment while preserving or enhancing Gi activation suggests a potential mechanism for biased signaling. Å）和空间重叠（≤350 Å³）是比能量打分更快速、更物理的过滤标准。在构象采样任务中，先以硬几何约束大幅缩减候选集，再对少量幸存者执行昂贵计算（MD、MM-PBSA），可显著提升整体效率。这一思想可迁移至构象生成管线的后处理阶段。 可解释 ML 排序优于通用打分函数 ：传统打分函数（GNINA 是预测 RMSD 的最重要特征，且与已知的 HePTP KIM 肽结合机制一致（R16/Q18 残基的氢键网络）。这提示在片段化对接中，末端片段的结合模式可能决定整体构象质量，可优先优化首片段的对接精度。 自动预处理是实际部署的瓶颈 ：3382 例中仅 257 例自动成功（7.6%），但 500 例失败案例经修正后 450 例成功（90% 恢复率）。这说明管线自动化程度（而非算法本身）是实际应用的主要限制。在开发计算管线时，应投入资源构建鲁棒的自动预处理模块（PDB 修复、拓扑生成、参数标准化）。 线性扩展性设计 ：STELLAR 的计算时间随片段数近似线性增长（4 片段 1.56h → 7 片段 2.27h 单组合），得益于片段对接的并行化。这种「每片段独立对接 + 并行调度」的架构适合 HPC 环境，可迁移至大规模虚拟筛选场景。 跨聚合物类型的适应性 ：STELLAR 通过修改成键原子定义（肽键 C-N vs 糖苷键 C1-O4/C1-O3）即可从多肽扩展至多糖，表明片段化对接框架对线性聚合物的通用性。这一设计启示：在开发通用对接/构象工具时，应将「键类型」抽象为可配置参数，而非硬编码。 Review setup Input scope Full manuscript text (abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations, outlook, conclusions) as provided. Assessment boundary Scientific and technical evaluation of the STELLAR workflow, its validation, and the claims made. No assessment of code availability, reproducibility beyond described methods, or comparison with unpublished tools. Shared manuscript claim summary The authors present STELLAR, a fragment-based docking workflow for highly flexible long-chain biopolymers (peptides 10–21 residues, polysaccharides 6–10 monosaccharides). They claim accurate pose prediction (RMSD < 5 Å) on a benchmark of 257 protein–peptide and 8 protein–polysaccharide complexes, linear computational scaling, minimal GPU usage, and a novel interpretable machine learning-derived ranking formula for the p38α–HePTP KIM peptide system. Visible evidence base Text descriptions of methods and results; references to Figures 1–4, S1–S19; Tables S1–S8. No actual figures, tables, or supplementary data were provided in the submitted material. Missing materials affecting confidence All figures, tables, and supplementary files are referenced but not included. This prevents verification of quantitative results, statistical analyses, and visual data. The specific benchmark composition, selection criteria, and per-case results are not fully described. Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript addresses a real and important gap in docking methodology: handling highly flexible long-chain biopolymers. The fragment-based approach with explicit filtering, recombination, and short MD relaxation is conceptually sound and the reported performance is promising. However, the current evidence base is incomplete, with all figures and tables absent, making it impossible to verify the central claims. The machine learning analysis is presented as a proof-of-concept but lacks external validation. The writing is generally clear but contains some redundancy and overstatement. The work has potential, but the case is not fully established from the provided material. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational chemists and structural biologists working on peptide–protein interactions, drug discovery researchers targeting protein–protein interfaces, and developers of docking software. The workflow's claimed efficiency and scalability would also interest groups performing high-throughput virtual screening of biopolymers. Major strengths 1. Addresses a genuine methodological gap: docking of long, flexible biopolymers is poorly handled by existing tools. 2. The fragment-based strategy with explicit geometric filtering is a pragmatic and potentially generalizable approach. 3. The inclusion of a short MD relaxation step to correct assembly artifacts is a sensible addition. 4. The attempt to derive an interpretable ranking metric, rather than relying on black-box scoring, is commendable. 5. The workflow is designed for CPU-based execution, which broadens accessibility. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer "STELLAR achieved RMSD values below 5 Å in validation experiments using benchmark complexes from Propedia and the Protein Data Bank (PDB)." Evidence pointer Results section; Figures 1–4; Tables S2–S5 (location not provided) Concern The central validation claim is that STELLAR achieves RMSD < 5 Å for the benchmark complexes. However, no figures or tables are provided in the submitted material. The text describes distributions and percentages but does not allow the reader to assess the quality of predictions, the distribution of RMSD values, or the specific cases that failed. The claim of "100% success" for minimum RMSD and ">95%" for all cases is stated without supporting data. Why it matters The entire utility of the workflow rests on its ability to predict near-native poses. Without the actual data, the claim cannot be evaluated. The reader cannot determine whether the success is uniform across peptide lengths, whether certain sequence features are problematic, or whether the 5 Å threshold is appropriate. Resolution test Provide the actual RMSD distributions for all 257 peptide and 8 polysaccharide cases, including per-case values, success rates at multiple thresholds, and a breakdown by peptide length. Include the referenced figures and tables. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Comparative validation Claim pointer "It offers a faster and more efficient alternative to several state-of-the-art tools across a range of peptide lengths." Evidence pointer Results section; Tables S7 and S8 (location not provided) Concern The claim of superiority over existing tools is made, but no direct comparison is presented in the text. The authors state that "direct quantitative comparison is difficult" and instead compare to literature-reported values. This is insufficient to support the claim of being "faster and more efficient." The runtime analysis is only presented for STELLAR itself, not against other tools under identical conditions. Why it matters A new docking workflow must demonstrate clear advantages over existing methods to justify adoption. Without a head-to-head comparison on the same benchmark with the same hardware, the claimed advantage is unsubstantiated. Resolution test Provide a direct comparison with at least one or two established docking tools (e.g., standard GNINA whole-peptide docking, HADDOCK, or similar) on the same benchmark complexes, reporting both accuracy (RMSD) and runtime. Alternatively, clearly frame the work as a proof-of-concept without claims of superiority. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Generalizability of ranking model Claim pointer "A novel scoring function derived from the STELLAR pipeline was successfully applied to the p38α–HePTP KIM peptide complex. This approach showed a strong correlation between the RMSD of the predicted poses and the values obtained from the proposed scoring function." Evidence pointer Results section; Figures 8–10, S8–S19; Table S1 (location not provided) Concern The machine learning-derived ranking formula is trained and tested on a single protein–peptide complex (p38α–HePTP). The authors acknowledge this is a proof-of-concept, but the claim that it "can be extended to other systems" is speculative. The formula includes interaction terms specific to this system's features, and there is no evidence of transferability. Why it matters A ranking metric that works for one system may not generalize. The value of the approach depends on whether the identified features are system-specific or broadly applicable. Without cross-validation on multiple complexes, the utility of the ranking formula is unclear. Resolution test Apply the same methodology to at least 2–3 additional protein–peptide complexes with known structures, and report the correlation between the derived score and RMSD. If transferability is not yet established, temper the claims accordingly. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Assembly rate and selection bias Claim pointer "The revised pipeline successfully recovered 450 of 500 previously unsuccessful cases, corresponding to a 90% recovery rate." Evidence pointer Results section; Table S6 (location not provided) Concern The initial assembly rate is described as "relatively low" but the exact figure is not stated. The recovery of 450/500 previously failed cases is presented as a success, but it is unclear whether these recovered cases were then included in the final benchmark of 257 successful cases. If the benchmark only includes cases that assembled successfully, there is a potential selection bias that could inflate the reported accuracy. Why it matters If the benchmark excludes cases that failed to assemble, the reported RMSD values may not be representative of the workflow's performance on arbitrary inputs. The reader needs to know the total number of attempted cases and the success rate to assess practical utility. Resolution test Report the total number of cases attempted, the number that assembled successfully, and the number that failed at each stage. Clarify whether the 257 reported cases are a subset of a larger attempted set, and discuss the implications of assembly failures on practical applicability. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Methods, Fragment Docking section Evidence pointer "An intermediate exhaustiveness value of 64 (default: 8) was employed" Issue The rationale for choosing exhaustiveness 64 is not explained. It is unclear whether this value was optimized, chosen based on prior experience, or determined by computational constraints. Required correction Provide a brief justification for the chosen exhaustiveness value, or state that it was selected based on preliminary testing. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Reproducibility Affected element Methods, Filtering and Joining section Evidence pointer "An overlap threshold of 350 Å3 is applied by default" Issue The overlap threshold is stated, but the sensitivity of the results to this parameter is not discussed. It is unclear whether the results are robust to reasonable variations in this threshold. Required correction Add a brief sensitivity analysis or discussion of how the threshold affects the number of valid combinations and final RMSD values. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Statistical reporting Affected element Results, Poses Obtained section Evidence pointer "The median RMSD value was 3.47 Å, and the mean was 3.49 Å" Issue Only mean and median are reported. No confidence intervals, standard deviations, or measures of dispersion are provided for the RMSD distributions. Required correction Report standard deviations or interquartile ranges for the RMSD distributions, and consider providing confidence intervals for the mean values. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Terminology Affected element Throughout Evidence pointer "very short molecular dynamics simulation" Issue The term "very short" is vague. The total simulation time (26 ps) is stated later, but the phrase is imprecise. Required correction Replace "very short" with the specific duration (26 ps) or a more precise descriptor. Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected element Methods, Benchmark Design section Evidence pointer "Complexes were retrieved from the Propedia database" Issue The criteria for selecting the 257 peptide complexes from the larger Propedia database are not described. It is unclear whether the selection was random, stratified, or biased toward certain peptide lengths or sequence features. Required correction Describe the selection criteria for the benchmark complexes, including any filtering based on peptide length, sequence diversity, or structural quality. Concern ID R1-m6 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Results, Runtime Performance section Evidence pointer "STELLAR enables extensive parallelization of its workflow" Issue The parallelization strategy is described qualitatively. It is unclear whether the parallelization is across fragments, across complexes, or across both. Required correction Clarify the parallelization strategy and how it scales with the number of available cores or nodes. Risk / unsupported claims The claim of "100% success" for minimum RMSD < 5 Å across the benchmark is unverifiable without the actual data. The claim of being "faster and more efficient" than existing tools is unsupported without direct comparative benchmarks. The generalizability of the machine learning-derived ranking formula to other systems is speculative, as it is derived from a single complex. The statement that STELLAR "addresses a critical limitation in current docking methodologies" is an overstatement given the limited validation presented. The claim that the workflow "scales linearly in computational time" is only supported by a single figure reference (Figure 4) that was not provided. The assertion that STELLAR "avoids reliance on generative approximations" is presented as an advantage, but the manuscript does not provide a systematic comparison against generative approaches to substantiate this.

个复合物）及首个以已批准药物为核心的子集 FARMA2025（165 个复合物）；(2) 在统一标准化条件下系统比较了 DOCK6、Vina、AD4 三种主流开源对接程序在四种任务（构象重现、交叉对接、数据库富集、反向对接）上的表现。该工作为对接方法开发者提供了公平比较的平台，也为用户选择对接工具和参数提供了数据驱动的建议。 02 一句话总结 本文构建了包含 1,244 个蛋白质-配体复合物的 SB2025 基准测试集及其已批准药物子集 FARMA2025（165 个复合物），在标准化条件下系统评估了 DOCK6、AutoDock Vina 和 AutoDock 4 在构象重现、交叉对接、数据库富集和反向对接四种任务中的表现，发现三种程序在不同任务和蛋白家族上各有优劣，且 FARMA2025 的药物靶标类别分布与 FDA 2023 年批准的小分子药物靶标分布高度一致（R²=0.72）。 03 研究问题 具体问题 : 在统一、标准化、大规模且包含已批准药物的基准测试条件下，DOCK6、AutoDock Vina 和 AutoDock 4 三种主流开源对接程序在构象重现（PR）、交叉对接（CD）、数据库富集（DE）和反向对接（RD）四种任务中的表现如何？ 为什么重要 : 分子对接是早期药物发现中最常用的计算方法之一，但不同程序使用不同的采样算法和打分函数，其性能高度依赖于测试集的选择。缺乏大规模、多样化、计算就绪且包含临床相关药物-靶标复合物的基准测试集，导致：(1) 开发者难以公平比较不同方法；(2) 用户难以根据实际需求选择最合适的工具和参数；(3) 已有基准测试结果差异大（如 PR 成功率从 23% 到 78%），部分原因是测试集偏差和协议不一致。 现有方法为何不足 : 已有基准测试存在以下问题：(1) 测试集规模有限（多数为 100-700 个复合物）；(2) 蛋白类别覆盖不全，特别是缺乏膜蛋白（GPCR、离子通道等）和转运体；(3) 多数测试集未包含已批准药物与其治疗靶标的复合物，无法反映真实药物发现场景；(4) 不同研究使用不同的准备协议、打分函数版本和评估标准，结果难以直接比较。 精确的 "Can ... ?" 研究问题 : 在标准化条件下，DOCK6、Vina 和 AD4 能否在不同蛋白类别和任务类型中保持一致的性能排名？已批准药物子集（FARMA2025）是否比通用测试集更能反映程序在真实药物发现场景中的表现差异？ 04 背景与发展脉络 （注：此脉络基于本文引言及参考文献构建，经外部核验部分已标注） 阶段 代表性方法/工作 优点 局限 本文位置 早期对接程序（1980s-1990s） DOCK（Kuntz
