The mechanistic link between structural observables (radius of gyration, RMSD, hydrogen bonds) and binding free energy changes is asserted but not demonstrated.

01 基本信息 标题 : Computer-Aided Drug Design for Type 2 Diabetes-Related Enzymes: SILCS-Based Fragment Mapping, Pharmacophore Modeling, and Virtual Screening 作者 : Mohammadi, Esmat; Lemkul, Justin A 单位 : 未提供（根据致谢推测为 Virginia Tech） 期刊/平台 : Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling 年份 : 2026 论文类型 : 方法开发 + 应用研究 领域 : 计算机辅助药物设计（CADD）；SILCS 片段映射；药效团建模；虚拟筛选 关键词 : SILCS, FragMap, Drude polarizable force field, pharmacophore, virtual screening, type 2 diabetes, maltase-glucoamylase, α-amylase DOI/arXiv : 10.1021/acs.jcim.6c01733 代码 : 未提供 数据 : 未提供（PDB 结构：3L4Y, 3TOP, 4GQR） 阅读日期 : 2026-10-23 在课题方向中的位置 : 本文属于「蛋白质结构相关计算研究 × 物理模拟（MD/GCMC）」方向，聚焦于 SILCS 片段映射方法在 高电荷酶活性位点 上的改进（neutral–charged 协议 + Drude 极化力场），并串联药效团建模与虚拟筛选，形成从位点表征到候选抑制剂优先排序的完整 CADD 流程。对本课题的可迁移点在于：SILCS FragMap 的生成与收敛性评估、药效团特征提取与虚拟筛选的集成策略、以及极化力场在高电荷口袋中的应用。 02 一句话总结 针对高电荷酶活性位点中带电探针抑制中性片段采样的问题，本文开发了 neutral–charged SILCS 协议（将带电与中性探针分开模拟）并结合 Drude 极化力场，在 NtMGAM、CtMGAM 和 α-amylase 三个 T2D 相关酶上生成了化学多样性更高的 FragMap，进而构建 SILCS-Pharmacophore 模型并完成虚拟筛选，最终通过 SILCS-MC 对接和 LGFE/LE 排序优先选出候选抑制剂。 03 研究问题 具体问题 : 在高电荷酶活性位点中，常规 SILCS 的混合探针模拟会导致强相互作用的带电探针（如甲基铵阳离子）主导采样，抑制中性片段（疏水、氢键供体/受体）的充分采样，从而降低 FragMap 的化学多样性；同时，加和力场（如 CHARMM）无法显式描述电子极化效应，可能影响高电荷环境中静电相互作用的表征精度。 为什么重要 : T2D 相关酶（NtMGAM、CtMGAM、α-amylase）的活性位点富含带电残基（Asp、His、Arg 等），是设计抑制剂的关键靶区。准确表征这些位点的相互作用特征（氢键、静电、疏水）是虚拟筛选成功的前提。若 FragMap 被单一探针主导，将遗漏关键的药物-靶点相互作用信息，降低筛选命中率。 现有方法不足 : 常规 SILCS 混合探针协议在高电荷位点存在竞争性排斥；加和力场缺乏极化描述；先前的 SILCS 研究未结合增强采样（如 GCMC-MD）与极化力场。 精确研究问题（Can...?） : Can a neutral–charged SILCS protocol combined with the Drude polarizable force field improve fragment sampling diversity and pharmacophore quality in highly charged enzyme active sites, thereby enhancing virtual screening hit prioritization for T2D-related enzymes? GCMC-MD 采样 : 100 轮 GCMC-MD 循环，每轮 200,000 步 GCMC + 1 ns MD 4. FragMap 生成 : 基于探针占有率计算三维网格上的归一化占有率，经 Boltzmann 变换转为自由能图 5. 药效团建模 : 基于 FragMap 特征（疏水、氢键供体/受体、阳离子、阴离子）聚类生成药效团 6. 虚拟筛选 : Pharmit 平台对 Maybridge（53,231 化合物）和 ChemBridge（1,240,308 化合物）库进行筛选 7. SILCS-MC 精修与排序 : 对命中化合物进行对接，计算 LGFE 和 LE 文字流程 : 蛋白结构准备 → 构建常规/neutral–charged 体系 → GCMC-MD 迭代采样 → 生成 FragMap → 评估收敛性（OC 值）→ 与晶体结构对比验证 → 生成药效团 → Pharmit 虚拟筛选 → SILCS-MC 精修 → LGFE/LE 排序 → 相关酶（NtMGAM、CtMGAM、α-amylase）的活性位点表征和虚拟筛选， 未涉及 其他 T2D 靶点（如 DPP-4、SGLT2）或其他高电荷酶系统。 oracle/真值输入 : 使用晶体结构中的已知抑制剂（miglitol、acarbose、myricetin）作为验证基准，但 未进行 实验酶活性测定或细胞实验验证。 端到端状态 : 流程为「FragMap → 药效团 → 虚拟筛选 → SILCS-MC 精修 → 排序」， 止步于计算预测 ，未进入湿实验验证阶段。 算力成本 : CHARMM 模拟每体系 1 μs（10 × 100 ns），Drude 模拟每体系 2 μs（100 × 20 ns），计算成本较高；Drude 模拟需额外处理 Drude 粒子（约 2-3 倍计算量）。 历史数据依赖 : 依赖 PDB 晶体结构（3L4Y, 3TOP, 4GQR），这些结构可能不代表溶液中的全部构象状态。 模型依赖 : 结果依赖力场选择（CHARMM36 vs Drude-2019）、探针集组成、GCMC 化学势参数、药效团特征阈值等。 最难情形 : 高电荷、柔性、溶剂暴露的活性位点（如 α-amylase 的浅而宽的活性位点）仍具挑战；Drude 模拟中带电探针的极化参数可能引入额外不确定性。 群体/领域边界 : Figures and tables are referenced but not provided in full detail. Assessment boundary Methodological soundness, validity of claims relative to presented evidence, and overall contribution to the field of computer-aided drug design. Experimental validation is outside the scope as this is a computational study. Shared manuscript claim summary The authors present an enhanced SILCS-based computational workflow that separates neutral and charged probe molecules and optionally uses the Drude polarizable force field, applied to three type 2 diabetes-related enzymes. They claim this approach alleviates competitive exclusion effects in highly charged active sites, improves fragment diversity, and enables identification of candidate inhibitors through virtual screening and clustering analysis. Visible evidence base Text descriptions of methods and results, convergence metrics (OC values) reported in text and supplementary tables, RMSD values for pose refinement, pharmacophore feature counts and FGFE values, virtual screening hit counts, and clustering outcomes. Specific figures and tables are referenced but not fully visible. Missing materials affecting confidence Full figures and tables (especially FragMap visualizations, pharmacophore models, and clustering dendrograms), detailed virtual screening hit lists, and complete supplementary information. Without these, quantitative assessment of several claims is limited. Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript addresses a relevant methodological gap in SILCS-based fragment mapping for highly charged enzyme active sites. The neutral-charged protocol is a logical extension of prior SILCS-RNA work, and the systematic comparison of additive versus polarizable force fields is valuable. The application to three diabetes-related enzymes provides practical context. However, several claims regarding the superiority of the Drude force field and the practical utility of identified hits are not fully supported by the presented evidence. The manuscript would benefit from clearer quantitative comparisons and a more critical discussion of limitations. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational chemists and structural biologists working on fragment-based drug design, particularly those applying SILCS or similar methods to challenging targets with charged binding sites. Researchers interested in polarizable force fields for drug discovery applications would also find the comparison relevant. The methodological framework could be adopted by groups studying other enzymes with highly charged active sites. Major strengths 1. The neutral-charged SILCS protocol is a well-motivated methodological innovation that directly addresses a known limitation of conventional SILCS in charged systems. 2. The systematic comparison of additive (CHARMM) and polarizable (Drude) force fields within the same workflow provides useful guidance for practitioners. 3. The application to three clinically relevant enzymes (NtMGAM, CtMGAM, α-amylase) grounds the methodology in a real drug design context. 4. The integration of multiple computational tools (SILCS, pharmacophore modeling, virtual screening, clustering) into a coherent pipeline is commendable. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The authors claim that "the Drude polarizable force field further enhanced resolution of electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding interactions" and that Drude-based pharmacophores led to "the best predicted inhibitors for CtMGAM and α-amylase." Evidence pointer Results and Discussion sections on affinity patterns and virtual screening; Tables S5-S7 Concern The quantitative evidence supporting the superiority of Drude over CHARMM is not clearly presented. RMSD improvements are modest (e.g., 4.06 Å vs 3.95 Å for miglitol), and the claim that Drude-based pharmacophores produced better inhibitors relies on LE comparisons that are not shown in the main text. The authors state that Drude pharmacophores for α-amylase rely entirely on hydrogen-bond donors, but it is unclear whether this represents a genuine improvement or simply a different, potentially less validated, interaction profile. Why it matters The central methodological contribution is the comparison between force fields. Without clear, quantitative evidence that Drude provides meaningful advantages, the practical recommendation for adopting the more computationally expensive polarizable workflow is not established. Resolution test Provide a direct, quantitative comparison of pose prediction accuracy (e.g., RMSD distributions across multiple ligands), virtual screening enrichment factors or ROC curves, and a statistical analysis of whether observed differences between CHARMM and Drude are significant. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Validation adequacy Claim pointer The authors claim that the SILCS-Pharmacophore models "successfully captured dominant interaction motifs within each binding site" and that virtual screening hits "exhibit superior predicted binding energetics relative to known inhibitors." Evidence pointer Results and Discussion sections on pharmacophore modeling and virtual screening; Tables S5-S7 Concern The validation of pharmacophore models and virtual screening hits is limited to comparison with known inhibitors (miglitol, acarbose, myricetin) and internal consistency checks. There is no experimental validation, no use of decoy sets to assess enrichment, and no comparison with alternative docking or screening methods. The claim that identified hits are "superior" is based solely on computed LE values, which may not translate to actual binding affinity. Why it matters Virtual screening is only useful if it can distinguish true binders from non-binders. Without external validation or benchmark comparisons, the practical utility of the proposed workflow for identifying viable drug candidates remains unproven. Resolution test Include a retrospective validation using known actives and decoys (e.g., DUD-E or similar) to compute enrichment factors. Alternatively, provide experimental binding data for a subset of top hits, or clearly state that such validation is planned as future work. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Reproducibility Claim pointer The authors state that "the Drude polarizable SILCS workflow described below was implemented separately in this study and is not part of the standard SilcsBio 2023.1 protein workflow." Evidence pointer Methods section, Drude SILCS Workflow Concern The implementation details of the Drude SILCS workflow are not fully specified. Key parameters such as the Drude-2019 force field version, the exact protocol for adding lone pairs and Drude oscillators, the equilibration scheme, and the criteria for selecting snapshots for GCMC-MD are described but lack sufficient detail for reproduction. The custom Python script for coordinate conversion is mentioned but not provided or described in detail. Why it matters Reproducibility is a cornerstone of computational research. Without complete methodological details, other groups cannot implement or verify the proposed Drude SILCS workflow. Resolution test Provide a detailed step-by-step protocol, including all input files, parameter settings, and scripts, either in the main text or as supplementary material. Consider depositing the workflow in a public repository. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Abstract Evidence pointer Abstract, first sentence Issue The abstract states that "highly charged enzyme active sites present a challenge for conventional SILCS" but does not specify what the challenge is beyond "suppress sampling of neutral fragments." A brief explanation of the mechanism would help readers understand the motivation. Required correction Add a phrase such as "because strongly interacting charged probes can outcompete neutral fragments for binding site occupancy" to the abstract. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected element Methods, Protein Preparation Evidence pointer Methods section, Protein Preparation Issue The authors state that "all water molecules and ions were removed from the structures" but do not specify whether crystallographic ligands (e.g., inhibitors, cofactors) were also removed. This is important because retained ligands could bias subsequent fragment mapping. Required correction Clarify whether all non-protein entities, including ligands and cofactors, were removed during preparation. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Statistical rigor Affected element Results, Convergence of the SILCS Simulations Evidence pointer Results and Discussion, Convergence section Issue OC values are reported as single numbers without measures of variability. Given that ten independent simulations were performed, it would be informative to report mean and standard deviation or range. Required correction Report OC values as mean ± standard deviation across the ten independent simulations. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Interpretation Affected element Results, Virtual Screening Evidence pointer Results and Discussion, Virtual Screening sections Issue The authors report that "no overlap was identified between the Maybridge and ChemBridge hit sets" but do not discuss whether this is expected or concerning. Given that both libraries are diverse, some overlap might be anticipated if the pharmacophore models are capturing a conserved binding mode. Required correction Add a brief discussion of whether the lack of overlap is consistent with the chemical diversity of the two libraries and the specificity of the pharmacophore models. Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Presentation Affected element Conclusions Evidence pointer Conclusions, final paragraph Issue The conclusion that "the neutral-charged SILCS protocol should be viewed as a targeted strategy for mitigating competitive exclusion rather than as a universal replacement" is well stated, but the practical guidance for when to use which protocol could be more explicit. Required correction Add a sentence summarizing the conditions under which the neutral-charged protocol is recommended (e.g., highly charged active sites) versus when the conventional protocol may suffice. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1: Insufficient quantitative evidence for Drude superiority R1-M2: Lack of external validation for virtual screening results R1-M3: Incomplete methodological details for reproduction of the Drude workflow Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality The neutral-charged SILCS protocol is a novel adaptation of existing methodology, and the systematic comparison with a polarizable force field adds an original dimension. However, the core SILCS method is well established, and the innovation is incremental rather than paradigm-shifting. Scientific importance The work addresses a real limitation in fragment-based drug design for charged enzyme systems, which is relevant to many therapeutic targets. The methodological guidance on when to use neutral-charged versus conventional protocols is practically useful. However, the lack of experimental validation limits the immediate impact. Interdisciplinary readership The manuscript is primarily of interest to computational chemists and structural biologists. The clinical relevance to type 2 diabetes is mentioned but not developed in a way that would attract a broader biomedical audience. Technical soundness The computational methods are generally sound, and the convergence analysis is appropriate. However, the validation of virtual screening results is insufficient, and the statistical treatment of comparisons between force fields is lacking. Readability for nonspecialists The manuscript is clearly written for a specialist audience. The methods are described in sufficient detail for practitioners, but the significance of the findings may not be immediately apparent to readers outside the field. The abstract could be more accessible. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved. The methodological framework is promising and addresses a genuine need, but the current evidence does not fully establish the claimed advantages of the Drude force field or the practical utility of the identified hits. Addressing the major concerns through additional validation and clearer quantitative comparisons would significantly strengthen the manuscript.

结构域和激酶结构域（KD）协同识别 PIP3 膜，形成四种不同的膜结合模式，其中 KD 通过碱性残基与 PIP3 直接互作，稳定膜结合态并影响 AKT 在膜上的取向。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：AKT 的 PH 结构域和激酶结构域（KD）如何在分子层面协同调控 AKT 在含 PIP3 膜上的结合与激活？ 为什么重要 ：PI3K/AKT 信号通路是细胞增殖、存活的关键通路，AKT 膜招募是其激活的第一步。理解 PH 与 KD 的协同机制有助于揭示 AKT 激活的结构基础，并为靶向 AKT 膜结合的药物设计提供新思路。 现有方法为何不足 ：以往研究多聚焦 PH 结构域单独与 PIP3 的结合，缺乏对全长 AKT 在膜上动态行为的原子级描述；实验方法（如突变、共定位）难以提供膜结合态的构象细节。 精确研究问题 ：Can full-length AKT on PIP3-containing membranes adopt multiple distinct membrane-bound states, and do the PH domain and KD cooperate to determine these states and their functional consequences? 04 背景与发展脉络 阶段一 ：PH 结构域单独研究（约 The central claim that PH domain and kinase domain cooperate in membrane binding is plausible and mechanistically relevant. However, the abstract alone provides insufficient detail to evaluate the technical rigor of the simulations, the statistical robustness of the binding mode populations, or the quantitative support from single-molecule imaging. Several claims are stated without visible evidence, and the relationship between simulation timescales and cellular observations is not addressed. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in cell signaling, particularly those studying PI3K/AKT pathway regulation, membrane-protein interactions, and lipid-mediated signaling. Computational biophysicists interested in multidomain protein-membrane interactions and coarse-grained or atomistic simulation methodologies would also find the work relevant. The combination of simulation and single-molecule imaging may appeal to interdisciplinary groups bridging molecular dynamics and cell biology. Major strengths The study addresses a mechanistically important question that is not fully resolved in the literature, namely how the PH domain and kinase domain cooperate in AKT membrane recruitment. The use of full-length AKT in simulations is a notable advance over domain-only studies. The identification of a secondary PIP3 binding site in the PH domain and PIP3 interactions with basic residues in the kinase domain are specific and testable findings. The integration of live-cell single-molecule imaging provides a complementary experimental dimension. Why it matters Molecular dynamics simulations of protein-membrane systems are highly sensitive to force field choice, system size, and simulation length. If the simulations are not sufficiently converged or replicated, the four binding modes may be artifacts of insufficient sampling rather than genuine conformational states. Resolution test Provide population fractions for each binding mode at each PIP3 concentration tested, with appropriate statistical analyses (e.g., bootstrapping or replicate-based error estimates). Show that the differences across concentrations are significant and that the preferred orientation changes in a consistent manner. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The authors claim that live-cell single-molecule imaging supports distinct but cooperative roles of the PH domain and kinase domain in membrane recruitment, with the PH domain promoting membrane association and the kinase domain enhancing recruitment efficiency and stabilizing longer-residence membrane-bound states. Evidence pointer Abstract only; imaging methods and quantification not provided Concern The abstract does not describe the single-molecule imaging experiments, including the cell type, the labeling strategy, the constructs used (e.g., full-length AKT, PH domain alone, kinase domain alone, or mutants), the number of cells or molecules analyzed, or the statistical methods used to compare residence times and recruitment efficiencies. Without these details, the claim that the kinase domain stabilizes longer-residence states is not quantitatively supported. Why it matters Single-molecule imaging data are only meaningful if the experimental design includes appropriate controls and sufficient sampling. The claim of cooperative roles requires direct comparison of constructs with and without each domain, and the residence time distributions must be statistically robust. Resolution test Provide full experimental details, including construct design, labeling strategy, imaging conditions, number of molecules tracked, and statistical comparisons of residence times and recruitment efficiencies across constructs. Show that the differences are significant and that the kinase domain effect is not due to artifacts such as oligomerization or non-specific binding. It is unclear whether solvent exposure of the phosphorylation site is sufficient for phosphorylation by upstream kinases such as PDK1, or whether additional conformational changes are required. Without a mechanistic link between the observed orientation and phosphorylation or kinase activity, the significance of this finding is speculative. 01 基本信息 标题 ：beta-lactoglobulin from precision fermentation and milk exhibit similar protein structure but distinct aggregation behaviour: a multi-length-scale perspective 作者 ：Kornet, Remco; Subbarayadu, Kiran; Westberry, Benjamin P; Mladic, Marija; Pan, Zheng; Apostolidi, Isidora; Groot, Melanie; Schouten, Olaf; Stam, Pieter; Abello, Nicolas; Anema, Skelte G; Houben, Klaartje; Hill, Jeremy P; Wubbolts, Marcel G 单位 ：未提供（PubMed 记录未列出作者单位） 期刊/平台 ：Food Research International (Ottawa, Ont.) 年份 ：2026（在线日期 2026-10-23） 论文类型 ：研究论文（比较研究，多尺度表征） 领域 ：食品科学 / 蛋白质生物化学 / 精密发酵蛋白表征 关键词 ：beta-lactoglobulin; precision fermentation; protein structure; aggregation; thermal stability; UHT; molecular dynamics DOI/arXiv 号 ：10.1016/j.foodres.2026.120846 代码 ：未提供 数据 ：未提供（原始数据未公开） 阅读日期 ：2026-05-13（按当前日期） 在课题方向中的位置 ：本文属于「蛋白质结构相关计算研究 × 物理模拟（MD）」在食品蛋白场景的应用。核心对象 BLG 是脂质运载蛋白家族成员，其结构预测、构象变化与聚集行为是蛋白质计算研究的经典模型系统。本文的 MD 模拟用于解释 N 端修饰对聚集行为的影响，属于「序列修饰 → 结构/表面性质 → 聚集行为」的可迁移研究范式，对蛋白质设计（尤其是表面电荷工程）有直接参考价值。 02 一句话总结 本文通过多尺度表征（LC-MS、NMR、SEC-MALS、UPLC、流变、MD 模拟）证明：精密发酵来源的 BLG（f-BLG）因 N 端 "EAEA" 延伸导致表面负电荷增加，在 UHT 条件（140°C）下几乎不聚集，而牛奶来源 BLG（m-BLG）在 30 秒内 80–90% 聚集，尽管两者三级/四级结构等价。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：精密发酵来源的 β-乳球蛋白（f-BLG）与牛奶来源的 BLG（m-BLG）在初级到四级结构上是否一致？若结构一致，为何在 UHT 条件下的聚集行为存在显著差异？ 为什么重要 ：精密发酵乳蛋白作为食品成分需满足与天然蛋白一致的功能特性（如热稳定性、聚集行为），否则影响加工适用性。BLG 是乳清蛋白主要成分，其热聚集行为直接决定 UHT 乳制品的质地与稳定性。 现有方法为何不足 ：以往研究多关注序列一致性（"nature-equivalent" 主张），但缺乏对翻译后修饰、N 端加工、表面电荷分布等细微差异的系统表征，更未将结构差异与宏观聚集行为定量关联。 精确研究问题 ：Can a subtle N-terminal modification (EAEA extension) in precision fermentation-derived BLG explain the observed reduction in thermal aggregation under UHT-like conditions, despite equivalent tertiary and quaternary structure? evidence as presented in the abstract; no figures, tables, or methods sections were available for inspection Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report that beta-lactoglobulin produced by precision fermentation (f-BLG) and milk-derived BLG (m-BLG) share equivalent tertiary and quaternary structures, but differ in thermal aggregation behaviour under UHT-like conditions. The f-BLG variant carries an N-terminal "EAEA" extension, which is associated with increased negative surface charge, enhanced electrostatic repulsion, and markedly reduced aggregation at 140 degrees C. Molecular dynamics simulations are used to propose a mechanism involving outward-facing negatively charged N-termini that limit aggregate growth. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no figures, tables, supplementary materials, or methods details were provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full methods, all figures and tables, statistical analyses, simulation parameters, raw data, and any supplementary information Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially interesting comparative study of a precision-fermentation-derived dairy protein against its milk-derived counterpart, with a clear mechanistic hypothesis linking an N-terminal sequence extension to altered aggregation behaviour. The structural equivalence claim is supported by multiple orthogonal techniques, which is commendable. However, the central functional claim, that f-BLG shows no detectable aggregation under conditions where m-BLG aggregates rapidly, is presented without quantitative uncertainty or statistical context. The mechanistic attribution to electrostatic repulsion is plausible but not directly demonstrated in the abstract. The molecular dynamics component is mentioned but not described in sufficient detail to assess its validity. Overall, the work addresses a topic of practical relevance to food science and biotechnology, but the evidence as presented in the abstract alone is insufficient to fully establish the mechanistic case. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers and industry professionals in food science, dairy protein chemistry, and precision fermentation biotechnology would be interested. The findings have direct implications for the formulation of heat-stable protein ingredients from fermentation-derived sources, which is relevant to the development of animal-free dairy alternatives. The structural comparison approach may also interest protein biophysicists studying post-translational or sequence-extension effects on protein behaviour. Major strengths The use of multiple orthogonal structural techniques (LC-MS, LC-MS/MS, 2D methyl NMR, SEC-UV-MALS) to establish primary, tertiary, and quaternary structure equivalence is a rigorous approach. The comparison of thermal aggregation behaviour under UHT-like conditions is practically relevant. The proposed mechanism, linking the N-terminal extension to surface charge and electrostatic repulsion, is mechanistically coherent and testable. The inclusion of molecular dynamics simulations adds a molecular-level perspective that strengthens the hypothesis. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The abstract states that "no detectable aggregation occurred for f-BLG" at 140 degrees C over 1800 s, while 80-90% of m-BLG aggregated within 30 s. Evidence pointer Abstract text; location not provided Concern The claim of "no detectable aggregation" is presented as an absolute statement without any indication of the detection limit of the UPLC-UV method used. The abstract does not report the sensitivity threshold, the number of replicates, or the statistical significance of the difference between f-BLG and m-BLG. Without this information, it is impossible to determine whether f-BLG truly does not aggregate or whether aggregation occurs below the detection limit. Why it matters The central conclusion of the paper, that f-BLG is markedly more stable under UHT-like conditions, rests entirely on this comparative aggregation measurement. If the detection limit is not sufficiently low, the claim of "no aggregation" could be misleading and would not support the strong conclusion of enhanced stability. Resolution test The authors should report the detection limit of the UPLC-UV method for aggregated BLG, provide replicate measurements with standard deviations or confidence intervals, and state the statistical test used to compare f-BLG and m-BLG aggregation levels. If possible, a complementary method such as dynamic light scattering or turbidity measurements should be used to confirm the absence of aggregation. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Mechanistic support Claim pointer The abstract attributes f-BLG's increased thermal stability to "the additional glutamic acid residues in its N-terminal extension, which results in a more negative surface charge and increased electrostatic repulsion." Evidence pointer Abstract text; location not provided Concern The abstract does not report any direct measurement of surface charge, such as zeta potential, for f-BLG and m-BLG. The claim of "more negative surface charge" is inferred from the amino acid sequence, but no experimental evidence is presented to confirm that this sequence difference translates into a measurable difference in surface charge under the relevant conditions (pH, ionic strength, temperature). Why it matters The proposed mechanism is the core explanatory framework of the paper. If the surface charge difference is not experimentally verified, the mechanism remains speculative. Furthermore, the abstract does not address whether other factors, such as differences in glycosylation, disulfide bonding, or folding kinetics, could contribute to the observed behavioural differences. Resolution test The authors should provide zeta potential measurements or another direct surface charge characterisation for both proteins under the conditions used in the aggregation experiments. Alternatively, they could perform charge-modification experiments or use variants with neutral or positively charged N-terminal extensions to test the electrostatic repulsion hypothesis directly. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Simulation validity Claim pointer The abstract states that "molecular dynamics simulations further indicate that these negatively charged N-termini remain outward facing upon protein association, potentially maintaining electrostatic repulsion at the aggregate surface." Evidence pointer Abstract text; location not provided Concern The abstract provides no details on the simulation methodology, including the force field, simulation length, system size, number of replicates, or how the aggregation process was modelled. Without this information, the reliability and relevance of the simulation results cannot be assessed. The word "potentially" also indicates that the simulation evidence is suggestive rather than conclusive. Why it matters The simulation is used to support the proposed mechanism, but if the simulation conditions do not adequately represent the experimental system, the conclusions drawn from it may not be valid. The lack of methodological detail prevents the reader from evaluating whether the simulation is a meaningful test of the hypothesis. Resolution test The authors should provide a detailed description of the simulation setup in the methods section, including force field parameters, simulation time, system composition, and any validation against experimental data. If possible, they should also show that the simulation results are robust to changes in initial conditions or simulation parameters. The attribution of increased thermal stability to increased negative surface charge is unsupported without direct surface charge measurements. The molecular dynamics simulation results are unassessable without methodological details. 01 基本信息 标题 : Thermally induced conformational transition and binding affinity of beta-lactoglobulin and capsaicin: A multi-spectroscopic and molecular dynamics simulation study. 作者与单位 : Zhang, Dong; Cao, Jiaming; Duan, Min; Su, Chang; Yang, Li; Zhu, Yahui; Emara, A M; Gu, Xuedong; Tang, Jie; Yang, Lin（单位未提供） 期刊/预印本平台 : Food Research International (Ottawa, Ont.) 年份 : 2026（在线日期 2026-10-23） 论文类型 : 实验 + 计算模拟混合研究 领域 : 食品科学 / 蛋白质-配体相互作用 / 分子动力学模拟 关键词 : beta-lactoglobulin; capsaicin; heat treatment; conformational transition; binding affinity; molecular dynamics; MM-PBSA; free energy landscape DOI/arXiv 号 : 10.1016/j.foodres.2026.120727 代码 : 未提供 数据 : 未提供 阅读日期 : 2026-05-13（按当前日期） 在课题方向中的位置 : 该文属于「蛋白质结构相关计算研究 × 物理模拟（MD）」方向，聚焦热诱导构象转变对蛋白质-配体结合亲和力的调控机制，将多光谱实验与 MD 模拟（含 MM-PBSA 和自由能景观分析）结合，为食品加工中蛋白质-小分子相互作用的温度依赖性提供了计算-实验联合研究范式。 02 一句话总结 该研究通过多光谱实验与 MD 模拟，揭示 β-乳球蛋白（β-LG）在 25–95°C 热处理下经历熔球态转变、聚集和聚集体重排等多阶段构象转变，导致其与辣椒素（CAP）的结合亲和力呈非单调变化（25–65°C 上升、75°C 骤降、85–95°C 部分恢复），并确定 65°C 为 CAP 保留的最优加工温度。 03 研究问题 具体问题 : 热处理温度（25–95°C）如何通过改变 β-LG 的构象状态来调控其与 CAP 的结合亲和力？ 为什么重要 : 食品加工中热处理不可避免，理解温度对蛋白质-生物活性小分子结合的影响，对保留功能成分、优化加工条件、实现质量控制至关重要。 现有方法为何不足 : 以往研究多关注单一温度或单一技术，缺乏对温度连续变化下蛋白质构象转变与结合亲和力关系的系统刻画；纯实验方法难以解析原子层面的构象-结合机制。 精确研究问题 : Can temperature-driven conformational transitions of β-LG quantitatively explain the non-monotonic binding affinity profile toward CAP, and can simple physicochemical indicators serve as proxies for binding affinity? no access to full text, figures, tables, or supplementary materials Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report a rational design strategy for Bacillus subtilis lipase A (BSLA) that combines maintenance of flexibility in catalytically key regions with rigidification of the global scaffold. The optimal variant, M4, is claimed to show substantially improved thermostability (half-life 94.52 times wild type at 52 °C), enhanced organic-solvent tolerance, and 4.35 times higher catalytic activity. In application, M4 achieved 91.83% yield of vitamin E succinate (VES) under optimized conditions. Structural analyses and molecular dynamics simulations are claimed to support a redistribution of conformational dynamics as the mechanistic basis for simultaneous activity and stability enhancement. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no experimental methods, sequence data, structural coordinates, simulation parameters, or statistical analyses provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full methods, all figures and tables, supplementary data, statistical details, sequence information for variants, simulation protocols, and experimental replicates Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents an appealing and potentially impactful strategy for overcoming the activity-stability trade-off in enzyme engineering. The reported performance gains for M4 are substantial and the application to VES synthesis is practically relevant. However, the abstract alone provides insufficient detail to verify the robustness of the claims. Key issues include the absence of statistical context, unclear definitions of the "key-region flexibility maintenance" and "global scaffold rigidification" strategies, and a lack of comparative data against alternative approaches. The mechanistic interpretation rests on structural and simulation evidence that cannot be assessed from the abstract. The work is potentially significant for the food science and biocatalysis communities, but the current evidence base is too limited to establish the case. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in enzyme engineering, protein design, and industrial biocatalysis would be interested in the dual-strategy approach for decoupling activity and stability. The food science community, particularly those working on lipase-catalyzed synthesis of lipophilic bioactive compounds such as vitamin E derivatives, would find the VES synthesis application relevant. Computational biologists interested in molecular dynamics-guided protein engineering may also find the structural rationale of interest. Major strengths The reported performance improvements are large and potentially transformative if reproducible. The combination of two design principles (flexibility maintenance and rigidification) is conceptually elegant and addresses a well-known limitation in biocatalysis. The inclusion of an application-oriented evaluation (VES synthesis) strengthens the practical relevance. The proposed mechanistic explanation via conformational dynamics redistribution is plausible and testable. 一句话总结 本文通过 300 W 超声预处理改变大黄鱼骨蛋白构象，提高中性蛋白酶可及性与水解度，产生富含低分子量肽的酶解物，其成骨活性增强；结合 LC-MS/MS、分子对接与 100-ns MD 模拟，提出 GPPGPMGPPG、GPSGPVGP、APDPGPGP 三个富含脯氨酸的候选成骨肽，并预测其与 EGFR 的稳定结合。 03 研究问题 具体问题 : 超声预处理如何通过改变鱼骨蛋白构象来影响酶解行为，进而影响所得酶解物的成骨活性？哪些具体肽段负责该活性，其与潜在受体（EGFR）的相互作用机制如何？ 为什么重要 : 鱼类加工副产物（鱼骨）富含蛋白质，但利用率低。若能通过物理预处理（超声）调控蛋白构象、提高生物活性肽释放效率，则可将海洋副产物转化为功能性食品成分，用于骨骼健康管理。 现有方法为何不足 : 传统酶解鱼骨蛋白的成骨活性有限，肽段释放效率低；缺乏对「构象变化 → 酶可及性 → 活性肽释放」这一因果链的系统研究；活性肽的分子机制（受体结合）往往缺乏计算验证。 精确研究问题 : Can ultrasound pretreatment (300 W) induce conformational changes in large yellow croaker bone protein that enhance enzymatic hydrolysis efficiency and yield hydrolysates with higher osteogenic activity, and can the responsible peptides be identified and validated via molecular docking and MD simulation? 04 no access to full text, figures, tables, or supplementary materials Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report engineering a tannase from Paraburkholderia pallida (Tanpp) via active-site mutagenesis and computational hotspot prediction. The double mutant F384T/N307A is claimed to show a 2.7-fold increase in catalytic efficiency and an 11-fold longer half-life at 50 degrees C compared to wild-type. Structural modeling and molecular dynamics simulations are used to propose mechanistic explanations. Green tea clarification assays reportedly show improved turbidity reduction and catechin conversion. The authors conclude that coordinated active-site remodeling improves both catalytic performance and thermal stability, supporting the mutant's application potential. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no experimental details, numerical data tables, structural figures, or statistical analyses are visible Missing materials affecting confidence Full methods, enzyme kinetic data, thermal inactivation curves, structural models, MD simulation parameters and trajectories, green tea assay protocols, statistical analyses, and all figures and tables Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially useful enzyme engineering study with a clear application focus. The reported improvements in catalytic efficiency and thermal stability are quantitatively stated, and the proposed structural rationale is plausible. However, the abstract alone does not provide sufficient detail to verify the robustness of the kinetic measurements, the statistical significance of the improvements, the quality of the structural models, or the reproducibility of the tea clarification results. The mechanistic interpretation, while reasonable, is presented without supporting data. The application claims are promising but require experimental validation beyond what is visible here. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in enzyme engineering, protein stability engineering, and food biotechnology would find these results relevant. The work addresses a practical bottleneck in tea beverage processing, so industrial researchers working on beverage clarification and tannase applications would also be interested. The combination of computational prediction and experimental validation may appeal to those studying structure-function relationships in hydrolases. Major strengths The study addresses a real industrial problem with clear application relevance. The reported improvements are quantified with fold-changes, which is useful for comparative assessment. The combination of experimental mutagenesis with computational modeling and MD simulations provides a multi-pronged approach. The green tea clarification assays connect the engineering work to a practical end-use, strengthening the translational value. methods, figures, tables, or supplementary material were available for evaluation Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report that conventional peptide-level hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) workflows can identify productive T-cell receptor (TCR) engagement with cognate peptide-HLA (pHLA) complexes. They claim that TCRs binding centrally within the pHLA groove produce distinct deuterium uptake profiles compared with TCRs adopting alternative orientations, and that comparison with structure prediction data contextualizes these profiles for distinct binding modes. They conclude that existing HDX-MS workflows are rapid and accessible approaches for probing TCR-pHLA interactions, with implications for TCR-based biotherapeutics. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no experimental data, figures, tables, or methodological details were provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, methods section, all figures and tables, statistical analyses, structural prediction details, and any validation experiments Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially interesting application of an established biophysical technique to a question of immunological relevance. However, the claims as stated are broad and the evidence base is entirely inaccessible from the supplied material. The central assertion that peptide-level HDX-MS can distinguish TCR binding orientations is plausible but requires substantial experimental validation that cannot be assessed here. The abstract does not provide sufficient methodological detail to evaluate the robustness of the approach, and the comparison with structure prediction is described only superficially. The work may be of interest to the structural immunology and biotherapeutics communities, but the case is not established from the provided evidence. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in structural immunology, particularly those studying TCR-pHLA interactions and T-cell activation mechanisms. Developers of TCR-based therapeutics would also be interested, as the approach could offer a faster alternative to crystallography for screening TCR engagement. The HDX-MS community may find value in the extension of peptide-level workflows to a new class of protein-protein interactions. Major strengths The application of an accessible and established technique to a problem traditionally requiring crystallography is conceptually appealing. The integration of experimental HDX data with computational structure prediction is a sensible strategy that could enhance interpretability. The potential practical implications for biotherapeutic development are clear and relevant. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The authors claim that conventional peptide-level HDX-MS workflows can identify productive TCR engagement with cognate pHLAs and that TCRs binding centrally within the pHLA groove have distinct uptake profiles compared with those adopting alternative orientations. Evidence pointer Abstract only; no figures or tables provided Concern The abstract provides no quantitative data, no representative uptake profiles, no statistical comparisons, and no details on the number of TCR-pHLA pairs examined. The claim that distinct uptake profiles correlate with binding orientation is presented without any visible supporting evidence. Why it matters The central conclusion rests entirely on this correlation. Without access to the actual HDX data, including replicate measurements, deuterium uptake curves, and statistical significance testing, the claim cannot be evaluated. Peptide-level HDX-MS is known to have limited spatial resolution, and the ability to distinguish subtle orientational differences at this resolution is not self-evident. Resolution test Provide the full dataset including uptake plots for all TCR-pHLA complexes studied, statistical analyses demonstrating significant differences between central and alternative binding modes, and a clear description of how binding orientation was assigned independently of the HDX data. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Methodological clarity Claim pointer The authors state that comparison of uptake data with information from structure prediction further contextualized the HDX data for distinct TCR-pHLA binding modes. Evidence pointer Abstract only; methods not provided Concern The abstract does not specify which structure prediction method was used, how predictions were validated, or how the comparison with HDX data was performed. It is unclear whether the structure predictions were used to interpret the HDX data or to validate them, and whether the predictions were generated for the same TCR-pHLA complexes studied experimentally. Why it matters The integration of computational and experimental approaches is presented as a key feature of the work. Without details on the prediction method, its accuracy, and the nature of the comparison, the value of this integration cannot be assessed. If the structure predictions were used to assign binding modes that were then correlated with HDX profiles, circularity becomes a concern. Resolution test Describe the structure prediction method, its validation, and the specific procedure for comparing predicted structures with HDX uptake data. Clarify whether predictions were made blind to the experimental results. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Generalizability Claim pointer The authors conclude that existing HDX-MS workflows are rapid and accessible approaches for probing TCR-pHLA interactions. Evidence pointer Abstract only; no systematic variation described Concern The abstract does not indicate how many TCR-pHLA complexes were studied, whether different HLA alleles or peptide lengths were included, or whether the approach was tested on TCRs with known non-central binding modes beyond the examples implied. The generalizability of the approach across the diverse TCR-pHLA interaction space is therefore unsubstantiated. Why it matters The conclusion is framed as a general statement about the utility of HDX-MS for TCR-pHLA interactions. If only a small number of complexes were examined, or if the tested set was biased toward particular binding modes, the conclusion would be overreaching. Resolution test Provide the full panel of TCR-pHLA complexes studied, including details on HLA alleles, peptide sequences, and TCR affinities. Demonstrate that the approach works across a representative range of binding orientations and affinities. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Terminology precision Affected element Use of the term "productive TCR engagement" Evidence pointer Abstract, first sentence of results description Issue The term "productive" is not defined. It could imply functional activation, binding affinity, or simply a detectable interaction. This ambiguity affects interpretation of the claims. Required correction Define "productive TCR engagement" explicitly, for example in terms of binding affinity thresholds or functional assays, and use the definition consistently throughout the manuscript. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Clarity of comparison Affected element Statement that centrally binding TCRs have "distinct uptake profiles compared with those adopting alternative orientations" Evidence pointer Abstract, results description Issue The abstract does not specify the direction or magnitude of the differences, nor whether the differences were consistent across all complexes tested. A reader cannot gauge the robustness of the observed effect. Required correction Include a brief quantitative summary of the observed differences, such as effect sizes or representative uptake differences, in the abstract or clearly reference a figure that displays these data. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Reproducibility Affected element Experimental replicates and statistical treatment Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Issue No mention is made of experimental replicates, technical variability, or statistical methods used to compare uptake profiles. This is essential for a technique like HDX-MS where variability can be substantial. Required correction State the number of replicates and the statistical tests used in the abstract or clearly reference the methods section where these are described. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that peptide-level HDX-MS can distinguish TCR binding orientations is unsupported from the abstract alone; no data are visible. The claim that structure prediction contextualized the HDX data is unverifiable without details on the prediction method and comparison procedure. The general conclusion that existing HDX-MS workflows are rapid and accessible approaches for probing TCR-pHLA interactions is not established from the provided evidence, as the scope of validation is unknown. The term "productive TCR engagement" is used without definition, making the central claim ambiguous.

They report median predicted fold change of 1.52 in Kcat across seven out-of-distribution enzymes spanning EC classes 1-7, with all variants retaining pLDDT above 70, and claim superior balance between predicted activity and structural confidence relative to RFdiffusion3-LigandMPNN and ZymCtrl. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no quantitative distributions, baselines, ablations, or methodological details are visible Missing materials affecting confidence Full methods, all figures and tables, baseline implementation details, dataset construction and split criteria, hyperparameters, uncertainty quantification, and any experimental validation Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a conceptually appealing idea, namely making kinetic objectives differentiable for enzyme sequence design, which is a timely and potentially impactful direction. However, the evidence provided is insufficient to establish the core claims. The reported performance metrics are limited to a single median value and a structural threshold, with no indication of variance, statistical testing, or comparison of distributions. The absence of methodological detail prevents assessment of the differentiable relaxation scheme, the cross-modal predictor architecture, and the validity of the out-of-distribution evaluation. The work is promising in principle but not established from the supplied material. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational protein engineers and enzyme designers would be interested because the approach addresses a recognized gap between sequence generation and kinetic evaluation. Machine learning researchers working on differentiable design and protein language models would also find the cross-modal optimization framework relevant. Biocatalysis practitioners seeking function-oriented design tools may be interested if the predicted improvements translate to experimental validation, though that is not demonstrated here. Major strengths The conceptual framing is clear and addresses a real limitation in current enzyme design pipelines. The idea of making substrate-conditioned kinetic objectives differentiable is a logical extension of structure- and binding-centered differentiable design. The choice of seven enzymes spanning EC classes 1-7 suggests an intention to demonstrate generalizability, which is appropriate for the claim of a general route to function-oriented engineering. no access to full text, figures, tables, or supplementary materials Shared manuscript claim summary The authors use molecular dynamics (MD) and mixed quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) free energy simulations to compare conformational flexibility and hydrogen-bonding interactions between preturnover and midturnover states of E. coli ribonucleotide reductase (RNR). They report that Y731 samples multiple conformations in both states, interfacial water channels are present, E623 can adopt conformations distal to Y730 in the preturnover state, and forward radical transfer from Y731 to Y730 is thermodynamically favorable with a reasonable barrier even without E623 mediation. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no simulation details, force field parameters, convergence criteria, free energy profiles, or structural validation data provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full methods, simulation protocols, force field choices, system setup, equilibration and production lengths, convergence assessments, free energy calculation details, error estimates, and comparison with experimental structures Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a plausible computational study addressing conformational dynamics relevant to PCET in RNR. The claims are internally consistent and align with prior work in the field, but the evidence base is insufficient to evaluate technical rigor or quantitative support. The central conclusion that conformational flexibility regulates PCET is reasonable but not established from the abstract alone. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in enzymology, particularly those studying radical transfer mechanisms, PCET theory, and conformational dynamics in multi-subunit enzymes. The work may also interest computational chemists developing QM/MM methods for biological systems and structural biologists using cryo-EM to capture functional states. Major strengths The study addresses a mechanistically important question using two experimentally defined states. The focus on conformational sampling and water channels is timely. The inclusion of QM/MM free energy calculations adds quantitative dimension beyond qualitative MD analysis. Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The abstract provides no quantitative values for the free energy barrier or reaction free energy, nor any indication of statistical uncertainty, convergence, or comparison with experimental rates. Without numbers, error bars, or convergence criteria, the claim is not verifiable and may mislead readers about the strength of the conclusion. Without these details, the claim of "multiple conformations" is not quantitatively supported. Why it matters Conformational sampling claims require evidence of adequate sampling and statistical convergence. Insufficient sampling could lead to overinterpretation of transient states as stable conformations. The claim that Y731 "samples multiple conformations" is unsupported without sampling statistics or convergence metrics. The statement that E623 "can also sample conformations distal to Y730" is unsupported without quantitative conformational analysis. Claims and evidence as presented in the abstract; no methods, figures, tables, or supplementary material were provided Shared manuscript claim summary The authors present MP4, a transformer-based model that translates natural language prompts into de novo protein sequences. They claim state-of-the-art performance on a benchmark of 96 prompts across three metrics, experimental validation of two designs showing expression, thermostability, high-resolution crystal structures including a novel fold, and in vitro ATP binding and hydrolysis. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no numerical data, statistical analyses, structural coordinates, or experimental protocols are available Missing materials affecting confidence Full methods, model architecture details, training data description, benchmark construction and evaluation protocol, experimental procedures, crystallographic statistics, functional assay data, and all figures and tables Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract describes an ambitious and potentially impactful approach to protein design via natural language. However, the evidence provided is insufficient to evaluate the core claims. Key performance metrics are presented without numerical values, the benchmark is not described in sufficient detail, and the experimental validation is summarized without supporting data. The claim of a "paradigm-shifting novel fold" is particularly strong and cannot be assessed without structural evidence and comparison to known folds. The work is interesting and timely, but the current abstract does not establish the case. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in protein design, computational biology, and machine learning would be interested in the model architecture and benchmark results. Structural biologists would be interested in the novel fold claim. Synthetic biologists and molecular engineers would be interested in the potential for natural-language-driven design. The broader AI community may also find the text-to-sequence mapping approach of interest. Major strengths The concept of translating natural language directly to functional proteins is novel and addresses a real limitation in current protein design approaches. The combination of computational prediction with experimental validation, including crystallography and functional assays, is commendable. The reported resolution of the crystal structures (1.30 A and 1.77 A) suggests careful experimental work. Major Concerns R1-M1: The benchmark performance claims are not supported by any numerical data. R1-M2: The "paradigm-shifting novel fold" claim is not substantiated. R1-M3: The functional claims (ATP binding and hydrolysis) are not supported by quantitative data. R1-M4: The training dataset description is insufficient to evaluate model validity. Minor Comments R1-m1: The abstract does not specify how the 96 prompts were selected or whether they are representative. R1-m2: The relationship between the two experimentally validated designs and the benchmark prompts is unclear. R1-m3: The statement "incomplete coverage and controllability" is vague and not quantified. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1, R1-M2, R1-M3, R1-M4 Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: High. The concept of natural-language-to-protein translation appears novel and distinct from existing sequence- or structure-based design methods. Scientific importance: Potentially high, but not established from the abstract alone. The impact depends on the robustness of the benchmark and the validity of the novel fold claim. Interdisciplinary readership: The work would appeal to multiple communities, but the abstract lacks sufficient detail for nonspecialists to evaluate the significance. Technical soundness: Cannot be assessed. No methods, statistics, or experimental details are provided. Readability for nonspecialists: The abstract is generally clear, but terms like "sequence realism" and "predicted fold quality" are not defined. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The concept is promising and the work may be significant, but the abstract alone does not provide sufficient support for the core claims. A full manuscript with detailed methods, data, and analyses would be required for a supportive assessment. Input scope Abstract only Assessment boundary Claims and conclusions as presented in the abstract; no access to full text, figures, tables, or supplementary materials Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report that inositol hexakisphosphate (IP6) promotes an open pore state in the HIV-1 capsid protein lattice by reconfiguring subunit contacts. They base this on high-speed atomic force microscopy (HS-AFM) observations of individual hexamer pores, constant-pH molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and mechanical fatigue assays. They conclude that IP6 acts as a proviral regulator coupling pore dynamics, intersubunit contact rewiring, and mechanical resilience. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no figures, tables, methods, or numerical data provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, experimental methods, simulation parameters, statistical analyses, and any supplementary information Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially interesting and mechanistically ambitious study that combines single-molecule imaging, simulation, and mechanical testing to address a relevant question in HIV-1 biology. However, the current evidence base is insufficient to evaluate the validity of the central claims. The abstract reports qualitative findings without quantitative data, statistical support, or methodological detail. The link between the observed pore states, the simulated contact rewiring, and the mechanical fatigue results is asserted rather than demonstrated. The claim that IP6 is a "proviral regulator" coupling multiple phenomena is a strong interpretive leap that requires substantially more evidence than is presented here. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers studying HIV-1 capsid biology, viral uncoating and reverse transcription, capsid-targeting antiviral development, and biophysical studies of protein lattice dynamics. The mechanical properties of the capsid and the role of IP6 may also interest the broader community studying virus mechanics and nanomaterials. Major strengths The study addresses a specific and important mechanistic question about how IP6 modulates pore conformation. The combination of experimental single-molecule imaging, computational simulation, and mechanical testing is a potentially powerful approach. The focus on individual hexamer dynamics rather than averaged structures is a notable methodological advance. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The authors claim that HS-AFM visualized asynchronous motions of individual hexamer pores and identified dynamic transitions between two major states, and that quantitative analysis enabled estimation of IP6-induced pore conformations and populations. Evidence pointer Abstract only; no figures or tables provided Concern The abstract provides no quantitative data, no statistical measures, no sample sizes, and no description of how the two states were defined or distinguished. The claim that "quantitative analysis enabled estimation" is unsupported by any presented numbers or error estimates. Why it matters Without quantitative evidence, the reader cannot assess whether the two-state model is robust, whether the populations are significantly different between conditions, or whether the observations are reproducible. This is the foundational experimental claim on which the entire mechanistic interpretation rests. Resolution test Provide the actual population estimates, transition frequencies, dwell times, and statistical comparisons between IP6-present and IP6-absent conditions, with appropriate error bars and significance tests. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Mechanistic support Claim pointer The authors claim that constant-pH MD simulations reveal that IP6 induces contact rewiring at the pore entrance, stabilizing the open state through coordinated rearrangement of intersubunit interactions. Evidence pointer Abstract only; no simulation details provided Concern The abstract does not describe the simulation system, force field, simulation length, number of replicas, or how "contact rewiring" was defined and quantified. The claim that simulations "reveal" a mechanism is not supported by any specific data on which contacts change, how they change, or how this relates to the experimentally observed states. Why it matters The simulation is presented as a key piece of mechanistic evidence. Without details on the simulation setup and analysis, the claim that IP6 stabilizes the open state via contact rewiring is not verifiable. The connection between the simulated contact changes and the experimentally observed pore states is also not established. Resolution test Provide simulation parameters, convergence criteria, a clear definition of contact rewiring, and a direct comparison between simulated contact changes and experimentally inferred pore conformations. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Interpretive validity Claim pointer The authors claim that mechanical fatigue assays show IP6 markedly enhances the resistance of the capsid lattice to mechanical fatigue, and that this reveals its role as a mechanically stabilized nanomaterial. Evidence pointer Abstract only; no data provided Concern The abstract reports a qualitative result ("markedly enhances") without any quantitative measure of fatigue resistance, such as number of cycles to failure, force thresholds, or comparison to controls. The relevance of mechanical fatigue resistance to the pore state model is also not explained. Why it matters The mechanical fatigue result is used to support the broader claim that IP6 couples pore dynamics to mechanical resilience. Without quantitative data and a clear mechanistic link, this claim is not established. The connection between pore opening and lattice-level mechanical properties is not obvious and requires explicit demonstration. Resolution test Provide quantitative fatigue data with statistical comparisons, and show how the mechanical changes relate to the pore state populations or contact rewiring. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Claim scope Claim pointer The authors conclude that IP6 is a "proviral regulator" that couples nanoscale pore dynamics, intersubunit contact reconfiguration, and mechanical resilience, providing a "unified mechanistic framework" for its role in viral replication. Evidence pointer Abstract only Concern This conclusion extends beyond the presented data. The abstract does not provide any direct evidence linking the observed pore states, contact rewiring, or mechanical properties to viral replication outcomes. The term "proviral regulator" implies a functional consequence that is not demonstrated. Why it matters The conclusion overreaches the evidence. While the individual observations may be consistent with a role in replication, the abstract does not show that the open pore state, the contact rewiring, or the mechanical stabilization actually affect reverse transcription or viral infectivity. Resolution test Provide functional data linking the observed biophysical changes to viral replication, such as reverse transcription assays or infectivity measurements under conditions where the pore state is modulated. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Terminology Evidence pointer Abstract Issue The term "asynchronous motions" is used without definition. It is unclear whether this refers to temporal asynchrony between different hexamers, or to stochastic switching within individual hexamers. Required correction Define the term explicitly and describe how asynchrony was assessed in the analysis. Required correction Provide the relevant concentrations and conditions in the methods or results. Required correction State explicitly what control conditions were used and how they were compared. The abstract does not provide sufficient quantitative or methodological detail to evaluate any of the three main experimental or computational pillars, nor the integrative conclusion. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The approach of combining single-hexamer HS-AFM with MD simulations and mechanical testing is potentially original, but the abstract does not provide enough detail to assess the novelty of the findings relative to prior structural studies. Scientific importance: The question of how IP6 modulates the HIV-1 capsid pore is of clear importance for understanding viral replication and for antiviral development. However, the importance of the specific mechanistic claims cannot be assessed without supporting data. Interdisciplinary readership: The topic bridges virology, biophysics, and computational biology, and the findings could interest a broad readership. The abstract is written in a way that is accessible to nonspecialists, though some terms require definition. Technical soundness: Not assessable from the abstract. No methods, controls, or statistical analyses are presented. Readability for nonspecialists: The abstract is generally clear and well-structured, but the lack of quantitative detail limits its usefulness to a general audience. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The abstract presents an interesting hypothesis and a plausible experimental strategy, but the claims are not supported by the information provided. A full evaluation requires access to the complete manuscript with figures, methods, and data. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that HS-AFM identified two major pore states and estimated their populations is unsupported without quantitative data. The claim that MD simulations reveal contact rewiring stabilizing the open state is unsupported without simulation details and analysis. The claim that IP6 markedly enhances mechanical fatigue resistance is unsupported without quantitative fatigue data. The conclusion that IP6 is a "proviral regulator" coupling pore dynamics, contact rewiring, and mechanical resilience is an interpretive leap not supported by the abstract. The "unified mechanistic framework" for IP6's role in viral replication is not established from the presented evidence.

The reported result, a 2.5-fold activity increase for the Arg318Lys mutant, is potentially valuable for enzyme engineering. However, the evidence base is limited to the abstract, and several critical details are absent, including quantitative kinetic parameters, thermal stability data, structural validation, and statistical treatment. The claim of "largely preserving" thermal stability is vague and cannot be assessed without numerical data. The mechanistic interpretation, that softening a salt bridge increases flexibility, is plausible but not directly demonstrated. The work may be of interest to enzyme engineers and biochemists, but the case is not fully established from the supplied material. Those working on cold-adapted enzymes and psychrophile biology may also find the results relevant. Industrial biotechnologists seeking enzymes with improved activity at moderate temperatures could benefit from the approach. The focus on a specific structural feature, salt bridges involving arginine and glutamic acid/aspartic acid, provides a targeted and testable design rationale. The reported improvement in low-temperature activity is substantial and potentially useful. The inclusion of thermostability and cytotoxicity assessments indicates attention to practical applicability. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer Binder506 exhibited high affinity against Stx2aB Evidence pointer Abstract, biolayer interferometry mentioned but no data provided Concern The abstract states that Binder506 exhibited high affinity but provides no quantitative binding parameters such as KD values, association or dissociation rates, or comparison to controls or known binders. Why it matters Affinity is a central claim of the work. Without quantitative data, the reader cannot assess whether the affinity is genuinely high, moderate, or comparable to existing binders. This is essential for evaluating the novelty and utility of the designed protein. Resolution test Provide KD values from biolayer interferometry, including replicates, error estimates, and comparison to a relevant positive or negative control. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Mechanistic support Claim pointer Binder506 inhibited Stx2a attachment to and uptake by Vero cells without disrupting holotoxin integrity Evidence pointer Abstract, size-exclusion chromatography, coimmunoprecipitation, cellular binding and internalization assays mentioned but no data shown Concern The mechanistic conclusion is based on assays that are only named, not described with results. It is unclear how inhibition of attachment and uptake was quantified, whether the effect was dose-dependent, and whether the holotoxin integrity assessment was sufficiently sensitive to detect partial disruption. Why it matters The proposed mechanism distinguishes this work from other neutralization strategies. If the evidence is weak or ambiguous, the mechanistic claim is not established, and the potential advantage of this binder over alternatives is unclear. Resolution test Show dose-response data for inhibition of binding and uptake, include appropriate controls such as a non-binding protein or a known neutralizing antibody, and demonstrate the sensitivity and specificity of the holotoxin integrity assay. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Reproducibility and validation Claim pointer AI-assisted de novo design combined with bacterial surface display screening identified Binder506 Evidence pointer Abstract, no details on design pipeline, screening hits, or selection criteria Concern The abstract does not describe the AI design pipeline, the number of candidates generated, the screening hit rate, or the criteria by which Binder506 was selected over other candidates. Without this information, the contribution of the AI component relative to the screening step cannot be assessed. Why it matters The novelty of the work rests partly on the claim that AI-assisted design was effective. If the screening was extensive and the AI contribution marginal, the significance of the approach is diminished. Conversely, if the AI design was highly predictive, this would strengthen the case. Resolution test Describe the design pipeline, report the number of designs tested, the number of hits, and the selection criteria. Ideally, include a comparison of AI-designed binders versus a control set to demonstrate the value of the AI component. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected element Cytotoxicity claim Evidence pointer Abstract, Vero cell cytotoxicity mentioned Issue The claim of minimal intrinsic cytotoxicity is made without any quantitative data or comparison to a control. Required correction Report cell viability values, assay type, concentration range tested, and comparison to untreated or vehicle-treated cells. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Specificity Affected element Neutralization claim Evidence pointer Abstract, Stx2a-neutralizing activity mentioned Issue The abstract does not specify how neutralization was measured, what concentration of Binder506 was effective, or whether the effect was specific to Stx2a versus other Stx subtypes. Required correction Describe the neutralization assay, report effective concentrations, and test or discuss specificity against other Shiga toxin variants. The absence of quantitative affinity data, detailed mechanistic evidence, and design pipeline information means the central claims are not currently verifiable from the provided material. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: the application of AI-assisted de novo design to Shiga toxin binders is a reasonable extension of existing work but not clearly transformative based on the abstract alone. Scientific importance: the topic is relevant to food safety and toxin neutralization, but the significance depends on the affinity and efficacy relative to existing approaches, which cannot be assessed. Interdisciplinary readership: the work bridges computational design, protein biochemistry, and food safety, which could appeal to a broad audience if the evidence is strong. Technical soundness: the methods named are appropriate, but the lack of data prevents evaluation of their execution and interpretation. Readability for nonspecialists: the abstract is clear and accessible, though some terms such as de novo design and biolayer interferometry may require background knowledge. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The abstract describes a plausible and potentially valuable study, but the absence of quantitative data and methodological detail means the claims cannot be evaluated. I would be supportive if the full manuscript provides the missing evidence and addresses the major concerns. The claim that Binder506 inhibited Stx2a attachment to and uptake by Vero cells is unsupported without dose-response and control data. The claim that Binder506 did not disrupt Stx2a holotoxin integrity is unsupported without assay sensitivity details. The claim that the AI-assisted design was effective is not assessable without pipeline details and hit rate information. The claim of minimal intrinsic cytotoxicity is unsupported without quantitative cell viability data. The claim of potent Stx2a-neutralizing activity is unsupported without assay details and effective concentration data.

04 背景与发展脉络 （标注：此脉络为「经外部核验」的领域通用框架，结合本文定位） 1. 定向进化（directed evolution） : 代表方法如易错 PCR、DNA shuffling。优点：无需结构信息；局限：依赖高通量筛选，耗时耗力，且对无颜色/荧光读出的酶不适用。 2. 理性设计（rational design） : 基于晶体结构和催化机制进行定点突变。优点：目标明确；局限：对机制理解要求高，常忽略远端残基的变构效应。 3. 半理性设计（semi-rational design） : 结合序列保守性分析（如 CONSURF）与结构信息，聚焦热点残基进行饱和突变或组合突变。优点：缩小筛选库、提高命中率；局限：热点选择质量依赖结构/序列数据质量。 4. 计算辅助设计（computational enzyme design） : 引入分子对接、MD 模拟、QM/MM 等方法评估突变对底物结合、过渡态稳定和构象动态的影响。优点：可解释机制、减少实验筛选；局限：计算成本高、力场精度有限。 5. 本文位置 : 将上述策略整合为「序列保守性 → 结构筛选 → 分子对接 → MD 模拟 → 组合突变」的多维流程，强调热点间的协同效应（Asn301 与 Met259），而非单点优化。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 野生型 XylB 催化效率低 木糖磷酸化速率不足，限制木糖生物转化通量 底物 D-xylulose 结合亲和力有限，ATP 结合/利用效率不高 摘要：野生型比活性显著低于突变体（>200% 提升） 单点突变效果有限 单一热点突变难以大幅提升活性 催化效率受多个残基协同调控，单点改造忽略协同效应 摘要：组合突变（M259H/N301G 和 M259H/N301H）优于单点 热点残基识别困难 难以从序列/结构中准确预测功能关键残基 功能热点往往涉及底物结合、辅因子结合和构象动态的多重角色 摘要：需整合序列保守性 + 结构筛选 + 对接 + MD 多维策略 突变可能损害稳定性 活性提升常伴随表达量下降或环境适应性变差 突变可能破坏疏水核心或引入不利的构象应力 摘要：突变体「retaining stable expression and environmental adaptability」 06 核心思想 表面方法 : 半理性设计流程——序列保守性分析筛选候选残基 → 基于结构的虚拟筛选 → 分子对接评估底物/ATP 结合 → MD 模拟验证构象动态 → 组合突变构建突变体 → 实验表征活性与稳定性。 核心洞察 : 催化效率的提升不依赖单一「关键」残基，而是多个热点残基的协同效应。Asn301 直接参与底物结合/催化（功能热点），Met259 通过调节活性位点疏水环境间接影响底物定位和 ATP 结合。两者协同突变（M259H + N301G/H）产生超加性效应（>200% 活性提升），而非简单叠加。 可能的普适教训 [Analysis]: 酶工程中，远端残基（如 Met259）通过微调活性位点微环境（疏水性、柔性）可显著影响催化效率，且与直接功能残基（如 Asn301）存在协同。这提示在设计策略中应同时考虑「直接催化残基」和「微环境调节残基」，而非仅聚焦保守的催化三联体或底物结合残基。 07 方法总览 输入 : XylB 氨基酸序列（Lactococcus lactis N8）、XylB 结构（同源建模或晶体结构，具体来源未提供）、D-xylulose 和 ATP 结构 输出 : 高活性 XylB 突变体（XylB^M259H/N301G、XylB^M259H/N301H） 模块 : 1. 序列保守性分析（识别保守/可变残基） 2. 结构筛选（基于同源模型或晶体结构，筛选活性位点附近残基） 3. 分子对接（评估 D-xylulose 和 ATP 与突变体的结合模式） 4. biosynthesis）受限于 O-甲基转移酶（O-methyltransferase）的低催化效率，导致产量无法达到工业化水平。 为什么重要 ：VNA 是制药工业等领域的高价值化合物，其微生物合成路线具有绿色、可持续的优势，但酶催化瓶颈限制了其经济可行性。 现有方法为何不足 ：O-甲基转移酶对底物 3,4-dihydroxybenzyl alcohol 的催化效率低，且底物/中间产物（如 3,4-dihydroxybenzaldehyde）积累对宿主产生生长抑制，同时辅因子 S-腺苷甲硫氨酸（SAM）供给不足，这些瓶颈缺乏系统性解决方案。 精确的「Can ... ?」研究问题 ：Can structure-guided protein engineering of O-methyltransferase, combined with pathway engineering 01 基本信息 标题 ：Predicting the Post-translational Modification Effects on Protein-Ligand Interactions via End-Point Binding Free Energy Calculation: Database Creation and Strategy Optimization 作者与单位 ：Wang, Zihao; Xu, Xiaowei; Wang, Zhe; Xu, Kexin; Yang, Kaimo; Jiang, Zhiliang; Yin, Chen; Wang, Yiheng; Zhao, Yun; Chen, Zhengting; Hou, Tingjun; Sun, Huiyong（单位未提供，推测为杭州师范大学与浙江大学药学院合作团队，Hou Tingjun 与 Sun Huiyong 为通讯作者） 期刊/预印本平台 ：Journal of Medicinal Chemistry 年份 ：2026（在线日期 2026-10-23） 论文类型 ：数据库构建 + 方法评估/策略优化研究 领域 ：蛋白质-配体相互作用、翻译后修饰（PTM）、结合自由能计算、分子动力学（MD）模拟、MM/GBSA 关键词 ：PTM、protein-ligand interaction、binding free energy、MM/GBSA、molecular dynamics、drug design DOI/arXiv 号 ：10.1021/acs.jmedchem.6c00581 代码 ：未提供 数据 ：PLAC（PTM-mediated Ligand Activity Change）数据集，文中描述为已提供（"The PLAC dataset is provided"），但未给出下载链接 阅读日期 ：2026-05-12（按系统日期） 该文在课题方向中的位置 ：本文属于「蛋白质结构相关计算研究 × 物理模拟（MD + 端点自由能）」方向，聚焦 PTM 对蛋白-配体结合亲和力的影响预测。其核心贡献是构建了首个系统性的 PTM-配体活性变化实验数据集（PLAC），并系统评估了 MM/GBSA 协议中 MD 时长与介电常数两个关键参数对预测 PTM 效应的最优组合。该工作为「PTM 感知的药物设计」提供了数据基础与计算策略参考，与 AlphaFold 等结构预测方法互补（PTM 常被结构预测忽略）。 02 一句话总结 本文构建了实验验证的 PTM-配体活性变化数据集（PLAC），发现影响相互作用的 PTM 在空间上更接近配体，并通过系统评估 MM/GBSA 协议发现 100 ns MD + 高介电常数（εin = 4）给出最强相关性（rp = -0.70），而低介电常数（εin = 1）更利于 PTM 效应三分类（增强/减弱/中性）。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：翻译后修饰（PTM）经常改变蛋白质结构和药物结合亲和力，但缺乏系统性的数据集来验证和预测这种效应；同时，端点结合自由能方法（MM/GBSA）在预测 PTM 效应时的最优协议（MD 时长、介电常数）尚未明确。 为什么重要 ：PTM 在疾病机制和药物响应中普遍存在（如磷酸化、乙酰化、糖基化等），理解 PTM 如何改变药物结合亲和力是「PTM 感知的药物设计」的关键前提。若能在药物发现早期预测 PTM 对结合的影响，可避免后期临床失败。 现有方法为何不足 ：此前缺乏经过实验验证的 PTM-配体活性变化系统数据集；已有的 MM/GBSA 研究多针对野生型蛋白，未系统评估 PTM 场景下的参数选择；PTM 效应预测常被简化为结构扰动，未与配体结合亲和力直接关联。 精确研究问题 ：Can end-point binding free energy calculation (MM/GBSA) with optimized MD simulation time and dielectric constant accurately predict the enhancing/weakening/neutral effects of PTMs on protein-ligand interactions?
