Review setup Input scope Full manuscript text (abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion) as provided Assessment boundary Scientific validity, methodological soundness, clarity of claims, and alignment with stated evidence; no assessment of formatting or editorial style beyond Nature-style criteria Shared manuscript claim summary The authors propose a simulation-free method (graph-driven sampling, GDS) to generate a basis set for constructing Koopman models of protein folding, eliminating the need for extensive molecular dynamics (MD) simulations in basis construction. They demonstrate this on a 2D model and the WW domain protein, claiming improved variational estimates of folding timescales and identification of kinetic traps. Visible evidence base Methods descriptions, results for 2D model and WW domain, comparisons to prior work, supplementary material referenced but not provided Missing materials affecting confidence Supplementary figures and tables (Figure S2, SI methods for lagtime selection, NTL9 results, Q-based comparisons), full MD trajectory details, code availability, and detailed parameter choices for GDS and Koopman fitting Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript presents a conceptually interesting and potentially impactful idea: using a graph-based, simulation-free approach to construct basis sets for Koopman models of protein folding. The 2D proof-of-concept is well described and supports the core hypothesis. However, the WW domain application, while promising, raises several concerns regarding the validity of the kinetic estimates, the interpretation of the identified "kinetic trap," and the generalizability of the approach. The reliance on existing ANTON MD data for parameterization, while pragmatic, limits the claim of being "simulation-free" in a practical sense. The manuscript is clearly written and accessible, but the evidence as presented is insufficient to fully establish the superiority or broad utility of the method over existing approaches. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational biophysicists and chemists working on protein folding, Markov state models, and enhanced sampling. Researchers developing new methods for kinetic model construction that aim to reduce computational cost. The work may also interest method developers in the Koopman operator and dynamical systems community. Major strengths 1) The core idea is novel and addresses a real bottleneck in MSM construction (basis selection without MD). 2) The 2D model provides a clear, controlled demonstration of the concept. 3) The use of the SCH metric is physically motivated and appears to offer advantages over simpler metrics. 4) The identification of a kinetic trap in the WW domain, if validated, is a significant finding. 5) The manuscript is generally well-written and accessible to a broad audience. Major Concerns See detailed items below. Minor Comments See detailed items below. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1 (validation of kinetic trap), R1-M2 (simulation-free claim), R1-M3 (comparison to prior work), R1-M4 (generalizability). Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: High. The concept of using GDS for basis construction is novel and distinct from existing MD-based or order-parameter-based approaches. Scientific importance: Potentially high, as it addresses a fundamental computational bottleneck in studying protein dynamics. However, the importance is contingent on the robustness and generalizability of the method, which are not fully established here. Interdisciplinary readership: Moderate. The work is primarily of interest to computational chemists and biophysicists; the broader biological or chemical community may find the technical details less accessible. Technical soundness: The 2D model is sound. The WW domain application is suggestive but has unresolved issues regarding the interpretation of the kinetic trap and the comparison to prior work. Readability for nonspecialists: The abstract and introduction are accessible, but the methods and results sections are dense and require specialist knowledge. Overall, the manuscript has strong potential but requires substantial revision and additional evidence to meet the high bar for a Nature-style publication. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved. The core idea is promising, but the current evidence does not fully establish the method's validity and superiority. The authors must address the concerns regarding the kinetic trap, the practical scope of the "simulation-free" claim, and the robustness of the comparison to prior work. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Validity of interpretation Claim pointer The manuscript claims that the GDS-constructed Koopman model "definitively identifies a 'kinetic trap' within the folding pathway(s) of the FIP35 WW domain which previous conventional VAMP-based approaches struggled to resolve." Evidence pointer Results and Discussion, WW Domain section, Figure 4 and associated text; location not provided Concern The identification of the "kinetic trap" is a central result, but the evidence presented is not sufficient to support the claim of "definitive" identification. The interpretation relies on visual inspection of free energy surfaces and contact map averages. It is not clear how the authors distinguish a true kinetic trap (a metastable state with a significant residence time) from a transient, non-committal intermediate. The manuscript does not provide quantitative metrics such as state populations, mean first passage times into and out of the trap, or a comparison of the trap's stability relative to thermal fluctuations. Furthermore, the claim that previous methods "struggled to resolve" this trap is not substantiated with a direct comparison of the resolved free energy surfaces or state decompositions from prior work. Why it matters The identification of a novel kinetic trap is a key selling point of the method. If this interpretation is not robust, the primary advantage of the GDS approach over existing methods is weakened. A definitive claim requires quantitative evidence of metastability and a clear demonstration that the trap is not an artifact of the basis set or the analysis procedure. Resolution test The authors should provide quantitative evidence of the trap's metastability, such as: (1) the population of the trap state from the MSM; (2) the residence time or mean first passage time to escape the trap; (3) a comparison of the free energy barrier separating the trap from the unfolded and folded states; (4) a direct comparison of the free energy surface and state decomposition obtained from the GDS-based model with that from a conventional MSM built on the same ANTON data, to demonstrate the claimed improvement in resolution. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Claim accuracy Claim pointer The title and abstract state the method is "Simulation-Free" and that it "does not rely on extensive, computationally demanding MD data for configuration space partitioning." Evidence pointer Title, Abstract, Introduction; location not provided Concern The claim of being "simulation-free" is misleading. While GDS itself does not generate MD trajectories, the method's validation and parameterization for the WW domain rely entirely on the existing ANTON MD dataset. The kinetic parameters (timescales) are extracted by projecting this MD data onto the GDS-generated basis. The method is therefore not "simulation-free" in a practical sense; it is "MD-basis-construction-free." This distinction is crucial. The authors do acknowledge this in the conclusion, but the title and abstract overstate the case. This could mislead readers about the method's true requirements and potential applications. Why it matters The primary claim of novelty and utility is the removal of the MD bottleneck. If the method still requires MD data for any meaningful kinetic output, its advantage is reduced to a pre-processing step. The claim must be accurately scoped to avoid overstating the method's capabilities. Resolution test The authors should revise the title and abstract to accurately reflect the method's scope, e.g., "Simulation-Free Basis Construction for Koopman Models" or "MD-Free Basis Selection for Koopman Models." The text should clearly state that while GDS generates the basis without MD, the parameterization of the kinetic model (i.e., estimating transition probabilities) still requires MD data, and the method's primary advantage is in reducing the amount of MD data needed for basis selection, not eliminating it entirely. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Evidence quality Claim pointer The manuscript claims that the GDS-based model "variationally improves folding time scale estimates" compared to previous studies, citing a folding time of 13.8 μs vs. 10.2 μs from prior work. Evidence pointer Results and Discussion, WW Domain section; location not provided Concern The comparison to prior work is not sufficiently detailed. The authors compare their folding time to a single value (10.2 μs) from previous studies, but it is unclear if this is an apples-to-apples comparison. The previous studies may have used different lag times, different state definitions, different analysis methods, or even different definitions of the "folding time." The manuscript does not provide a table comparing the key parameters of the different models (e.g., number of states, lag time, basis functions, clustering method). Without this context, the claim of "variational improvement" is not convincing. A variational improvement means that the estimated timescale is closer to the true value, but the true value is unknown. A longer timescale could also be an artifact of a poorly converged model or a different definition of the folded state. Why it matters The claim of variational improvement is a key quantitative result. If the comparison is not rigorous, the claim is unsupported. The authors need to demonstrate that the difference in timescales is significant and that it arises from the quality of the basis set, not from other methodological differences. Resolution test The authors should provide a detailed comparison table (in the main text or SI) listing the model parameters for their GDS-based model and the prior models they compare against. They should also discuss the uncertainty in their estimate (e.g., via bootstrapping) and the sensitivity of the result to the choice of lag time and basis function parameters. A more robust demonstration would be to show that their model converges to a stable timescale with fewer basis functions than a conventional model built on the same data. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Generalizability Claim pointer The manuscript suggests the method is "quite general" and "could equally be applied to protein–protein interaction networks, drug–protein binding, protein misfolding, and other complex transient biophysical processes." Evidence pointer Conclusion; location not provided Concern The generalizability claim is not supported by the evidence. The method is demonstrated on a single, small protein (WW domain, 35 residues) and a 2D toy model. The success of GDS relies on the ability to generate a connected path of physically plausible intermediate contact maps between unfolded and folded states. For larger proteins or more complex processes (e.g., binding), the contact map space becomes vastly larger and the GDS optimization may struggle to find relevant paths. The manuscript does not discuss the computational scaling of GDS with system size or the potential challenges in applying it to more complex systems. Why it matters The potential impact of the method depends on its applicability to a wide range of problems. If the method only works for small, simple proteins, its significance is limited. The authors should either provide evidence of scalability or temper their claims about generalizability. Resolution test The authors should discuss the computational cost of GDS as a function of protein size and contact map complexity. They could also perform a proof-of-concept on a second, larger protein to demonstrate scalability. If this is not feasible, the claims of generalizability should be significantly softened. The choice of the parameter k_cont = 0.05 for the WW domain is mentioned but not justified in detail. Required correction Provide a more detailed algorithmic description, including pseudo-code if possible. Justify the choice of k_cont and other key parameters, perhaps with a sensitivity analysis. However, the specific parameters of the fitting procedure (e.g., regularization, number of basis functions used in the final model) are not provided. 研究问题 具体问题 ：如何从缺乏时间信息的 Monte Carlo（或增强采样）系综中提取分子动力学信息（如速率常数、平均首次通过时间、隐含时间尺度）？ 为什么重要 ：MC 和增强采样方法能高效探索构象空间并准确估计平衡态布居，但无法直接描述动力学。对于 MD 收敛代价过高的体系（如大蛋白、慢折叠过程），若能利用热力学采样推断动力学，将大幅降低计算成本。 现有方法为何不足 ：传统 MSM 需要大量 MD 轨迹数据来构建转移概率矩阵，其时间分辨率受限于 MD 轨迹长度和采样充分性；而 MC 系综本身不含时间信息，无法直接用于 MSM 构建。 精确研究问题 ：Can a continuous-time Markov chain, parameterized solely by the free energy surface of a static Boltzmann-weighted ensemble, reproduce MD-derived kinetic observables (rate matrices, mean first-passage times, implied time scales) after a short calibration step? 04 背景与发展脉络 （标注：此脉络为「经外部核验」——基于 Markov state model 领域公认发展史，结合本文引言中的描述） - 阶段 1：MD 直接模拟 （1970s–至今） - 代表方法：全原子 MD、增强采样（umbrella sampling, metadynamics） - 优点：提供真实动力学轨迹 - 局限：时间尺度受限（μs–ms 级需大量算力），对慢过程收敛困难 - 阶段 2：Markov State Models（MSM） （2000s–至今） - 代表方法：Pande 等提出的 MSM 框架，基于 MD 轨迹聚类、构建转移矩阵 - 优点：从短轨迹拼接长时尺度动力学，可估计隐含时间尺度 - 局限：依赖 MD 数据质量与数量；对采样不足的体系（如高能垒）难以构建可靠模型 - 阶段 3：从热力学采样推断动力学 （2010s–至今，本文所属） - 代表方法：基于自由能面的动力学重建（如 Kramers 理论、diffusion maps）、本文的 DIME - 优点：利用 MC/增强采样的高效性，避免 MD 长时间模拟 - 局限：需要自由能面准确估计；时间尺度需外部校准 - 本文主张的位置 ：DIME 是首个系统性地从静态 MC 系综构建 CTMC 并验证于多尺度体系（从二面角到毫秒级 BPTI）的框架，填补了「热力学采样 → 动力学」的空白。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 MC 系综缺乏时间信息 MC The potential to predict binding sites on apo RNA structures without requiring accurate holo structures addresses a practical bottleneck in early-stage drug discovery. The multimodal fusion approach may also interest those working on integrating heterogeneous biomolecular representations. Major strengths The problem is well motivated and practically relevant. The proposed integration of molecular surface fingerprints with sequence and secondary structure information is a sensible response to the identified gap in existing methods. The reported performance on independent benchmarks, if reproducible, would represent a meaningful advance. The attention to apo RNA structures and flexibility is a practical consideration that strengthens the potential utility. 验证方式 ：保守位点的突变实验。 - 可能的失败模式 ：家族成员间脂质结合机制差异大。 - 创新状态 ：unverified。 Review setup Input scope Abstract only Assessment boundary Claims and conclusions as presented in the abstract, without access to full methods, figures, or simulation details Shared manuscript claim summary The authors use multiscale molecular dynamics simulations to characterize lipid binding dynamics and sodium ion coordination in the TRAP transporter HiSiaQM from Haemophilus influenzae. They report validation of an experimentally known lipid-binding site (BS1) with preferential POPG occupancy, discovery of a novel POPE-selective site (BS2), and differential stability of two sodium binding sites (Na1 stable, Na2 less stable), with tunnel analysis suggesting distinct functional roles for Na1 and Na2. Visible evidence base Abstract text only. No figures, tables, methods, or supplementary materials were provided. Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, simulation protocols, force field parameters, convergence criteria, structural coordinates, lipid composition details, ion concentration settings, tunnel analysis methodology, and experimental validation data are all unavailable. Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a plausible and potentially interesting computational study of lipid and ion dynamics in a membrane transporter of biological relevance. The findings are internally coherent and the proposed mechanistic distinction between Na1 and Na2 is intellectually appealing. However, the abstract alone provides insufficient evidence to evaluate the technical rigor of the simulations, the statistical significance of the observed differences, or the robustness of the conclusions. Several claims are presented as definitive without visible quantitative support. The work may be of interest to the membrane transporter and molecular simulation communities, but the case is not fully established from the supplied material. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers studying TRAP transporters and other secondary active transporters would be interested in the proposed mechanistic roles of sodium binding sites. Computational biophysicists and molecular dynamics practitioners would be interested in the multiscale simulation approach and the identification of lipid binding dynamics. Structural biologists working on membrane proteins could find the lipid interaction data useful for understanding native-like environments. The potential link between lipid composition and transporter function may also appeal to microbiologists studying Haemophilus influenzae pathogenesis. Major strengths The study addresses a relevant and under-explored aspect of TRAP transporter function, namely the dynamic behavior of lipids and ions rather than static structures. The use of multiscale simulations is appropriate for capturing both local interactions and larger-scale dynamics. The authors explicitly acknowledge that the distinct lipid-binding behaviors remain to be tested experimentally, which is an appropriate level of caution. The proposed functional asymmetry between Na1 and Na2 provides a testable hypothesis that could guide future experimental work. Major Concerns R1-M1 R1-M2 R1-M3 Minor Comments R1-m1 R1-m2 R1-m3 R1-m4 Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1 (simulation validation and convergence), R1-M2 (quantitative support for lipid selectivity), R1-M3 (sodium site stability comparison) Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The study offers a novel perspective on TRAP transporter dynamics by focusing on lipid and ion behavior rather than static structure, which is a reasonable contribution to the field. Scientific importance: The findings could inform understanding of ion-coupled transport mechanisms, but the significance is moderate and largely hypothesis-generating at this stage. Interdisciplinary readership: The topic bridges structural biology, computational biophysics, and microbiology, which could attract a broad audience if the evidence is robust. Technical soundness: Cannot be adequately assessed from the abstract alone. The absence of methodological details and quantitative results prevents verification of simulation quality, sampling adequacy, or statistical rigor. Readability for nonspecialists: The abstract is clearly written and accessible, with appropriate use of terminology and a logical flow from background to findings to implications. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The abstract presents a coherent narrative, but the lack of visible quantitative data and methodological detail means the core claims cannot be verified. A supportive posture would require access to the full manuscript demonstrating simulation convergence, statistical robustness, and appropriate controls. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The simulations validated an experimentally identified lipid-binding site (BS1) and provided insight into its lipid-binding dynamics. Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Concern The abstract states that BS1 was validated and that its dynamics were characterized, but no information is provided about simulation length, number of replicates, force field parameters, lipid bilayer composition, or convergence criteria. Without these details, it is impossible to assess whether the simulations adequately sampled the relevant conformational space or whether the observed lipid binding events are statistically meaningful rather than stochastic artifacts. Why it matters Molecular dynamics simulations of membrane proteins are highly sensitive to system setup and sampling. Claims of validation and dynamic characterization require evidence that the simulations reached equilibrium, that multiple independent runs produced consistent results, and that the chosen force field and membrane model are appropriate for the system. The absence of this information undermines confidence in the central findings. Resolution test Provide simulation protocols including system size, simulation time per replicate, number of replicates, force field and water model, lipid composition, ion concentration, and temperature/pressure coupling schemes. Show convergence metrics such as root-mean-square deviation over time, lipid occupancy as a function of simulation time, and replicate-to-replicate variability. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence strength Claim pointer BS1 is preferentially occupied by the anionic POPG, which is stabilized through persistent hydrogen bonds involving residues H100, R104, and R181. A novel, less stable lipid-binding site (BS2) is selectively occupied by POPE. Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Concern The claims of preferential and selective lipid occupancy are presented without quantitative data. No occupancy percentages, free energy estimates, residence times, or statistical comparisons between lipid types are provided. The statement that POPG forms more persistent interactions at BS1 and POPE engages more transiently at BS2 is qualitative and lacks supporting numbers. It is unclear how selectivity was determined and whether the observed preferences are statistically significant given the simulation time and lipid concentrations used. Why it matters Lipid selectivity in membrane protein simulations can be influenced by initial conditions, lipid composition, and simulation length. Without quantitative occupancy data and appropriate statistical tests, the claim of preferential binding cannot be distinguished from random fluctuation or setup bias. This is a core finding of the study and must be rigorously supported. Resolution test Report occupancy fractions for each lipid type at each site, residence time distributions, and statistical comparisons (e.g., standard errors across replicates or bootstrapped confidence intervals). If possible, provide potential of mean force calculations or free energy estimates for lipid binding at each site. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer Na1 exhibited stable ion retention through backbone carbonyl coordination, while Na2 displayed lower stability due to involvement of the flexible side chain of T561. Geometric tunnel analysis identified possible sodium-exit pathways, supporting a working hypothesis that Na1 may act as a stable anchoring site and Na2 may function as a transient ion-exchange point. Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Concern The differential stability of Na1 and Na2 is described qualitatively, with no quantitative measures such as ion occupancy over time, coordination bond lifetimes, or root-mean-square fluctuations of coordinating residues. The role of T561 in destabilizing Na2 is asserted but not demonstrated with data. The tunnel analysis is mentioned without any description of the method, the criteria for identifying tunnels, or the statistical significance of the proposed exit pathways. Why it matters The proposed functional asymmetry between Na1 and Na2 is a central mechanistic claim. Without quantitative evidence of differential ion retention and a rigorous tunnel analysis, the hypothesis remains speculative. The involvement of T561 in particular requires demonstration that its flexibility correlates with reduced ion occupancy or increased coordination bond breaking events. Resolution test Provide ion occupancy time series for both sites, coordination bond lifetime distributions, and fluctuation analysis of T561 compared to other coordinating residues. Describe the tunnel analysis method (e.g., CAVER or similar), the parameters used, and the frequency and persistence of the identified exit pathways across simulation replicates. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Abstract wording Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Issue The phrase "HiSiaQM horizontal line a membrane-embedded TRAP subunit" appears to contain a formatting artifact where "horizontal line" is used in place of an em dash or similar separator. This is likely a typesetting error but should be corrected for clarity. Required correction Replace "horizontal line" with the appropriate punctuation or rephrase the sentence to avoid the artifact. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected element Experimental validation statement Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Issue The authors state that the distinct lipid-binding behaviors "remain to be tested experimentally," which is appropriate. However, it is unclear whether any experimental data already exist that could partially support or contradict the simulation findings, such as mutagenesis studies on H100, R104, R181, or T561. Required correction Clarify whether any prior experimental data on these residues exist and, if so, briefly state how the simulation results relate to them. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Precision Affected element Terminology Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Issue The term "multiscale molecular dynamics simulations" is used, but the abstract does not specify which scales were combined or how. This could mean coarse-grained and atomistic simulations, or it could refer to different time-scale approaches. The term is ambiguous without further detail. Required correction Specify the types of simulations used (e.g., coarse-grained and atomistic) and briefly indicate how they were integrated in the study. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Interpretation Affected element Mechanistic hypothesis Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Issue The proposed roles of Na1 as a "stable anchoring site" and Na2 as a "transient ion-exchange point" are presented as a working hypothesis, which is appropriate. However, the abstract does not explain how these roles would mechanistically couple to substrate transport or the overall transport cycle. Required correction Add one or two sentences connecting the proposed sodium site functions to the broader transport mechanism, or explicitly state that this connection remains to be established. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that BS1 is "preferentially occupied" by POPG is unsupported without quantitative occupancy data or statistical analysis. The claim that BS2 is "selectively occupied" by POPE is unsupported for the same reason. The assertion that POPG forms "persistent" interactions and POPE engages "transiently" is qualitative and lacks residence time or bond lifetime data. The differential stability of Na1 versus Na2 is asserted without quantitative ion occupancy or coordination dynamics data. The role of T561 in reducing Na2 stability is stated as fact but not demonstrated with fluctuation or coordination analysis. The tunnel analysis and proposed sodium-exit pathways are mentioned without methodological detail or statistical support. The overall mechanistic conclusion that lipid interactions and sodium coordination "could modulate" transporter function is appropriately framed as a possibility, but the strength of the underlying evidence cannot be evaluated from the abstract alone.

04 背景与发展脉络 （标注：以下脉络为「仅本文框架」——基于本文引言与讨论的推断，未逐条外部核验） - 阶段一：实验结构静态分析 。代表性方法：X 射线晶体学、冷冻电镜解析 GPCR 不同功能态结构。优点：提供高分辨率原子模型。局限：仅捕获热力学稳定态，无法直接观察动态转换路径。 - 阶段二：MD 模拟靶向分析 。代表性方法：对已知微开关（如 toggle switch W6.48、ionic lock）进行距离/二面角监测。优点：可量化构象变化。局限：需预先知道"看什么"，可能遗漏未知元件。 - 阶段三：无监督/数据驱动分析 。代表性方法：PCA、tICA、Markov state models 等降维与状态划分。优点：可发现主要构象态。局限：降维后的投影可能难以直接映射回原子级结构解释，且特征选择仍依赖人工。 - 本文位置 ：提出一个介于"完全人工"与"全自动"之间的半自动化管线——先对 featurized 数据聚类，再反向识别判别性特征，将"发现"过程自动化，但保留化学直觉在特征工程层面。该方法不依赖预定义反应坐标，可输出可解释的原子级结构元件。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 人工分析主观性强 不同研究者对同一轨迹可能关注不同特征，结论不一致 分析依赖预先选择的反应坐标或已知结构元件 未提供（作者在引言中暗示，但无直接引用） 已知元件遮蔽新发现 靶向分析只验证已知微开关，无法发现新基序 分析框架被已有知识锚定 未提供（作者在讨论中提及"in addition to these known structural elements"作为新发现对比） 大数据集不可扩展 微秒级轨迹人工检查不现实 轨迹长度与维度超出人工处理能力 未提供（作者在引言中提及"routine to obtain trajectories tens of microseconds"） 降维方法丢失原子级可解释性 PCA/tICA 投影难以直接映射到具体残基或螺旋运动 降维目标是全局方差而非功能判别 未提供（作者在方法选择上采用聚类+特征判别而非降维，暗示此问题） 06 核心思想 表面方法 ：对 MD 轨迹进行 featurization（提取距离、二面角、螺旋几何等），对特征矩阵做无监督聚类（如 k-means 或 GMM），然后对每个簇训练分类器（如随机森林或逻辑回归），用特征重要性分数识别哪些输入特征最能区分簇身份。 核心洞察 ：聚类本身不关心"功能"，但簇间的判别性特征天然对应构象状态转换的结构决定因素——因为 MD 轨迹中的 metastable 状态往往由少数关键结构参数区分。通过"聚类→判别"两步，将"发现功能相关结构元件"转化为"识别簇间判别特征"的统计问题。 可能的普适教训 [Analysis]：在蛋白质构象分析中，与其预先定义反应坐标，不如让数据自己"说话"——先让聚类算法划分状态，再反向工程判别特征。这种"先分后析"策略可迁移到任何 MD 或构象采样数据，且不限于 GPCR。 07 方法总览 输入 ：GPCR MD 模拟轨迹（微秒级，多体系），已进行 featurization 的特征矩阵（具体特征类型未详述，推测含残基间距离、螺旋几何参数、二面角等）。 输出 ：一组判别性结构特征列表，每个特征对应一个结构元件（如微开关、螺旋 kink、螺旋间运动），并标注其所属簇及功能相关性。 模块 ： 1. Shared manuscript claim summary The authors propose HelixDTA, a dual-branch deep learning framework that integrates sequence-derived and complete target structure-derived features for drug-target affinity prediction. They report competitive performance on Davis and KIBA benchmarks, robust generalization in cold-start settings, interpretability via attention mechanisms, and a WRN case study demonstrating structure-aware allosteric candidate prioritization. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no quantitative results, benchmark tables, methodological details, or case study figures are provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, benchmark datasets and splits, hyperparameter settings, baseline comparisons, statistical significance tests, attention visualization details, WRN case study methodology and outcomes, code availability Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a plausible and potentially valuable contribution to the drug-target affinity prediction field, specifically in combining sequence and complete structural information within a dual-branch architecture. However, the abstract lacks quantitative evidence, methodological specificity, and comparative rigor. The claims of robustness, interpretability, and practical utility cannot be evaluated from the supplied material. The work may be of interest to computational drug discovery researchers, but the current evidence base is insufficient to establish the stated advantages. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational biologists, medicinal chemists, and machine learning researchers working on drug discovery, particularly those focused on structure-aware prediction models, protein-ligand interaction modeling, and interpretable AI for biomedical applications. The dual-branch design and cold-start evaluation may appeal to groups developing generalizable prediction tools for novel targets and scaffolds. Major strengths The conceptual motivation is clear and addresses a recognized limitation in existing DTA models, namely the incomplete use of structural information. The dual-branch architecture that preserves modality-specific features until the prediction layer is a reasonable design choice. The inclusion of cold-start settings and a case study on allosteric candidate prioritization suggests attention to practical deployment scenarios beyond standard benchmark performance. The abstract does not provide any performance metrics, baseline comparisons, or statistical measures to support the claims of strong, competitive, or advantageous performance. Why it matters Without numerical evidence, the central performance claims cannot be verified or compared against existing methods. The phrase "clear advantages" is subjective and unsupported. Resolution test Provide benchmark tables with metrics (e.g., CI, RMSE, MAE) for HelixDTA and at least several baseline methods, including statistical significance tests or confidence intervals, across all evaluated settings. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Methodological clarity Claim pointer "a parallel dual-branch architecture that independently learns representations from two distinct but complementary modalities: sequence context and complete target structures" Evidence pointer Abstract only; location not provided Concern The abstract does not describe how "complete target structures" are obtained, represented, or processed. Why it matters The novelty and feasibility of the approach depend critically on the structural data pipeline. If complete structures are required, the method's applicability to proteome-wide or novel target settings is questionable. Clarify whether predicted structures are used and how their quality is assessed. Why it matters Interpretability claims in machine learning for drug discovery require demonstration that attention weights are biologically meaningful, not merely that they exist. no access to full text, figures, tables, or supplementary materials Shared manuscript claim summary The review argues that AlphaFold-based predicted structures have substantially expanded structure-based drug discovery (SBDD) capabilities across target identification, binding site prediction, docking, virtual screening, lead optimization, and SAR, while acknowledging persistent limitations in protein flexibility, ligand-induced conformational changes, affinity prediction, and the need for experimental validation. It proposes an evidence-graded decision framework for when predicted structures suffice for specific applications and cites two prospective examples (TAAR1 and CDK20) as evidence of utility. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; two quantitative examples (TAAR1 hit rates, CDK20 IC50 and selectivity) are described but without methodological detail or source references Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, figures, tables, references, the evidence-graded decision framework details, and the primary data behind the two prospective examples Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a timely and potentially useful review topic, but the claims of capability and the proposed decision framework cannot be adequately evaluated from the abstract alone. The two prospective examples are promising but lack sufficient context to assess their validity or generalizability. The review's value will depend heavily on the rigor of the full text, particularly the evidence grading methodology and the completeness of the limitations discussion. Who would be interested in the results, and why Medicinal chemists and computational biologists engaged in structure-based drug design, particularly those considering whether to adopt AlphaFold models in their workflows. The review could also interest researchers in AI-driven drug discovery, structural biology, and translational pharmacology who need guidance on when predicted structures are reliable enough for specific applications. Major strengths The abstract addresses a highly relevant and rapidly evolving area. It explicitly acknowledges the heterogeneity of prediction confidence across targets and regions, which is a critical nuance often missing in such reviews. The inclusion of an evidence-graded decision framework is a valuable conceptual contribution, and the two prospective examples provide concrete, quantitative illustrations of both success and remaining challenges. The terms "efficient," "highly enantioselective," and "diverse" are undefined and cannot be assessed. Why it matters The core claim of the manuscript rests on these performance metrics. Without numbers, the reader cannot judge whether the results represent a meaningful advance over existing systems or whether the claims are overstated. Resolution test Provide quantitative data in the full manuscript, including enantiomeric excess values for all substrates, turnover numbers, reaction yields, and recycling data, with appropriate controls. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Mechanistic evidence Claim pointer The abstract states that "spectroscopic studies show that the protein environment extends the photocatalyst excited-state lifetime and organizes substrate near the cofactor, altering energy transfer and controlling stereoselectivity." Evidence pointer Abstract only; location not provided Concern The mechanistic claims are presented as established findings, but no spectroscopic data, experimental conditions, or comparative controls are described. The link between excited-state lifetime extension, substrate organization, and stereocontrol is asserted without evidence. Why it matters These mechanistic claims are central to understanding why the design works and are likely a major part of the paper's novelty. If not rigorously supported, the mechanistic narrative is speculative. Resolution test Present time-resolved spectroscopic data (e.g., transient absorption or emission lifetimes) for the cofactor in solution versus in the protein, structural or binding data showing substrate proximity, and mutagenesis or control experiments linking these effects to enantioselectivity. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Generality of the design approach Claim pointer The abstract claims that "these findings establish de novo protein design as a route to functional scaffolds for synthetic metal complexes that lack natural protein partners." Evidence pointer Abstract only; location not provided Concern The abstract describes a single class of metal complexes (metal polypyridine photocatalysts) and does not indicate how many distinct scaffolds or catalysts were designed and tested. The claim of establishing a general route requires demonstration across multiple scaffolds or catalyst types. Why it matters The generality claim elevates the work from a specific example to a broadly applicable strategy. Without evidence of generality, the claim is premature. Resolution test Show successful design and evolution for multiple metal complexes or at least multiple scaffold topologies, with data on success rates and failure analysis. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: High. The concept of de novo designing scaffolds for metal polypyridine photocatalysts and evolving them for enantioselectivity appears novel and distinct from prior trial-and-error approaches. Scientific importance: Potentially high, if the claims are substantiated. The work could open new avenues in asymmetric photocatalysis and expand the scope of de novo protein design. Interdisciplinary readership: Strong. The work bridges chemistry, biology, and protein engineering, and would appeal to a broad audience if the results are compelling. Technical soundness: Not assessable from the abstract. No methods or data are available to evaluate the rigor of the design, evolution, or characterization. Readability for nonspecialists: The abstract is generally clear, but the mechanistic claims and the significance of the design approach would benefit from more explicit framing for a general audience. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The abstract presents a promising concept, but the absence of quantitative data and mechanistic support prevents evaluation of the core claims. A full manuscript with detailed methods, results, and controls is required to assess whether the case is made. Risk / unsupported claims The claim of "efficient, highly enantioselective photocatalysts" is unsupported without quantitative data. The claim that the protein environment "extends the photocatalyst excited-state lifetime and organizes substrate near the cofactor, altering energy transfer and controlling stereoselectivity" is unsupported without spectroscopic and structural evidence. The claim that the findings "establish de novo protein design as a route to functional scaffolds" is unsupported as a general statement without demonstration across multiple systems. The claim of "diverse light-driven reactions" is unverifiable without a list of reactions. The claim of "high catalyst turnover and catalyst recycling" is unverifiable without turnover numbers and recycling data.

MD）与「构象采样/构象生成」子方向直接相关；其「多模式调控汇聚于共享能量轴」的结论对理解膜蛋白变构调控具有方法论和概念上的可迁移性。该文不涉及 AlphaFold 或序列设计，但展示了如何将增强采样 MD 与电生理实验结合来解析构象-功能关系。 02 一句话总结 本文使用 OneOPES 增强采样 MD 模拟，定量表征了 TREK-2 钾通道在磷酸化、膜拉伸和疾病突变（A314P）条件下沿 up-down 构象转变路径的自由能景观，发现这些不同调控输入通过耦合 M4 螺旋、pCt 和选择性滤过器的共享能量轴来改变通道的门控平衡，并用状态依赖性抑制剂 norfluoxetine 的电生理实验验证了突变对 up 态的稳定作用。 03 研究问题 具体问题 : TREK-2 通道如何整合多种生理刺激（磷酸化、膜拉伸）和疾病突变（A314P）来调节其门控构象平衡？这些不同调控输入是否共享一个能量耦合网络？ 为什么重要 : TREK 通道是多模式门控钾通道，参与神经保护、麻醉、疼痛感知等关键生理过程；其功能失调与癫痫、神经发育障碍等疾病相关。理解其调控机制对于开发靶向药物和理解通道病理性激活的分子基础至关重要。 现有方法为何不足 : 先前的无偏 MD 模拟虽能观察到 up/down 态转换和 SF 重排，但采样不足，无法定量计算自由能差异，也无法建立不同调控输入之间的能量联系。传统增强采样方法（如 metadynamics）在高维、柔性大的膜蛋白系统中难以收敛。 精确的「Can ... ?」研究问题 : Can a carefully designed set of collective variables, combined with the OneOPES enhanced-sampling framework, quantitatively resolve how phosphorylation, membrane stretch, and a disease mutation reshape the free-energy landscape of the TREK-2 up-down transition and reveal a shared energetic coupling between the M4/pCt region and the selectivity filter? 04 背景与发展脉络 （标注：以下脉络主要基于本文 Introduction 和 Results 的叙述，属于「仅本文框架」，未经外部系统核验。） 结构生物学阶段 : X 射线晶体学解析了 TREK/TRAAK 通道的 up 和 down 两种构象状态（PDB: 4BW5, 4XDJ, 4WFE 等），揭示了 M4 螺旋相对于膜的不同取向和 pCt 的定位差异。但晶体结构显示 up/down 态的 SF 构象几乎相同，这引发了关于 SF 是否作为门控位点的争论。 无偏 MD 模拟阶段 : 本课题组之前的无偏 MD 模拟（Turkaydin 等，2024）观察到 down 态 SF 在 S1 位点附近出现主链重排，损害离子传导，提示 SF 可能是真正的门控位点。但采样不足，无法进行定量自由能分析。 增强采样 MD 阶段（本文） : 采用 OneOPES 框架（结合 OPES Explore 与 replica exchange），以路径 CV 为主坐标，辅以 M4-M2 距离、SF 二面角、离子/水配位数等 CV，实现了 up-down 转变的充分采样和自由能定量。这是首次对 TREK-2 多模式调控进行定量能量景观表征。 电生理验证阶段 : 使用状态依赖性抑制剂 norfluoxetine（NFx）作为构象探针，通过 inside-out patch-clamp 实验验证了 A314P 突变对 up 态的稳定作用，将计算预测与功能实验联系起来。 本文主张的位置 : 在结构生物学和无偏 MD 的基础上，通过增强采样 MD 将定性观察提升为定量自由能框架，并首次提出「不同调控输入（磷酸化、拉伸、突变）汇聚于同一能量轴」的统一模型。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 无偏 MD 采样不足 无法观察到足够的 up-down 自发转换，无法计算自由能差 up-down 转变涉及大尺度、慢速的 M4 螺旋运动，在 μs 时间尺度上难以充分采样 Introduction: "the slow Scientific soundness, methodological rigor, validity of conclusions relative to evidence presented, and suitability for the stated venue Shared manuscript claim summary The authors use OneOPES enhanced-sampling molecular dynamics to characterize the energetics of the up-to-down conformational transition in TREK-2 potassium channels, proposing a shared energetic axis coupling lower helices, proximal C-terminus, and selectivity filter. They validate predicted effects of a disease-mimicking mutation (A314P) using electrophysiology with a conformation-sensitive inhibitor. Visible evidence base Computational free-energy surfaces (1D and 2D), structural analyses, and electrophysiological recordings (TEVC and inside-out patch-clamp) from Xenopus oocytes Missing materials affecting confidence Supplementary figures and tables referenced but not provided; no methodological details for the norfluoxetine dose-response curve fitting beyond the Hill equation; no raw trajectory data or convergence metrics beyond those described; no information on how the path CV was validated against unbiased simulations Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript presents a computationally intensive study aimed at establishing an energetic framework for TREK-2 channel regulation, linking conformational changes in the lower helices and proximal C-terminus to selectivity filter dynamics. The use of OneOPES to quantify free-energy differences between up- and down-states under different conditions is a reasonable and potentially valuable approach. The electrophysiological validation using norfluoxetine as a state-dependent inhibitor is a thoughtful experimental design. However, several concerns limit the strength of the conclusions as currently presented. The manuscript would benefit from clearer presentation of convergence criteria, more direct evidence linking the simulated free-energy differences to functional outcomes, and a more cautious interpretation of the selectivity filter dynamics given acknowledged limitations in sampling. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in the ion channel biophysics community, particularly those studying two-pore domain potassium channels, mechanosensitive channels, and polymodal regulation. The methodological community interested in enhanced-sampling techniques applied to membrane proteins would also find value. The potential link to disease mechanisms (FHEIG syndrome) broadens relevance to translational researchers studying channelopathies. Major Strengths The application of OneOPES to a large, complex membrane protein system is technically ambitious and represents a methodological advance for the field The combination of computational predictions with electrophysiological validation using a state-dependent inhibitor is a strong experimental design The acknowledgment of limitations (e.g., inability to resolve full SF gating, variability across runs) is commendable and indicates scientific honesty The proposed framework of a shared energetic axis is conceptually appealing and could stimulate further research Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The manuscript claims that the free-energy landscapes obtained from OneOPES provide a quantitative framework for understanding how phosphorylation, membrane stretch, and mutation modulate TREK-2 gating. Evidence pointer Results section "The global conformational transition of TREK-2 is driven by the coordinated motion of M4-pCt"; Figures 2b–d, 5d; Supplementary Table 3 Concern The convergence of the OneOPES simulations is not adequately demonstrated. The authors report run-to-run variability but do not provide quantitative convergence metrics (e.g., free-energy difference estimates as a function of simulation time, overlap between replica ensembles, or comparison of independent runs beyond standard deviation envelopes). Given that the central claims rest on free-energy differences between conditions (e.g., ΔΔG values of 31.8 and −23.0 kJ/mol), the reader needs stronger evidence that these differences are converged and not artifacts of insufficient sampling. The authors state that formal significance tests were not applied, which is acceptable, but the separation relative to propagated error (|ΔΔG|/σ) should be reported explicitly for all comparisons. Why it matters Without demonstrated convergence, the quantitative free-energy differences that form the core of the manuscript's claims cannot be reliably interpreted. The conclusions about condition-dependent shifts in conformational equilibria depend entirely on the accuracy of these numbers. Resolution test Provide convergence plots showing free-energy estimates as a function of simulation time for each system, report the |ΔΔG|/σ values for all pairwise condition comparisons, and show that the qualitative conclusions are robust to the choice of analysis window (e.g., comparing the first and second halves of the trajectories). Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Scientific importance / Claim substantiation Claim pointer The manuscript states that "the free-energy landscapes obtained from OneOPES... establish an energetic framework for TREK-2 regulation and dysfunction" and that the A314P mutation "shifts the equilibrium strongly toward the up-state." Evidence pointer Results section "Disease-mimicking mutation reshapes the TREK-2* energy landscape toward a conductive state"; Figures 5d–f; Supplementary Figure 7 Concern The link between the simulated up-state stabilization in A314P and the experimentally observed increase in current is indirect. The authors show that A314P increases current ~9-fold and that the mutation stabilizes the up-state in simulations, but the causal chain connecting these observations is not established. Specifically, the manuscript does not demonstrate that the up-state is more conductive than the down-state in the same simulation framework, nor does it rule out alternative mechanisms for increased current (e.g., changes in single-channel conductance, open probability, or surface expression). The norfluoxetine shift in IC50 is consistent with a conformational shift but could also be explained by altered drug binding affinity independent of the up/down equilibrium. Why it matters The manuscript's central claim is that a shared energetic axis couples lower helices, pCT, and SF to govern gating. The A314P data are presented as key supporting evidence, but the connection between simulated conformational preferences and functional outcomes is not rigorously established. Resolution test Perform additional simulations or analyses that directly compare ion conduction in up- vs. down-state conformations (e.g., using the same force field and system setup), or provide experimental data (e.g., single-channel recordings) that link the conformational shift to conductance changes. Alternatively, temper the claims to reflect that the simulations predict a conformational shift that is consistent with, but does not prove, the functional mechanism. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The manuscript acknowledges that "the energetic description of the Y175 deviates from our previous unbiased simulations" and attributes this to missing CVs. Evidence pointer Results section "Energetic coupling between the pCT and SF defines the thermodynamic basis of TREK-2* gating"; Supplementary Figure 6 Concern The authors acknowledge that Y175 dynamics were not adequately sampled, yet Y175 is described as an important component of the selectivity filter. This limitation is disclosed, which is good, but it raises questions about the completeness of the proposed energetic framework. If a key SF residue's dynamics are not reliably characterized, can the authors confidently claim a "shared energetic axis" that includes the SF? The manuscript would be strengthened by a more explicit discussion of how this limitation affects the overall conclusions. Why it matters The proposed framework's generality depends on the reliability of the SF characterization. An acknowledged sampling failure for one of the two key SF residues weakens the claim that the framework captures the essential coupling. Resolution test Either improve sampling of Y175 dynamics (e.g., by adding CVs that capture the M4 loop/EC loop interactions identified in prior work) or explicitly state that the framework's conclusions regarding SF coupling are based primarily on F284 dynamics, with Y175 requiring future investigation. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Readability Affected element Figure 2a Evidence pointer Figure 2a Issue The representation of the path CV preparation is difficult to interpret. The salmon-colored regions are described as "highly flexible regions that are affecting the RMSD changes," but it is unclear which specific residues or structural elements these correspond to, and how they were selected. Required correction Provide a clearer figure legend or annotation identifying the specific residues/regions excluded from alignment, and briefly justify why these were chosen based on the crystal structures and prior simulations. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Technical soundness Affected element Methods section "OneOPES simulations" Evidence pointer Methods section "OneOPES simulations" Issue The description of the replica-exchange setup is somewhat unclear. The authors state that "Replica 0 acted as the convergence monitor, while the remaining seven replicas (1–7) were used to enhance exploration," but then describe that replicas 1–6 biased auxiliary CVs and the eighth replica implemented multi-thermal expansion. This is confusing: are there 8 replicas total (0–7) or 9 (0–8)? Required correction Clarify the total number of replicas and the specific role of each replica in the setup. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Readability Affected element Discussion section Evidence pointer Discussion section, paragraph on Y175 Issue The discussion of Y175 limitations is somewhat buried in the broader discussion of methodology. Given that this is a significant limitation, it deserves more prominent placement and a clearer statement of its implications. Required correction Move the Y175 limitation discussion to a more prominent position, perhaps in the Results section where Y175 data are first presented, and explicitly state what conclusions can and cannot be drawn from the Y175 data. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Technical soundness Affected element Methods section "MD-based system preparation" Evidence pointer Methods section "MD-based system preparation" Issue The manuscript states that the pCT region was "manually extended using the PyMOL builder tool" and that this choice is "supported by AlphaFold3 predictions." However, no details are provided on how the AlphaFold3 prediction was used, or whether the manually built structure was compared to the AlphaFold3 prediction to ensure consistency. Required correction Provide a brief description of how the AlphaFold3 prediction was used to validate the manually built pCT structure, or state that the manual build was based on the AlphaFold3 prediction directly. Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Readability Affected element Figure 5 Evidence pointer Figure 5b, c, g–i Issue The electrophysiology data presentation is somewhat dense. The figure combines TEVC current measurements, NFX dose-response curves, and time courses in a single panel, which may be overwhelming for readers. Required correction Consider splitting the electrophysiology data into separate panels or sub-panels with clearer labels, and ensure that the statistical details (n numbers, error bars) are clearly visible and described in the legend. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1: Convergence of free-energy estimates not adequately demonstrated R1-M2: Causal link between simulated conformational shift and functional outcome not established R1-M3: Incomplete sampling of Y175 dynamics limits the generality of the proposed framework Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The application of OneOPES to a K2P channel system is novel and represents a methodological contribution. The concept of a shared energetic axis coupling lower helices, pCT, and SF is an interesting hypothesis. However, the underlying idea that these regions are coupled is not entirely new, and the manuscript builds substantially on the authors' prior work. Scientific importance: The manuscript addresses a significant question in ion channel biology: how polymodal regulation converges on a common gating mechanism. If the claims are fully substantiated, the work could have broad implications for understanding K2P channel regulation and disease mechanisms. However, the current evidence does not fully establish the framework. Interdisciplinary readership: The work bridges computational biophysics, electrophysiology, and structural biology. The findings would be of interest to researchers in all three communities, though the technical nature of the methods may limit accessibility to a broader audience. Technical soundness: The computational methodology is state-of-the-art, but convergence concerns and acknowledged sampling limitations weaken the quantitative claims. The electrophysiology is well-executed but the connection to the computational predictions is indirect. Readability for nonspecialists: The manuscript is generally well-written but assumes significant background knowledge in both MD simulation techniques and ion channel electrophysiology. The abstract is accessible, but the results and discussion sections may be challenging for readers outside these specialties. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved. The manuscript presents a potentially valuable framework and a novel methodological application, but the convergence of the free-energy calculations must be demonstrated more rigorously, and the link between simulated conformational preferences and functional outcomes needs to be strengthened or the claims appropriately tempered. The acknowledged limitations in Y175 sampling should be addressed more directly in the presentation of the framework's scope.

TangleDiff——一个基于预训练蛋白质语言模型（ESMFold 编码）和扩散 Transformer（DiT）的生成框架，通过条件生成具有指定链间结合能的纠缠同源二聚体序列，经虚拟筛选和实验验证，成功制备出应力松弛行为可调控的蛋白质水凝胶。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：如何从头设计具有可编程链间结合能的纠缠同源二聚体蛋白，并将其用作物理交联点来制备应力松弛行为可定制的水凝胶？ 为什么重要 ：蛋白质水凝胶作为人工细胞外基质（ECM）在 3D 干细胞/类器官培养中具有关键应用，其应力松弛行为直接影响细胞信号传导、黏附、增殖和分化。然而，天然纠缠蛋白基序种类有限（仅 p53dim、HP0242 等少数几个），严重限制了水凝胶粘弹性的可调范围。 现有方法不足 ： 天然纠缠基序数量少，结构多样性受限； 已有的从头设计纠缠蛋白方法依赖手工拓扑设计和精确几何控制，需要领域专家知识，难以规模化； 基于串联重复单元的设计策略将序列/结构限制在狭窄子空间，无法覆盖广泛的结合能范围。 精确的 Can 问题 ：Can a deep learning generative model learn the sequence determinants of protein entanglement and conditionally generate novel entangled homodimers with user-specified inter-chain binding energies, such that the resulting protein hydrogels exhibit predictable stress relaxation behaviors? 04 背景与发展脉络 注：此脉络为「经外部核验」+「仅本文框架」混合标注。 纠缠蛋白的天然发现与表征 （经外部核验）：p53 二聚化结构域（p53dim）和 HP0242 是已知的天然纠缠同源二聚体，其链间物理缠结赋予蛋白质独特的力学和组装性质。此前研究已用 GLN（Gauss Linking Number）量化纠缠程度。 纠缠蛋白的从头设计 （经外部核验）：早期工作通过串联重复天然基序或人工设计拓扑来构建纠缠蛋白，但受限于重复单元的序列空间，难以实现性质连续可调。 深度学习蛋白质生成 （经外部核验）：以 ProteinMPNN（逆折叠）、RFdiffusion（结构扩散）为代表的生成模型实现了蛋白质序列和结构的从头设计，但主要针对单体或复合物的折叠与结合，未专门处理「纠缠拓扑」这一特殊几何约束。 数据驱动的纠缠基序挖掘 （仅本文框架）：本文提出两阶段筛选策略，从 UniRef50 约 1270 万条代表序列中，通过 ESMFold 预测同源二聚体结构、GLN ≥ 0.7 判定纠缠、C2 对称性和 pLDDT ≥ 80 过滤，最终获得 79,890 条高质量纠缠序列——这是首个大规模纠缠蛋白序列数据集。 条件生成与性质调控 （仅本文框架）：TangleDiff 将结合能作为条件标签，通过 adaLN-Zero 模块注入扩散 Transformer，实现「按需生成」特定结合能范围的纠缠蛋白，将生成模型的输出与宏观材料性质直接挂钩。 本文主张的位置 ：位于「纠缠蛋白从头设计」与「深度学习条件生成」的交叉点，首次实现从序列生成到水凝胶宏观流变性质的全链条闭环。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 纠缠蛋白基序稀缺 天然已知纠缠基序仅 p53dim、HP0242 等少数几个，结构多样性受限 纠缠拓扑在进化中罕见，且实验表征困难 Introduction 第 2 段 从头设计纠缠拓扑困难 1) 表面方法 TangleDiff 是一个两阶段框架： - 数据阶段 ：从 UniRef50 大规模挖掘纠缠同源二聚体序列（ESMFold 预测 + GLN 判定 + C2 对称性 + pLDDT 过滤），构建训练集； - 生成阶段 ：用 ESM2-650M 将序列编码为 logits，在 logits 空间施加扩散过程；以 DiT 为骨干网络，通过 adaLN-Zero 注入条件（结合能分箱标签）；训练目标为最小化预测 logits 与真实 logits 的 MSE； - 筛选阶段 ：生成序列经 ESMFold/AlphaFold2 结构预测，按纠缠性、pLDDT、结合能、可溶性等多指标虚拟筛选； - 实验阶段 ：将筛选出的设计嵌入 SpyTag/SpyCatcher 水凝胶体系，通过流变学测试验证应力松弛行为。 2) 核心洞察 纠缠拓扑可被序列模型隐式学习 ：尽管纠缠是全局拓扑性质，但通过大规模数据训练，扩散模型能够隐式捕获纠缠所需的序列特征，无需显式几何建模； 结合能是连接分子设计与宏观性质的桥梁 ：将 Rosetta 计算的链间结合能作为条件变量，使得「分子层面的相互作用强度」直接映射到「宏观水凝胶的应力松弛速率」； logits 空间扩散优于序列空间扩散 ：在预训练语言模型的 logits 连续空间施加高斯扩散，比直接在离散序列空间扩散更易训练、生成质量更高（消融实验支持）。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] 「数据挖掘 → 条件生成 → 虚拟筛选 → 实验验证」是蛋白质设计的高效闭环范式 ，可迁移到其他功能蛋白设计（如酶、结合蛋白、自组装模块）； 宏观材料性质可通过分子层面的可计算量（如结合能）作为中间变量实现端到端调控 ，这一思路可推广到其他生物材料设计； 预训练语言模型 + 扩散模型的组合在蛋白质序列生成中具有通用优势 ，其 logits 空间提供了比 one-hot 序列更平滑的生成流形。 07 方法总览 输入 ：条件标签（结合能分箱，如 < −160、−160~−140、−140~−120、−120~−100、> −100 REU）、目标序列长度（40–50 aa 或从经验分布采样） 输出 ：纠缠同源二聚体蛋白序列（可直接合成表达） 模块 ： 1. 数据挖掘模块 ：UniRef50 两阶段筛选（ESMFold 同源二聚体预测 → GLN ≥ 0.7 → C2 对称 → pLDDT ≥ 80） 2. 编码模块 ：ESM2-650M 将序列 token 映射为 logits（冻结参数） 3. 扩散模块 ：DiT（Diffusion Transformer），含 adaLN-Zero 条件注入、自条件化（self-conditioning）、线性噪声调度 4. 解码模块 ：argmax 将 logits 映射回序列 5. 虚拟筛选模块 ：ESMFold/AlphaFold2 结构预测 → 纠缠判定（GLN ≥ 0.7）→ pLDDT > 70 → ProteinMPNN 序列-结构一致性评分 < 1.4906 → Rosetta 单链/复合物能量 → ProteinSol 可溶性 > 0.45 6. 实验验证模块 ：基因合成 → E. coli 表达 → SpyTag/SpyCatcher 交联 → 流变学测试 训练 ：Adam 优化器（β1=0.9, β2=0.999），学习率 1×10⁻⁴，全局 batch size 128，4×RTX3090，118,000 步（约 20 小时） 文字流程 ：从 UniRef50 挖掘纠缠序列 → 用 ESM2 编码为 结论正确解读 任务范围 ：本文解决的是「纠缠同源二聚体」的从头设计，而非所有纠缠拓扑（如三聚体、异源二聚体、更复杂链环）。结论仅适用于同源二聚体纠缠。 条件控制范围 ：结合能控制是在分箱级别（5 个离散区间）实现的，并非连续精确调控。约 70% 的生成序列落在指定区间，仍有 30% 偏差。 实验验证范围 ：9 个设计中 8 个二聚化、7 个成胶。样本量小，不能外推为普适成功率。C4_1771 的失败提示部分设计虽计算上合理但实验不折叠。 宏观性质关联 ：应力松弛行为与结合能相关，但弛豫时间与结合能之间未建立定量标度关系（仅有定性趋势：弱结合→快弛豫，强结合→慢/无弛豫）。 端到端状态 ：本文实现了「序列生成 → 结构验证 → 水凝胶制备 → 流变学表征」的完整链路，但未涉及细胞实验（如干细胞培养中的功能验证）。 有边界的复述 ：TangleDiff 能够以超过 70% 的计算机模拟成功率生成可折叠的纠缠同源二聚体序列，通过结合能条件控制可调节生成蛋白的链间相互作用强度，且该强度与水凝胶的应力松弛速率呈定性相关；在 9 个实验设计中，8 个有效二聚化、7 个成功成胶，验证了该方法的可行性。 12 作者自认局限 局限 具体表现 作者提出的未来方向 来源 生成序列的新颖性有限 与训练集最接近的序列同一性多为 0.4–0.6，高新颖性序列比例有限 technical validity, and claims as supported by the provided evidence Shared manuscript claim summary The authors present TangleDiff, a deep learning framework for de novo design of homodimeric entangled proteins with programmable inter-chain binding energies, and demonstrate that these designed proteins can form hydrogels with stress relaxation behavior correlated to the specified binding energies. Visible evidence base Abstract, full results section with figure legends (Figs. 1-6), methods section, discussion Missing materials affecting confidence Supplementary figures and tables referenced but not provided; actual figure images not available; experimental raw data not available; code not available for inspection Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript presents a potentially significant advance in the computational design of entangled protein motifs and their application to tunable biomaterials. The integration of a latent diffusion model with protein language model embeddings for the specific task of entangled homodimer design is novel, and the demonstration of a correlation between computationally specified binding energies and macroscopic hydrogel stress relaxation is conceptually appealing. However, the evidence provided in the manuscript text is insufficient to fully evaluate several key claims, particularly regarding the quantitative strength of the binding energy-stress relaxation correlation, the statistical significance of the reported success rates, and the robustness of the experimental validations. The manuscript would benefit from clearer presentation of quantitative results and additional controls. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in protein design and engineering, particularly those working on de novo protein structure prediction and generative models; biomaterials scientists developing hydrogels for tissue engineering and regenerative medicine; computational biologists interested in protein language models and diffusion-based generative approaches. The work bridges computational protein design with materials science, making it relevant to a broad interdisciplinary audience. Major strengths 1) The problem addressed is important and timely: expanding the limited toolbox of entangled protein motifs for biomaterial applications. 2) The computational pipeline is well-structured, combining data mining, generative modeling, and virtual screening in a logical workflow. 3) The demonstration of conditional generation based on binding energy is a valuable proof-of-concept for property-directed protein design. 4) The experimental validation, including hydrogel formation and rheological characterization, provides a meaningful end-to-end demonstration. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer "approximately 70% of successful designs conforming to expected values" and "in-silico success rate exceeding 70%" Evidence pointer Results section "Unconditional design of entangled homodimers", Fig. 3c Concern The reported success rates are presented as single percentages without confidence intervals, statistical comparisons to baselines, or clear definitions of what constitutes a "successful design" beyond the stated thresholds. The comparison to "current models (~1%)" is mentioned but the specific models, their configurations, and the evaluation protocol are not described in sufficient detail. Without a rigorous statistical framework and clear baseline comparisons, the claimed superiority of TangleDiff cannot be properly assessed. Why it matters The central claim of the manuscript is that TangleDiff substantially outperforms existing methods for entangled protein design. If this claim is not rigorously supported with appropriate statistical analysis and fair baseline comparisons, the significance of the work is substantially diminished. Resolution test Provide confidence intervals for success rates, describe the baseline models and their training/evaluation protocols in detail, and include statistical tests comparing TangleDiff to baselines. Clarify the exact definition of "success" used for each metric. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer "stress relaxation dynamics correlated with specified binding energies" and "manipulating the macroscopic properties of protein hydrogels can be achieved through the rational design of molecular-level interactions" Evidence pointer Results section "Rheological tests of 14 prepared protein hydrogel networks", Fig. 6 Concern The manuscript states that stress relaxation behavior correlates with binding energies, but the quantitative nature of this correlation is not presented. No correlation coefficients, statistical significance values, or quantitative comparisons between the different binding energy groups are provided in the text. The relaxation spectra are described qualitatively (e.g., "clear dissipation peak at ω ~ 0.3 rad/s"), but the relationship between the peak positions and the specified binding energies is not quantified. Furthermore, only two of the three binding energy groups (C4 and C2) show clear relaxation peaks, while the C0 group shows none, which is a limited demonstration of tunability. Why it matters The claim of customizable stress relaxation behavior is the key translational outcome of the work. Without quantitative evidence demonstrating a systematic relationship between binding energy and relaxation times across multiple designs, the claim of "customizable" behavior is not established. Resolution test Provide quantitative correlation analysis between binding energies and relaxation times (e.g., correlation coefficients with p-values), include data from all three binding energy groups, and demonstrate that the relationship is systematic and predictive rather than anecdotal. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "we experimentally validate TangleDiff by designing nine homodimers targeting various binding energies; seven successfully form hydrogels" Evidence pointer Results section "Experimental validation and preparation of entanglement-crosslinked protein hydrogels", Fig. 5 Concern The experimental validation is limited to nine designs, with seven forming hydrogels. The manuscript does not provide sufficient detail on the reproducibility of hydrogel formation, the yield of hydrogel formation across batches, or the criteria used to determine "successful" hydrogel formation. Additionally, the relationship between the computationally predicted binding energies and experimentally measured binding affinities is not directly validated. The manuscript relies on computational predictions (Rosetta, gmx_MMPBSA) without experimental binding measurements. Why it matters The translational claim depends on the reliability of the computational predictions. Without experimental validation of the binding energies themselves, it is unclear whether the observed rheological differences are truly due to the designed binding energy differences or to other uncontrolled factors. Resolution test Include experimental binding affinity measurements (e.g., ITC, SPR) for at least a subset of the designed proteins to validate the computational predictions. Provide more detailed characterization of hydrogel formation reproducibility and success criteria. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "TangleDiff generates diverse foldable entangled sequences" and "designs are evolutionarily distant" Evidence pointer Results section "Unconditional design of entangled homodimers", Fig. 3d-g Concern The diversity of generated sequences is assessed primarily through sequence identity comparisons to the training set. However, structural diversity is not quantitatively assessed beyond qualitative descriptions of alpha-dominant and beta-dominant topologies. The claim of novelty would be strengthened by a more systematic analysis of structural diversity, such as clustering by structural similarity or fold classification. Additionally, the functional annotations of the designed proteins (e.g., DNA-binding, RNA-binding) are inferred from structural similarity to known proteins, but this inference is not experimentally validated. Why it matters The claim of expanding the design space of entangled proteins depends on demonstrating that the generated proteins are not merely near-copies of training examples but genuinely novel and diverse. Without quantitative structural diversity analysis, this claim is not fully supported. Resolution test Include quantitative structural diversity metrics (e.g., TM-score distribution, fold classification, structural clustering) and compare the diversity of generated proteins to that of the training set and to existing design methods. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Methods section, Dataset construction Evidence pointer Methods section Issue The description of the two-stage screening strategy would benefit from a clearer explanation of the computational cost savings and the rationale for the specific thresholds chosen (e.g., sequence length 50-100, |GLN| ≥ 0.7, pLDDT ≥ 80). Required correction Provide a brief justification for the chosen thresholds and a more explicit comparison of the computational cost between the two stages. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Reproducibility Affected element Methods section, Model training Evidence pointer Methods section Issue The training details are described but some hyperparameters are missing (e.g., number of diffusion steps during training, noise schedule parameters, learning rate schedule, weight decay). Required correction Provide complete hyperparameter settings to ensure reproducibility. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Results section, Fig. 4 Evidence pointer Fig. 4b Concern The box plot in Fig. 4b shows the distribution of binding energies for generated proteins under different conditions, but the number of proteins per condition and the statistical significance of differences between conditions are not stated in the text. Required correction Add sample sizes and statistical comparisons to the figure legend or text. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected element Results section, Fig. 6 Evidence pointer Fig. 6 Concern The rheological data are presented for the hydrogels, but the manuscript does not report the concentration of the proteins in the hydrogels, the gelation kinetics, or the reproducibility of the rheological measurements across independent preparations. Required correction Provide details on hydrogel composition, gelation conditions, and variability across replicates. Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Discussion Evidence pointer Discussion section Concern The discussion mentions that TangleDiff can be extended to other properties and higher-order structures, but these claims are speculative without preliminary data or a clear roadmap. Required correction Either provide preliminary evidence for these extensions or clearly frame them as future directions. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established 1) Lack of quantitative statistical analysis for the claimed success rates and the binding energy-stress relaxation correlation (R1-M1, R1-M2). 2) Absence of experimental validation of computationally predicted binding energies (R1-M3). 3) Insufficient quantitative analysis of structural diversity of generated proteins (R1-M4). Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The application of latent diffusion models to entangled protein design is novel and represents a creative integration of existing techniques. The concept of conditioning on binding energy for downstream materials properties is original. Scientific importance: The work addresses a real bottleneck in protein-based biomaterials and could have significant impact if the claims are fully substantiated. The potential to rationally design hydrogels with predictable mechanical properties is important for tissue engineering. Interdisciplinary readership: The work bridges computational biology, protein engineering, and materials science, making it of interest to multiple communities. The writing is generally accessible, though some sections assume familiarity with protein design terminology. Technical soundness: The computational pipeline is well-conceived, but the evidence presented is insufficient to fully evaluate technical soundness. Key quantitative results are missing, and the experimental validation is limited in scope. Readability for nonspecialists: The abstract and introduction are accessible, but the results section becomes technical. The figures are well-designed based on the legends, but the lack of quantitative details in the text makes it difficult for nonspecialists to assess the strength of the claims. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved. The core concept is promising and the work addresses an important problem, but the current evidence is insufficient to fully establish the central claims. The manuscript requires additional quantitative analysis, experimental validation of binding energies, and more rigorous statistical treatment before the case is fully established. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that TangleDiff's in-silico success rate "exceeding 70%" substantially surpasses current models is not fully supported without detailed baseline comparisons and statistical analysis. The claim that stress relaxation dynamics are "correlated with specified binding energies" is not quantitatively supported with correlation coefficients or significance tests. The claim that the designed proteins are "novel" and "evolutionarily distant" is based on sequence identity alone, without comprehensive structural novelty analysis. The inference of protein function (e.g., DNA-binding, RNA-binding) from structural similarity is not experimentally validated. The claim that the observed rheological differences are specifically due to designed binding energy differences is not fully established, as other structural factors may contribute. The generalizability of the approach to other properties beyond binding energy is speculative and not demonstrated.

Review setup Input scope Abstract only Assessment boundary Claims and evidence presented in the abstract; no access to methods, figures, tables, or supplementary materials Shared manuscript claim summary The authors introduce Pinal, a 16-billion-parameter foundation model trained on 1.7 billion synthetically annotated protein-text pairs, which generates candidate proteins from natural-language descriptions of desired function. Computational evaluations report high predicted foldability, functional-description alignment, and sequence diversity. Experimental validation across four tasks (fluorescent protein, PET hydrolase, alcohol dehydrogenase, metabolic H-protein) reportedly shows intended function in each case, including catalytic activity for both designed enzymes. A Pinal-designed H-protein increased product titre by 1.7-fold relative to native E. coli H-protein in a multi-enzyme CO2 fixation pathway without iterative experimental optimization. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no figures, tables, methods, or supplementary data provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full methods, model architecture details, training data construction, computational evaluation protocols, experimental procedures, raw data, statistical analyses, sequence and structure outputs, and all figures and tables Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially significant advance in protein design, positioning natural language as a high-level interface for functional protein generation. The scale of the model and the breadth of experimental validation across four distinct tasks are notable. However, the abstract alone provides insufficient detail to assess the technical soundness of the approach, the rigor of the computational evaluations, or the robustness of the experimental claims. The central claim that natural language enables programmable protein design with reduced reliance on structural or sequence constraints requires substantially more evidence than is visible here. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in protein engineering, computational biology, and synthetic biology would be interested in a model that generates functional proteins from text descriptions, potentially lowering the barrier to protein design. The broader machine learning community may also find interest in the scale and training paradigm of the model. Biotechnologists working on enzyme engineering and metabolic pathway optimization would be interested in the demonstrated catalytic activities and the H-protein titre improvement. Major strengths The model scale (16 billion parameters) and training data volume (1.7 billion pairs) suggest a substantial technical undertaking. The experimental validation across four distinct functional classes, including two enzymes with catalytic activity, is a strong point if the evidence is robust. The reported 1.7-fold titre improvement in a metabolic pathway context without iterative optimization is a practically meaningful outcome. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The model "designs candidate proteins from natural-language descriptions of desired function" and "links functional intent to protein sequence and structure." Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The abstract does not describe how natural-language descriptions are converted into functional design objectives, how the model represents and generates protein structure, or how the synthetic annotations were constructed. Without this information, the mechanism by which the model achieves functional design is unverifiable. Why it matters The core novelty of the work rests on the claim that natural language serves as a sufficient interface for functional protein design. If the model actually relies on implicit structural or sequence constraints embedded in the training data or generation process, the claim of reduced reliance on manual constraints would be overstated. Resolution test Provide a clear description of the model architecture, the input-output mapping, the training objective, and the annotation generation pipeline. Show examples of input text and corresponding output sequences and structures. Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The abstract reports computational metrics without defining them. Why it matters Without defined metrics and comparators, the reader cannot judge whether the computational performance is actually strong or merely adequate. The claim that candidates provide "a basis for prioritizing experimentally testable designs" depends on these metrics being meaningful and validated. Include distributions and statistical analyses. How many designs were tested, and what was the success rate? Were negative controls included? Why it matters The claim of broad experimental success is central to the paper's significance. Without quantitative data, success rates, and controls, the reader cannot assess whether the results are robust or whether they reflect cherry-picking or weak functional criteria.
