The claim that this improvement demonstrates the utility of the design approach depends on the statistical robustness of the measurement. 01 基本信息 标题 : The evolutionary processes of bacterial aromatic polyketide ketosynthases 作者 : Wang, Xiaoyu; Gao, Qiandi; Ge, Liangjun; Qin, Zhiwei 单位 : 未提供（致谢提及北京师范大学跨学科智能超级计算中心） 期刊/平台 : Genome Biology 年份 : 2026-10-22（在线发表） 论文类型 : 研究论文（Research Article） 领域 : 计算进化生物学 × 蛋白质语言模型 × 聚酮合酶（PKS）进化 关键词 : Type II polyketides (T2PKs); Ketosynthase (KS); Chain length factor (CLF); Protein language model (PLM); ESM-2; MAAPE; Horizontal gene transfer (HGT); Coevolution DOI/arXiv : 10.1186/s13059-026-04215-7 代码 : 未提供 数据 : 166对KS-CLF序列及对应产物结构（补充表S1-S9） 阅读日期 : 2026-05-12 在课题方向中的位置 : 本文属于「蛋白质结构相关计算研究 × AI方法」交叉方向，具体为利用蛋白质语言模型（ESM-2）嵌入表征来推断蛋白质进化关系，而非直接预测结构。其核心方法MAAPE（Modular Assembly Analysis of Protein Embeddings）将PLM嵌入与KNN网络、方向性图分析结合，用于重建KS/CLF的进化轨迹，并识别水平基因转移（HGT）与共进化信号。该工作为结构预测/构象采样之外的「序列-进化-功能」关系研究提供了新范式，其方法学可迁移至其他蛋白质家族的进化分析。 02 一句话总结 本文利用基于ESM-2蛋白质语言模型嵌入的MAAPE算法，对166对细菌芳香族聚酮合酶KS/CLF序列进行进化轨迹重建，发现二者存在共同祖先簇（Cluster A），并揭示非氧化型T2PKs的CLF通过水平基因转移获得KS样功能，支持KS/CLF共起源后分化、共进化的假说。 03 研究问题 具体问题 : 细菌II型聚酮合酶（T2PKS）中，酮合酶（KS/KSα）与链长因子（CLF/KSβ）的进化关系如何？它们是否源自共同祖先？进化过程中经历了怎样的分化、共进化和水平基因转移事件？ 为什么重要 : T2PKS负责合成大量具有药用和工业价值的芳香族聚酮化合物，其链长控制机制由KS/CLF异源二聚体决定。理解KS/CLF的进化历史有助于揭示天然产物多样性的产生机制，并为理性设计新型聚酮合酶提供进化指导。 现有方法为何不足 : 传统系统发育分析（基于多序列比对）在KS/CLF序列一致性低于30%的情况下难以解析深层进化关系，且无法捕捉结构保守但序列高度分化的同源蛋白之间的进化信号。已有进化假说（共同祖先→基因复制→功能分化）缺乏严格验证。 精确研究问题 : Can protein language model embeddings, analyzed via the MAAPE algorithm, reveal the evolutionary trajectories and ancestral relationships of structurally homologous but sequence-divergent KS and CLF domains? methodological soundness, evidence quality, and alignment with stated conclusions Shared manuscript claim summary The authors use a protein language model-based algorithm (MAAPE) to infer evolutionary relationships between bacterial aromatic polyketide ketosynthases (KS) and chain length factors (CLF), proposing a common ancestral cluster (Cluster A), distinct evolutionary trajectories, coevolution, and horizontal gene transfer as major drivers of diversification. Visible evidence base Main text figures (Fig. 1a-c, Fig. 2a-e, Fig. 3a-b, Fig. 4a-b), supplementary tables S1-S9, supplementary figures S1-S3, methods descriptions Missing materials affecting confidence Supplementary files (Tables S1-S9, Figs. S1-S3) were not provided for inspection; raw data, code, and MAAPE algorithm implementation details are not accessible; statistical validation metrics for clustering and network analyses are not fully described Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript presents a novel application of protein language model embeddings to study the evolution of type II polyketide synthases, a topic of considerable interest in natural product biosynthesis. The central claim of a common ancestral cluster and subsequent functional divergence is plausible and consistent with prior hypotheses, but the evidence provided in the main text is largely descriptive and lacks rigorous statistical validation. The MAAPE algorithm is not described in sufficient detail to assess its reliability, and the absence of supplementary data prevents verification of key results. The biological interpretations, while reasonable, are often speculative and not directly supported by the presented analyses. The manuscript has potential but requires substantial strengthening of the analytical framework and evidence base before the conclusions can be considered established. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in natural product biosynthesis, enzymology, and evolutionary biology would find this work relevant. The application of protein language models to evolutionary inference is a growing area, and the specific focus on type II polyketide synthases connects to efforts in genome mining and rational engineering of polyketide pathways. The proposed coevolution and HGT hypotheses could inform experimental design for pathway engineering, making the work of interest to both fundamental and applied microbiologists. Major strengths 1. The use of a protein language model (ESM-2) to capture evolutionary signals beyond traditional sequence alignment is a timely and potentially powerful approach. 2. The identification of a mixed KS-CLF cluster (Cluster A) as a putative ancestral group is an interesting observation that challenges purely sequence-based phylogenies. 3. The integration of functional prediction (DeepFRI) with embedding-based clustering provides a multi-layered perspective on protein evolution. 4. The manuscript is clearly written and the figures are visually informative, aiding comprehension of complex network analyses. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The MAAPE algorithm reliably reconstructs evolutionary trajectories and identifies ancestral states from protein embeddings. Evidence pointer Methods section "MAAPE analysis", Fig. 2a-c Concern The MAAPE algorithm is described only at a conceptual level. The sliding window approach, co-occurrence matrix construction, and directionality assignment are not specified with enough detail to evaluate their validity or reproducibility. No benchmarks, simulations, or comparisons against known evolutionary scenarios are provided to demonstrate that the method accurately recovers true evolutionary relationships. The absence of statistical measures (e.g., bootstrap support, confidence intervals) for the inferred network topology is a critical gap. Why it matters The central conclusions of the paper rest entirely on the reliability of MAAPE. Without validation, the inferred ancestral cluster and evolutionary trajectories could be artifacts of the embedding space or the algorithm's parameters. Readers cannot assess whether the method distinguishes genuine phylogenetic signal from noise. Resolution test Provide a detailed algorithmic description, release code, and validate MAAPE on simulated datasets with known evolutionary histories or on empirical datasets with well-established phylogenies. Include statistical support values for the network edges and cluster assignments. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence quality Claim pointer Cluster A represents a shared ancestral group for KS and CLF sequences, supporting a common origin. Evidence pointer Fig. 1b, Fig. 2a, Additional file 1: Table S2 Concern The designation of Cluster A as ancestral is based on its mixed composition and the presence of the FABF outgroup. However, the criteria for defining "ancestral" are not explicitly stated. The cluster contains only 22 of 166 pairs, and the authors acknowledge potential biases in their product-focused dataset. The possibility that Cluster A reflects convergent sequence features or artifacts of the embedding reduction is not excluded. The claim of common ancestry requires independent support, such as phylogenetic analysis of the cluster members or structural evidence. Why it matters The common origin hypothesis is a key conclusion and a foundation for subsequent interpretations of coevolution and HGT. If Cluster A is not truly ancestral, the evolutionary narrative collapses. Resolution test Perform a rigorous phylogenetic analysis of Cluster A members using multiple methods and models. Test whether the cluster is robust to dataset composition (e.g., including non-product-associated sequences). Provide explicit criteria for ancestral state inference and rule out alternative explanations such as convergence or long-branch attraction. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer Coevolution between KS and CLF pairs is demonstrated by the ratio of distances to the ancestral node being close to 1. Evidence pointer Fig. 2d, Additional file 1: Table S9 Concern The distance ratio analysis is presented as evidence of coevolution, but the statistical framework is unclear. The mean ratio of 1.0082 is reported without a measure of variance, a null model, or a test of significance. The six outlier pairs are identified but not analyzed in detail. The choice of the ancestral node as the centroid of Cluster A embeddings is arbitrary and may bias the results. Coevolution is a strong claim that requires more direct evidence, such as correlated mutation analysis or functional assays. Why it matters Coevolution is a central biological interpretation. If the distance ratio is not a valid proxy, the claim is unsupported. Overinterpretation of a descriptive metric as evidence of coevolution could mislead readers. Resolution test Provide a statistical test comparing the observed distance ratios to a null distribution (e.g., randomized pairings). Report confidence intervals and effect sizes. Use complementary methods (e.g., coevolutionary analysis of residue contacts) to corroborate the finding. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence quality Claim pointer Horizontal gene transfer is a main driving force of KS/CLF polymorphism. Evidence pointer Fig. 4a-b, Discussion section Concern The inference of HGT is based on network edge weights and directionality, but no direct evidence of HGT (e.g., phylogenetic incongruence, GC content analysis, or taxonomic distribution) is presented. The interpretation of high-weight edges as HGT events is speculative. The authors do not account for alternative explanations such as gene duplication, loss, or convergent evolution. The claim that HGT is a "main" driving force is not quantitatively supported. Why it matters HGT is a major evolutionary mechanism, and attributing KS/CLF diversity to it has implications for understanding pathway evolution. An unsupported claim could lead to incorrect conclusions about the mobility and distribution of these biosynthetic genes. Resolution test Conduct explicit HGT detection analyses (e.g., phylogenetic reconciliation, sequence composition bias tests). Quantify the contribution of HGT relative to other mechanisms. Provide species-level context to support the HGT interpretation. Concern ID R1-M5 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Reproducibility Claim pointer The dataset of 166 KS-CLF pairs is comprehensive and curated. Evidence pointer Methods section "Data collection and phylogenetic analysis", Additional file 1: Table S1 Concern The curation criteria are described briefly, but the source databases, search terms, and filtering steps are not fully specified. The exclusion of sequences with >90% identity is mentioned, but the impact of this threshold on diversity and representation is not discussed. The supplementary table containing the dataset was not available for review. Why it matters Reproducibility is a core requirement. Without a complete description of data acquisition and processing, other researchers cannot replicate the study or assess potential biases. Resolution test Provide a detailed data curation protocol, including database versions, accession numbers, and filtering criteria. Make the full dataset publicly available in a standard format. The reader cannot assess the variability of the ratios. Required correction Add error bars or a confidence band to the plot and report the standard deviation or interquartile range in the text. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected element Methods section "Functional prediction" Evidence pointer Methods section "Functional prediction" Issue The DeepFRI analysis is described, but the specific GO terms used for the vectorization are not listed. A similarity of 0.5 is mentioned as "comparable," but the scale is not defined. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that Cluster A represents a shared ancestral group is not statistically validated and may be influenced by dataset composition. The inference of coevolution from distance ratios lacks a formal statistical framework and alternative explanations are not excluded. The assertion that HGT is a main driving force of KS/CLF polymorphism is speculative and not supported by direct HGT detection analyses. The functional convergence between nonoxidative CLFs and KSs is inferred from similarity scores without experimental validation. The general statement that PLM embeddings capture evolutionary information beyond sequence alignment is plausible but not rigorously demonstrated in this study. The biological interpretations regarding selective pressures (chemical competition, ecological niches, metabolic trade-offs) are presented as conclusions but are not directly tested.

：结构预测器的 distogram 输出不仅是几何预测，还隐式编码了能量学信息——因为预测器必须「理解」哪些残基对倾向于靠近/远离，才能做出准确预测。 洞察二 ：以模型自身的末端状态为参考（而非外部参考态），可以消除模型偏差，使提取的势能具有自洽性。 洞察三 ：构象判别（区分天然态 vs 非天然态）与突变效应预测（序列变化对稳定性的影响）是结构表征的两个不同属性，DEEP Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially interesting framework for extracting energetic information from protein structure predictors without training on experimental stability data. The reported performance metrics are striking, particularly the claim of outperforming all 97 published zero-shot methods while matching supervised predictors. However, the abstract alone provides insufficient detail to evaluate the methodological soundness, the statistical rigor of the comparisons, or the validity of the interpretational claims. The distinction drawn between conformational discrimination and mutation-effect prediction is conceptually interesting but requires substantially more evidence than the abstract can provide. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in protein biophysics, computational protein design, and protein engineering would be interested in a method that extracts energetic information from structure predictors without additional training. The zero-shot stability prediction capability has direct applications in variant effect prediction, protein design, and understanding mutational landscapes. The comparative analysis between Boltz-2 and AlphaFold2 also addresses questions about what different structure predictors learn internally, which is relevant to the machine learning for biology community. Major strengths The framework concept is elegant, using the model's own terminal distance state as an internal reference to avoid training on experimental data. The reported benchmark coverage is broad, spanning 64 stability assays and over 180,000 decoys. The comparative analysis between two major predictors (Boltz-2 and AlphaFold2) provides a useful scientific contribution by demonstrating that conformational discrimination and energetic sensitivity are separable properties. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "DEEP-Boltz achieves a mean per-assay Spearman correlation of 0.720 across 64 ProteinGym stability assays, numerically outperforming all 97 published zero-shot methods in the matched comparison on level with the best performing predictors trained directly on experimental stability measurements" Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Concern The abstract reports a single mean Spearman correlation aggregated across 64 assays, but provides no information on the distribution of correlations, the statistical significance of the comparison against the 97 zero-shot methods, or the criteria used for the "matched comparison." Without knowing whether the comparison was performed on identical assay subsets, identical mutation sets, and with identical preprocessing, the claim of outperforming all 97 methods cannot be evaluated. The phrase "on level with the best performing predictors trained directly on experimental stability measurements" is ambiguous regarding whether this is a statistical equivalence claim or a numerical proximity claim. Why it matters The central claim of the paper rests on this benchmark comparison. If the comparison is not properly matched, or if the variance across assays is high, the headline number of 0.720 may not represent a robust improvement. The distinction between "numerically outperforming" and "statistically significantly outperforming" is critical for assessing whether this method genuinely advances the state of the art. Resolution test Provide per-assay correlation values, confidence intervals, and a clear description of the matched comparison protocol. Specify which assays were included, whether the same mutation subsets were used for all methods, and whether any assays were excluded and why. Report statistical tests comparing DEEP-Boltz against the best-performing zero-shot and supervised methods. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "DEEP (Distogram Encoded Energetic Potential), a general framework that extracts effective statistical potentials directly from predicted residue-pair distance distributions, using the models own terminal distance state as an internal reference without training on experimental stability data" Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Concern The methodological description is too brief to assess the validity of the approach. The concept of using the model's "terminal distance state as an internal reference" is not defined. It is unclear how the statistical potential is derived from distance distributions, how the reference state is constructed, what functional form the potential takes, and how it is applied to compute stability changes for single mutations. Without this information, the framework cannot be evaluated for internal consistency or compared to existing statistical potential approaches. Why it matters The novelty of the paper depends on the methodological contribution. If the potential extraction procedure has hidden dependencies on training data or if the reference state construction introduces biases, the claim of extracting "accessible energetic information" without experimental training data would be weakened. The method must be described in sufficient detail for replication. Resolution test Provide a complete mathematical description of the potential extraction procedure, including the definition of the reference state, the transformation from distance distributions to energies, and the aggregation across residue pairs. Include a schematic or pseudocode. Clarify what "terminal distance state" means operationally. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "DEEP-Boltz accurately distinguishes native-like from non-native conformations across more than 180,000 Rosetta decoys" Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Concern The abstract reports accurate discrimination of native-like from non-native conformations across 180,000 decoys but provides no quantitative metric. "Accurately" is undefined. It is unclear whether this is a classification task, a ranking task, or a threshold-based discrimination. The choice of decoy set, the definition of "native-like," and the baseline comparators are not specified. Without these details, the claim cannot be evaluated. Why it matters This result is presented as evidence that DEEP captures conformational preferences beyond mutation effects. If the discrimination accuracy is modest or if the decoy set is biased, the conclusion that structure predictors encode accessible energetic information about conformational preferences would be weakened. Resolution test Report the discrimination metric (e.g., AUC, enrichment factor, or correlation with RMSD to native), the decoy generation protocol, the definition of native-like, and comparisons to existing scoring functions or energy functions on the same decoy sets. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Interpretational validity Claim pointer "Applying DEEP to AlphaFold2 reveals nearly identical conformational discrimination but substantially weaker mutation-effect prediction, demonstrating that recognizing favorable conformations and capturing their energetic sensitivity to sequence changes are distinct properties of learned structural representations" Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Concern The abstract interprets the differential performance between Boltz-2 and AlphaFold2 as evidence for distinct properties of learned representations. However, alternative explanations are plausible. The difference could arise from architectural differences, training data differences, or differences in the distance distribution granularity between the two models. The claim that this demonstrates distinct properties of learned representations is a strong interpretational leap that requires controlled comparisons. Why it matters This is a conceptual claim about what protein structure predictors learn internally. If the difference is attributable to technical factors rather than fundamental representational differences, the scientific contribution of this finding would be substantially reduced. Resolution test Provide controlled comparisons that rule out technical explanations, such as matching architecture components, training data, or output granularity. Discuss alternative explanations and provide evidence that the observed difference reflects fundamental representational properties. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Abstract, first sentence Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Issue The phrase "the extent to which their internal representations capture the energetic principles governing protein stability and conformational preferences remains unclear" is vague. It is not specified what "energetic principles" means in this context or how "capture" would be operationalized. Required correction Define "energetic principles" and "capture" more precisely, or rephrase to state the specific question being addressed. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Abstract, methods description Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Issue The term "effective statistical potentials" is used without definition. It is unclear how these differ from standard statistical potentials used in protein structure modeling. Required correction Briefly define what makes these potentials "effective" and how they differ from existing statistical potentials. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Reproducibility Affected element Abstract, code availability Evidence pointer Footnotes, GitHub link provided Issue The GitHub repository is mentioned but its contents, documentation, and license are not described. Required correction State the repository contents, provide documentation details, and specify the license in the abstract or methods. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected element Abstract, benchmark description Evidence pointer Abstract, location not provided Issue The abstract mentions "64 ProteinGym stability assays" but does not specify which assays or the diversity of proteins covered. Required correction Briefly describe the assay composition or refer to a table listing the assays. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1 (benchmark comparison validity), R1-M2 (methodological description completeness), R1-M3 (decoy discrimination metric missing), R1-M4 (interpretational claim requires controlled comparisons) Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The concept of extracting energetic information from structure predictors without experimental training data is novel and potentially significant. However, the abstract does not provide enough detail to assess whether the methodological approach is genuinely new or an incremental adaptation of existing statistical potential methods. Scientific importance: If the claims hold, the method would be valuable for zero-shot variant effect prediction and for understanding what structure predictors learn. The comparative analysis between Boltz-2 and AlphaFold2 addresses a question of growing interest. However, the importance depends on the robustness of the benchmark results. Interdisciplinary readership: The topic bridges machine learning, structural biology, and biophysics. The abstract is written in a way that is accessible to a broad audience, though some terms require domain knowledge. Technical soundness: Cannot be assessed from the abstract alone. The missing methodological details and benchmark validation are critical gaps. Readability for nonspecialists: The abstract is generally clear, but terms such as "effective statistical potentials," "terminal distance state," and "distogram encoded" may be opaque to readers outside the immediate field. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The abstract presents promising results, but the absence of methodological detail, benchmark validation, and statistical rigor prevents assessment of whether the claims are supported. A full manuscript review is required to evaluate the technical soundness and validity of the conclusions. Risk / unsupported claims The claim of outperforming all 97 published zero-shot methods cannot be evaluated without details of the matched comparison protocol and statistical significance testing. The claim that DEEP-Boltz matches the best supervised predictors is ambiguous and unsupported without statistical equivalence testing. The claim of "accurately" distinguishing native-like from non-native conformations is unsupported without a defined metric and baseline comparison. The interpretational claim that conformational discrimination and mutation-effect prediction are distinct properties of learned representations is unsupported without controlled comparisons ruling out technical explanations. The claim that structure predictors "encode accessible energetic information" is a strong statement that requires more evidence than the abstract provides.

：表位/互补位映射是治疗性抗体工程的核心环节。现有最准确方法（如 docking、AlphaFold 复合物预测）依赖三维结构，计算成本高且对孤儿抗原（无同源结构）不适用。序列-only 方法可大幅降低门槛，实现高通量筛选。 现有方法为何不足 ：多数序列-based 方法或依赖同源建模（隐含结构信息），或在评估中存在泄漏（如随机划分而非序列聚类划分），导致泛化性能被高估。此外，现有方法很少利用功能实验数据（如竞争性阻断）作为监督信号。 精确研究问题 ：Can a frozen ESM2 feature extractor paired with a lightweight trainable module predict HER2 epitopes and VHH paratopes from sequences alone, under a leakage-safe evaluation protocol, and can a structure-derived residue prior improve epitope prediction on a specific antigen (HER2)? 04 背景与发展脉络 no full text, figures, tables, or supplementary materials were provided Shared manuscript claim summary The authors propose a sequence-only deep learning pipeline for predicting HER2 epitopes and VHH nanobody paratopes, using a frozen ESM2 650M model as a feature extractor and a lightweight trainable module with cross-attention. Training uses three public data sources, including a competition assay dataset ("AVIDa hHER2") that is not yet public. A structure-derived residue prior is introduced for HER2-specific epitope prediction. The authors report high performance on binder classification (PR AUC 0.999) and moderate paratope prediction (PR AUC 0.659), while acknowledging near-baseline performance for epitope prediction on novel antigens (PR AUC 0.070). A leakage-safe evaluation protocol is emphasized. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no figures, tables, code, or dataset documentation provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, dataset access details, model architecture specifics, hyperparameters, training/validation split details, and the "AVIDa hHER2" dataset itself (not yet public) Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a technically plausible approach to a challenging problem in antibody engineering, with a commendable emphasis on leakage-safe evaluation. However, the evidence base is limited to the abstract, and several claims cannot be verified without the full manuscript. The reported performance numbers are inconsistent in their implications, and the near-baseline epitope prediction result, while honestly reported, raises questions about the practical utility of the method. The reliance on a not-yet-public dataset for a central training signal is a significant concern for reproducibility. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers and practitioners in therapeutic antibody engineering, computational immunology, and protein language model applications. The focus on HER2, a clinically relevant target, and the sequence-only formulation would appeal to those seeking to avoid costly structure prediction steps. The leakage-safe evaluation protocol would interest methodologists in the field. Major strengths The explicit commitment to leakage-safe evaluation with a sealed test set opened once is a notable strength. The honest reporting of a near-baseline result for novel antigen epitope prediction is commendable. The use of a frozen protein language model as a feature extractor with a lightweight trainable head is a sensible design choice for computational efficiency. Major Concerns The central training dataset is not public, undermining reproducibility. The performance numbers are difficult to interpret without context, and the relationship between the competition-derived domain signal and the residue-level predictions is unclear. The abstract does not provide sufficient detail on the cross-attention mechanism or the residue prior construction to assess technical soundness. Minor Comments The abstract is dense and would benefit from clearer separation of the different prediction tasks. The claim of "leakage free" for the 87.7% domain recovery result needs more precise definition. The release of "two submission variants" per test clone is mentioned but not explained in terms of how they are reconciled. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established The unavailability of the "AVIDa hHER2" dataset is a primary technical failing for reproducibility. The lack of detail on the residue prior and its validation is a secondary concern. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: Moderate. The combination of a frozen ESM2 with a structure-derived prior is not entirely novel, but the specific application to VHH nanobodies on HER2 with a leakage-safe protocol has some originality. Scientific importance: Moderate. The problem is important, but the near-baseline epitope result limits the immediate impact. Interdisciplinary readership: Limited. The abstract is highly specialized and would not attract a broad readership. Technical soundness: Not fully assessable from the abstract; the evaluation protocol is a strength, but the dataset issue is a weakness. Readability for nonspecialists: Poor. The abstract is dense and assumes significant background knowledge. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The abstract shows promise, but the dataset availability issue and the lack of methodological detail prevent a supportive recommendation. 等结构预测方法不同，本文不预测结构本身，而是利用结构注释来解释变异效应异质性，属于「结构注释驱动的统计推断」类别。其方法可迁移至蛋白质结构预测模型的评估、构象相关变异效应建模等场景。 02 一句话总结 本文提出 Kernel Allelic Series Model (KASM)，利用核回归框架将 35 种蛋白质结构与功能注释整合进稀有编码变异的效应协方差建模，在 UK Biobank 和 All of Us 共 786,871 例外显子组、26 个性状中，将稀有错义变异遗传力下界从 0.54% 提升至 1.27–1.83%，并识别出 PIEZO1 等基因中特定结构位点（如亚基间氢键残基）的显著功能富集。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：稀有错义变异对复杂性状的遗传贡献（heritability）有多大？这些贡献在蛋白质结构/功能空间中如何分布？哪些结构特征能解释变异效应的异质性？ 为什么重要 ：稀有编码变异是基因发现的主要驱动之一，但单个变异频率极低，效应估计噪声大，必须聚合分析。然而，简单聚合（burden test）假设所有变异效应相同，忽略了效应异质性，导致统计功效损失和遗传力低估。理解变异效应的功能架构（functional architecture）有助于改进基因发现、揭示疾病机制、指导功能实验设计。 现有方法不足 ： Burden test 假设变异效应完全相关（完美相关），忽略异质性； 方差分量模型（如 BHR）虽允许异质性，但仅使用简单的功能类别（如错义 vs. 同义），未利用精细的蛋白质结构信息； 现有方法无法回答「哪些结构特征最能解释变异效应差异」这一功能架构问题。 精确研究问题 ：Can a kernel-based model integrating protein structural and functional annotations recover a substantially larger fraction of rare missense heritability than burden-based approaches, and can it identify specific structural contexts (e.g., inter-subunit hydrogen bonds) 分数）完全相关； Cross-burden 核 ：允许两个不同权重向量（如 AlphaMissense 与 PolyPhen-2）之间的协方差； Identity 核 ：允许变异效应独立（不相关）； Position 核 ：编码变异对之间的空间邻近性（1D 或 3D）。 模型通过 Haseman-Elston 回归拟合，输入为 GWAS 摘要统计和 LD 矩阵，输出为各核的方差分量、遗传力、富集估计。 2) 核心洞察 变异效应的协方差结构可以由蛋白质结构/功能注释预测。 具体而言： 功能相似的变异（如位于同一结构域、同一界面、具有相似理化性质的替换）倾向于有相似的效应大小和方向； 这种相似性可以通过核函数量化，且核的权重可以从数据中学习； 通过比较不同核的解释力，可以识别哪些结构特征最能预测变异效应——这本身就是对蛋白质功能架构的定量描述。 关键创新 ：KASM 不是简单地将注释作为协变量，而是将注释转化为效应协方差核，从而在统计上自然地处理「部分相关」的变异效应。这比 burden test（完全相关）和独立效应模型（完全不相关）都更灵活。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] 核方法是将领域知识注入统计模型的通用框架 ：任何能定义「相似性」的注释（结构、进化、功能）都可以通过核函数整合进遗传力分解。这为蛋白质结构预测模型（如 AlphaFold）的输出在统计遗传学中的使用提供了模板。 「下界」思维 ：KASM 估计的是遗传力下界（kernel heritability），而非总遗传力。这种保守估计在存在未建模异质性时更稳健，但也意味着结果解读需谨慎。 功能富集分析可从「变异中心」转向「结构中心」 ：传统富集分析关注变异是否落在某注释内；KASM 关注的是注释能否解释变异效应的协方差——这是更强的功能证据。 07 Review setup Input scope Full manuscript text, including abstract, main text, methods, figure legends, and supplementary table descriptions. Assessment boundary Scientific validity, methodological soundness, clarity of claims, and alignment with the stated evidence. No assessment of editorial fit or publication policy. Shared manuscript claim summary The authors introduce the Kernel Allelic Series Model (KASM), a statistical framework that integrates multiple functional annotations to model the covariance of rare variant effects within genes. Applied to exome-wide association data from 786,871 individuals across 26 traits, KASM estimates that rare missense heritability is at least 1.27±0.09% on average, and 1.83±0.11% under a flexible model, exceeding pLoF heritability. The model identifies enriched structural features, quantifies effect concordance among proximal variants, and nominates gene-specific functional hypotheses. Visible evidence base Abstract, full methods section, results narrative, figure legends, and supplementary table titles. No actual figures, tables, or numerical results are provided in the submitted material. Missing materials affecting confidence All figures, tables, and supplementary data files are absent. The manuscript text references specific numerical results (e.g., enrichment values, P values) without the underlying data being visible. Simulation details are described but not shown. This substantially limits the ability to verify the central claims. Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript presents a conceptually interesting and technically ambitious framework for integrating functional annotations into rare variant heritability estimation. The methodological development appears thoughtful, with careful attention to estimand definition, confounding control, and estimator properties. However, the absence of all figures, tables, and numerical results makes it impossible to evaluate whether the claims are supported by the evidence. The text alone cannot establish the validity of the central estimates or the robustness of the findings. The manuscript would benefit from a clearer presentation of the relationship between the proposed kernel heritability and existing estimands, and from a more explicit discussion of the assumptions required for causal interpretation. Who would be interested in the results, and why Statistical geneticists developing methods for rare variant analysis, researchers studying the genetic architecture of complex traits, and investigators using functional annotations to prioritize variants in exome sequencing studies. The framework could also interest those working on heritability estimation from biobank-scale data, and those interested in the relative contribution of missense versus loss-of-function variation to complex trait heritability. Major strengths The methodological framework is well-motivated and addresses a real gap in the literature, namely the limited integration of functional annotations into heritability estimation for rare variants. The distinction between kernel heritability and burden heritability is clearly articulated. The use of both random-effects and fixed-effects estimators, with a clear rationale for their respective roles, is a thoughtful design choice. The attention to confounding, particularly the inclusion of overdispersion kernels and the discussion of identifiability, demonstrates methodological maturity. The application to a large biobank dataset with multiple ancestry groups is a strength. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The manuscript claims that "rare missense heritability is at least 1.27±0.09% on average, 1.83±0.11% under our most flexible model, exceeding pLoF heritability (0.87±0.05%) and far exceeding missense burden heritability as previously estimated (0.54±0.04%)." Evidence pointer Abstract, Results section "Functional informed kernel heritability", Figure 2b, Supplementary Table 7 Concern The central quantitative claims of the manuscript are presented without any visible supporting data. No figures or tables are provided, and the text does not include the underlying estimates, confidence intervals, or model comparison statistics. The reader cannot assess the magnitude of the effects, the precision of the estimates, or the statistical significance of the differences between models. Why it matters The primary contribution of this work is empirical, providing revised estimates of rare missense heritability. Without the actual numbers, the claims are unverifiable. The comparison to previous estimates (e.g., BHR) is central to the narrative, but the reader cannot evaluate whether the differences are meaningful or within sampling variation. Resolution test Provide the full set of numerical results in Figure 2b and Supplementary Table 7, including point estimates, standard errors, and sample sizes for each model and trait. Include a comparison of model fit statistics (e.g., likelihood or information criteria) to support the claim that the flexible models are preferred. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Methodological validation Claim pointer The manuscript claims that "KASM accurately estimated the kernel heritability across simulation settings" and that "Enrichment estimates were well calibrated in both significant genes and subthreshold genes." Evidence pointer Results section "Simulations", Figure 1a, 1b, 1c, Supplementary Figures 1-5, Supplementary Tables 1-3 Concern The simulation results are described in text but no actual simulation outcomes are shown. The reader cannot evaluate the bias, variance, or coverage properties of the estimators. The claim of accurate estimation is unsupported without seeing the simulation results. Additionally, the simulation design is described only briefly; it is unclear how the data-generating process relates to the model assumptions, and whether the simulations adequately capture the complexity of real exome data. Why it matters The validity of the empirical findings depends entirely on the statistical properties of the estimator. If the estimator is biased or has poor coverage in realistic settings, the central claims would be compromised. The simulations are the primary evidence for estimator performance, and their absence is a critical gap. Resolution test Provide the full simulation results, including bias, root mean squared error, and coverage probabilities for each estimator and simulation setting. Describe the simulation design in sufficient detail to assess its realism, including how variant effects, LD, and population structure were simulated. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Confounding control Claim pointer The manuscript claims that the random-effects estimator "features diagonal kernels which absorb confounding due to residual population stratification, analogous to the BHR intercept." Evidence pointer Methods section "Random-effects estimator for subthreshold genes", Results section "Functional informed kernel heritability", Supplementary Figure 13 Concern The identifiability of the heritable kernel coefficients in the presence of overdispersion kernels is a central methodological issue. The text states that overdispersion kernels are included to absorb confounding, but the conditions under which this separation is identifiable are not fully specified. The assumption that confounding effects are uncorrelated with functional annotations is stated but not justified. The sensitivity of the results to violations of this assumption is not discussed. Why it matters If the overdispersion kernels absorb part of the biological signal, the heritability estimates would be biased downward. Conversely, if the heritable kernels absorb confounding, the estimates would be biased upward. The validity of the central estimates depends on the identifiability of these components. Resolution test Provide a formal identifiability analysis, including conditions under which the heritable and overdispersion components are separately identifiable. Present sensitivity analyses that vary the assumptions about the correlation between confounding and functional annotations, and show how the estimates change. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Interpretability of enrichment Claim pointer The manuscript claims that "a series of structural features is enriched for heritability, from amino acid chemical features and structural motifs to residue contacts and protein-protein interaction interfaces." Evidence pointer Results section "Structural and functional enrichments", Figure 4, Supplementary Table 11 Concern The enrichment analysis is described in text, but the actual enrichment values, confidence intervals, and multiple testing corrections are not shown. The interpretation of enrichment is not fully developed. For example, the authors report that charge-reversing substitutions at interchain hydrogen-bond residues have 27±2-fold enrichment, but it is unclear how this relates to the baseline enrichment of charge-reversing substitutions or interchain hydrogen-bond residues individually. Why it matters The enrichment results are used to draw conclusions about the biological mechanisms underlying trait-associated variation. Without the full results, the reader cannot assess the robustness of these findings or the specificity of the enrichment to particular features. Resolution test Provide the full enrichment results, including point estimates, standard errors, and multiple testing corrections. Include a discussion of how the enrichment of combined features relates to the enrichment of individual features, and whether the interactions are statistically significant. Concern ID R1-M5 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Generalizability Claim pointer The manuscript claims that "we find that most missense effects are modestly correlated, but an exception is when residues are close in 3D structure but distant in 1D sequence; such pairs also covary across species." Evidence pointer Results section "Effect concordance of variant pairs", Figure 6, Supplementary Table 13 Concern The concordance analysis is described, but the actual estimates and their precision are not shown. The interpretation of the concordance parameter is not fully developed. The claim that 3D-proximal/1D-distant pairs have higher concordance is interesting, but the biological interpretation is speculative. The relationship between the estimated concordance and the underlying mutational processes is not discussed. Why it matters The concordance results are used to draw conclusions about the functional architecture of missense variation. Without the full results, the reader cannot assess the strength of the evidence for the claims. Resolution test Provide the full concordance results, including point estimates, standard errors, and the number of pairs in each category. Include a discussion of the biological interpretation of the concordance parameter and the potential confounders. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Abstract Evidence pointer Abstract, first sentence Issue The abstract states that "Protein coding variants span the gamut of structural and functional effects on proteins, and they have similarly heterogeneous effects on traits." This is a general statement that does not clearly motivate the specific contribution of the paper. Required correction Consider revising the opening to more directly state the gap in current methods for integrating functional annotations into rare variant heritability estimation. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Reproducibility Affected element Methods, "Functional informed kernels" Evidence pointer Methods section, equation for β_g Issue The notation for the genotype matrix and effect size vector is introduced but the dimensions are not fully specified. The text states "Let denote the genotype dosage matrix" but the symbol is missing. Required correction Ensure all mathematical symbols are properly defined and that the dimensions of all matrices and vectors are explicitly stated. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected element Results, "Benchmarking missense deleteriousness predictors" Evidence pointer Results section, Figure 3 Issue The comparison of predictors is described, but the text does not specify how the "top decile" is defined when there are ties in predictor scores, or how the enrichment estimates are combined across traits. Required correction Provide details on the handling of ties and the meta-analysis procedure for the enrichment estimates. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Results, "Characterizing functional allelic series" Evidence pointer Results section, PIEZO1 example Issue The text states that "7 of 14 hydrogen-bond contact variants had nominally significant effects, all lowering HbA1c (Z<−3)." It is unclear what threshold is used for "nominally significant" and how the Z-scores are computed. Required correction Specify the significance threshold and the source of the Z-scores (e.g., from the association analysis or from a joint model). Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Interpretation Affected element Discussion Evidence pointer Discussion, paragraph on gain-of-function Issue The discussion of gain-of-function mechanisms is speculative and not directly supported by the presented analyses. The authors note that "we can rule out a narrow model in which missense variants produce weaker loss-of-function effects in a manner that is uniform across genes," but the evidence for this claim is not clearly presented. Required correction Clarify the evidence that supports this claim and consider softening the language if the evidence is indirect. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established The absence of all figures, tables, and numerical results is a critical failing that prevents evaluation of the central claims. The simulation results are described but not shown, making it impossible to assess estimator performance. The identifiability of the heritable and overconfounding components is not formally established. The sensitivity of the results to key assumptions (e.g., uncorrelated confounding) is not assessed. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The framework is a novel integration of functional annotations into kernel-based heritability estimation, extending prior work in a meaningful direction. Scientific importance: The revised estimates of rare missense heritability, if correct, would be of substantial interest to the field. Interdisciplinary readership: The work bridges statistical genetics, protein biology, and complex trait genetics, and would appeal to a broad audience. Technical soundness: The methodological development appears sound in principle, but the absence of results prevents verification. Readability for nonspecialists: The manuscript is clearly written and the concepts are accessible, though the methods section is dense. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The methodological framework is promising and the writing is clear, but the absence of all quantitative results makes it impossible to evaluate the validity of the claims. The authors should provide the full set of figures, tables, and numerical results, along with a more detailed description of the simulation outcomes and sensitivity analyses, before the case can be assessed. Risk / unsupported claims The central quantitative claims (missense heritability estimates, enrichment values, concordance estimates) are unsupported in the provided material, as no figures or tables are included. The claim that "KASM accurately estimated the kernel heritability across simulation settings" is unsupported without the simulation results. The claim that "Enrichment estimates were well calibrated" is unsupported without the simulation results. The claim that "a composite score outperformed every individual predictor" is unsupported without the benchmark results. The claim that "3D-proximal/1D-distal pairs have greater effect concordance" is unsupported without the concordance results. The claim that "we can rule out a narrow model in which missense variants produce weaker loss-of-function effects in a manner that is uniform across genes" is not directly supported by the presented evidence.

Encoding）方法，通过将肽段构象系综的统计信息（如构象多样性、聚类中心结构）作为条件输入注入蛋白质编码器，使编码器在保持静态结构编码能力的同时感知构象柔性，从而在多个下游任务上获得性能提升。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：蛋白质（尤其是肽段）在生理条件下并非单一静态结构，而是呈现构象系综。现有 protein encoder（如基于 GNN、Transformer 的结构编码器）通常以单一 PDB 结构或 AlphaFold 预测结构为输入，忽略了构象多样性信息，导致编码表示无法充分反映蛋白质的动态行为与功能相关构象。 为什么重要 ：构象系综与蛋白质功能（如结合、催化、变构调控）密切相关。若编码器能感知系综信息，有望提升下游任务（如结合位点预测、肽-蛋白相互作用预测、功能注释）的准确性与泛化能力。 现有方法为何不足 ： 静态结构编码器（如 ensemble statistics (e.g., cluster centers and diversity) improve downstream task performance compared to single-structure encoding, without requiring end-to-end MD simulation during inference? 04 本文提出将课程学习策略应用于生成式柔性对接模型，通过从易到难的训练样本排序，改善模型在柔性对接任务上的收敛速度和对接精度，并在多个对接基准上验证了该策略的有效性。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：生成式柔性对接模型（如基于扩散模型的对接方法）在训练时面临样本难度分布不均的问题，导致模型收敛慢、对接精度不稳定。如何设计有效的训练策略以提升生成式柔性对接的性能？ 为什么重要 ：柔性对接是药物发现和蛋白质功能研究中的关键步骤，生成式方法（如扩散模型）在对接中展现出潜力，但其训练效率和对柔性构象的建模能力仍有待提升。课程学习作为一种通用训练策略，有望在不改变模型架构的前提下提升性能。 现有方法为何不足 ：现有生成式对接模型通常采用均匀随机采样训练样本，忽略了样本难度差异，导致模型在困难样本（如高度柔性区域、大构象变化）上表现不佳。课程学习在其他领域（如视觉、NLP）已被证明有效，但尚未系统应用于分子对接。 精确研究问题 ：Can a curriculum learning strategy, which orders training samples from easy to hard, ：本文属于「蛋白质结构域分割」这一结构计算子领域，采用 基于物理准则（Voronoi 接触面积 + 亲水性加权）的无监督方法 ，不依赖深度学习训练数据。其核心贡献在于：将 Voronoi 镶嵌从蛋白-蛋白相互作用分析迁移到域分割任务，并设计了统一的归一化准则（F 和 G），同时用于候选分割的生成与评估。与 Chainsaw、Merizo 等深度学习方法形成对照，属于「物理模拟/几何准则 × 结构计算」路线，而非 AI 方法。对课题的启示在于： 物理可解释的准则可以替代或补充学习到的表征 ，且双向层次搜索（top-down + bottom-up）的策略可迁移到其他结构分割/构象划分任务。 02 一句话总结 BiHC 提出一种基于全重原子 Voronoi 接触面积、经残基亲水性和片段尺寸归一化的成对自包含分数 F 及全局分割质量分数 G，通过独立的 top-down 递归分裂和 bottom-up 递归合并两条层次搜索轨迹生成候选域分割，在 CATH–ECOD 共识基准上达到与深度学习方法 Chainsaw 相当、优于其他准则型方法的域分割性能。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：如何仅凭显式的物理/几何准则（而非学习到的表征）自动识别蛋白质结构域边界？ 为什么重要 ：蛋白质结构域是结构、进化、功能的基本单元，域分割是结构分类、进化分析、基于结构的设计的必要前置步骤。随着实验和预测结构数量激增，自动化、可解释的域分割工具需求日益增长。 现有方法为何不足 ： 深度学习方法（Chainsaw、Merizo、DPAM-AI）性能强，但边界决策依赖学习到的表征，难以追溯每个决策的结构依据； 传统准则型方法（PUU、DomainParser、PDP、SWORD、DDOMAIN、UniDoc）多使用距离截断或距离函数表示接触，未直接度量界面的几何范围；且候选生成与候选评估常使用不同准则，需要额外校准，增加过拟合风险。 精确的「Can ... ?」研究问题 ：Can a single Voronoi-based physical criterion, normalized for fragment size and internal packing and supplemented by hydropathy, be used consistently for both candidate domain-boundary discovery and partition quality assessment, achieving performance competitive with deep learning methods? 04 背景与发展脉络 注：此脉络基于本文 Introduction 与 Discussion 的叙述，属于「仅本文框架」，未经外部系统核验。 阶段 代表性方法 优点 局限 本文位置 早期物理/几何准则 Wodak & Janin (1981)：界面面积极小值；STRUDL (Wernisch et al. 1999)：加权 Voronoi 是一个纯准则型（criterion-based）域分割器，包含三个核心组件： - 结构表示 ：以 SSE（二级结构元件）为基本单元，用全重原子 Voronoi 镶嵌（Voronota v1.29，1.4 Å 探针）计算残基间接触面积； - 成对自包含分数 F ：将残基间 Voronoi 接触面积按残基亲水性（Kyte-Doolittle 标度归一化到 [0,1]）加权，再除以片段尺寸相关的归一化项（约化尺寸项 µ_AB 的 β 次方，β = 0.86）； - 全局分割质量分数 G ：由 F 导出的全局分数，同时要求域间接触弱（低 F）且域内最弱可允许切割也弱（高 F），以调和平均组合。 搜索策略为 双向层次聚类 ：top-down 从完整结构开始递归施加最弱可允许切割（单切或双切），bottom-up 从 SSE 开始递归合并 F 最高的接触对，两条轨迹的所有中间分割均作为候选，最后用 G 排序选择。 2) 核心洞察 Voronoi 接触面积直接度量界面几何范围 ，比距离截断更物理； 亲水性加权 ：域间界面平均而言比域内接触更亲水（极性），因为疏水残基更倾向于埋在域内部； 归一化是关键 ：原始接触面积随片段尺寸增长，必须用约化尺寸项归一化才能跨候选比较； F 同时用于生成与评估 ：同一准则贯穿候选发现与候选排序，避免生成-评估准则分离带来的校准问题； 双向搜索互补 ：top-down 和 bottom-up 各自覆盖不同的分割空间，保留所有中间分割可避免早期停止的局部最优问题。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] 物理准则的「可解释性红利」 ：当深度学习模型在基准上占优时，显式物理准则仍可提供可追溯的决策依据，且可作为集成、蒸馏或异常检测的补充信号； 「生成-评估同源」原则 ：若生成候选与评估候选使用同一准则，可减少超参数校准负担，降低过拟合风险——这一原则可迁移到其他结构分割/聚类任务； 双向搜索 + 全轨迹保留 ：不依赖单一方向的贪心停止，而是保留所有中间状态再全局排序，是一种通用的搜索策略，适用于构象采样、聚类等存在层次结构的问题； 归一化设计需匹配任务几何 ：尺寸归一化的指数（β）需与接触面积的标度行为匹配（本文通过 PDP 的 α 推导 β = 2α = 0.86），这种「从已有方法推导标度指数」的思路可迁移。 07 方法总览 输入 ：蛋白质链的 3D 结构（PDB 格式），需 ≥60 残基 输出 ：域分割（每个残基的域分配），以及每个候选分割的全局质量分数 G 模块 ： 1. 结构表示模块 ：SSE 分配（STRIDE）→ 全重原子 Voronoi 镶嵌（Voronota v1.29）→ 残基-残基接触面积矩阵 2. Assessment boundary Scientific soundness, methodological clarity, validity of claims relative to presented evidence, and suitability for a general structural biology audience. Shared manuscript claim summary The authors introduce BiHC, a criterion-based protein domain parser that uses Voronoi tessellation-derived contact areas, normalized by fragment size and internal packing, and weighted by residue hydropathy, to define a pairwise self-containment score F and a global partition quality score G. BiHC performs independent top-down and bottom-up hierarchical searches, and is claimed to achieve state-of-the-art performance among criterion-based parsers and comparable performance to deep learning methods on CATH-ECOD consensus benchmarks. Visible evidence base Abstract, full introduction, results overview (including dataset construction, tuning, benchmark performance, and case studies), discussion, and methods sections. Figures are referenced but not provided. Supplementary files are referenced but not provided. Missing materials affecting confidence Figures 1-7, all supplementary tables (S1-S7), Supplementary File 1 (including ablation study), Supplementary File 2 (per-chain results), and the actual benchmark datasets. Without these, quantitative claims cannot be independently verified. Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript presents a conceptually interesting approach to protein domain segmentation, leveraging Voronoi tessellation in a way that has been underexplored in modern domain parsers. The methodological framework is clearly described and the motivation is well-articulated. However, the manuscript as presented has several critical gaps. The results section is largely descriptive without presenting actual numerical data, making it impossible to assess the strength of the claimed performance. The reliance on a single-author submission with no code or data available at the time of review further limits verification. The core claims, while plausible, are not substantiated by the evidence visible in this manuscript. The work has potential, but in its current form, the case is not fully established. Who would be interested in the results, and why Structural biologists, bioinformaticians, and researchers working on protein structure annotation and classification would be the primary audience. The work is relevant to those interested in criterion-based (non-machine-learning) approaches to domain parsing, as it offers a transparent alternative to deep learning methods. The use of Voronoi tessellation and physical self-containment criteria may also appeal to researchers studying protein geometry and packing. The comparative benchmarking against Chainsaw and Merizo would be of interest to the broader protein structure prediction community. Major Strengths 1. The conceptual framing is strong. The authors correctly identify a gap in the field: most modern domain parsers rely on learned representations, and explicit geometric criteria are underrepresented. The use of Voronoi contact areas, normalized for size and packing, is a thoughtful and physically motivated approach. 2. The methodological design is coherent. The bidirectional search strategy (independent top-down and bottom-up) is a sensible way to explore the partition space, and the use of a single scoring function F throughout both candidate generation and evaluation is a principled improvement over methods like STRUDL that use different criteria at different stages. 3. The authors are appropriately cautious in their claims. They acknowledge the multi-domain performance gap and the potential for curated annotations to reflect non-geometric information. This balanced perspective is commendable. 4. The inclusion of a reconstructed STRUDL (STRUDL-R) as a baseline is a useful contribution, as it allows for direct comparison with a historical Voronoi-based method. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The manuscript claims that "On the primary CONSENSUS-43 benchmark, BiHC showed a clear class-dependent performance profile" and that "BiHC achieved the strongest performance among all tested criterion-based parsers and was comparable to Chainsaw" under balanced evaluation. Evidence pointer Results section, "BiHC performance on benchmark datasets"; Figures 4 and 5 are referenced but not provided; Tables S2-S7 are referenced but not provided. Concern The central quantitative claims of the manuscript are entirely unsupported by the visible text. No numerical results are presented in the body of the manuscript. The reader is told that BiHC performed well, but is not shown any actual performance values, confidence intervals, or statistical comparisons. The figures and supplementary tables that would contain this information are not available for review. This is a fundamental issue, as the entire case for BiHC's utility rests on these benchmark results. Why it matters Without access to the actual performance numbers, it is impossible to evaluate whether the claims of "strongest among criterion-based parsers" and "comparable to Chainsaw" are justified. The reader cannot assess the magnitude of differences, the variance across protein classes, or the practical significance of the results. This is a blocking issue for any assessment of the manuscript's validity. Resolution test The authors must provide the actual numerical results in the main text or in accessible supplementary materials. This should include at minimum: exact-K accuracy, K-score, IoU, NDO, CSD, and DBD for all methods on both benchmarks, with appropriate measures of uncertainty. The figures must be made available for review. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Methodological completeness Claim pointer The manuscript states that "BiHC applies F in two independent hierarchical searches" and that "Intermediate partitions from both searches are ranked by a global partition quality score G, derived on the same principle." Evidence pointer Results section, "Overview of the BiHC framework"; Materials and Methods, "Pairwise self-containment score" and "Global partition quality score". Concern The mathematical definitions of the key quantities F and G are not fully specified in the visible text. The methods section describes the components of F (hydropathy-weighted interface, reduced-size term, geometric Voronoi contact density) but the actual equations are not shown. The text refers to equations that are not present in the manuscript. Similarly, the definition of G is described verbally but the exact formula is not given. The threshold t is mentioned but its precise role in the scoring is not fully formalized. Why it matters The manuscript's central contribution is a novel scoring function. Without the explicit mathematical formulation, the method cannot be reproduced, evaluated for correctness, or compared to alternative approaches. The reader cannot assess whether the normalization is sound, whether the hydropathy weighting is appropriate, or whether the thresholding scheme is principled. This is a fundamental gap in a methods-focused paper. Resolution test The authors must provide the complete mathematical definitions of F, G, and the thresholding procedure. This should include all equations, definitions of all variables, and a clear statement of how the threshold t is applied. The equations should be numbered and referenced in the text. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Benchmark validity Claim pointer The manuscript claims that CONSENSUS-43 and CONSENSUS-44 are appropriate benchmarks, with CONSENSUS-43 being "the primary benchmark" and CONSENSUS-44 used "to assess the stability of tool performance." Evidence pointer Results section, "Overview of the dataset construction"; Materials and Methods, "Data preprocessing" and "CATH-ECOD consensus filtering". Concern The benchmark construction is described in detail, but several aspects raise concerns. First, the CONSENSUS-44 set is derived from CATH v4.4, which the authors acknowledge "is not fully independent of that method" (i.e., Chainsaw) because CATH v4.4 used Chainsaw in its annotation pipeline. This means that the benchmark itself may be biased toward Chainsaw's predictions, making any comparison on this set difficult to interpret. Second, the filtering criteria (CATH-ECOD agreement on domain count and partition IoU ≥ 0.90) may select for "easy" cases where the two databases agree, potentially reducing the difficulty of the benchmark and limiting its ability to discriminate between methods. Third, the number of multi-domain structures in CONSENSUS-43 (200 out of 3231) is small, which may limit the statistical power of the multi-domain comparisons. Why it matters The validity of the benchmark directly affects the interpretability of the performance claims. If the benchmark is biased or too easy, the reported performance may not generalize to real-world domain parsing tasks. The small number of multi-domain structures is particularly concerning, as this is where the authors acknowledge BiHC struggles. Resolution test The authors should provide a more detailed analysis of the benchmark characteristics, including the distribution of domain counts, protein lengths, and structural classes. They should also discuss the potential impact of the CATH v4.4 annotation bias on CONSENSUS-44 results and consider whether additional benchmarks (e.g., from ECOD alone or from a manually curated set) would strengthen the evaluation. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Comparison fairness Claim pointer The manuscript states that "BiHC achieved the strongest performance among all tested criterion-based parsers and was comparable to Chainsaw, the best-performing deep learning method tested." Evidence pointer Results section, "BiHC performance on benchmark datasets"; Materials and Methods, "Evaluated domain parsers". Concern The comparison with other methods is described, but the details of how these methods were run are not fully specified. For example, were the deep learning methods (Chainsaw, Merizo) run with their default settings, or were they fine-tuned on the benchmark? Were the criterion-based methods (UniDoc, SWORD2) run with their default parameters, or were they optimized for the benchmark? The manuscript mentions that "All tools were obtained from their official repositories" but does not state the specific versions or configuration used. Additionally, the reconstruction of STRUDL (STRUDL-R) is described as having a "logistic classifier... fitted on the tuning set," which raises the question of whether STRUDL-R was given an advantage by being trained on data from the same distribution as the benchmark. Why it matters Fair comparison is essential for the validity of the performance claims. If other methods were not given the same opportunity to perform well (e.g., through hyperparameter tuning), the comparison may be biased in favor of BiHC. Conversely, if STRUDL-R was trained on the tuning set, it may have an unfair advantage over methods that were not similarly tuned. Resolution test The authors should provide a detailed description of how each comparison method was configured and run, including specific versions, parameters, and any tuning procedures. They should also clarify whether the tuning set was used to optimize any aspect of the comparison methods, and if so, how this was done. Concern ID R1-M5 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Ablation study rigor Claim pointer The manuscript states that "we conducted an ablation study on the tuning set to assess the contributions of its individual components" and that "most components of F, including hydropathy and size-dependent terms, contributed to the performance." Evidence pointer Discussion section; Supplementary File 1, "Ablation study" section (not provided). Concern The ablation study is only mentioned in passing, with no results presented in the main text. The reader is told that removing components led to "a slight decrease in balanced domain-count performance, although the differences were not significant." This is a critical piece of evidence for the design of F, but the details are entirely relegated to a supplementary file that is not available for review. The lack of significance is also concerning, as it suggests that the individual components may not be essential, which would weaken the justification for the specific form of F. Why it matters The ablation study is the primary evidence that the specific formulation of F is well-justified. If the components do not significantly contribute, the method could potentially be simplified, or the choice of components may be arbitrary. The reader cannot evaluate this without seeing the actual results. Resolution test The authors should present the ablation study results in the main text or provide the supplementary file for review. They should also discuss the implications of the lack of statistical significance for the design choices. 06 核心思想 1) 表面方法 Chaperone 是一个 Python 框架，核心抽象是 block ——一个轻量级类，输入 DataFrame、输出扩展后的 DataFrame。每个 block 封装一个工具（如 RFdiffusion3、ProteinMPNN、AlphaFold3），负责将 DataFrame 行转换为工具所需的输入文件、执行工具、解析输出并追加到 DataFrame。执行引擎将 DataFrame 分块并行分发到 HPC 集群（基于 Submitit 调度器），支持断点续跑。智能体通过调用 Chaperone 的 API 来构建和运行工作流，而非直接操作底层工具。 2) 核心洞察 洞察一：DataFrame 作为统一数据模式 。几乎所有蛋白质设计工具都可以抽象为「输入结构/序列 → 输出结构/指标」的映射。DataFrame 的每一行代表一个设计候选，携带其结构历史（ordered list of structure records）和指标集合（JSON-encoded metrics）。这种统一模式使智能体无需理解每个工具的特定格式，只需操作 DataFrame 即可。 洞察二：工具即黑盒，接口即契约 。Chaperone 不修改工具本身，而是通过 block 封装层将工具视为黑盒。block 的输入/输出契约（DataFrame→DataFrame）是唯一需要智能体理解的接口。这使得新工具的接入成本极低——只需编写一个 block 类。 洞察三：智能体的 token 消耗与工具接口的标准化程度成反比 。基线智能体需要反复生成代码来处理格式转换、作业提交、错误恢复，而 Chaperone 将这些操作封装为一次性 API 调用。标准化接口将智能体的认知负担从「如何调用工具」转移到「如何设计策略」。 洞察四：Test mode 作为智能体的「沙箱」 。Chaperone 提供 test mode，减少采样量以支持快速端到端检查。这使得智能体可以在小规模上验证工作流正确性，再扩展到全规模——类似于软件工程中的「先跑通再优化」。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] 接口标准化比工具本身更能提升智能体效率 任务范围 ：本文的评估覆盖 9 个 in silico 设计任务和 3 个湿实验验证任务，但湿实验验证仅针对 cortisol 结合剂、纳米颗粒和蛋白质晶体融合三个特定任务，不能推广到所有蛋白质设计场景。 智能体范围 ：评估使用 GPT-5.6-sol 智能体，结果可能不适用于其他 LLM 或专用智能体架构。作者也指出「we chose to more deeply evaluate GPT-5.6 Sol with the resources available」，说明评估的模型范围有限。 基线条件 ：基线智能体允许网络访问以安装工具，但 Chaperone 智能体网络被禁用。这模拟了「预装环境 vs 自主安装」的对比，但实际部署中网络访问策略可能不同。 通过率解读 ：平均通过率从 6% 提升至 12% 是相对提升 100%，但绝对通过率仍较低。这意味着 Chaperone 改善了工具编排效率，但设计质量仍受限于底层生成模型（RFD3、ProteinMPNN 等）的能力。 资源消耗解读 ：Token 减少 86% 和 GPU 减少 64% 是在特定任务集和智能体配置下测得的，不同任务复杂度下节省幅度可能不同。作者未提供逐任务的资源消耗明细。 湿实验验证的边界 ：Cortisol 结合剂 Kd = 1.32 nM 是「零轮亲和力成熟」的结果，但未与 Lee et al. 的 68 nM 在相同实验条件下直接对比。纳米颗粒成功率为 6.7%（1/15），样本量小，统计功效有限。 有边界的复述 ：Chaperone 在 GPT-5.6-sol 智能体上、9 个 in silico 任务和 3 个湿实验任务中，展示了通过统一 DataFrame 接口降低 token 和 GPU 消耗、提升设计通过率的效果，但该效果受限于任务类型、智能体模型和底层生成工具的能力。 12 abstract, main text, supplementary methods, and funding information Assessment boundary Scientific claims, methodological soundness, experimental validation, and framework utility as presented in the provided material Shared manuscript claim summary The authors present Chaperone, a lightweight Python framework that standardizes protein design tool orchestration through a DataFrame-based block interface, and demonstrate that this framework improves agentic workflow efficiency (86% token reduction, 64% GPU cost reduction) and enables successful experimental validation across three distinct design tasks: small-molecule binders, nanoparticles, and protein fusions Visible evidence base In silico evaluation across nine design tasks comparing agent performance with and without the harness; wet lab validation for cortisol binders (fluorescence polarization), nanoparticles (negative stain EM), and protein fusions (bright-field microscopy); supplementary descriptions of evaluation protocols Missing materials affecting confidence No code repository contents or version information; no raw scoring data or per-task breakdowns; no negative control experiments for the harness comparison; no quantitative EM analysis for nanoparticle validation; no diffraction data for crystal claims; no statistical analysis of replicate variability Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript presents a timely and potentially valuable contribution to the growing field of agentic protein design. The Chaperone framework addresses a real bottleneck in computational protein design, and the reported efficiency gains are substantial. However, the evidence base for the central claim that Chaperone improves agent performance is thinner than the abstract suggests, and several experimental validations lack quantitative rigor. The framework itself appears well-designed and the wet lab results are encouraging, but the manuscript would benefit from more detailed evaluation methodology, additional controls, and clearer presentation of limitations. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational protein designers and developers of scientific agent frameworks will find the Chaperone architecture directly relevant to their work. The demonstrated efficiency gains in agentic workflows are of broad interest to the AI-for-science community. Experimental protein designers may be interested in the cortisol binder results, though the single-target demonstration limits generalizability. The framework's open-source availability increases its potential impact. Major strengths 1. The block-based DataFrame abstraction is elegant and addresses a genuine pain point in protein design tool integration 2. The in silico evaluation suite spans diverse design tasks and uses held-out scoring, which is methodologically sound 3. The reported efficiency gains (86% token reduction, 64% GPU cost reduction) are substantial and practically meaningful 4. Experimental validation across three distinct design challenges demonstrates real-world utility 5. The framework is made freely available, which will facilitate adoption and further testing Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer "we find using Chaperone reduces total token usage relative to baseline agents by 86% and GPU costs by 64%, while increasing the overall computational design pass rate" Evidence pointer Section 3, Figure 1f, Figure 1g Concern The central quantitative claim of the manuscript rests on a comparison between agents with and without the Chaperone harness, but the evaluation methodology has a critical asymmetry: harnessed agents had internet access disabled while baseline agents had web access. This confounds the effect of the harness itself with the effect of restricted tool access. Additionally, only a single agent model (GPT-5.6-sol) was evaluated, and the manuscript does not report per-task results, variance across runs, or statistical significance testing. The pass rate increase from 6% to 12% is reported as a mean, but no confidence intervals or per-task breakdowns are provided. Why it matters The efficiency and pass rate improvements are the primary quantitative evidence for the manuscript's central claim. Without addressing the internet access confound and providing statistical rigor, the magnitude of the harness benefit cannot be reliably assessed. The single-model evaluation also limits generalizability claims. Resolution test Provide per-task results with variance measures, run the comparison with matched internet access conditions (both enabled or both disabled), evaluate at least one additional agent model, and report statistical significance testing for the efficiency and pass rate differences. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Experimental validation rigor Claim pointer "yielding low nanomolar binders to cortisol zero shot" and "one successfully assembled into a protein nanoparticle" and "form crystalline assemblies" Evidence pointer Section 4.1, Section 4.2, Section 4.3, Figure 2 Concern The experimental validations are presented with insufficient quantitative detail. For the cortisol binder, the manuscript reports a best affinity of 1.32 nM but does not provide the full binding curve, replicate measurements, or the number of proteins tested. The nanoparticle validation reports one success out of 15 designs but provides no quantitative EM analysis (e.g., particle size distribution, symmetry assessment). The crystal claim is supported only by bright-field microscopy images, which cannot demonstrate crystallinity; no diffraction data are shown. The fusion validation lacks any biochemical characterization beyond microscopy. Why it matters These experimental results are presented as demonstrations of the framework's utility, but the level of validation is not commensurate with the strength of the claims. For a framework paper, the experimental sections should either be more rigorously quantified or presented with appropriately hedged language. Resolution test Provide full binding curves with replicate measurements for cortisol binders, quantitative EM analysis (particle dimensions, symmetry metrics) for nanoparticles, and X-ray diffraction or electron diffraction data for crystal claims. Alternatively, soften the claims to match the evidence level. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Reproducibility Claim pointer "we make Chaperone freely available to the community on GitHub" Evidence pointer Abstract, Section 5 Concern The manuscript states the framework is available on GitHub but provides no repository URL in the visible text, no version information, no installation instructions, and no documentation of the block interface beyond the single algorithm example. The supplementary material describes evaluation protocols but does not include the actual evaluation prompts, scoring functions, or agent configuration details needed to reproduce the benchmark results. Why it matters Reproducibility is a core expectation for computational framework papers. Without access to the code, evaluation prompts, and scoring implementations, independent verification of the reported results is not possible. Resolution test Provide the GitHub URL, a versioned release, documentation of the block API, and include evaluation prompts and scoring function implementations in the supplementary material. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Comparison to existing approaches Claim pointer "Previous efforts targeting cortisol involved iterative computational design followed by experimental affinity maturation, with Lee et al. ultimately achieving a binding affinity of 68 nM" Evidence pointer Section 4.1 Concern The comparison to prior work is limited to a single affinity value from one study. The manuscript does not discuss how the Chaperone-based approach compares to other agentic frameworks or automated design pipelines in terms of efficiency, success rate, or design quality. The claim that Chaperone "accelerates" the design process is supported only by the two-week timeline, but no comparison to a non-harnessed timeline for the same task is provided. Why it matters The manuscript positions Chaperone as an improvement over existing approaches, but the evidence for this improvement is largely internal to the study. A meaningful comparison to alternative frameworks or to manual workflows would strengthen the contribution. Resolution test Include a comparison to at least one alternative agentic framework or to a manual workflow for the same design task, reporting comparable efficiency and success metrics. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Figure 1 Evidence pointer Figure 1 Issue The figure is referenced extensively but the visible text does not describe the figure panels in sufficient detail. The relationship between panels b, c, d, f, and g is not immediately clear from the text alone. Required correction Add a detailed figure legend that explains each panel and how they relate to the claims in the text. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Terminology Affected element Section 2, "block" definition Evidence pointer Section 2 Issue The term "block" is used to describe both the framework's computational unit and the experimental design blocks in the supplementary methods, which could cause confusion. Required correction Consider using a distinct term for the framework unit, such as "tool block" or "pipeline block," to avoid ambiguity. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected element Section 4.2 Evidence pointer Section 4.2, Figure 2h, 2i Issue The nanoparticle section reports one success out of 15 designs but does not describe what happened to the other 14 designs or whether any iterative refinement was attempted. Required correction Briefly describe the outcomes for the unsuccessful designs and whether any design modifications were made based on the initial results. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Statistical reporting Affected element Section 3 Evidence pointer Section 3, Figure 1f Issue The pass rate improvement from 6% to 12% is reported as a mean, but the number of evaluation runs and the distribution of results across the nine tasks are not reported. Required correction Report the per-task pass rates and the number of independent evaluation runs. Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Accessibility Affected element Abstract Evidence pointer Abstract Issue The abstract claims "more than 50 other protein design tools" are integrated, but the main text does not provide a list or categorization of these tools. Required correction Include a supplementary table listing the integrated tools and their categories. Concern ID R1-m6 Severity Minor Axis Language precision Affected element Section 4.1 Evidence pointer Section 4.1 Issue The phrase "zero shot" in the abstract and Section 4.1 is potentially misleading, as the design process involved iterative refinement and human guidance. Required correction Clarify what "zero shot" means in this context, or use alternative phrasing such as "without affinity maturation." Risk / unsupported claims The claim that Chaperone reduces token usage by 86% and GPU costs by 64% is confounded by the asymmetric internet access conditions in the evaluation and lacks statistical rigor The claim of "low nanomolar binders to cortisol zero shot" is not fully supported, as the manuscript does not demonstrate that no affinity maturation occurred and does not provide full binding characterization The claim of "crystalline assemblies" is unsupported by the evidence presented, as bright-field microscopy cannot demonstrate crystallinity The claim that Chaperone integrates "more than 50 other protein design tools" is not verifiable from the provided material, as no tool list is given The generalizability of the efficiency gains to other agent models is not established, as only GPT-5.6-sol was evaluated The claim that the framework "enables rapid iteration and scalable exploration" is supported only by the two-week cortisol campaign, which lacks a comparison to non-harnessed timelines
