Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report the discovery and characterization of phenyl-glutarimide-based CRBN molecular glues that selectively degrade VAV1 via a non-canonical RT-loop degron (RDxS motif, residues 796–799). They introduce GluePlex, an AI/physics-based pipeline for ternary complex prediction, and validate it with mutagenesis, SAR, FEP calculations, and dose-response proteomics. They also identify LIMD1 as an off-target with a canonical G-loop degron. Visible evidence base Main text figures (Figs 1–7), supplementary figures (S1–S12 as referenced), supplementary tables (S1), methods section, and source data statements. No raw proteomics data, no uncropped blots, no structural coordinates, no compound characterization data (NMR/HRMS/purity) were provided in the submitted material. Missing materials affecting confidence Raw mass spectrometry data and analysis outputs; uncropped Western blots; compound synthesis and characterization data (purity, NMR, HRMS); ternary complex structural coordinates (PDB files); FEP convergence metrics and perturbation maps; LIMD1 mutagenesis data; statistical analysis details for proteomics (number of replicates per condition, variance estimates); details on the "high-throughput" nature of the proteomics workflow (sample throughput, multiplexing strategy). Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript presents a compelling and timely contribution to the molecular glue degrader field. The discovery of a non-canonical RT-loop degron in VAV1, the development of the GluePlex pipeline, and the identification of LIMD1 as an off-target are all significant findings. The integration of unbiased proteomics, AI-based structural prediction, and medicinal chemistry is exemplary and aligns well with the scope of Nature Communications. However, several technical concerns, particularly around the validation of the computational predictions, the quantitative rigor of the proteomics data, and the incomplete characterization of the off-target effects, need to be addressed before the case is fully established. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in targeted protein degradation, chemical biology, medicinal chemistry, and structural biology. The work is also relevant to those studying VAV1 biology in hematological malignancies and autoimmune diseases. The GluePlex pipeline will be of interest to computational chemists and AI practitioners in drug discovery. Major strengths 1. The identification and validation of a non-canonical RDxS degron in the VAV1 SH3-2 domain is a novel and important finding that expands the known substrate recognition repertoire of CRBN. 2. The GluePlex pipeline, integrating PeSTo, HADDOCK, and Boltz-2, is a well-conceived and reproducible approach that addresses a critical bottleneck in molecular glue discovery. 3. The use of unbiased dose-response proteomics to identify both the on-target (VAV1) and an off-target (LIMD1) is rigorous and highlights the importance of global profiling in degrader development. 4. The medicinal chemistry principle of conformational restriction via halogen substitution, rationalized by DFT calculations, is a valuable and generalizable strategy. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "Applying Free Energy Perturbation (FEP) to predicted ternary structures yields cooperativity metrics that correlate with degradation potency, overcoming limitations of standard docking and enabling prospective ranking of analogs—even from weak initial binders." Evidence pointer Figure 6, Methods (FEP+ section) Concern The correlation between FEP-derived cooperativity metrics and experimental degradation potency is presented as a key validation of the computational approach. However, the manuscript does not report the statistical significance of these correlations (e.g., p-values for Pearson r values are given, but the confidence intervals are wide given n=10). More critically, the FEP calculations are performed on predicted ternary structures from GluePlex, not on experimentally determined structures. The accuracy of FEP is highly sensitive to the starting structure, and the manuscript does not provide a rigorous assessment of the uncertainty in the predicted structures or how this propagates to the FEP results. The claim of "prospective ranking" is not fully supported, as the FEP calculations appear to be retrospective on a small set of analogs. Why it matters The central premise of the paper is that the GluePlex/FEP workflow can accelerate molecular glue discovery. If the FEP predictions are not robustly validated, the utility of the pipeline for prospective design is questionable. The lack of structural validation (e.g., co-crystal structure) for the predicted ternary complex is a significant gap. Resolution test Provide a more detailed statistical analysis of the FEP correlations, including confidence intervals and cross-validation. Ideally, validate the predicted ternary complex structure with an experimentally determined structure (e.g., X-ray or Cryo-EM) for at least one compound. If not possible, provide a rigorous error analysis of the FEP predictions, including convergence checks and sensitivity to the starting structure. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "Dose-response proteomics confirms VAV1 as the primary target and reveals LIMD1, bearing a canonical G-loop, as an off-target, showing that one glue can engage disparate degrons." Evidence pointer Figure 7, Methods (proteomics section) Concern The identification of LIMD1 as an off-target is a significant finding, but the manuscript does not provide sufficient quantitative detail on the proteomics data. The heatmap in Figure 7A is qualitative. The authors do not report the number of replicates, the magnitude of LIMD1 degradation (e.g., percentage change at specific concentrations), or the statistical significance of the changes. Furthermore, the functional consequences of LIMD1 degradation are not explored. The claim that LIMD1 degradation is "off-target" is based on the presence of a G-loop, but the potential implications for toxicity or efficacy are not discussed. Why it matters The identification of off-targets is critical for assessing the therapeutic window and safety of the compounds. Without quantitative data, the reader cannot assess the selectivity of the compounds. The lack of functional data on LIMD1 degradation leaves the biological significance of this off-target activity unclear. Resolution test Provide quantitative proteomics data (e.g., log2 fold-changes, adjusted p-values) for VAV1 and LIMD1 across all compounds and concentrations tested. Include a discussion of the potential functional consequences of LIMD1 degradation. If possible, include a simple functional assay (e.g., proliferation or signaling) to assess the impact of LIMD1 loss. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "We further show that conformational restriction via halogen substitution (e.g., NGT-201-17, NGT-201-18) potentiates degradation, a principle rationalized by DFT calculations." Evidence pointer Figure 4, Methods (DFT section) Concern The DFT calculations are used to rationalize the observed potency differences, but the manuscript does not provide a clear link between the calculated rotational barriers and the experimental degradation data. The DFT calculations are performed on isolated molecules in the gas phase (or with implicit solvent), which may not accurately represent the conformational preferences in the bound state. The manuscript does not report the calculated barriers for all compounds, only a representative example. The claim that conformational restriction "potentiates degradation" is based on a limited set of analogs. Why it matters The medicinal chemistry hypothesis is interesting, but the evidence is not fully convincing. A more rigorous analysis would involve calculating the conformational energy landscape in the context of the ternary complex, or at least correlating the calculated barriers with the experimental potencies across a larger set of compounds. Resolution test Provide a table correlating the calculated rotational barriers (or energy differences between conformers) with the experimental DC50 and Dmax values for all compounds tested. Discuss the limitations of the DFT approach in the context of the bound state. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Readability for nonspecialists Affected element Introduction Evidence pointer Introduction, paragraph 3 Issue The introduction mentions "YDS-GlueFold" and "FEP+" without sufficient context for a general reader. The sentence "Computational tools like YDS-GlueFold is combining diffusion model with statistic mechanics for predicting ternary complex structures and guiding molecular design25, while FEP+ binding free energy calculation in the ternary system for explaining cooperativity and target selectivity26" is grammatically awkward and lacks a clear explanation of what these tools do and why they are relevant. Required correction Rewrite this sentence to be clearer and more accessible. For example: "Recent computational approaches, such as YDS-GlueFold, combine diffusion models with statistical mechanics to predict ternary complex structures, while alchemical free energy perturbation (FEP) methods can be used to estimate binding cooperativity and selectivity." Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Technical soundness Affected element Methods (proteomics) Evidence pointer Methods, "High-throughput global proteomics" section Issue The methods state that "at least two biological replicates with two MS technical replicates were analyzed for each treatment condition." This is a relatively low number of replicates for a quantitative proteomics experiment, especially for a dose-response analysis. The authors should justify this choice and discuss the potential impact on the statistical power of the analysis. Required correction Add a sentence justifying the number of replicates and discussing the statistical power. If possible, include a supplementary figure showing the reproducibility of the replicates. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Technical soundness Affected element Figure 3E Evidence pointer Figure 3E Issue The dose-response curves in Figure 3E are presented as mean ± SD from two independent experiments. Two independent experiments are generally insufficient for a robust statistical analysis. The authors should provide more replicates or acknowledge this limitation. Required correction Provide additional replicates or clearly state the limitation in the figure legend. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Technical soundness Affected element Methods (FEP+) Evidence pointer Methods, "Schrodinger Glide Docking and FEP+" section Issue The FEP+ methods section is brief and lacks details on the perturbation map, the number of lambda windows, the simulation length, and the convergence criteria. This makes it difficult to assess the reliability of the FEP results. Required correction Provide a more detailed description of the FEP+ setup, including the perturbation map, simulation parameters, and convergence assessment. Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Readability for nonspecialists Affected element Results (SAR sections) Evidence pointer Results, "Structure-activity relationship studies" sections Issue The SAR sections are dense and difficult to follow for a reader not deeply familiar with medicinal chemistry. The authors should consider adding a summary table or a more accessible description of the key findings. Required correction Consider adding a summary paragraph at the end of each SAR section that highlights the key takeaways in plain language. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that GluePlex can "prospectively rank" analogs is not fully supported, as the FEP calculations appear to be retrospective on a small set of compounds. The claim that conformational restriction "potentiates degradation" is based on a limited set of analogs and a simplified DFT analysis. The identification of LIMD1 as an off-target is not supported by quantitative proteomics data. The claim that the VAV1 RT-loop degron is "non-canonical" is supported by mutagenesis, but the manuscript does not provide a direct comparison to known G-loop degrons in the same experimental system. The statement that "the recent independent report by Petzold et al.19 highlights the versatility of CRIN" (as quoted in the Discussion) is not verifiable from the provided text, as reference 19 is not described in detail.

SMD 模拟模块：结构准备、溶剂化、平衡、恒速/恒力 SMD、力-延伸分析 4. 桥接模块：实验与模拟结果的定量对比（加载速率匹配、能量景观参数比较） 训练 ：不适用（非机器学习方法） 工具 ：AFM 仪器（具体型号未提供）；MD 引擎（如 GROMACS/NAMD，具体未提供）；分析软件（未提供） 反馈回路 ：实验参数（如加载速率）→ 模型预测 → SMD 验证 → 修正模型或设计新实验 假设 ：蛋白质去折叠遵循能量景观理论；SMD 在适当加载速率下可捕捉与实验相关的去折叠路径；分析模型的简化假设（如单能垒）在特定条件下成立 文字流程 ： 1. 制备蛋白质样品并固定于基底/探针 2. 使用 AFM（或其他力谱技术）采集力-距离曲线，提取去折叠/断裂事件 3. 将力谱数据按加载速率分组，用分析模型（Bell/DHS）拟合，得到能量景观参数 4. 构建蛋白质结构的原子模型，进行 MD 平衡 5. 执行 SMD（恒速或恒力），记录力-延伸曲线与去折叠路径 6. 将 SMD 结果与实验力谱对比，必要时调整模拟协议或模型假设 7. 整合实验、模型、模拟结果，形成对蛋白质力学-结构关系的统一描述 08 核心模块拆解 模块 功能 为何需要 输入输出 支撑证据 移除后的已知或预期影响 力谱实验（AFM等） 测量蛋白质去折叠/键断裂的力学响应 提供真实体系的定量力学数据 输入：固定化蛋白；输出：力-距离曲线 文中作为方法学基础（未提供具体数据） 失去实验基准，模拟与模型无法验证 分析模型（Bell/DHS） 从力谱提取能量景观参数 将原始力谱转化为可解释的物理量 输入：力-加载速率数据；输出：Δx、k_off、ΔG 文中「phenomenological characterization」论述 无法定量描述能量景观，实验数据仅停留在现象层面 SMD 模拟 提供原子级去折叠机制 解释实验无法直接观测的过渡态与路径 输入：原子结构；输出：力-延伸曲线、去折叠路径 文中「atomic detail」论述 失去机制解释能力，实验与模型只能停留在唯象层面 桥接协议 统一实验-模型-模拟的对比框架 使不同方法的结果可定量比较 输入：实验参数+模拟参数；输出：一致性评估 文中「bridging」论述 各方法孤立使用，无法交叉验证，结论可靠性下降 注：本文为方法学综述，未提供消融实验数据。上述「移除后影响」为基于方法学逻辑的预期效应，非实测消融结果。 09 关键公式符号 本文为方法学章节，摘要中未列出具体公式。以下基于力谱领域标准公式，标注为 [Analysis] 推断，非原文直接引用。 1) Bell-Evans 模型 （力依赖的解离速率） [ k_{off}(F) = k_{off}^0 \exp\left( rac{F \Delta x}{k_B T}ight) ] - ( k_{off}(F) )：施加力 ( F ) 时的解离速率 - ( k_{off}^0 )：零力解离速率 - ( \Delta x )：过渡态到束缚态的距离（能量景观宽度） - ( k_B T )：热能量 - 用途 ：从力谱数据提取 ( \Delta x ) 和 ( k_{off}^0 ) - 直觉 ：力降低能垒，加速解离 - 来源 ：本文「available theories」部分提及，但未给出具体公式编号 [Analysis] 2) DHS (Dudko-Hummer-Szabo) 模型 （考虑能垒形状） [ k_{off}(F) = k_{off}^0 \left(1 -  rac{

MTGase（交联型）在微生物细胞工厂中的功能定位，提出了一个从「催化转化」到「蛋白质水平工程」的层级演化框架，并整合了实验与计算策略（AlphaFold、分子对接、MD、机器学习）来指导 MTGase 工程改造。 2) 核心洞察 ： MTGase 与经典酰胺转化酶的本质区别不在于催化化学（都作用于酰胺键），而在于其产物是 共价连接的蛋白质组装体 而非小分子产物。这使得 MTGase 能够作为「蛋白质水平控制元件」，直接操纵代谢酶的空间组织、稳定性和组装状态，从而在转录调控之外提供一条更快速、更直接的调控维度。作者强调，这一潜力能否实现取决于三个关键控制：底物选择性（正交识别标签）、时间控制（前体酶原激活）、空间控制（区室化/固定化）。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] ： - 酶的工程价值不仅取决于其催化活性，更取决于其 产物类型在细胞中的功能层级 ——能改变蛋白质组装状态的酶，其工程杠杆远大于仅转化小分子的酶。 - 计算工具（AlphaFold、MD、ML）在酶工程中的角色应定位为「假设生成器」而非「结论来源」，所有预测必须经过实验验证（文中多个案例支持此观点）。 - 合成生物学的调控层级正在从「基因→转录→翻译」向「翻译后/蛋白质组装」延伸，这为蛋白质结构计算研究提供了新的应用出口：预测哪些蛋白对适合 MTGase 介导的交联、如何设计正交标签等。 07 方法总览 本文为综述，无原始实验方法。但提出了一个集成框架（Figure 2），其逻辑流程为： 输入 ：环境信号与系统感知（Stage 1）→ 多组学数据采集（基因组、转录组、蛋白质组、代谢组、通量组）（Stage 2） 计算设计 ：AI 辅助的酶设计、结构预测（AlphaFold）、代谢网络建模、机器学习预测（Stage 3） 合成生物学工具 It reviews experimental and computational advances, identifies key barriers, and proposes an integrated framework for future engineering. Visible evidence base The manuscript cites numerous primary research articles, including specific experimental examples (e.g., PsaA amidase, PamC amidase, MTGase immobilization on magnetic nanoparticles, computational enzyme engineering studies). Figures 1 and 2 are described in text but not visible to the reviewer. Missing materials affecting confidence Figures 1 and 2 are not provided. Tables 1, 2, and 3 are referenced but not included. No supplementary information was supplied. The absence of these visual and tabular elements limits full assessment of the framework's clarity and completeness. Reviewer Overall assessment This is a well-structured and thoughtfully written review that addresses a timely and interesting topic: the potential of MTGase as a protein-level control element in synthetic biology. The authors are careful to distinguish established capabilities from prospective applications, which is a strength. However, the review is largely conceptual and forward-looking, with limited critical depth in some sections. The central thesis, while plausible, is not supported by a systematic analysis of the existing evidence. The manuscript would benefit from a more rigorous and critical evaluation of the literature, clearer definitions of key concepts, and a more explicit discussion of the feasibility and potential impact of the proposed framework. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in synthetic biology, metabolic engineering, and enzyme biotechnology would find this review of interest. The focus on post-translational control and spatial organization as a complement to transcriptional regulation is relevant to those designing dynamic and robust microbial production systems. The review also touches on computational enzyme design, which may appeal to a computational biology audience. Major strengths The manuscript clearly articulates a distinct perspective on MTGase, moving beyond its traditional food-industry role to propose it as a synthetic biology tool. The authors consistently and commendably distinguish between experimentally validated findings and speculative or prospective applications. The review is well-organized, with a logical flow from general enzyme classes to specific MTGase properties and future integration strategies. The discussion of limitations (e.g., off-target crosslinking, proteostatic burden) is relevant and identifies key challenges for the field. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Support for central thesis Claim pointer The central thesis is that MTGase "may provide a protein level engineering interface between genetic regulation and cellular phenotype" and that it can be a "controllable protein level platform for synthetic biology." Evidence pointer Sections "Scope of the review", "MTGase as a programmable synthetic biology tool", "Discussion" Concern The central thesis is presented as a plausible vision, but the review does not provide a critical, evidence-based assessment of whether this vision is realistic. The manuscript cites examples of MTGase use in extracellular contexts (e.g., biomaterials, immobilization) but does not systematically analyze the evidence for its successful use as an intracellular tool in microbial hosts. The discussion of challenges (e.g., off-target crosslinking) is largely theoretical. The review would be significantly strengthened by a dedicated section that critically evaluates any existing experimental evidence for intracellular MTGase applications, even if limited, and clearly states what evidence is missing to support the central claim. Why it matters The review's primary contribution is its central thesis. Without a rigorous evaluation of the evidence for and against this thesis, the manuscript risks being a well-written opinion piece rather than a critical scientific review. The claim that MTGase can be a "controllable" platform is not supported by evidence demonstrating control in a complex intracellular environment. Resolution test The authors should add a section that systematically reviews and critically evaluates all available experimental evidence for intracellular MTGase applications in microbial systems. This section should clearly state what has been demonstrated, what has failed, and what critical experiments are needed to validate the central thesis. The thesis should be reframed as a testable hypothesis with specific milestones. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Critical analysis and depth Claim pointer The manuscript claims to "critically examine" the transition from classical enzymes to engineered systems and to evaluate the "current limitations" of MTGase. Evidence pointer Sections "Amide transforming enzymes and evolution toward programmable biocatalysis", "Current limitations, engineering bottlenecks, and mitigation strategies" Concern The review is largely descriptive and uncritical. For example, the sections on amidases and asparaginases provide a summary of their functions and applications but do not critically compare their performance, stability, or engineering potential against each other or against MTGase. The "Current limitations" section lists challenges but does not deeply analyze the root causes or the relative importance of these challenges. The discussion of mitigation strategies is often generic (e.g., "protein engineering," "directed evolution") without a critical assessment of their likelihood of success. Why it matters A review's value lies in its critical synthesis. A descriptive summary of the literature, while useful, does not provide the deep insight expected of a high-quality review. The authors are well-positioned to provide a more critical perspective, given their stated expertise. Resolution test The authors should revise the manuscript to include more critical analysis. For example, they could compare the strengths and weaknesses of different engineering approaches, discuss why certain challenges are more fundamental than others, and critically evaluate the potential of different mitigation strategies. The "Current limitations" section should be reorganized to prioritize challenges based on their impact and tractability. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Clarity and definition of key concepts Claim pointer The manuscript uses terms like "programmable," "adaptive," "controllable," and "protein level control" to describe the proposed MTGase-based systems. Evidence pointer Throughout the manuscript, particularly in the Abstract, Introduction, and "MTGase as a programmable synthetic biology tool" section Concern These terms are used frequently but are not clearly defined. What specifically does "programmable" mean in this context? Is it the ability to target specific substrates via engineered tags? Is it the ability to control activity in time or space? What is the difference between "protein level control" and standard post-translational regulation? The lack of clear definitions makes it difficult to assess the novelty and feasibility of the proposed approach. Why it matters The manuscript's central argument rests on these concepts. Without clear definitions, the reader cannot fully understand what the authors are proposing or how it differs from existing approaches. This ambiguity weakens the manuscript's impact. Resolution test The authors should provide explicit, operational definitions of these key terms early in the manuscript. For example, they could define "programmable" as the ability to achieve predictable and controllable crosslinking of specific target proteins through the use of engineered recognition tags and/or engineered MTGase variants with defined substrate specificity. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Readability and structure Affected element Section "Amide transforming enzymes and evolution toward programmable biocatalysis" Evidence pointer Subsections on amidases, asparaginases, and other enzymes Issue The subsections on individual enzyme classes are somewhat formulaic, following a similar pattern of "function, applications, engineering." This becomes repetitive. Required correction Consider integrating the discussion of these enzymes more tightly around the central theme of the review. For example, instead of separate subsections, the authors could structure the section around key concepts, such as "substrate specificity," "engineering strategies," and "integration into synthetic circuits," and discuss how each enzyme class exemplifies these concepts. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Technical accuracy Affected element Section "Structural biology and catalytic mechanism" Evidence pointer Description of the catalytic mechanism Issue The description of the catalytic mechanism is accurate but very brief. A slightly more detailed description of the active site residues and the catalytic triad (Cys-His-Asp) would be helpful for readers unfamiliar with the enzyme. Required correction Add a sentence or two detailing the key catalytic residues and their roles in the acyl transfer reaction. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected element Section "MTagase as a programmable synthetic biology tool" Evidence pointer Subsection "Synthetic genetic circuits and dynamic regulation" Issue The discussion of integrating MTGase with genetic circuits is highly speculative and does not cite any specific examples where this has been attempted. Required correction The authors should either provide specific examples of such integration or more clearly state that this is a purely prospective area with no experimental precedent. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Section "Digital twin biofactories and autonomous design build test learn platforms" Evidence pointer Entire section Issue This section is very brief and reads more like a list of future trends than a substantive discussion. The connection to MTGase is particularly weak. Required correction Either expand this section to provide a more detailed discussion of how digital twins could specifically be applied to MTGase-based systems, or integrate this content into the "Future perspectives" section to avoid a fragmented discussion. Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Presentation Affected element Figures and Tables Evidence pointer Figures 1 and 2, Tables 1, 2, and 3 Issue The figures and tables are not provided, so their quality and relevance cannot be assessed. Required correction Ensure that the figures and tables are clear, informative, and directly support the text. Figure 1 should effectively summarize the enzyme classes and their applications. Figure 2 should clearly illustrate the proposed integrated framework. The tables should provide useful comparative data. Risk / unsupported claims The central claim that MTGase can serve as a "controllable protein level platform for synthetic biology" is a forward-looking hypothesis. The review does not provide sufficient experimental evidence to support this as an established capability, and the authors correctly note that intracellular applications remain to be demonstrated. This is a risk to the review's impact if not framed clearly as a hypothesis. The claim that "MTGase mediated protein assembly systems may support spatial biocatalysis through programmable enzyme clustering, scaffold formation, and biomolecular compartmentalization" is speculative. The cited evidence is from extracellular or in vitro systems, and the leap to intracellular microbial engineering is not supported by direct evidence. The statement that "AI guided protein engineering... can be used to connect protein sequence and structure with catalytic properties" is a general claim. The specific application to MTGase is supported by a few examples, but the review does not critically assess the general limitations of these computational approaches. The "Integrated microbial cell factory framework" presented in Figure 2 is a conceptual model. Its utility and validity cannot be assessed without the figure and without a more detailed explanation of how it would be implemented.

如何构建一个集成多模型AI方法的统一管线，以克服传统线性药物发现流程中AMP临床转化的关键瓶颈（稳定性差、效力不足、细胞毒性、新颖性有限）？ 为什么重要 : 全球AMR危机日益严峻，传统抗生素开发管线枯竭，AMP作为替代方案具有广谱活性和低耐药倾向，但其临床转化受限于多重相互关联的缺陷。AI驱动的多目标优化有望同时解决这些问题。 现有方法为何不足 : 传统方法以线性流程为主，各环节（活性预测、毒性筛选、稳定性评估、结构优化）相互独立，缺乏闭环反馈；单一模型仅优化单一目标，无法平衡效力与安全性等多维指标；且多数模型在重叠数据集上训练，泛化能力有限。 精确研究问题 : "Can a multi-model, closed-loop AI pipeline simultaneously optimize AMP efficacy, safety, novelty, and stability to reduce late-stage attrition and accelerate clinical translation?" 04 背景与发展脉络 （标注：此脉络基于本文框架，未经外部系统核验） 阶段 代表性方法 优点 局限 本文主张的位置 传统实验驱动 化学合成 + 表型筛选 可靠、直接 通量低、成本高、周期长 需被AI加速替代 新颖性筛选（基因组/蛋白序列比对）；(f) 结构预测（AlphaFold2/3）与分子对接（AutoDock Vina、DiffDock等）用于结构验证与机制解析；(g) 稳定性预测（蛋白酶切割位点、半衰期）。各模块在闭环迭代中协同工作。 2) 核心洞察 ： - 多目标同步优于串行筛选 ：将效力、毒性、稳定性、新颖性作为并行约束而非串行过滤，可避免早期过度筛选导致候选空间枯竭。 - 结构信息作为连接层 ：AlphaFold等结构预测工具不仅用于验证，更可作为连接序列空间与功能空间的桥梁，为对接和机制研究提供输入。 - 闭环反馈是管线核心 ：湿实验数据应回流至计算模型，形成"设计-预测-验证-学习"的迭代循环，而非一次性筛选。 - 数据集质量决定模型上限 ：数据重叠、负样本缺失、标签异质性是当前AMP计算模型泛化能力的根本限制。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] ： - 对蛋白质结构相关计算研究而言，本文的管线架构思想可迁移：任何"序列→功能"预测任务（如酶活性、结合亲和力）都可拆分为判别、生成、结构验证、稳定性评估等模块，并以闭环方式集成。 - 结构预测工具（AlphaFold）在多模块管线中的定位不仅是"最终验证"，更可作为中间特征提取器，为下游对接、动力学模拟提供起点。 - 数据集偏差问题在蛋白质计算领域普遍存在（如PDB偏向可溶性蛋白），本文对数据重叠和标签异质性的批判性讨论具有普适警示意义。 07 方法总览 输入 : 已知AMP序列数据库（正样本）、非AMP蛋白序列（负样本）、基因组/宏基因组数据、目标病原体信息 输出 : 优先化的候选AMP序列（附带预测的效力、毒性、稳定性、新颖性评分） 模块 : 1. 尚无完整"计算设计→临床批准"的AMP案例。最接近的pexiganan和iseganan均在III期失败，说明计算预测到临床转化仍有显著鸿沟。 算力成本 : 未提供具体算力需求。AlphaFold2/3和扩散模型等模块的计算成本可能较高，但文中未量化。 历史数据依赖 : 所有模型均依赖现有AMP数据库，这些数据库偏向已表征的阳离子、短序列AMP，可能限制探索新型化学空间。 模型依赖 : 各模块独立训练，模块间误差可能累积；生成模型的输出质量高度依赖训练数据分布。 最难情形 : 对S. aureus等革兰氏阳性菌的预测成功率显著低于E. coli（44.4% vs 95%），说明不同病原体的可预测性差异大。 群体/领域边界 : 结论主要适用于抗菌肽，对其他抗菌分子（如小分子、抗体）的可迁移性未验证。 有边界的复述 : 本文表明，多模型AI管线在AMP计算发现中展现出潜力，能够在体外和动物模型中产生较高比例的活性候选，但临床转化仍受限于生理环境复杂性、数据集偏差和模块间误差累积，尚无端到端临床成功案例。 12 作者自认局限 局限 具体表现 作者提出的未来方向 来源 数据集重叠与信息泄漏 同源序列跨训练/测试集分布导致性能虚高 相似性感知的划分、冗余控制、独立数据集评估 Limitations节 负样本稀缺 content, methodological soundness, reproducibility, and alignment with stated aims; no assessment of formatting or editorial compliance Shared manuscript claim summary The manuscript proposes that multi-model AI-driven pipelines integrating discriminative classifiers, generative models, potency and toxicity predictors, novelty filters, stability screens, and molecular docking can overcome key bottlenecks in antimicrobial peptide (AMP) discovery, reduce late-stage attrition, and accelerate translation from in silico prediction to wet-lab validation. Visible evidence base Narrative review with cited literature; tables summarizing model performance (Tables 1–10); figures illustrating pipeline architecture (Figures 1–15); no primary experimental data or code provided Missing materials affecting confidence No code, datasets, or benchmark implementations; no quantitative comparison of proposed pipelines against existing methods; no wet-lab validation data; figure contents not fully described in text; table details (e.g., exact metrics, dataset versions) not fully specified Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript provides a broad, well-structured narrative review of AI-driven AMP discovery, with a useful emphasis on multi-objective, closed-loop pipeline design. The authors correctly identify key limitations in current approaches, including dataset bias, negative-set construction, and over-generalization. However, the manuscript is largely descriptive and does not provide a concrete, reproducible pipeline architecture, benchmark evaluation, or comparative analysis. The central claim that such pipelines "overcome key bottlenecks" is asserted rather than demonstrated. The review would benefit from a more critical, quantitative treatment of existing methods and a clearer articulation of what is novel relative to prior reviews. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational biologists and bioinformaticians working on antimicrobial peptide discovery, machine learning practitioners interested in drug design applications, and microbiologists seeking an overview of AI tools for AMP development. The review may also be of interest to researchers in AMR policy and translational medicine who want a high-level understanding of computational approaches in this space. HN、Hα、13Cα、15N 化学位移作为伪标签，在迭代模拟退火框架中引入异核维度约束与交替评分策略，使超过 100 个氨基酸残基的未标记蛋白（HEWL 103 aa、TRX 107 aa、ArsC 139 aa）实现全自动主链归属，准确率分别为 84%、85%、71%。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：如何在不进行 13C/15N 同位素标记的前提下，对超过 100 个氨基酸残基的蛋白质实现可靠的自动化 NMR 主链共振归属？ 为什么重要 ：同位素标记成本高、周期长、表达困难，是 NMR 在蛋白质研究中的主要瓶颈；同时，AI 结构预测（如 AlphaFold）需要实验验证，而 NMR 是关键的验证手段。若能免除标记，将大幅降低 NMR 应用门槛，加速 AI 预测结构的实验确认。 现有方法为何不足 ：作者前期工作（基于 MCD 方法 + AI 预测 HN/Hα 化学位移）仅适用于 <100 残基的蛋白（如泛素 76 aa）。对更大蛋白，两个问题导致收敛失败：(1) AI 化学位移预测对部分残基偏差增大，削弱评分函数判别力；(2) 二维同核谱峰重叠严重，NOE 约束可靠性下降，组合空间爆炸。 精确研究问题 ：Can a pseudo-labeling strategy that integrates multi-AI predicted 13Cα and 15N chemical shifts into an iterative simulated annealing framework achieve reliable automated backbone resonance assignment for unlabeled proteins exceeding 100 amino acid residues? 04 背景与发展脉络 注：此脉络主要基于本文框架，部分经外部核验（标注）。 1980s–1990s：人工 MCD 方法时代 。研究者用主链直接（main chain direct, MCD）方法人工归属未标记蛋白的二维 NMR 谱，极其耗时耗力。计算机辅助方法因当时算力与算法限制未成主流。[本文框架] 2000s–2010s：同位素标记成为标准 。13C/15N 标记 + 三维异核实验（HNCA、HNCO 等）成为常规归属手段，但成本高、表达难。[外部核验：NMR 结构生物学标准实践] 2020s：AI 化学位移预测兴起 。UCBShift2.0、EFG-CS、PLMs 等工具可从序列或结构预测化学位移，精度逐步提升。[外部核验：UCBShift 系列、EFG-CS、PLM 文献] 2023–2025：AI 结构预测与实验验证需求爆发 。AlphaFold 等模型可高精度预测结构，但存在高置信度错误拓扑，需 NMR 等实验手段验证；同时 NMR 约束可融入 AI 结构生成框架。[本文引言引用 9–15] 本文位置 ：在前期工作（AI 预测 HN/Hα + SA 归属 <100 aa 未标记蛋白）基础上，引入多 AI 集成 + 异核伪标签 + 交替评分，将适用范围扩展到 >100 aa，并展示在 AI 结构验证与配体结合位点确认中的潜在应用。 05 表面方法 ：用三种 AI 化学位移预测工具（UCBShift2.0、EFG-CS、PLMs）分别预测目标蛋白每个残基的 HN、Hα、13Cα、15N 化学位移，将预测值作为"伪标签"；在迭代模拟退火框架中，将实验观测的交叉峰与伪标签进行匹配评分，通过交替使用不同评分策略逐步固定高置信度归属。 核心洞察 ： 异核维度约束可以替代同位素标记的部分信息 。虽然未标记蛋白无法直接实验测量 13Cα 和 15N 化学位移，但 AI 预测的异核化学位移可以作为"计算伪标签"引入评分函数，从而在二维同核谱严重重叠时提供额外的判别维度。这本质上是 用计算预测弥补实验信息的缺失 ，将"实验-计算"边界向计算侧推移。 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] ：在实验数据不足或质量受限时， 多源计算预测的集成 + 迭代自举（pseudo-labeling） 可以显著扩展自动化方法的适用范围。这与半监督学习中的伪标签思想高度一致——先用高置信度预测固定部分变量，再逐步扩展。对蛋白质结构计算研究而言，这意味着：当实验约束稀疏时，AI 预测（化学位移、距离图、接触图等）可作为软约束融入优化框架，而非仅作为最终验证工具。 07 方法总览 输入 ： 未标记蛋白样品（~0.5 mM，50 mM 磷酸钠缓冲液 pH 5.0，10% D2O） 实验谱：1H-1H >14 h/异核谱；未标记蛋白浓度需 ~0.5 mM。这些条件并非所有实验室都具备。 oracle/真值输入 ：AI 化学位移预测（UCBShift2.0、EFG-CS、PLMs）是核心 oracle，其预测精度直接决定归属质量；BMRB 参考归属作为评估基准。 端到端状态 ：方法实现了从原始谱图到主链归属的自动化流程，但自旋系统提取仍需人工干预（"pre-extracted spin system data"），并非全自动。 算力成本 ：SA 每轮 100 次独立运行，ArsC 需 15 轮，总运行次数达 1500 次；虽未给出具体耗时，但计算成本显著高于简单贪心方法。 历史数据依赖 ：RF+SVM 氨基酸类型分类器依赖 BMRB 训练数据；AI 化学位移预测工具的训练集覆盖度影响泛化。 模型依赖 ：结果高度依赖三种 AI 预测工具的准确性；工具更新或替换可能改变性能。 最难情形 ：139 aa 的 ArsC 准确率降至 71%，且需 15 轮才收敛，表明分子量增大时性能显著下降。作者归因于 NOE 谱峰重叠和 AI 预测精度下降的协同效应。 群体/领域边界 ：仅测试 3 种球状蛋白，未覆盖膜蛋白、 intrinsically disordered proteins（IDPs）、多结构域蛋白或蛋白复合物。 不确定性 ：未报告置信区间或多次独立实验的标准差；"准确率"基于与 BMRB 参考归属的单次比较。 有边界的复述 ：本文证明，在 950 MHz 谱仪 + 低温探头条件下，通过三 AI 工具集成的伪标签策略，可在无同位素标记的情况下对 103–139 aa 的球状蛋白实现 71–85% 的主链归属准确率；该方法在更大蛋白或更复杂体系上的表现尚未验证。 12 作者自认局限 局限 具体表现 作者提出的未来方向 ：unverified Review setup Input scope Full manuscript text including abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion, and supplementary data description. Assessment boundary Scientific and technical evaluation of the proposed pseudo-labeling approach for automated NMR resonance assignment of unlabeled proteins exceeding 100 amino acid residues. Assessment is limited to the provided manuscript content. Shared manuscript claim summary The authors present a computational pipeline that integrates AI-predicted chemical shifts (HN, Hα, 13Cα, 15N) from three tools (UCBShift2.0, EFG-CS, PLMs) into an iterative simulated annealing framework with alternating scoring schemes, enabling automated backbone resonance assignment of unlabeled proteins larger than 100 residues. Demonstrated on hen egg white lysozyme (HEWL, 129 aa), thioredoxin (TRX, 107 aa), and arsenate reductase (ArsC, 139 aa), with reported assignment accuracies of 84%, 85%, and 71%, respectively. Visible evidence base Abstract; Introduction; Methods sections including NMR spectroscopy, pseudo-labeling approach, and assignment workflow; Results and discussions with Figures 1-5 and Tables 1-2; Conclusion; Data availability statement. Missing materials affecting confidence Raw NMR spectra, detailed spin system extraction protocols, parameter settings for the simulated annealing algorithm, validation metrics beyond assignment accuracy, comparison with existing automated assignment tools, and the supplementary data file referenced as "Multimedia component 1" were not available for assessment. Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript addresses a relevant and timely problem in structural biology, namely the validation of AI-predicted protein structures using NMR without isotopic labeling. The proposed pseudo-labeling strategy is conceptually interesting and represents a logical extension of the authors' prior work on ubiquitin. However, the evidence presented is insufficient to fully establish the reliability and generalizability of the method. Key technical details are missing, the reported accuracies are modest, and the validation approach lacks rigor in several respects. The manuscript would benefit from additional benchmarking, error analysis, and clarification of the methodology before the claims can be considered fully supported. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in NMR spectroscopy, structural biology, and computational biology would be interested, particularly those seeking to reduce the cost and technical barriers of protein structure determination. The work may also appeal to the AI-driven protein structure prediction community, as it offers an experimental validation pathway for predicted models. Additionally, laboratories without specialized NMR expertise but with access to high-field instruments could find the automated aspect attractive. Major strengths 1) The problem addressed is of practical importance, as isotope labeling remains a bottleneck in NMR-based structural studies. 2) The integration of multiple AI prediction tools into a consensus scoring framework is a sensible strategy to mitigate individual tool biases. 3) The pseudo-labeling concept, using AI-predicted heteronuclear shifts as computational substitutes for experimental labeling, is creative and potentially impactful. 4) The iterative alternating scoring scheme is a thoughtful design to leverage complementary information across spectral dimensions. 5) The demonstration on three proteins of different sizes provides some evidence of generalizability. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The manuscript claims that the method enables "reliable automated backbone resonance assignment for unlabeled proteins exceeding 100 amino acid residues." Evidence pointer Results and discussions, Table 1 Concern The reported assignment accuracies are 84% (HEWL), 85% (TRX), and 71% (ArsC). These figures indicate that a substantial fraction of residues (16-29%) are incorrectly assigned. The manuscript does not provide an analysis of the nature or distribution of these errors. It is unclear whether errors are concentrated in specific regions (e.g., flexible loops, termini) or randomly distributed. Without this information, the claim of "reliable" assignment is not well supported. Moreover, the accuracy metric itself is not clearly defined (e.g., residue-level vs. spin-system-level, and how partial assignments are counted). Why it matters For the method to be useful in practice, users need to know where errors are likely to occur and how to interpret the confidence of individual assignments. A 71-85% accuracy range may be insufficient for many downstream applications, such as structure calculation or binding site validation, where incorrect assignments could lead to erroneous conclusions. Resolution test Provide a detailed error analysis, including per-residue accuracy as a function of sequence position, secondary structure, and solvent accessibility. Define the accuracy metric precisely and report precision and recall separately. If possible, compare assigned chemical shifts with experimentally determined values for a subset of residues to validate the assignments independently. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The manuscript states that the method "effectively resolves severe cross-peak overlap during the automated assignment process by introducing heteronuclear dimensional constraints." Evidence pointer Methods, Pseudo-labelling approach; Results and discussions, Figures 2-3 Concern The mechanism by which the pseudo-labeling strategy resolves cross-peak overlap is not quantitatively demonstrated. The manuscript shows schematic figures and heat maps, but there is no quantitative analysis of how many ambiguous assignments were resolved by the heteronuclear constraints versus the homonuclear data alone. The authors do not report the number of spin systems that were ambiguous at each stage, nor do they quantify the improvement attributable to the pseudo-labeling approach. Why it matters The central claim of the paper is that the pseudo-labeling strategy overcomes the convergence failure observed for larger proteins. Without a clear demonstration that the heteronuclear constraints are responsible for the improved performance, the causal link between the proposed method and the reported results is not established. Resolution test Perform ablation studies where the assignment is run with and without the heteronuclear constraints, and report the resulting accuracies and convergence behavior. Quantify the number of spin systems that were resolved uniquely by the heteronuclear information. Provide a detailed example of a specific ambiguous region that was resolved by the pseudo-labeling approach. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The manuscript claims that the method is "fully automated" and that the workflow is applicable to "researchers without specialized NMR expertise." Evidence pointer Methods, Assignment workflow; Results and discussions Concern The manuscript does not describe the level of manual intervention required at various stages of the pipeline. Spin system extraction from COSY, TOCSY, HSQC, and HMQC spectra is a non-trivial step that typically requires expert judgment, especially in crowded regions. The authors do not specify whether spin system identification was performed manually, semi-automatically, or fully automatically. If manual curation was involved, the claim of full automation is overstated. Why it matters The stated goal of lowering the technical barrier for non-experts depends critically on the degree of automation. If expert intervention is required for spectral interpretation, the practical utility of the method for the target audience is diminished. Resolution test Clearly describe the spin system extraction procedure, including any manual steps. If manual curation was used, quantify the time and expertise required. Ideally, demonstrate the pipeline on a dataset where spin systems are extracted automatically without expert intervention, and report the resulting accuracy. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Scientific importance Claim pointer The manuscript states that the approach "will lower the technical barrier to biomolecular NMR, enabling researchers without specialized NMR expertise to employ NMR spectroscopy in fundamental life science research and drug development." Evidence pointer Abstract; Conclusion Concern The broader impact claim is not supported by the data presented. The method requires high-field NMR spectrometers (≥800 MHz) with cryoprobes and acquisition times exceeding 14 hours per heteronuclear experiment. These requirements represent significant infrastructure and time investments that may not be accessible to many potential users. The manuscript does not discuss the cost-benefit trade-off compared to conventional isotope labeling, which, while expensive, is a well-established and reliable approach. Why it matters The significance of the work depends on whether it genuinely lowers barriers to NMR use. If the method still requires specialized equipment and long acquisition times, the practical advantage over conventional approaches may be limited. Resolution test Provide a quantitative comparison of the total cost and time required for the proposed method versus conventional isotope labeling and assignment, including sample preparation, NMR acquisition, and data analysis. Discuss the accessibility of the required instrumentation and whether the method is feasible in typical structural biology laboratories. Concern ID R1-M5 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The manuscript claims that "integrating predictions from multiple tools produces a substantially more robust and accurate assignment than any single tool alone." Evidence pointer Results and discussions, Table 2 Concern The comparison in Table 2 shows that individual tools perform poorly on some proteins (e.g., PLMs at 7% on HEWL), but the integrated approach achieves 84-85% on HEWL and TRX. However, the manuscript does not explain why the integration is effective or how the consensus scoring is weighted. It is unclear whether the improvement is due to genuine complementarity or simply to a majority-voting effect. Additionally, the performance of the integrated approach on ArsC (71%) is not substantially better than the best individual tool (EFG-CS at 68% for HEWL, but the ArsC column shows EFG at 30%, UCB at 33%, PLMs at 50%), suggesting that integration does not always provide a large benefit. Why it matters Understanding the source of the improvement is important for assessing the robustness of the method and for potential users who may have access to only one or two prediction tools. Resolution test Provide a more detailed analysis of the consensus scoring mechanism, including the weights assigned to each tool and the sensitivity of the results to these weights. Report the performance of all pairwise combinations of tools to assess the marginal contribution of each. Discuss scenarios where integration may not be beneficial. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established 1) Lack of ablation studies demonstrating the specific contribution of the pseudo-labeling heteronuclear constraints to the reported assignment accuracy (R1-M2). 2) Insufficient error analysis, including the distribution and nature of incorrect assignments (R1-M1). 3) Unclear degree of automation in spin system extraction, which is critical for the claimed accessibility of the method (R1-M3). 4) Incomplete specification of the simulated annealing parameters and scoring function details, preventing reproducibility (R1-m2). 5) The accuracy metric is not precisely defined, and the reported values (71-85%) may not be sufficient for the claimed applications (R1-M1). Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The pseudo-labeling concept, using AI-predicted heteronuclear shifts as computational substitutes for isotopic labeling, is a creative and original contribution that extends prior work in a meaningful way. Scientific importance: The problem of reducing the cost and complexity of NMR-based structure validation is important, particularly in the context of AI-driven structure prediction. However, the demonstrated performance (71-85% accuracy) and the requirement for high-field instruments with long acquisition times limit the immediate practical impact. Interdisciplinary readership: The work bridges NMR spectroscopy, computational biology, and AI, and would appeal to researchers in these fields. Technical soundness: The methodology is plausible, but the evidence provided is insufficient to fully establish its reliability. Key technical details are missing, and the validation is not sufficiently rigorous. Readability for nonspecialists: The manuscript is generally well-written and accessible, with clear figures and a logical structure. However, some technical aspects, such as the PCA-based scoring and the SA algorithm, may be challenging for readers without a computational background. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved. The core idea is promising and relevant, but the manuscript requires substantial revisions to address the technical concerns outlined above, particularly the need for ablation studies, error analysis, and clarification of the automation level. The reported accuracies, while modest, may be acceptable for specific applications if the limitations are clearly stated and the method is shown to be robust across a wider range of proteins. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that the method enables "reliable automated backbone resonance assignment" is not fully supported given the reported accuracies of 71-85% and the lack of error analysis. The claim that the pseudo-labeling strategy "effectively resolves severe cross-peak overlap" is not quantitatively demonstrated. The claim that the method "will lower the technical barrier to biomolecular NMR" is not supported by a cost-benefit analysis and may be overstated given the requirement for high-field instruments and long acquisition times. The generalizability of the method beyond the three tested proteins is not established, and the manuscript does not discuss potential failure modes for other protein classes (e.g., membrane proteins, intrinsically disordered proteins). The statement that the first-round assignments are "particularly well suited" for validating AI-predicted binding sites is speculative and not supported by experimental validation of this specific application.

Abstract only Assessment boundary Claims and evidence presented in the abstract; no access to methods, figures, tables, or supplementary material Shared manuscript claim summary The authors present RNADaemon, a reinforcement learning framework that applies adaptive external force-field biases to steer all-atom molecular dynamics simulations toward native-like RNA tertiary structures, trained on 479 monomeric RNA structures and evaluated on 14 test cases. The agent reportedly approaches SimRNA and FARFAR2 in median RMSD, recovers global folds of most reference structures, but underperforms AlphaFold 3 and trRosettaRNA. The authors attribute a performance ceiling to the scalar Bellman error and claim this is the first continuous-action deep RL application with all-atom force fields for RNA tertiary structure prediction. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no quantitative results, figures, tables, or methodological details provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, training and evaluation protocols, hyperparameters, baseline comparison details, statistical significance tests, and code availability Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a technically ambitious framework that combines deep reinforcement learning with all-atom molecular dynamics for RNA structure prediction. The core idea is novel and potentially of interest to the structural biology and machine learning communities. However, the abstract provides insufficient quantitative detail to evaluate the strength of the reported results. The performance claims are stated qualitatively, and the central diagnostic claim regarding the scalar Bellman error is presented without supporting evidence. The framing is honest about current limitations relative to state-of-the-art methods, which is commendable, but the evidence base is too thin to establish the case for the framework's utility or the diagnostic insight. Major strengths The formulation of RNA tertiary structure prediction as a Markov Decision Process with continuous-action Soft Actor-Critic is conceptually novel and represents a meaningful departure from existing prediction paradigms. The honest reporting of performance relative to AlphaFold 3 and trRosettaRNA is scientifically appropriate. The identification of a specific information bottleneck, the scalar Bellman error, provides a concrete hypothesis for future investigation. The claim of approaching SimRNA and FARFAR2 in median RMSD is vague without actual numbers or statistical comparisons. 01 基本信息 标题 ：Branching Suppresses Self-Aggregation while Preserving Membrane Association in SET-M33: An Atomistic Molecular Dynamics Study 作者 ：Satvati S; Rigoli M; Fortuna S; Falciani C; Pini A; Rocchia W 单位 ：未提供（通讯作者 Walter Rocchia，推测为意大利 Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia 相关机构，但原文未明确） 期刊/平台 ：bioRxiv（预印本） 年份 ：2026（预印本日期 2026-10-13） 论文类型 ：计算研究（all-atom MD 模拟） 领域 ：抗菌肽（AMP）结构-活性关系；分支多肽自聚集与膜结合；蛋白质/多肽构象采样 关键词 ：antimicrobial peptide, branched peptide, SET-M33, Q33, molecular dynamics, self-aggregation, membrane binding, anionic bilayer DOI/arXiv ：10.64898/2026.10.12.757849 代码 ：未提供 数据 ：未提供（模拟轨迹未公开） 阅读日期 ：2026-05-14（按当前日期） 在课题方向中的位置 ：本文属于「蛋白质/多肽构象与互作 × 物理模拟（MD）」方向，具体为分支拓扑对多肽自聚集和膜结合行为的调控机制研究。与 AlphaFold 等结构预测方法无直接关联，但为多肽构象采样、多肽-膜互作模拟提供了可迁移的方法学参考（如非标准残基力场参数化、hydration-tuning 增强采样）。 02 一句话总结 本文通过全原子 MD 模拟比较四分支 SET-M33 与其线性分支序列 Q33 在水溶液和阴离子膜模型中的行为，发现分支拓扑通过空间位阻和高阳离子电荷抑制多肽-多肽自聚集，同时通过多价静电作用维持与膜的紧密结合，两者均以表面结合为主而非穿膜。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：分支化修饰如何改变抗菌肽的自聚集倾向和膜结合行为？具体而言，四分支 SET-M33 与其线性对应序列 Q33 在自聚集、膜结合模式、二级结构稳定性方面有何差异？ 为什么重要 ：分支化（dendrimeric/MAP）是提高 AMP 稳定性和活性的常用策略，但分支化如何从分子层面改变肽-肽和肽-膜相互作用的平衡尚不清楚。理解这一机制有助于合理设计更优的分支 AMP 构建体。 现有方法为何不足 ：实验上，高度阳离子、易聚集的 AMP 难以在原子分辨率下表征其聚集路径和膜结合构象；已有的 MD 研究多针对线性 AMP，缺乏对分支拓扑的系统比较。 精确研究问题 ：Can tetra-branching of the Q33 sequence suppress peptide self-aggregation while preserving efficient membrane association at an atomistic level? No assessment of experimental data not included in the manuscript. Shared manuscript claim summary The manuscript claims that tetra-branched SET-M33 suppresses peptide self-aggregation while preserving membrane association, in contrast to its linear branch sequence Q33, which readily forms oligomers. The authors propose an atomistic rationale for this difference based on all-atom MD simulations. Visible evidence base Abstract, introduction, computational methodology, results and discussion sections, figures referenced (Figures 1-15), Table 1 (simulated systems), Table 2 (RDF/CN data). No raw simulation trajectories, no input parameter files, no force field modification details beyond description. Missing materials affecting confidence No supplementary information file was provided (only a statement that representative snapshots exist). No convergence metrics, no block-averaging or error analysis details beyond standard deviation. No control simulations (e.g., with neutral membranes or different ionic strengths). No experimental validation data for the simulation predictions. Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript addresses a relevant question in antimicrobial peptide design, namely how branching alters self-association and membrane binding. The simulation setup is reasonable and the comparison between linear and branched architectures is well motivated. However, the evidence presented is largely qualitative, and several key claims are not quantitatively supported by the data shown. The lack of convergence analysis, the absence of free-energy estimates, and the limited description of the enhanced sampling protocol weaken the conclusions. The manuscript is potentially interesting but requires substantial revision and additional analysis before the claims can be considered established. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in antimicrobial peptide design, computational biophysics of membrane-active peptides, and those interested in multivalent ligand-membrane interactions. The work may also be of interest to experimental groups working on SET-M33 or similar branched AMPs, as it provides a molecular-level hypothesis for their observed behavior. Major strengths The comparison between linear and branched architectures with equivalent sequence units is a well-designed approach. The use of multiple complementary analyses (contacts, RDF, SASA, hydration) is commendable. The manuscript is clearly written and the figures appear to support the qualitative narrative. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "SET-M33 remained more dispersed, as the branched scaffold and its high cationic charge limited peptide-peptide association while allowing multivalent membrane binding." Evidence pointer Results and Discussion, "M33 Membrane Association and Suppressed Self-Aggregation" section; Figure 8 Concern The claim that SET-M33 suppresses self-aggregation is based on visual inspection of density maps and qualitative descriptions of contact analysis. No quantitative measure of aggregation propensity (e.g., cluster size distributions, aggregation free energies, or mean cluster lifetimes) is provided. The statement that "SET-M33 remained largely dispersed" is not supported by any numerical metric. Why it matters The central conclusion of the manuscript rests on the difference in aggregation behavior between Q33 and M33. Without quantitative metrics, the reader cannot assess the magnitude of the effect or whether the difference is statistically significant given the short simulation times and limited sampling. Resolution test Provide cluster size distributions over time, mean cluster sizes with error bars across replicas, and a statistical test comparing Q33 and M33 aggregation. Alternatively, compute potential of mean force (PMF) between two peptides of each architecture to quantify association free energies. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "Hydration-tuning enhanced sampling was applied to the system containing 10 Q33 peptides in water... allowing the effective hydration of selected species to be tuned and thereby accelerating association events." Evidence pointer Computational Methodology, "Hydration-Tuning Enhanced Sampling" section Concern The enhanced sampling method is described only by reference to prior work. The specific implementation details for this system are not provided: how the bias is scaled, how the "reduction" is calculated, what the coupling parameter is, and how the three bias levels (90%, 80%, 50%) were chosen. More critically, the authors state that "the resulting trajectories were not used to infer equilibrium populations," yet they use these biased trajectories to draw conclusions about aggregation propensity ("Q33 rapidly formed compact assemblies containing up to nine peptides"). The logic of using a non-equilibrium biased method to support a claim about intrinsic aggregation propensity is unclear. Why it matters The enhanced sampling results are used as key evidence for Q33 aggregation propensity. If the method is not rigorously described and its limitations not properly accounted for, the conclusions drawn from it are not reliable. Resolution test Provide a detailed description of the bias potential, its functional form, and how the reduction level is computed. Show that the observed aggregation is not an artifact of the bias by demonstrating that the same contacts are sampled in unbiased simulations at longer timescales, or by computing the bias-induced shift in the aggregation free energy. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "Both architectures associated rapidly with the bilayer but remained predominantly surface-bound, without persistent pore formation or complete insertion." Evidence pointer Results and Discussion, "Membrane Binding Mode" section Concern The claim that no pore formation or insertion occurs is based on 300 ns simulations (and 1 μs for selected M33 systems). This timescale is very short for observing membrane disruption events, which typically occur on microsecond to millisecond timescales. The authors acknowledge this limitation in the text, but the claim is still presented as a finding rather than as a limitation of the simulation timescale. Why it matters The absence of pore formation in short simulations does not establish that the peptides cannot form pores. The claim as stated overreaches the evidence. Resolution test Rephrase the claim to explicitly state that no pore formation was observed within the simulated timescales, and discuss the timescale limitation more prominently. Alternatively, perform longer simulations or use enhanced sampling methods to probe membrane disruption. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Scientific importance Claim pointer "Overall, these results suggest that branched topology reduces uncontrolled peptide self-aggregation while maintaining efficient membrane engagement. This provides an atomistic rationale for the distinct behavior of SET-M33 relative to its linear branch sequence." Evidence pointer Conclusions section Concern The manuscript does not connect the simulation findings to the experimentally observed differences in antibacterial activity or stability between M33 and Q33. The introduction mentions that M33 shows increased resistance to proteases and peptidases, but the simulations do not address proteolytic stability. The relevance of the observed aggregation differences to the biological activity is asserted but not demonstrated. Why it matters The broader significance of the work depends on linking the molecular-level observations to the functional differences that motivate the study. Without this connection, the impact of the findings is limited. Resolution test Discuss how the observed differences in aggregation and membrane binding might relate to the experimentally measured antibacterial activity and stability. If possible, compare simulation predictions with experimental data on M33 and Q33 behavior. Concern ID R1-M5 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "The initial models were constructed with α-helical Q33 segments, including the four branch segments of M33." Evidence pointer Computational Methodology, "Peptide Models and System Construction" section; Results and Discussion, "Secondary-Structure Evolution" section Concern The manuscript does not state how the initial α-helical conformations were generated, whether the helical content was stable during equilibration, or whether the results depend on the initial conformation. The secondary-structure analysis reports average helical content but does not show the time evolution or the distribution across replicas. Why it matters The secondary-structure results are used to support the claim that Q33 is stabilized by membrane binding while M33 is not. If the initial helical bias influences the results, the conclusions may not be robust. Resolution test Provide time series of secondary-structure content for each replica, and discuss whether the initial helical conformation relaxes to a common ensemble. Consider running simulations from different initial conformations (e.g., fully extended) to test convergence. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Readability Affected element Abstract Evidence pointer Abstract Issue The abstract states "to do this, systems containing equivalent numbers of Q33 sequence units were simulated." This phrasing is awkward and the connection to the preceding sentence is unclear. Required correction Rephrase for clarity, e.g., "Systems were constructed with equivalent numbers of Q33 sequence units to enable direct comparison." Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Technical soundness Affected element Computational Methodology, "Peptide Models and System Construction" Evidence pointer Computational Methodology section Issue The lipid composition is described as a ratio of 2:1.3:1 for DOPE, DPPG, and DPPE. The use of a non-integer ratio (1.3) is unusual and the total number of lipids per leaflet (245) is not divisible by the sum of the ratio components (4.3). This suggests the actual numbers of each lipid type are not integers, which is impossible. Required correction Clarify the exact number of each lipid type in the bilayer. If the ratio is approximate, state the exact composition used. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Technical soundness Affected element Computational Methodology, "Molecular Dynamics Protocol" Evidence pointer Computational Methodology section Issue The manuscript states that "Electrostatic and van der Waals interactions were truncated at 1.2 nm." This is a relatively short cutoff for electrostatic interactions, and the use of PME with a 1.2 nm real-space cutoff is standard, but the manuscript should clarify whether the van der Waals interactions were simply truncated or if a switching function was used. Required correction Specify the treatment of van der Waals interactions at the cutoff (e.g., plain truncation, switch function) and justify the choice. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Readability Affected element Results and Discussion, "Membrane Coverage, Lateral Organization, and Contact Distance" Evidence pointer Results and Discussion section Issue The section title mentions "Contact Distance" but the text describes minimum-distance distributions. The term "contact distance" is not defined and could be confused with contact maps used elsewhere. Required correction Use consistent terminology, e.g., "peptide-membrane minimum distance" throughout. Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Technical soundness Affected element Results and Discussion, "Secondary-Structure Evolution" Evidence pointer Results and Discussion section Issue The reported helical content values are given as "25 ± 0.19%" and "42 ± 0.56%" for Q33 in solution and membrane-bound, respectively. The standard deviations are extremely small, which is surprising given the expected conformational variability. It is unclear whether these are standard deviations across replicas or across time. Required correction Clarify how the mean and standard deviation were computed, and report the variability across replicas separately from temporal fluctuations. Concern ID R1-m6 Severity Minor Axis Readability Affected element Conclusions Evidence pointer Conclusions section Issue The conclusions section largely repeats the results without adding new interpretation or discussing limitations. A more critical discussion of the limitations of the simulation approach would strengthen the manuscript. Required correction Add a paragraph discussing the limitations of the study, including timescale constraints, the simplified membrane model, and the lack of experimental validation. Concern ID R1-m7 Severity Minor Axis Technical soundness Affected element Computational Methodology, "Peptide Models and System Construction" Evidence pointer Computational Methodology section Issue The manuscript states that the branched core was parameterized using PyRED with RESP charges at HF/6-31G(d) level. This is a standard approach, but the manuscript does not report the resulting partial charges or provide validation of the parameterization (e.g., comparison with quantum mechanical reference data). Required correction Provide the partial charges as supplementary material or describe validation of the parameterization. Concern ID R1-m8 Severity Minor Axis Readability Affected element Results and Discussion, "Q33 Aggregation in Solution and at the Membrane" Evidence pointer Results and Discussion section Issue The text states "In the 8-Q33 system, dimers and occasional tetramers were observed at the membrane interface." It is unclear whether these observations are from a single trajectory or averaged across replicas, and how "occasional" is quantified. Required correction Specify the number of replicas and the frequency of tetramer formation across replicas. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that SET-M33 suppresses self-aggregation is not quantitatively supported; no aggregation metrics are provided. The use of hydration-tuning enhanced sampling to infer aggregation propensity is not rigorously justified, as the method is described only by reference and the biased trajectories are not used for equilibrium analysis. The claim that both architectures remain surface-bound without pore formation is only valid for the simulated timescales and should be stated as such. The connection between the simulation results and the experimentally observed differences in antibacterial activity and stability is asserted but not demonstrated. The secondary-structure analysis is based on initial α-helical models, and the dependence of the results on the initial conformation is not assessed. The lipid composition ratio (2:1.3:1) is internally inconsistent with the stated total number of lipids per leaflet.

01 基本信息 标题 ：Conserved molecular compatibility for MIZ1 function in cytokinin signaling in land plants 作者与单位 ：Smoljan A; Das S; Vladimirstev D; Teplova A; Tkachenka M; Yang W; Lu M; Benková E; Friml J（单位未提供，推测为 Institute of Science and Technology Austria, ISTA，依据致谢部分） 期刊/预印本平台 ：bioRxiv 年份 ：2026-10-12（预印本发布日期） 论文类型 ：预印本（研究论文） 领域 ：植物进化发育生物学；细胞分裂素信号转导；蛋白质进化与功能分化 关键词 ：MIZ1；hydrotropism；cytokinin signaling；land plant evolution；Marchantia polymorpha；protein-protein interaction DOI/arXiv 号 ：10.64898/2026.10.12.758437 代码 ：未提供 数据 ：未提供（转录组数据引用 MarpolBase 公开数据） 阅读日期 ：2026-10-13 该文在「蛋白质结构相关计算研究 × AI 方法/物理模拟」方向中的位置 ：本文属于「蛋白质结构预测 + 蛋白质-蛋白质对接」在进化生物学中的应用型研究。使用 AlphaFold2 预测蛋白结构、HDOCK 进行蛋白-蛋白对接，结合 BiFC 实验验证跨物种蛋白互作的特异性。核心方法学贡献在于将计算结构预测与实验互作验证相结合，用于解释蛋白质功能进化中的分子兼容性问题。对结构计算课题的可迁移点：跨物种蛋白互作界面的结构比较、AlphaFold 结构 + 对接预测互作特异性的工作流。 02 一句话总结 本文通过系统发育分析、跨物种功能互补实验、AlphaFold2 结构预测和 HDOCK 蛋白-蛋白对接，发现 MIZ1 蛋白是陆地植物中保守的细胞分裂素信号调控因子，但其与细胞分裂素受体的分子兼容性及发育功能在进化中发生了分化，根向水性（hydrotropism）是 MIZ1 在被子植物中衍生出的新功能。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：MIZ1 蛋白在拟南芥中介导根向水性反应，但 MIZ1 同源蛋白广泛存在于整个陆地植物谱系（包括无根植物如苔藓植物）。这些非被子植物中的 MIZ1 同源蛋白的祖先功能是什么？MIZ1 与细胞分裂素受体的互作是否在进化中保守？ 为什么重要 ：理解 MIZ1 蛋白家族的祖先功能有助于阐明根向水性这一重要环境适应性状的进化起源，同时揭示信号通路模块如何在进化中被"招募"到新的发育过程中。 现有方法为何不足 ：此前研究主要聚焦于拟南芥中 MIZ1 的向水性功能，缺乏对 MIZ1 蛋白家族在陆地植物进化中功能保守性与分化性的系统研究。跨物种功能互补实验和蛋白互作分析尚未被用于解析 MIZ1 的祖先功能。 精确的「Can ... ?」研究问题 ：Can MIZ1 orthologs from early-diverging land plants functionally substitute for Arabidopsis MIZ1 in hydrotropism and cytokinin sensitivity, and is the MIZ1-cytokinin receptor interaction conserved across land plants? 04 背景与发展脉络 注：以下脉络基于本文框架，未经外部核验。 MIZ1 的发现与功能鉴定阶段 ：通过正向遗传筛选在拟南芥中鉴定出 miz1 突变体，确立 MIZ1 为根向水性的关键调控因子（Kobayashi et al., 2007）。MIZ1 被定位于内质网（ER）相关蛋白，参与调控长距离 Ca²⁺ 信号（Shkolnik et al., 2018）。 MIZ1 结构域与系统发育分析阶段 ：MIZ1 结构域（原 DUF617）被鉴定为陆地植物特有结构域，系统发育分析显示 MIZ1 存在于所有陆地植物谱系但不存在于绿藻（Kobayashi et al., 2007; Fujii et al., 2018）。 MIZ1 与细胞分裂素信号交叉阶段 ：近期研究揭示拟南芥 MIZ1 通过与细胞分裂素受体（AHK2/3/4）互作调控细胞分裂素信号和稳态（Fu et al., 2025），将 MIZ1 功能从向水性扩展到激素信号调控。 本文的进化功能解析阶段 ：通过跨物种功能互补、CRISPR 突变体、AlphaFold2 结构预测和 HDOCK 对接，系统解析 MIZ1 在陆地植物中的祖先功能与进化分化，提出"向水性是 MIZ1 衍生功能"的假说。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 MIZ1 功能认知局限于拟南芥 此前研究几乎全部聚焦于拟南芥 MIZ1 的向水性功能，对非模式植物中 MIZ1 的功能缺乏了解 MIZ1 最初通过拟南芥向水性突变体筛选鉴定，研究范式以模式植物为主 Introduction 节 跨物种功能互补失败但机制不明 远缘植物 MIZ1 同源蛋白无法恢复拟南芥 miz1 突变体的向水性和细胞分裂素敏感性，但原因未知 作者假设可能是蛋白互作兼容性问题，而非蛋白本身功能丧失 Results 图 2、图 3 蛋白互作兼容性的分子基础不清 MIZ1 与细胞分裂素受体的互作界面和关键氨基酸残基未知 缺乏高分辨率复合物结构，仅依赖 AlphaFold 预测和对接模拟 Results 图 6 祖先功能与衍生功能的区分困难 无法仅通过序列保守性判断 MIZ1 的祖先功能 需要结合功能实验（突变体、互补、互作）与进化分析 Discussion 节 06 核心思想 1) 表面方法 ： - 系统发育分析鉴定陆地植物 MIZ1 同源蛋白 - 跨物种功能互补实验（拟南芥 miz1 突变体中表达异源 MIZ1） - Marchantia polymorpha CRISPR 突变体与过表达系的功能表征 - AlphaFold2 结构预测 + HDOCK 蛋白-蛋白对接 - BiFC 实验验证蛋白互作 2) 核心洞察 ： - MIZ1 蛋白家族的祖先功能是参与细胞分裂素信号调控，而非根向水性 - MIZ1 与细胞分裂素受体（AHK/CHK）的互作在陆地植物中保守，但互作的分子兼容性具有物种特异性 - 根向水性是 MIZ1 在被子植物谱系中被"招募"到根特异性环境响应通路的衍生功能 - 蛋白互作的物种特异性兼容性（而非蛋白功能本身）是跨物种功能互补失败的原因 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] ： - 蛋白家族的祖先功能不能仅通过模式生物的功能研究推断，需要结合跨物种功能实验 - 蛋白互作的分子兼容性（"lock-and-key"）可能在进化中比蛋白功能本身更快分化 - AlphaFold 结构预测 + 对接 + 实验验证（BiFC）是解析跨物种蛋白互作特异性的有效工作流 - 功能"招募"（recruitment）是进化中新功能产生的重要机制——一个保守的信号模块可以被不同谱系用于不同的发育过程 07 方法总览 输入 ：MIZ1 蛋白序列（拟南芥、地钱、小立碗藓、卷柏、无油樟等）；MIZ1 突变体材料；细胞分裂素受体序列 输出 ：MIZ1 蛋白家族的进化关系；跨物种功能互补表型；MIZ1-受体互作模型；Marchantia 突变体表型 模块 ： 1. 系统发育分析（HMMER 搜索 + 聚类 + 多方法建树） 2. 亚细胞定位分析（GFP 融合蛋白 + 共聚焦显微镜） 3. 跨物种功能互补（拟南芥 miz1 突变体 + 异源表达） 4.
