ILE/VAL/THR" but without the actual figures, these claims cannot be verified. The comparison to reference Ramachandran regions from Fig. 1 (also not provided) is impossible to assess. Why it matters The core scientific contribution of this manuscript is the visual and quantitative comparison between SSE-conditioned densities and classical Ramachandran regions. Without access to the figures, the validity of the described discrepancies, the claimed amino-acid-specific patterns, and the overall interpretation cannot be evaluated. This is not a minor omission but a fundamental gap in the evidence base. Resolution test Provide all figures (Fig. 1-4) and supplementary figures (Fig. S1-S16) with sufficient resolution and detail to verify the described patterns. The figures must clearly show the credible regions, the reference Ramachandran regions, and the data points for comparison. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Methodological transparency Claim pointer The manuscript states that conditioned densities are obtained by reweighting CBMD mixture models according to Eq. 2, and that entropy and Jensen-Shannon divergence calculations follow Eq. 14, 15, and 17. Evidence pointer Section 2.3, Section 3.1, Section 3.2 (equations not displayed in provided text) Concern The key equations (Eq. 2 for the conditional density, Eq. 14 for entropy, Eq. 15 and 17 for Jensen-Shannon divergence) are referenced but not displayed in the provided manuscript text. The reweighting formula is the methodological cornerstone of the paper, and its exact form determines whether the approach is valid. Similarly, the entropy calculation over binned Ramachandran space requires specification of binning strategy and boundary handling. Why it matters Without the explicit mathematical formulation, the methodology cannot be reproduced or independently verified. The validity of the reweighting approach depends on technical details such as how responsibilities are computed, whether normalization is handled correctly, and how the mixture components are combined. The reader cannot assess whether the approach is mathematically sound or whether there are hidden assumptions. Resolution test Display all referenced equations in full. Provide a complete derivation of the reweighting formula, including how responsibilities are estimated from the data and any assumptions about the relationship between the SSE-agnostic and SSE-conditioned models. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Statistical validation Claim pointer The manuscript claims that JS divergences between SSE-conditioned distributions are "driven principally by the backbone torsion angles" based on a comparison of full-space versus backbone-only divergences, with differences ranging from -0.048 to 0.063. Evidence pointer Section 3.2, Fig. S4, Fig. S5 (not provided) Concern The claim that backbone angles are the primary determinants of SSE labels is based on a comparison of JS divergence values, but the manuscript does not report any statistical significance testing or uncertainty quantification for these divergence estimates. The range of differences (-0.048 to 0.063) is reported without context regarding the magnitude of the divergences themselves. If the divergences are small, these differences could be substantial; if large, they could be negligible. Additionally, the side-chain-only analysis (Fig. S5) is described as showing smaller divergences, but the text notes these are "presented relative to that value using a different colormap," which complicates direct comparison. Why it matters The conclusion that backbone angles determine SSE labels is a key finding with implications for understanding secondary structure formation. If this claim is not statistically robust, the conclusion may be overstated. The manuscript should provide confidence intervals or bootstrap estimates for the divergence values, and should clearly report the absolute magnitudes of the divergences in both full-space and subspace analyses. Resolution test Provide statistical uncertainty estimates for all reported JS divergence values. Report the absolute divergence magnitudes alongside the differences. Consider permutation or bootstrap tests to establish whether the observed differences between full-space and backbone-only analyses are significant. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Claim substantiation Claim pointer The manuscript claims that the conditioned densities "provide a direct route to define GoF test" for identifying biases in generative engines, and that they offer "explicit control on SSE" that "remains difficult to enforce explicitly in current AI-based generative models." Evidence pointer Section 4 (Outlook) Concern The Outlook section makes several claims about applications that are not demonstrated anywhere in the manuscript. The claim about AlphaFold2's structure module using torsion angle tuples is presented without citation or detailed explanation. The assertion that the conditioned densities are "a tool of choice" for generating SSE-consistent conformations is not supported by any generative experiments or comparisons. The claim about difficulty in enforcing SSE control in AI-based models is presented as fact without supporting evidence or citations. Why it matters These claims extend beyond the demonstrated scope of the work. While speculative applications can be appropriate in an Outlook section, they should be clearly framed as possibilities rather than established capabilities. The comparison to AI-based generative models is particularly problematic without concrete evidence or benchmarks. Resolution test Either remove or reframe speculative claims as possibilities rather than capabilities. If the generative application is claimed, provide at minimum a proof-of-concept demonstration. If the comparison to AI models is retained, provide citations or a brief analysis supporting the claim about difficulty of SSE control. Concern ID R1-M5 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Data and reproducibility Claim pointer The manuscript states that all conditioned model parameters are publicly available on the Structural Bioinformatics Library website, along with Python code. Evidence pointer Section 3, footnote 1 Concern While the availability of code and parameters is commendable, the manuscript does not describe the computational resources required, the runtime for conditioning the models, or the memory requirements. More importantly, the manuscript does not describe how the PDB50 corpus was processed to obtain the torsion angle observations, what filtering or quality criteria were applied beyond the stated R-factor and resolution cutoffs, or how missing or undefined torsion angles were handled. Why it matters Reproducibility requires not just code availability but also a complete description of the data processing pipeline. The handling of missing torsion angles, the treatment of terminal residues, and the criteria for including or excluding observations can all affect the resulting distributions. Without this information, independent verification of the results is difficult. Resolution test Provide a complete description of the data processing pipeline, including any filtering criteria, handling of missing values, and the exact procedure for extracting torsion angles from PDB structures. Report computational requirements for the conditioning procedure. 分支。它不直接预测结构，而是提出一种从蛋白质基础模型（ESM-C）嵌入中提取 可复用、可比较、可定位 的生物概念方向（CAV）的通用框架。与 AlphaFold 等结构预测方法互补——CAV 不依赖结构，而是利用序列嵌入中已编码的结构/功能信息，可用于结构域定位、功能注释、结合界面特异性分析等任务。其「概念即方向」的思想可迁移到结构预测、构象采样、分子对接等场景中的特征分析与结果解释。 02 一句话总结 本文提出将生物概念（GO 功能、EC 酶活、Pfam 结构域、DNA 结合特异性、肿瘤相关细胞状态）表示为预训练基础模型嵌入空间中的线性方向（CAV），通过训练逻辑回归分类器并保留权重向量，实现对蛋白质功能注释、结构域定位、结合界面特异性判别及单细胞状态转变的 统一、可比较、可复用 的表征框架。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：能否将多样化的生物概念（功能注释、结构域、结合特异性、细胞状态）统一表示为预训练基础模型嵌入空间中的 方向（向量） ，从而实现对概念的比较、定位、搜索和操作？ 为什么重要 ： 1. 当前基础模型（如 ESM-C、Geneformer）的嵌入包含丰富生物信息，但提取特定属性通常需要训练任务特定的预测模型，缺乏统一框架。 2. 不同注释系统（GO、EC、Pfam）之间难以直接比较，阻碍跨系统知识整合。 3. 研究者常需探索 新定义的概念 （如新发现的基序、未注释的结合界面），现有方法缺乏灵活性。 现有方法不足 ： - 任务特定预测模型：输出不可复用、不可比较，需为每个任务重新训练。 - 线性探针（linear probing）：关注预测性能而非方向本身的可复用性。 - 稀疏自编码器（如 MotifAE）、结构域发现方法（TED）、序列分割方法（InterPro-N）：复杂且计算成本高，不提供统一的概念比较框架。 精确研究问题 ：Can diverse biological properties be mapped to interpretable, reusable directions in pretrained foundation model embedding space, such that these directions can be compared, localized, and manipulated across different biological contexts? 04 背景与发展脉络 注：此脉络基于本文引用与论述整理，标注为「经外部核验」的部分来自文中引用的已发表工作。 阶段 代表性方法 优点 局限 本文位置 基础模型时代 CAV。查询时通过点积计算嵌入与 CAV 的 alignment score。支持三种变体： - 标准 CAV ：正例 vs 通用背景（10,000 随机蛋白/细胞） - 对比 CAV ：正例 vs 特定负例（如 SERK 结合 vs 非 SERK 结合） - 转移方向 ：两个 CAV 之差（如 tumor CAV − non-tumor CAV） 2) 核心洞察 预训练基础模型已将复杂生物概念线性化到嵌入空间中 。尽管概念本身可能是高度非线性、多因素交互的结果（如蛋白质折叠、结合特异性），但经过大规模预训练后，这些概念在嵌入空间中表现为 近似线性的方向 。因此，一个简单的线性分类器就能提取出该方向的权重向量，且该向量： - 可与其他概念向量直接比较（余弦相似度） - 可投影到局部序列窗口进行定位 - 可进行向量运算（如相减得到状态转变方向） - 可跨系统比较（GO vs EC） 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] 线性方向是「可操作」的表征形式 ：相比黑箱预测器，显式向量允许比较、搜索、编辑、组合，这是「可解释性」的一种实用形式——不追求理解每个维度，而是让概念之间的关系可计算。 对比训练是提取细粒度特异性的关键 ：标准 CAV 捕获「是什么」，对比 CAV 捕获「与什么不同」。后者在区分相近概念（如不同结合特异性）时至关重要。 中间层嵌入最适合概念提取 ：ESM-C 第 21–31 层（而非最后层）信号最强，说明概念信息在中间层达到峰值，这与其他表示学习研究的发现一致。 PCA 降维可增强泛化 ：将嵌入投影到 128 个主成分后再训练 CAV，可避免过拟合单个示例的噪声，使概念方向更鲁棒。 07 方法总览 输入 ： - 蛋白质序列（UniProt 下载）→ ESM-C 600M 嵌入（layer CAV 评分（核心公式） $$s = \langle h, v \rangle = h^T v$$ $s$：CAV score（标量） $h$：标准化后的查询嵌入向量 $v$：单位 L2 范数的 CAV 向量（逻辑回归权重归一化后） 直觉 ：查询嵌入在概念方向上的投影长度，衡量该查询与概念的 alignment。 2. 逻辑回归目标（CAV 训练） $$\min_{w} \frac{1}{2} |w|^2 + C \sum_{i=1}^{n} \log(1 + e^{-y_i (w^T h_i + b)})$$ $w$：权重向量（训练后归一化为 CAV） $C$：L2 正则化强度（文中用 C=10⁻⁴ 或 C=1） $y_i \in {+1, -1}$：正例/背景标签 $h_i$：第 i 个样本的标准化嵌入 $b$：偏置项 直觉 ：L2 正则化逻辑回归，权重向量方向即概念在嵌入空间中的线性分离方向。 3. 对数似然比（LLR） $$LLR(s) = \log \left[ \frac{p(s \mid \text{positive})}{p(s \mid \text{negative})} \right]$$ $p(s \mid \text{positive})$：正例 CAV 分数的高斯分布密度 $p(s \mid \text{negative})$：负例 CAV 分数的高斯分布密度 直觉 ：将 CAV 分数转换为概率意义上的置信度，LLR ≤ 0 视为无预测。 4. 转移方向 $$d = \hat{v} {\text{tumor}} - Shared manuscript claim summary The authors propose that biological concepts, including protein function, structural motifs, binding-interface specificity, and single-cell transcriptional states, can be represented as linear directions (Concept Activation Vectors, CAVs) in the embedding spaces of pretrained biological foundation models. They argue that these directions are interpretable, reusable, comparable across annotation systems, and can be used for localization and hypothesis generation. Visible evidence base The manuscript provides textual descriptions of results, including quantitative comparisons against baselines (DeepGO-SE, CLEAN-SupAN, DIAMOND), performance metrics (AUROC, AUPR, Spearman correlations), and specific case studies (e.g., Plexin-A1, PF25029, DUF2797, MYC, LRR-RK receptors). Methodological details are given in the Online Methods section. Missing materials affecting confidence All figures and figure legends, all supplemental files (including the Pfam clustering data and zinc-binding candidate list), and the referenced external data repositories. Without these, the validity of the visual data, the completeness of the clustering analysis, and the specifics of the candidate screen cannot be assessed. Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript presents a conceptually appealing and potentially unifying framework for interrogating biological foundation models. The idea of representing diverse biological concepts as comparable linear directions in a shared embedding space is elegant and could be of significant utility to the community. The authors demonstrate the application of this framework across several distinct biological problems, from functional annotation to structural hypothesis generation. However, the strength of the claims is heavily dependent on the quality and rigor of the validation, which is difficult to fully assess from the text alone. The most significant concerns revolve around the novelty of the approach relative to existing linear probing methods, the robustness of the CAV directions to hyperparameter choices, and the depth of the validation for the more speculative claims, particularly regarding novel structural hypotheses. The single-cell analysis, while showing correlation with differential expression, needs clearer demonstration of its unique added value. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational biologists developing and using protein language models and single-cell foundation models would be the primary audience. Researchers interested in model interpretability, functional annotation of proteins, and the discovery of novel structural or functional relationships would also find this work relevant. The promise of a lightweight, reusable, and comparable representation for biological concepts could be attractive to those seeking to move beyond task-specific prediction heads. Major strengths Unifying Framework: The central idea of using CAVs as a common currency for biological concepts across different modalities (protein sequence, single-cell expression) is a strong and compelling conceptual contribution. Breadth of Applications: The authors demonstrate the framework's versatility by applying it to hierarchical annotation systems (GO, EC), structural motif localization, binding-interface specificity, and single-cell state transitions. This breadth suggests the framework's potential generality. Direct Comparability: The emphasis on training CAVs against a common background to enable direct comparison and clustering of concepts is a powerful and practical feature, enabling the construction of a unified "concept map." Hypothesis Generation: The framework's ability to generate specific, testable hypotheses for poorly characterized domains (e.g., the cystine knot in CILP1) is a significant strength, moving beyond simple annotation transfer. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Novelty and Significance Claim pointer The authors claim that their approach addresses the "mismatch between the generality of foundation-model representations and the specificity of many biological questions" by providing a framework that is distinct from "task-specific prediction models." Evidence pointer Introduction, Discussion Concern The conceptual novelty of using linear classifiers (probes) to interpret embeddings is well-established. The manuscript does not sufficiently differentiate the CAV approach from standard linear probing, other than a shift in focus from predictive performance to the direction itself. The claim of a "common representation" is predicated on the common background, but the impact of this choice on the resulting geometry and comparability is not deeply explored. The authors should more clearly articulate what fundamentally new capability or insight this framework provides over existing interpretability methods, beyond being a convenient tool. Why it matters If the approach is essentially a re-framing of linear probing, its significance as a novel contribution is diminished. The paper's impact hinges on demonstrating that treating the direction as a reusable entity enables new types of analyses that are not possible or practical with existing methods. Resolution test The authors should provide a more explicit and critical comparison with standard linear probing, perhaps by showing a task where the CAV framework provides a unique advantage that probing cannot. A discussion on how the choice of background set fundamentally changes the nature of the learned concept would also help clarify its novelty. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical Soundness and Robustness Claim pointer The authors state that "PCA dimensionality, feature scaling, and regularization strength can substantially alter the learned direction, potentially changing which proteins are retrieved and how concepts relate to one another, even when classification performance remains similar." Evidence pointer Discussion Concern This admission in the Discussion is a critical caveat that undermines the robustness and reproducibility of the core method. If the resulting "concept" is highly sensitive to standard hyperparameters, its utility as a stable, reusable representation is questionable. The manuscript does not provide a systematic analysis of this sensitivity, nor does it offer clear guidelines for choosing these parameters to ensure the biological interpretation is stable. Why it matters A scientific representation must be robust. If the concept directions are unstable, then the clustering, comparisons, and hypotheses derived from them are potentially artifacts of the specific hyperparameter choices. This directly impacts the reliability of all downstream analyses and the validity of the structural hypotheses. Resolution test The authors should include a systematic robustness analysis, showing how the key results (e.g., GO/EC clustering, Pfam map, single-cell axes) change across a range of PCA dimensions, regularization strengths, and background sets. They should demonstrate that the main conclusions are qualitatively stable or provide clear criteria for parameter selection that lead to stable and meaningful concepts. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Validation and Evidence Claim pointer The authors claim that the Pfam CAV map "could expose relationships and structural features not captured by existing domain annotations" and present several "candidate reinterpretations" and "hypotheses" for poorly characterized domains. Evidence pointer Results section "CAVs distinguish and localize structural motifs", Figure 4 Concern While the generation of hypotheses is a strength, the evidence for these specific claims is presented as textual assertion. For example, the claim that PF25029 "adopts a cyclin-like fold" or that DUF2797 has a "GIY-YIG-like endonuclease fold" is stated without showing the supporting data (e.g., structural alignments, confidence scores, or comparisons to other methods). The statement that the DUF2797 relationship "was not recovered by Foldseek" is a single comparison and does not establish the superiority of the CAV approach. Why it matters The significance of the framework is partly based on its ability to make novel predictions. If these predictions are not rigorously validated or presented with clear evidence, they remain anecdotal. The reader cannot judge the reliability of the method from these examples. Resolution test The authors should provide the quantitative or structural evidence for these claims, perhaps in the form of figures showing structural superimpositions, alignment scores, or a more comprehensive benchmark against other structure/sequence search tools. The claims should be tempered to match the level of evidence provided. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Significance and Added Value Claim pointer The authors state that in single-cell embeddings, "gene variation along these axes substantially agrees with conventional differential-expression analysis despite being a distinct computational approach." Evidence pointer Results section "CAVs organize single-cell gene expression", Figure 6 Concern The analysis shows a correlation with differential expression, but it is not clear what new biological insight this provides. If the CAV axis simply recapitulates the results of standard DE analysis, its utility is primarily as a visualization tool. The claim that it can "reveal expression variation beyond conventional differential-expression testing" is only supported by a single example of genes excluded by filtering. A more compelling demonstration of its unique value is needed. Why it matters For the framework to be significant in the single-cell domain, it must demonstrate that it can uncover or represent biological variation that is not readily accessible through established methods. Simply correlating with existing approaches is not sufficient to establish its importance. Resolution test The authors should provide a more in-depth analysis showing a specific case where the CAV axis provides a unique biological insight, such as identifying a continuous transition that is missed by discrete DE analysis, or enabling a comparison between different cell states that is not possible with standard methods. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity and Presentation Affected element Abstract, Results Evidence pointer Abstract, Results section "CAVs unify and organize protein functional annotations" Issue The abstract states that CAVs "recover" GO and EC annotations, but the results section indicates that performance is better for terms with fewer families and weaker for broader terms. The abstract could be more nuanced. Required correction Rephrase the abstract to accurately reflect the performance characteristics, e.g., "effectively recover annotations for terms with consistent representation" or similar. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Technical Detail Affected element Online Methods Evidence pointer Online Methods, "Training concept activation vectors" Issue The description of the single-cell embedding process is brief. It is unclear how the "top 4,094" genes were selected and whether this is a standard practice for Geneformer. Required correction Provide a brief justification for the gene selection and ranking method. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Reproducibility Affected element Online Methods, "Interaction Interface analysis" Evidence pointer Online Methods, "Interaction Interface analysis" Issue The description of the LRR-RK analysis is somewhat circular. It states that a CAV trained on SERB-binding interfaces "failed to sharpen this distinction," leading to the use of a contrastive CAV. The criteria for "failing" are not defined. Required correction Define the quantitative or qualitative criteria used to determine that the initial CAV was not sufficient. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Results, "CAVs can capture binding-interface specificity" Evidence pointer Results section "CAVs can capture binding-interface specificity" Issue The statement "Recovering this specificity required pooling embeddings over local amino-acid regions rather than entire proteins" is a key methodological point but is only mentioned in passing. Required correction Elaborate on this point, as it has significant implications for how the framework should be applied to other problems. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M2: The acknowledged sensitivity of the CAV directions to hyperparameters is a major technical concern that needs to be addressed with a systematic robustness analysis. R1-M3: The evidence for the novel structural hypotheses is not presented in the text. The authors must provide the supporting data for these claims to be credible. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The idea of using CAVs as a common, reusable representation for biological concepts is a fresh perspective, although it builds directly on the established concept of linear probing. The specific applications, particularly the large-scale clustering of Pfam families and the contrastive approach for binding specificity, have original elements. Scientific importance: If the framework is robust and validated, it could provide a powerful and efficient tool for the community, enabling a more unified approach to interrogating foundation models. The potential for hypothesis generation for poorly characterized proteins is significant. Interdisciplinary readership: The work is primarily aimed at computational biologists and machine learning researchers. The conceptual framework is accessible, but the validation and methods are highly technical. The potential implications for experimental biologists are clear (e.g., hypotheses for protein function), but the paper is not written for that audience. Technical soundness: The core methodology is sound in principle, but the lack of a robustness analysis and the incomplete presentation of evidence for key claims are significant weaknesses. The comparison to baselines is present but needs more depth to be fully convincing. Readability for nonspecialists: The abstract and introduction are well-written and accessible. The results and methods sections are dense and would be challenging for a nonspecialist. The paper is well-structured, but the flow is sometimes interrupted by the need to describe multiple case studies. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved. The central concept is promising and the breadth of applications is impressive. However, the manuscript in its current form does not fully establish the robustness and validity of the method. A major revision that includes a thorough robustness analysis, a more detailed presentation of the evidence for the structural hypotheses, and a clearer demonstration of the unique value of the single-cell analysis is necessary before the claims can be fully accepted. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that the CAV map "reveal[s] novel structural relationships" is unsupported without the visual or quantitative data from Figure 4 and the supplemental files. The specific structural hypotheses for PF25029, PF18419, DUF2797, and the cystine knot in CILP1 are presented as findings but are not backed by evidence in the text. The claim that the framework can "manipulate" biological concepts is mentioned in the discussion but not demonstrated in the results. The generalizability of the framework to "other biological data types and models" is a reasonable speculation but is not tested. The performance comparison with DIAMOND and other methods is stated but the details of the comparison (e.g., statistical significance, parameter tuning) are not fully described.

01 基本信息 标题 : PrOMet: Accurate and Robust Metal-Binding Site and Type Prediction 作者与单位 : Park, Gangeun; Seok, Chaok; Park, Hahnbeom（首尔国立大学等，具体单位未提供） 期刊/预印本平台 : Advanced Science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) 年份 : 2026-10-12 论文类型 : 研究论文（方法学） 领域 : 蛋白质结构计算研究 × 深度学习（金属结合位点与类型预测） 关键词 : 金属结合位点预测、金属类型分类、Equivariant Graph Neural Network (EGNN)、Prune-and-Optimization、AlphaFold3 对比 DOI/arXiv 号 : 10.1002/advs.78003 代码 : https://github.com/qkrgangeun/LigMet 数据 : 基于 BioLiP 数据库（2025-02-19 检索），数据可从通讯作者处获取 阅读日期 : 未提供 方向定位 : 该文属于「蛋白质结构相关计算研究 × AI 方法」中的结构-功能预测子方向，聚焦金属结合位点的定位与金属类型分类，与 AlphaFold3 等结构预测工具形成互补，为金属蛋白功能注释和金属酶设计提供计算工具。 02 一句话总结 PrOMet 通过两阶段「剪枝-优化」策略（随机森林粗筛 + EGNN 精修），在蛋白质结构上同时预测金属结合位点位置与金属类型，在实验结构（X-ray/cryo-EM）和 AlphaFold3 预测结构上均达到优于现有方法的精度（PR-AUC 0.739，平均 F1 0.743），且对结构噪声具有鲁棒性。 03 研究问题 具体问题 : 给定一个蛋白质三维结构（实验测定或计算预测），如何准确预测金属离子结合位点的三维坐标位置以及结合的具体金属类型（Zn、Ca、Mg、Mn、Fe、Cu 等）？ 为什么重要 : 金属离子参与超过三分之一的 PDB 结构中蛋白质的催化、结构稳定、信号传导等功能。准确预测金属结合位点和类型对于理解金属蛋白功能、注释未知蛋白、设计金属酶和纠正实验结构中错误的金属注释至关重要。 现有方法不足 : ① 序列方法（如 M-Ionic）缺乏三维结构上下文，定位精度有限；② 现有结构方法（如 Metal3D）多局限于高分辨率晶体结构，对中等分辨率 cryo-EM 和 AlphaFold 预测结构鲁棒性差；③ 多数方法仅预测位点而不预测金属类型，或仅针对单一金属；④ 模板方法难以泛化到新蛋白。 精确研究问题 : Can a two-stage structure-based deep learning framework achieve accurate and robust metal-binding site localization and metal type classification across diverse experimental resolutions and predicted structures? 04 背景与发展脉络 （标注：以下脉络为「经外部核验」结合本文框架） 1. 序列基方法 （早期）：基于氨基酸序列组成和保守性预测金属结合残基，如 M-Ionic。优点：可扩展性好；缺点：缺乏三维空间信息，无法精确定位。 2. 几何启发式方法 （中期）：如 BioMetAll，基于几何模板匹配和化学规则。优点：可解释性强；缺点：对非经典配位几何适应性差。 3. 结构深度学习 （近期）：如 Metal3D，使用 3D-CNN 或图神经网络从结构提取特征。优点：精度提升；缺点：训练数据局限于高分辨率晶体结构，对噪声结构敏感，且多不预测金属类型。 4. 大模型结构预测 （当前）：AlphaFold3 等可预测蛋白-金属复合物，但需要用户指定金属类型和数量，且对非经典配位（如主链羰基配位）易失败。 5. 本文位置 ：提出两阶段「剪枝-优化」框架，结合粗粒度筛选与细粒度几何精修，首次系统性地在多种分辨率（X-ray、cryo-EM）和预测结构（AF3）上实现金属位点定位与类型分类的联合预测，并引入方向性特征（极性向量）增强几何感知。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 位点定位精度不足 现有方法在 2Å 精度下召回率低 金属结合位点遍布整个蛋白表面，正负样本极度不平衡（1224:1） Results 图 2a；Results "grid-level false-to-true ratio was reduced from 1224:1" 对结构噪声敏感 在 cryo-EM 和 AF 模型上性能显著下降 训练数据局限于高分辨率晶体结构，模型过拟合完美几何 Results 图 4a-c；"training only on high-resolution structures mainly reduces recall" 金属类型预测缺失 多数方法仅定位不分类 金属类型分类需要更精细的化学环境特征 Results 图 3a；"even the best-reported approaches reach only moderate localization accuracy" 非经典配位识别困难 主链羰基配位的金属位点易漏检 训练数据中此类位点占比低，模型偏向侧链配位 Results 图 5c；AF3 无法预测 K+ 位点案例 计算成本高 全表面细粒度搜索不可行 蛋白表面网格点数量巨大 Methods "Pruning stage"；"reducing the search space to 2.76%" 06 核心思想 表面方法 : 两阶段级联架构——第一阶段用随机森林（RF）在蛋白表面网格点上进行粗粒度筛选，保留高召回率的候选区域；第二阶段用等变图神经网络（EGNN）在候选区域上进行细粒度精修，同时输出金属结合概率和金属类型分布。 核心洞察 : 金属结合预测本质上是「多尺度问题」——全局搜索需要高效筛选（粗粒度特征即可），局部确认需要精细的几何与化学感知（原子级配位几何、方向性电子效应）。将两者解耦为级联的「剪枝-优化」过程，既保证召回率又提升精度。关键创新在于引入 极性方向特征 （原子极性向量与网格点方向的夹角 θ），编码孤对电子方向信息，这是距离-only 特征无法捕捉的。 可能的普适教训 [Analysis]: ① 对「全局搜索 + 局部精修」类任务（如其他配体结合位点预测、蛋白-蛋白相互作用界面预测），两阶段级联设计可有效平衡计算效率与精度；② 方向性/角度特征对配位化学至关重要，纯距离特征信息不足；③ 训练数据应覆盖分辨率谱系（而非仅高分辨率），以增强对结构噪声的鲁棒性。 07 方法总览 输入 : 蛋白质三维结构（PDB 格式），包含原子坐标、氨基酸类型、原子类型、二级结构注释、SASA、部分电荷等。 输出 : (1) 金属结合位点的三维坐标（概率加权聚类中心）；(2) 每个位点的金属类型预测（Zn/Ca/Mg/Mn/Fe/Cu 或 None）。 模块 : 1. 网格点采样 : 在蛋白表面原子范德华半径扩展区域采样候选网格点，去除空间冲突和冗余点（最小间距 0.6 Å）。 2. RF 剪枝器 : 对每个网格点提取三类特征——(a) 第一配位层特征（距离阈值 2.5/2.8/3.0/3.2/3.5 Å 内的供体原子计数、核心残基计数等）；(b) 几何与可及性特征（到非极性碳距离、到主链原子距离、rSASA 等）；(c) 第二配位层特征（3.2-5.0 Å 范围内的残基组成）。输出金属结合概率，保留概率 > 阈值的网格点。 3. EGNN 精修器 : 将保留的网格点与周围蛋白原子构建局部图（k=16 最近邻），节点特征包含原子类型、氨基酸身份、二级结构、SASA、电荷等；边特征包含距离、极性方向角 (sin θ, cos θ)。5 层 EGNN 编码器 + 双头解码器（结合概率头 + 金属类型头）。 4. 后处理 : DBSCAN 聚类（eps=2, min_samples=2）将网格点聚合成位点，位点位置为概率加权中心，类型为最高概率网格点的 top-1 预测。 训练 : 损失函数 L = L_occ + L_type + L_aux，其中 L_occ 为软标签二值交叉熵（高斯衰减标签），L_type 为类别平衡交叉熵，L_aux 为 2 Å 内网格点的辅助类型损失。Adam 优化器，lr=0.0001，5 层 EGNN，dropout=0.1。 流程 : 输入结构 → 网格采样 → RF 剪枝（保留 2.76% 网格）→ EGNN 精修 → DBSCAN 聚类 → 位点坐标 + 金属类型。 08 核心模块拆解 模块 功能 为何需要 输入输出 支撑证据 移除后的已知或预期影响 网格点采样 离散化蛋白表面为候选点 连续空间搜索不可行 输入：蛋白结构；输出：候选网格点集 Methods "Grid unverified Review setup Input scope Full manuscript text, including abstract, introduction, results, discussion, methods, and supplementary figure/table references. Assessment boundary Scientific validity, methodological soundness, robustness of claims, and clarity of presentation. No assessment of editorial fit or journal-specific policy. Shared manuscript claim summary The authors present PrOMet, a two-stage structure-based deep learning framework for predicting metal-binding sites and metal types in protein structures. The method combines a Random Forest pruning stage with an Equivariant Graph Neural Network (EGNN) optimization stage, trained on a broad dataset of protein-metal complexes from BioLiP. The authors claim state-of-the-art performance in metal localization and type classification, robustness to non-crystallographic structures (cryo-EM and AlphaFold models), and superiority over AlphaFold3 in dedicated metal-site prediction tasks. Visible evidence base Main text figures (Figures 1-5), Tables 1, supplementary figures and tables referenced (Figures S1-S23, Tables S1-S7), and detailed methods descriptions. Missing materials affecting confidence Actual figure images and table data are not provided; only figure/table captions and in-text descriptions are available. Supplementary figures and tables are referenced but not included. No quantitative performance values for baseline comparisons are given in the text beyond a few specific numbers. The GitHub repository link is provided but not assessed. Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript presents a well-motivated and technically sound approach to a challenging problem in structural bioinformatics. The two-stage architecture is a sensible design choice, and the inclusion of diverse experimental structures and predicted models in evaluation is commendable. However, the evidence provided in the text is insufficient to fully validate the claimed performance advantages, particularly against AlphaFold3 and other baselines. Several key quantitative results are only described qualitatively or with single summary statistics, and the robustness analysis on cryo-EM and AlphaFold models lacks sufficient detail. The work has clear potential, but the current manuscript does not fully establish the case for its claimed superiority. Who would be interested in the results, and why Structural biologists, computational biochemists, and researchers in metalloprotein engineering would find this work relevant. The method addresses a practical need for accurate metal-site annotation in increasingly common medium-resolution cryo-EM structures and AlphaFold-predicted models. The comparative analysis with AlphaFold3 is timely and of broad interest to the protein structure prediction community. Major strengths 1. The two-stage prune-and-optimize architecture is a well-reasoned approach to balance computational efficiency and prediction accuracy. 2. The dataset construction, including biological-site filtering and handling of metal heterogeneity, is thoughtful and addresses known pitfalls in the field. 3. The evaluation on non-crystallographic structures (cryo-EM, AF3) is a valuable contribution, as most existing methods are benchmarked only on high-resolution X-ray structures. 4. The comparison with AlphaFold3, including runtime analysis, provides practical guidance for users. Major Concerns R1-M1 (Blocking: Yes) The central claim of state-of-the-art performance is not fully supported by the quantitative evidence presented in the text. While PR-AUC values are given for the overall test set, per-metal-type breakdowns, confidence intervals, and statistical significance tests are not reported. The comparison with Metal3D and M-Ionic relies on a single summary metric, which may obscure important differences in performance across metal types or structural contexts. R1-M2 (Blocking: Yes) The robustness analysis on cryo-EM and AF3 structures is described qualitatively. The text states that performance "showed only a small degradation" and that Metal3D "dropped more sharply," but no numerical results are provided for these subsets. Without quantitative data, the claim of robustness cannot be adequately assessed. R1-M3 (Blocking: No) The comparison with AlphaFold3, while interesting, is limited to a small positive set (82 cases) and a negative set (316 cases). The text reports a top-1 site-and-type accuracy of 45% for PrOMet versus 23% for AF3, but the selection criteria for these sets, the potential for bias, and the statistical significance of the difference are not discussed. The runtime comparison, while useful, is based on a single example and may not be representative. R1-M4 (Blocking: No) The ablation study identifies the two-stage design and directional features as important contributors, but the analysis is incomplete. For example, the text does not report the performance of the EGNN without pruning when trained on the full (unfiltered) dataset, which would isolate the effect of the pruning stage from the training data distribution. The interaction between dataset composition and architecture choice is not fully explored. Minor Comments R1-m1 The abstract states that PrOMet achieves a PR-AUC of 0.739 for localization and an average F1 of 0.743 for type classification. It would be helpful to also report the range of F1 scores across metal types, as the average may mask poor performance on rare metals. R1-m2 The description of the directional feature (polarity vector and angle θ) is clear, but the physical interpretation could be expanded. The text mentions "lone-pair electrons" but does not explain how the polarity vector is computed from atomic properties. A brief clarification in the methods would improve reproducibility. R1-m3 The negative set for the AF3 comparison consists of proteins with no annotated metals. It would be informative to also test on proteins with metals that are not among the seven modeled types, to assess whether PrOMet can correctly reject non-target metals. R1-m4 The manuscript mentions that the dataset includes "all ligands and nucleic acids except waters." It would be useful to specify how ligand-metal interactions are handled in the feature computation, as this could affect performance on protein-ligand interfaces. R1-m5 The inference time is reported for a single medium-sized protein. A more systematic analysis across protein sizes would be helpful for users planning large-scale applications. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1 and R1-M2 are the primary technical concerns. The lack of quantitative results for the cryo-EM and AF3 subsets, and the absence of statistical rigor in the main benchmark, prevent a full assessment of the method's claimed advantages. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The two-stage architecture is a novel combination of existing techniques, and the focus on robustness to non-ideal structures is a meaningful contribution. However, the individual components (RF, EGNN) are well-established, and the novelty lies primarily in their integration and application. Scientific importance: The problem of metal-site prediction is of significant practical importance, and the potential to apply the method to cryo-EM and predicted structures broadens its utility. The comparative analysis with AlphaFold3 addresses a question of current interest. Interdisciplinary readership: The work is primarily of interest to computational structural biologists and bioinformaticians. The methods and results are presented in a way that is accessible to this audience, but the broader biological significance could be emphasized more. Technical soundness: The methodology is generally sound, but the evidence presented is insufficient to fully validate the claims. The lack of quantitative detail in key comparisons is a significant weakness. Readability for nonspecialists: The manuscript is well-written and the concepts are explained clearly. The abstract and introduction are accessible, but the results section assumes familiarity with machine learning and structural biology terminology. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved. The core idea is promising and the methodology is well-motivated, but the current manuscript does not provide sufficient quantitative evidence to establish the claimed performance advantages. The authors should provide detailed results for the robustness analyses, add statistical measures to the main benchmark, and expand the ablation study to fully support their conclusions. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that PrOMet "outperforms existing methods" is not fully supported, as only a single summary metric (PR-AUC) is reported for the main comparison, and no statistical significance testing is described. The claim of robustness to cryo-EM and AF3 structures is unsupported by quantitative data in the text; only qualitative descriptions are provided. The claim that PrOMet is "among the first" structure-based deep learning methods to accept ligand-bound inputs is plausible but not verified against a comprehensive literature search. The statement that the two-stage design is the "dominating factor" for success is based on a single ablation experiment and may be an overstatement, as the interaction with dataset composition is not fully explored. The generalizability of the method to unseen metal types or non-standard coordination environments is not assessed.

Scientific content, technical accuracy, logical coherence, and support for claims as presented in the provided text Shared manuscript claim summary The authors argue that AlphaFold 3 (AF3) represents a transformative advance in drug discovery and development (DDD), with specific roles in target identification, hit identification, lead optimization, and personalized clinical decisions. They acknowledge limitations in prediction accuracy across biomolecule categories and propose technical, ethical, and regulatory frameworks to address these challenges. Visible evidence base The manuscript text includes references to published work (citations [1]-[28]), descriptions of AF3 capabilities, and proposed frameworks. No original experimental data, benchmark results, or case studies are presented. Missing materials affecting confidence Figures (Figure 1), Tables (Tables 1-3), and all cited references are not provided. The manuscript is a perspective piece, so the absence of primary data is expected, but the absence of the figures and tables limits assessment of how specific claims are illustrated or quantified. Reviewer Overall assessment This perspective article provides a broad and generally well-structured overview of AlphaFold 3's potential applications in drug discovery, alongside a thoughtful discussion of technical limitations, ethical considerations, and regulatory implications. The authors correctly identify key strengths of AF3 (e.g., prediction of protein-ligand complexes, improved PAE maps) and acknowledge its limitations (e.g., static structures, variable accuracy for post-translational modifications). However, the manuscript suffers from a lack of specificity in several sections, with claims that are either unsupported by concrete examples or presented without quantitative context. The proposed frameworks for iterative validation, ethical governance, and regulatory oversight are reasonable but remain largely aspirational, with no discussion of feasibility or implementation challenges. The writing is clear but occasionally repetitive, and some sections (e.g., Regulatory Implications) introduce highly specific technical proposals (e.g., blockchain-verified multi-signature authentication) that appear disconnected from the current state of AF3 applications and may distract from the core message. Overall, the manuscript offers a useful synthesis for a broad audience but does not provide sufficient depth or novelty to be considered a major contribution to the field. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers and practitioners in computational biology, structural biology, and drug discovery would find this perspective useful as a high-level summary of AF3's capabilities and limitations. Those new to the field or seeking a framework for integrating AI-based structure prediction into their workflows may benefit from the structured discussion of target identification, lead optimization, and personalized medicine. However, experts in the field are unlikely to encounter new information, as the content largely recapitulates known features of AF3 and general challenges in AI-driven drug discovery. Major strengths The manuscript provides a comprehensive and accessible overview of AF3's potential roles across the drug discovery pipeline. The authors appropriately balance enthusiasm with caution, explicitly acknowledging that prediction accuracy varies across biomolecule categories and that experimental validation remains essential. The discussion of ethical and regulatory considerations, including data privacy, bias, and dual-use risks, is timely and relevant. The proposed iterative computational-experimental framework, with explicit use of confidence metrics (pLDDT, PAE) to guide decision-making, is a practical and sensible suggestion. The proposed technical mechanisms for biosecurity (e.g., blockchain-verified multi-signature authentication) are presented without feasibility analysis and are not supported by evidence.

01 基本信息 标题 ：Integrated computation-guided thermostabilization of the fungal sweet protein Honey Truffle Sweetener 作者与单位 ：Wang, Zhikuan; Wang, Wen; Zhu, Feifei; Zhang, Yutian; Li, Yirui; Zhu, Zhiqi; Lu, Ziwan; Huang, Ang; Yu, Mingjia; Liu, Si（天津大学等，具体单位未提供） 期刊/预印本平台 ：Current Research in Food Science 年份 ：2026（在线日期 2026-10-12） 论文类型 ：研究论文（实验 + 计算） 领域 ：蛋白质工程 / 热稳定性设计 / 甜味蛋白 / 计算辅助设计 关键词 ：Honey Truffle Sweetener (HTS)；热稳定化；Rosetta；ThermoMPNN；ESM2；分子动力学；Tm 预测；二硫键工程 DOI/arXiv 号 ：10.1016/j.crfs.2026.101584 代码 ：未提供 数据 ：晶体结构已存入 PDB（登录号 21WR）；其余数据见正文与补充材料 阅读日期 ：2026-05-14（按系统日期） 该文在课题方向中的位置 ：本文属于「蛋白质结构相关计算研究 × AI/物理模拟」中的 热稳定性工程 方向，核心是整合物理（Rosetta、MD）与深度学习（ThermoMPNN、ESM2）方法，对一种新发现的真菌甜味蛋白进行热稳定化改造。其方法框架（结构解析 → 互补打分筛选 → 实验反馈 → 模块化组装 → MD 机制分析）对同类紧凑型蛋白的稳定性设计具有直接参考价值。 02 一句话总结 本文通过解析 Honey Truffle Sweetener (HTS) 的晶体结构，整合 Rosetta 与 ThermoMPNN 互补筛选、实验 Tm 数据训练的 SMRC-Net 残差学习模型，以及模块化组装和工程二硫键，将 HTS 的 Tm 从 54.6 °C 提升至 82.1 °C（ΔTm = 27.5 °C），同时保留甜味与 pH 耐受性。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：如何对一种新发现的、缺乏突变历史数据的真菌甜味蛋白 HTS 进行理性的热稳定性改造，使其适用于热加工食品？ 为什么重要 ：甜味蛋白作为天然高倍甜味剂，其应用受限于热稳定性不足——甜味依赖于天然三维结构的保持，热变性会导致甜味丧失。HTS 虽甜度高（摩尔甜度约为蔗糖的 18,000 倍），但野生型 Tm 仅 54.6 °C，远低于巴氏杀菌等加工条件。 现有方法为何不足 ：传统热稳定化策略（二硫键、脯氨酸替换、定向进化、共有序列设计）多依赖已知突变数据或同源信息；对新发现的蛋白，缺乏突变历史与大规模实验数据集，且多数计算工具（如 Rosetta、ThermoMPNN）单独使用时预测精度有限，与实验 Tm 相关性弱（本文中 Pearson r 仅 0.206 和 0.248）。 精确研究问题 ：Can an integrated workflow combining crystal structure, complementary ΔΔG-based screening, experiment-derived residual learning (SMRC-Net), and modular assembly yield a thermostabilized HTS variant that retains sweetness? 04 背景与发展脉络 （标注：以下脉络为「经外部核验」的领域常识与「仅本文框架」的定位结合，具体标注见各阶段） 经典甜味蛋白热稳定化（外部核验） ：代表蛋白包括 thaumatin、monellin、brazzein、neoculin 等。早期策略包括二硫键引入（如 thaumatin 天然含 8 对二硫键）、脯氨酸替换、糖基化等。优点：有成功案例；局限：依赖天然稳定元件，对新蛋白缺乏可迁移规则。 计算辅助稳定性设计（外部核验） ：Rosetta（Kellogg et al., 2011）基于物理能量函数评估突变 ΔΔG；ThermoMPNN（Dieckhaus et al., 2024）基于深度学习的序列-结构兼容性。优点：可对任意结构进行全扫描；局限：单独使用时与实验 Tm 相关性有限（本文表 S18 显示 Pearson r 仅 0.2 左右）。 机器学习 Tm 预测（外部核验） ：PON-Tm、HoTMuSiC 等基于序列/结构的 Tm 预测器；ESM2（Lin et al., 2023）蛋白语言模型提供突变嵌入特征。优点：可学习序列-稳定性隐含规律；局限：跨骨架泛化差，需实验数据校准。 本文定位（仅本文框架） ：提出「结构解析 → 互补筛选 → 实验反馈训练 SMRC-Net → 模块化组装 → MD 机制验证」的闭环流程，强调实验数据对计算模型的校准作用，以及模块化组装降低多突变组合风险。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 新蛋白缺乏突变历史数据 HTS 为 2022 年新发现蛋白，无既有突变体库 发现时间短，尚未积累系统突变数据 Introduction 节 单一计算工具预测精度有限 Rosetta 与 ThermoMPNN 预测分数与实验 ΔTm 相关性弱（Pearson r = 0.206 和 0.248） 物理能量函数与深度学习打分各有盲区，无法完全捕捉折叠自由能变化 Discussion 节；表 S18 多突变组合效应不可预测 单点稳定突变叠加可能相互干扰或抵消 突变间协同/拮抗效应缺乏可靠预测方法 Discussion 节（"combined effects of individually stabilizing substitutions remain difficult to predict"） 热稳定性与甜味保持的权衡 过度刚性化可能破坏受体结合表面 甜味依赖天然构象，稳定化改造需避免全局刚性化 Discussion 节；MD 分析显示 FM 非均匀刚性化 实验筛选成本高 全组合突变体库不可行 121 残基 × 19 替换 = 2299 种单点突变，多突变组合空间更大 Methods 节（仅测试 72 个单点突变体） 06 核心思想 表面方法 ：解析 HTS 晶体结构 → Rosetta 与 ThermoMPNN 双工具全残基饱和突变扫描 → 人工挑选 72 个单点突变体实验测定 Tm → 用实验数据训练 SMRC-Net（ESM2 序列特征 + MD 结构特征残差学习）→ 模块化组装 10 个稳定突变 → 引入工程二硫键 → 最终获得 Tm 82.1 °C 的 FM 变体。 核心洞察 ：计算预测的价值不在于直接给出最终答案，而在于生成候选集；实验数据是校准计算模型的「锚点」。SMRC-Net 的残差学习设计（用 MD 特征修正 ESM2 基线预测）表明，序列信息与结构动态信息是互补的——ESM2 捕捉序列上下文隐含的稳定性倾向，MD 捕捉突变引起的局部动态重排，二者结合优于任一单独使用。 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] ：对于缺乏突变历史的新蛋白，采用「计算初筛 → 小规模实验反馈 → 机器学习校准 → 模块化组装」的迭代闭环，比依赖单一高精度预测器更实际。模块化组装（先验证小组合，再逐步合并）有效规避了多突变组合的不可预测性。此外，MD 分析揭示的「非均匀刚性化」机制提示：热稳定化不一定是全局刚性化，而是局部动态重排与构象系综收敛。 07 方法总览 输入 ：HTS 氨基酸序列（121 残基）、重组表达质粒、晶体结构（PDB: 21WR） 输出 ：热稳定化变体 FM（Tm = 82.1 °C）、SMRC-Net 预测模型、MD 机制分析 模块 ： 1. 结构解析 ：X 射线晶体学（1.58 Å，空间群 P1211，SSRF BL02U1 光束线） 2. 计算筛选 ：PyRosetta 饱和突变（ΔΔG = Emutant − EWT）+ ThermoMPNN 独立打分 3. 实验表征 ：72 个单点突变体表达纯化 + 热位移实验（TSA）测 Tm 4. no external data or unpublished materials consulted Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report an integrated computation-guided workflow for thermostabilizing the fungal sweet protein Honey Truffle Sweetener (HTS). They determined the HTS crystal structure, used Rosetta and ThermoMPNN for candidate mutation screening, developed a machine learning model (SMRC-Net) for Tm prediction, and assembled stabilizing mutations stepwise. The final variant FM achieved a melting temperature of 82.1 °C (27.5 °C above wild-type), retained sweetness in untreated samples, and showed improved heat and pH tolerance in terms of solubility and secondary structure. Visible evidence base Crystal structure (Table 1, Fig. 1), computational screening results (Fig. 2), SMRC-Net cross-validation metrics (Fig. 3, Table S4), prospective variant testing (Fig. 4, Table S16), modular assembly Tm data (Fig. 5, Table S9), CD spectra (Fig. 6), MD analyses (Fig. 7, Fig. 8, Tables S11–S13), sensory evaluation (Table S3), disulfide variant data (Table S1), H16A/F99A mutant data (Table S15) Missing materials affecting confidence Supplementary figures and tables referenced but not provided in full (Figs. S1–S7, Tables S1–S18); detailed SMRC-Net architecture and hyperparameters only in Supplementary Methods; sensory evaluation raw data not shown; statistical details for some comparisons not fully specified Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript presents a well-structured and potentially valuable workflow for protein thermostabilization, with a clear demonstration of success in a challenging target protein. The integration of structure determination, complementary computational screening, machine learning, and stepwise experimental assembly is logical and the reported Tm improvement is substantial. However, several technical aspects require clarification and additional evidence before the case is fully established, particularly regarding the generalizability of SMRC-Net, the statistical robustness of the sensory data, and the mechanistic interpretation of the MD analyses. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in protein engineering, food science, and structural biology would be interested. The work addresses a practical bottleneck in using sweet proteins as sugar substitutes, and the computation-guided workflow could be applicable to other compact proteins with limited stability. The combination of physics-based and deep learning methods, plus the residual learning framework, may interest computational biologists developing protein stability prediction tools. Major strengths 1) The crystal structure provides a solid foundation for rational design. 2) The complementary use of Rosetta and ThermoMPNN is sensible and well-justified. 3) The stepwise modular assembly strategy is methodologically sound and reduces risk of incompatible mutations. 4) The final Tm improvement of 27.5 °C is substantial and practically meaningful. 5) The inclusion of heat and pH tolerance assays adds practical relevance beyond simple Tm measurements. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness of SMRC-Net validation Claim pointer "Repeated nested cross-validation supported quantitative Tm prediction within the HTS scaffold, while prospective testing showed 9/10 directional agreement in a small, computationally selected variant set." Evidence pointer Section 3.3, Fig. 3, Table S4; Section 3.4, Fig. 4, Table S16 Concern The nested cross-validation is performed on 65 variants, all derived from the same protein scaffold and selected through the same computational pipeline. This creates a potential selection bias: the model is trained and tested on variants that were pre-filtered by Rosetta and ThermoMPNN, which may not represent the full mutation space. The prospective set of 10 variants is very small, and the reported 9/10 directional agreement, while encouraging, has wide confidence intervals. More critically, the manuscript does not report whether the SMRC-Net predictions were compared against simpler baselines (e.g., using only ESM2 features, or only MD features) in the nested cross-validation, which would be necessary to demonstrate the added value of the residual correction module. Why it matters The central methodological contribution of this work is the SMRC-Net framework. If its performance is not rigorously benchmarked against appropriate baselines and its generalizability is not demonstrated beyond a narrow, pipeline-selected variant set, the claim that it provides a useful "mutation-centered" prediction tool is not fully supported. Resolution test Provide ablation studies in the nested cross-validation (ESM2-only, MD-only, and combined models). Report confidence intervals for the 9/10 directional agreement. Ideally, test the frozen model on a set of variants that were not selected by the same Rosetta/ThermoMPNN pipeline, even if small. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence for retained sweetness Claim pointer "Untreated FM retained sweetness, while separate heat- and pH-treatment assays showed retained solubility and largely preserved secondary-structure profiles. Sweetness after these treatments was not evaluated." Evidence pointer Section 3.5, Table S3 Concern The sensory evaluation is described only in terms of threshold values in Table S3, which is not provided in the main text. The manuscript states that "sweetness thresholds of Mut10-1 and FM remained within a range similar to that of WT," but no statistical analysis of these thresholds is presented. With only eight panelists, the power to detect meaningful differences is limited. Furthermore, the critical claim for practical application would be sweetness retention after heat or pH treatment, which the authors explicitly state was not evaluated. This is a significant gap given that the stated motivation is use in thermally processed foods. Why it matters The practical value of the engineered variant depends on retaining sweetness under processing-relevant conditions. Without data on sweetness after heat or pH treatment, the claim that FM is suitable for thermally processed foods is not established. Resolution test Provide the full sensory data with statistical analysis (e.g., confidence intervals for thresholds). At minimum, evaluate sweetness of FM after a relevant heat treatment (e.g., 80 °C for 1 h) to demonstrate functional retention under the conditions where solubility and structure are maintained. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Mechanistic interpretation of MD analyses Claim pointer "Molecular dynamics analyses indicated that FM was not uniformly rigidified but instead exhibited localized flexibility redistribution and a more consolidated conformational ensemble." Evidence pointer Section 3.6, Fig. 7, Fig. 8, Tables S11–S13 Concern The MD analyses are descriptive and correlative. The manuscript reports differences in RMSF, SASA, contact persistence, and free-energy landscapes between WT and FM, but does not establish a causal link between specific mutations and the observed stability increase. For example, the H16-F99 contact is identified as contributing to stability based on a double mutant, but it is unclear how this contact relates to the other 11 mutations in FM. The free-energy landscape analysis (Fig. 8d) is qualitative; no quantitative metrics (e.g., free-energy differences between basins) are provided. Why it matters Without a clearer mechanistic link between the introduced mutations and the observed stability changes, the generalizability of the design principles to other proteins is uncertain. The manuscript would be strengthened by identifying which mutations contribute most to stability and why. Resolution test Perform additional MD analyses to quantify free-energy differences between conformational states. Consider alanine scanning or reversion mutants to identify key stabilizing mutations and test their individual contributions. Relate specific mutations to the observed flexibility redistribution. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity of methods Affected element SMRC-Net architecture description Evidence pointer Section 2.5 (implied), Supplementary Methods Issue The main text provides only a high-level description of SMRC-Net. Key details such as the number of MD features, the specific feature selection method, and the model architecture (e.g., number of layers, regularization) are relegated to the Supplementary Methods. Required correction Provide a concise summary of the SMRC-Net architecture and key hyperparameters in the main text or a table, so that readers can assess the model without consulting the supplement. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Statistical reporting Affected element Tm measurements and comparisons Evidence pointer Fig. 2c, Fig. 5c, Table S9 Issue The manuscript reports Tm values as mean ± SD from triplicate measurements but does not state the number of independent protein preparations or whether the triplicates are technical or biological replicates. The statistical significance of differences between variants is not consistently reported. Required correction Clarify the nature of replicates and report the number of independent experiments. Where comparisons are made, provide appropriate statistical tests and effect sizes. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Completeness of data presentation Affected element Sensory evaluation Evidence pointer Table S3 Issue The sensory evaluation is summarized only as threshold values. The manuscript does not describe the training of panelists, the number of sessions, or the variability across panelists. Required correction Provide a brief description of the sensory protocol in the main text and include individual panelist data or a measure of inter-panelist variability in the supplement. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Interpretation of CD data Affected element Fig. 6c, Fig. 6f, Table S10 Issue The CD spectra are described as showing "largely preserved secondary-structure profiles," but the quantitative secondary-structure content estimates (presumably from BeStSel) are only in Table S10. It is unclear whether the differences between WT and FM under stress conditions are statistically significant. Required correction Report the secondary-structure content estimates in the main text or a main-text figure, with appropriate statistical comparisons. Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Disulfide bond validation Claim pointer "The final variant, FM, had a melting temperature of 82.1 °C, 27.5 °C higher than that of wild-type HTS." Evidence pointer Section 3.5, Fig. 5b, Table S1 Issue The manuscript states that an engineered disulfide bond was introduced (Cys37-Cys46), but it is not explicitly stated whether formation of the disulfide bond was experimentally confirmed (e.g., by mass spectrometry or non-reducing SDS-PAGE). The Tm increase attributed to the disulfide bond could be confounded by the accompanying mutations. Required correction Provide evidence for disulfide bond formation in the purified FM protein, or acknowledge that the contribution of the disulfide bond to stability is inferred from the Tm of the disulfide-only variant. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established 1) Lack of ablation studies for SMRC-Net to demonstrate the added value of the MD residual correction over the ESM2 baseline alone. 2) Absence of sweetness evaluation after heat or pH treatment, which is central to the practical application claim. 3) Insufficient statistical detail for sensory data and some Tm comparisons. 4) No experimental confirmation of disulfide bond formation in FM. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The integration of complementary computational methods with a residual learning framework is a novel contribution, though individual components are established. Scientific importance: The work addresses a real bottleneck in sweet protein application and provides a potentially transferable workflow. Interdisciplinary readership: The work bridges structural biology, computational biology, and food science, and should appeal to readers across these fields. Technical soundness: The experimental design is generally sound, but the validation of SMRC-Net and the sensory data require strengthening. Readability for nonspecialists: The manuscript is clearly written and accessible, though the SMRC-Net section may be challenging for readers without machine learning background. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved. The core experimental achievement (a 27.5 °C Tm increase with retained sweetness) is significant and likely reproducible. However, the validation of the computational framework and the missing post-treatment sweetness data must be addressed before the broader claims of the workflow's utility are fully established. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that SMRC-Net provides "quantitative Tm prediction" is only supported within a narrow, pipeline-selected variant set; generalizability to other proteins or even other regions of the HTS sequence space is not demonstrated. The claim that FM "retained sweetness" is based on threshold data in the supplement without statistical analysis; the claim that it is suitable for thermally processed foods is unsupported because sweetness after heat or pH treatment was not evaluated. The mechanistic interpretation that FM stabilization arises from "localized flexibility redistribution and a more consolidated conformational ensemble" is correlative; no causal link between specific mutations and these changes is established. The statement that the engineered disulfide bond contributes to stability is inferred from Tm data but not directly confirmed by structural or biochemical evidence of disulfide formation.

Claims and evidence presented in the abstract; no access to full methods, figures, tables, or supplementary material Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report a computational analysis of non-synonymous SNPs in the human TNF gene, identifying I118F and I118N as high-risk variants with predicted destabilizing effects at a conserved residue. Molecular dynamics simulations (200 ns) are claimed to show increased structural fluctuations, reduced compactness, altered principal component and free energy landscapes, and weaker dynamic coupling for these mutants relative to wild-type TNF. The authors state that relevance to ALD-associated neuroinflammation remains hypothetical. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no quantitative data, simulation parameters, validation metrics, or statistical analyses are provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full methods, simulation setup and force field parameters, convergence criteria, replicate details, pathogenicity prediction scores, conservation analysis details, all figures and tables, and any supplementary data Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a plausible computational workflow for prioritizing nsSNPs in TNF and characterizing two candidate variants via MD simulations. However, the evidence base is limited to qualitative statements without quantitative support, and the link to ALD is explicitly acknowledged as hypothetical. The technical soundness cannot be fully assessed from the abstract alone, and the scientific advance over existing computational SNP prioritization studies is not clearly articulated. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in computational genomics and protein biophysics interested in TNF variant effects; investigators studying ALD pathophysiology who may use these predictions to guide experimental validation. The work may also interest methodologists applying MD simulations to disease-associated SNPs. Major strengths The study integrates multiple established pathogenicity prediction tools, which is a standard and defensible approach. The use of 200 ns MD simulations with multiple analyses (RMSD, Rg, PCA, FEL, DCCM) is comprehensive for a computational study. The authors appropriately acknowledge the hypothetical nature of the ALD connection, avoiding overclaiming. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "MD simulations demonstrated that these mutations result in heightened structural fluctuations, as indicated by elevated RMSD and Radius of Gyration (Rg) values, signifying a reduction in structural compactness." Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The abstract reports qualitative outcomes (elevated RMSD and Rg) without any numerical values, error estimates, or statistical comparisons between wild-type and mutants. It is unclear whether the observed differences exceed simulation noise or replicate variability. Why it matters Without quantitative data and appropriate statistical treatment, the claim of "heightened structural fluctuations" cannot be evaluated for significance. This is central to the paper's main conclusion about variant-induced destabilization. Resolution test Provide mean and standard deviation (or confidence intervals) for RMSD and Rg across replicates, with statistical tests (e.g., per-residue or per-time-point comparisons) demonstrating significant differences between wild-type and each mutant. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "The PCA and FEL analyses showed that the wild-type protein keeps a stable energy minimum, whereas DCCM analysis indicated that the I118F and I118N mutations exhibit weaker dynamic coupling with more than one metastable state, leading to lesser stable structure." Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The interpretation of PCA, FEL, and DCCM results is presented without methodological details or quantitative descriptors. No free energy values, projection plots, or correlation coefficients are given. The claim of "more than one metastable state" is not supported by any visible metric. Why it matters These analyses are used to support the conclusion of compromised trimer stability and dynamics. Without quantitative evidence, the conclusions are not reproducible or verifiable from the abstract. Resolution test Include free energy differences between basins, PCA eigenvalue spectra, and DCCM correlation matrices with significance thresholds. Provide representative plots in the main text or supplementary material. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Scientific importance Claim pointer "These findings suggest that the identified TNF variants may influence TNF protein stability and conformational dynamics; however, their relevance to ALD-associated neuroinflammation remains hypothetical and requires experimental and clinical validation." Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The abstract does not establish a mechanistic or epidemiological link between TNF nsSNPs and ALD. The selection of TNF as a target is motivated by its role in neuroinflammation, but no evidence is presented that I118F or I118N occur in ALD patients or are associated with disease severity. Why it matters The title and framing imply a role in ALD, but the abstract explicitly concedes the connection is hypothetical. This limits the translational significance and may overstate the relevance to the disease context. Resolution test Clarify whether these variants have been observed in ALD cohorts or general populations, and discuss their allele frequencies. If not, reframe the study as a general TNF variant analysis with potential relevance to neuroinflammatory conditions. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Readability for nonspecialists Affected element Methods description Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Issue The list of prediction tools is dense and may overwhelm nonspecialist readers without context on how they complement each other. Required correction Briefly explain the rationale for using multiple tools (e.g., consensus scoring) and define key terms like "nsSNP" and "conserved residue" for a broader audience. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Technical soundness Affected element Simulation length justification Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Issue The choice of 200 ns simulation time is stated but not justified. For a trimeric protein, this may be insufficient to sample large conformational changes. Required correction Provide a justification for the simulation length, referencing convergence tests or prior studies on similar systems. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Scientific importance Affected element Variant selection Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Issue Only two variants (I118F and I118N) are selected for MD simulations, but the criteria for this selection beyond "strong computational evidence" are not specified. Required correction State the exact thresholds or ranking criteria used to select these variants from the initial SNP pool. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1 and R1-M2 are blocking because the central claims of structural destabilization and altered dynamics are not quantitatively supported. The lack of statistical analysis and methodological detail prevents verification of the conclusions. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: Moderate. The application of standard computational tools to TNF is not novel, though the specific focus on position 118 may be new. Scientific importance: Limited. The ALD connection is hypothetical, and the abstract does not demonstrate clinical or functional relevance. Interdisciplinary readership: Narrow. The work is primarily of interest to computational biologists and ALD researchers; the abstract does not frame findings for a broader audience. Technical soundness: Not fully assessable from the abstract. The workflow is standard, but quantitative evidence is missing. Readability for nonspecialists: Acceptable but could be improved with clearer definitions and less jargon. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The abstract presents a reasonable computational study, but the lack of quantitative data and the explicitly hypothetical ALD link mean the core claims cannot be evaluated. Supportive if technical concerns are resolved and the ALD relevance is either substantiated or appropriately de-emphasized. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that I118F and I118N are "high-risk" variants is unsupported without population frequency data or experimental validation. The claim of "reduction in structural compactness" is unsupported without quantitative Rg values and statistical comparison. The claim of "more than one metastable state" is unsupported without free energy landscape data. The relevance of TNF variants to ALD-associated neuroinflammation is explicitly acknowledged as hypothetical and is therefore not an established claim.

01 基本信息 标题 ：Large-scale prospective evaluation of co-folding across hundreds of Mac1-ligand complexes and three virtual screens 作者与单位 ：Kim, Jongbin; Correy, Galen J; Hall, Brendan W; Rachman, Moira M; Mailhot, Olivier; Togo, Takaya; Gonciarz, Ryan L; Jaishankar, Priyadarshini; Neitz, R Jeffrey; Hantz, Eric R; Doruk, Yagmur U; Diolaiti, Morgan E; Reid, Rashad; Gopalkrishnan, Saumya; Krogan, Nevan J; Renslo, Adam R; Ashworth, Alan; Shoichet, Brian K; Fraser, James S（加州大学旧金山分校等，具体单位未提供） 期刊/预印本平台 ：eLife 年份 ：2026 论文类型 ：前瞻性基准评估（prospective evaluation） 领域 ：蛋白质-配体共折叠预测、虚拟筛选、结构生物学、AI 药物发现 关键词 ：co-folding, AlphaFold3, Boltz-2, Chai-1, Mac1, virtual screening, docking, structure-based drug design DOI/arXiv 号 ：10.7554/eLife.110475 代码 ：https://github.com/jongbin99/cofold-em 数据 ：468 个新 Mac1-配体复合物结构（PDB 收录），另有 22 个来自早期研究；三个虚拟筛选数据集来自 LSD（https://lsd.docking.org/） 阅读日期 ：2026-10-12 在课题方向中的位置 ：本文是共折叠（co-folding）深度学习方法（AF3、Boltz-2、Chai-1）在蛋白质-配体复合物结构预测与虚拟筛选重排序中的大规模前瞻性评估，直接面向「结构预测 × 分子对接 × AI 方法」交叉领域，提供了关于泛化性、记忆效应、置信度-亲和力相关性的关键证据。 02 一句话总结 本文通过 551 个训练截止日期后测定的 Mac1-配体共晶结构及三个大型虚拟筛选数据集，前瞻性评估了 AF3、Boltz-2、Chai-1 三种共折叠方法，发现它们能高保真重现多数配体构象（>50% 优于 2 Å RMSD），但无法捕捉蛋白构象变化，且其置信度/亲和力分数在区分真实配体与对接假阳性方面弱于传统对接打分。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：共折叠深度学习方法（AF3、Boltz-2、Chai-1）在训练截止日期后的全新蛋白质-配体复合物上，能否准确预测配体结合构象？其内部置信度/亲和力分数能否用于虚拟筛选命中重排序？ 为什么重要 ：共折叠方法被广泛用于结构预测和药物发现，但其评估多基于训练集内或回顾性数据，存在记忆效应风险；前瞻性、大规模、独立于训练数据的评估是判断其真实泛化能力的关键。 现有方法不足 ：已有评估样本量小、缺乏训练独立性控制，且多聚焦于蛋白结构预测而非配体构象与亲和力排序；DOCK 等物理方法虽快但精度有限，缺乏与深度学习方法在大规模前瞻性数据上的系统对比。 精确研究问题 ：Can co-folding methods (AF3, Boltz-2, Chai-1) prospectively predict ligand binding poses and rank ligands by affinity on complexes determined after their training cutoff dates, and do their confidence/affinity scores outperform docking in distinguishing true ligands from false positives in virtual screening hit lists? 04 背景与发展脉络 （标注：以下脉络为「经外部核验」的领域共识，结合本文引言整理） 1. AlphaFold2/RosettaFold 时代（2021-） ：革命性提升蛋白结构预测精度，但主要针对 apo 蛋白，无法直接处理配体。 2. 共折叠方法兴起（2024-） ：AF3、Chai-1、Boltz-2 等通过扩散模型或流匹配直接预测蛋白-配体复合物结构，并输出置信度分数（ipTM、pLTP）和亲和力预测（Boltz-2 pIC50）。 3. 回顾性评估的局限 ：早期评估多使用训练集内或已知结构，存在记忆效应；少量前瞻性研究样本量小，结论不一致。 4. 本文位置 ：首次在数百个训练截止后测定的复合物和三个大型虚拟筛选数据集上，系统评估共折叠方法的结构预测与亲和力排序能力，并与传统对接（DOCK3.7）对比，填补了前瞻性大规模评估的空白。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 训练数据记忆效应 模型可能在训练集内结构上表现好，但泛化未知 共折叠方法训练数据包含大量 PDB 结构，测试集若与训练集重叠会高估性能 作者特意选择训练截止日期后测定的 551 个复合物，并量化了与训练集的相似性（图 1d） 蛋白构象变化无法预测 配体结合诱导的肽段翻转、loop 开放等构象变化未被共折叠方法重现 共折叠方法倾向于预测 apo 或常见构象，缺乏对诱导-fit 的显式建模 19 个 twisted 态仅 4 个被 AF3 正确预测，20 个 open 态全部失败（图 2b） 置信度分数与亲和力相关性弱 AF3 L-pLDDT 与实验 IC50 相关性弱（r=0.314），DOCK 能量更弱（r=-0.225） 置信度分数主要反映结构确定性而非结合自由能；亲和力预测模块与结构模块解耦 图 4a，Results 节 虚拟筛选中假阳性区分度不足 AF3 L-pLDDT 在三个虚拟筛选数据集中 AUC 仅 46.4-60.5，部分低于随机 共折叠方法对高打分但非真实配体的分子缺乏物理化学区分能力 图 5a-c，Results 节 亲和力绝对误差大 Boltz-2 pIC50 在 Mac1 上 MAE 约 1.6 kcal/mol，校正后约 0.7 kcal/mol 亲和力预测模块训练数据有限，且对弱结合剂预测偏差大 图 4a，Results 节 06 核心思想 表面方法 ：对 551 个 Mac1-配体复合物和三个虚拟筛选数据集（AmpC、σ2、D4），分别运行 AF3、Boltz-2、Chai-1 共折叠预测，计算配体 RMSD、置信度分数（L-pLDDT、ipTM、pIC50），并与 DOCK3.7 对接打分对比，评估结构预测准确性和亲和力排序能力。 核心洞察 ： - 共折叠方法在配体构象预测上显著优于传统对接（>50% 优于 2 Å RMSD），且对训练集外分子泛化良好，说明其学到了可迁移的分子识别模式。 - 但共折叠方法无法预测蛋白构象变化（诱导-fit），且其置信度/亲和力分数在虚拟筛选假阳性区分上弱于对接打分，说明结构预测能力 ≠ 亲和力排序能力。 - 物理方法（DOCK）与深度学习方法（共折叠）的错误相关性低，提示两者在命中发现中可能互补。 可能的普适教训 [Analysis]：共折叠方法擅长「几何匹配」但缺乏「物理化学判别力」；在药物发现中，结构预测精度与亲和力排序是两种不同任务，应分别评估和优化；将物理打分与深度学习置信度结合可能是更优策略。 07 方法总览 输入 ：蛋白序列（Mac1、AmpC、σ2、D4）、配体 SMILES、蛋白结构（对接用，PDB 5SQW 等） 输出 ：预测的蛋白-配体复合物结构（mmCIF）、配体 RMSD、置信度分数（AF3 L-pLDDT、Chai-1 ipTM、Boltz-2 pIC50）、DOCK3.7 能量打分 模块 ： 1. They report that co-folding methods reproduce ligand poses with >50% accuracy at 2 Å RMSD, that confidence scores weakly track affinity, and that co-folding does not outperform docking in distinguishing true ligands from false positives in virtual screening hit lists. Visible evidence base Full text including results narrative, figure references, supplementary file references, methods section, and data availability statement Missing materials affecting confidence Figures, tables, and supplementary files referenced but not provided; specific numerical values for many reported statistics; details of statistical test implementations; complete crystallographic data Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript addresses an important and timely question: whether deep-learning co-folding methods can be applied prospectively to ligand pose prediction and virtual screening hit prioritization. The Mac1 dataset of 551 previously unpublished complexes is a substantial and valuable resource, and the prospective nature of the evaluation is a genuine strength. However, the manuscript's central claims are only partially supported by the evidence presented. The pose prediction results are convincing, but the affinity correlation analyses are weakened by the limited dynamic range of the dataset and the absence of key statistical details. The virtual screening results, while interesting, are presented in a way that makes it difficult to assess whether the conclusions are robust. The manuscript would benefit from clearer presentation of the statistical methods, additional analyses to support the claim of complementarity between docking and co-folding, and a more nuanced discussion of the limitations of the affinity predictions. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational chemists and structural biologists working on ligand-protein complex prediction and virtual screening will find this study directly relevant. Drug discovery scientists using structure-based methods will be interested in the practical implications for hit prioritization workflows. Developers of deep-learning methods for molecular modeling will find the prospective evaluation valuable for understanding the strengths and limitations of current approaches. The Mac1 dataset itself will be a useful benchmark for future method development. Major strengths The prospective design of the study is a significant strength, as it avoids the circularity that plagues many retrospective evaluations. The Mac1 dataset is large and previously unpublished, providing a genuinely independent test set. The comparison across three co-folding methods and three different targets in the virtual screening component adds breadth. The authors are appropriately cautious in their interpretation of the affinity correlations, acknowledging the limited dynamic range. The discussion of complementarity between physics-based and deep-learning approaches is thoughtful and well-framed. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Statistical rigor Claim pointer The authors report that Boltz-2 affinity predictions showed the strongest correlation with measured potency and achieved lower mean absolute error than a baseline predictor after calibration. Evidence pointer Results section, Figure 4a; Methods, Statistical analysis Concern The claim that Boltz-2 affinity predictions outperform a baseline predictor is based on a comparison to the mean pIC50 of the dataset. However, the dataset has a limited dynamic range (sub-micromolar to >500 µM), and the baseline predictor is not clearly defined. The manuscript does not report confidence intervals for the MAE values, nor does it specify how many compounds were used in the calibration. The statistical comparison between Boltz-2 and the baseline is not described with sufficient detail to assess its validity. Why it matters The claim that Boltz-2 provides meaningful affinity predictions is a key finding of the study. If the comparison to baseline is not statistically robust, the conclusion that co-folding methods can predict affinity is weakened. The limited dynamic range of the dataset may also inflate the apparent performance of the baseline predictor, making the comparison less meaningful. Resolution test The authors should provide a clear definition of the baseline predictor, report confidence intervals for all MAE values, and describe the statistical test used to compare Boltz-2 to the baseline. They should also report the distribution of pIC50 values in the dataset and discuss how the limited dynamic range affects the interpretation of the results. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The authors state that co-folding methods did not meaningfully outperform docking in distinguishing true ligands from false positives in the three virtual screening hit lists. Evidence pointer Results section, Figure 5; Methods, Benchmarking co-folding on experimentally validated compounds Concern The virtual screening analysis is presented with limited methodological detail. The manuscript does not specify how the hit lists were constructed, how many compounds were in each list, or how the thresholds for true hits and non-binders were defined for each target. The AUC values are reported, but the authors do not provide confidence intervals or statistical tests to determine whether the differences between methods are significant. The claim that co-folding methods "struggle" to re-rank hit lists is based on a comparison that may not be statistically powered. Why it matters The virtual screening results are a central component of the manuscript's conclusions about the limitations of co-folding methods. Without clear methodological details and statistical analysis, it is not possible to determine whether the findings are robust or whether they reflect the specific choices made in this study. Resolution test The authors should provide a detailed description of the hit list construction, including the number of compounds and the criteria for selecting them. They should report confidence intervals for all AUC values and perform statistical tests to compare the performance of different methods. They should also describe the thresholds used to define true hits and non-binders for each target.
