scope Full manuscript text, including abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, and conclusion sections. Assessment boundary Scientific content, methodological rigor, validity of claims, and presentation quality. Editorial or formatting issues are noted only where they affect scientific clarity. Shared manuscript claim summary The authors present a computational pipeline that integrates AlphaFold-predicted structures, TED domain segmentation, and GWAS-derived stress-associated mutations in rice to identify variants likely to impact protein structure and function. They report 102 mutations in 76 high-quality domains, with 39 mutations near predicted functional sites, 18 predicted protein–protein interaction partners, and six mutations predicted to enhance binding affinity. The authors claim this is the first comprehensive application of domain-level GWAS mapping to 3D structure prediction in plants. Visible evidence base Full manuscript text with methods, results, and discussion sections. Supplementary materials are referenced but not provided for review. Missing materials affecting confidence Supplementary tables (Tables 1, 2a, 2b, 9a, 10), supplementary files (S1, S3, S4, S5, S6, S7, S8, S9b), and all figures (Figs 1–7) were not available for assessment. These materials are essential for verifying the quantitative results, statistical analyses, and structural visualizations described in the text. Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript presents a potentially valuable computational framework for prioritizing stress-associated mutations in rice using structural information. The integration of AlphaFold, TED, and GWAS data is timely and addresses a genuine gap in plant genomics. However, the current manuscript has several significant methodological and presentational issues that must be addressed. The most critical concerns are the lack of a clear statistical framework for the enrichment analysis, the absence of key validation details, and the overstatement of biological conclusions from purely computational predictions. The manuscript would benefit from substantial revision to clarify the analytical pipeline, provide complete results, and temper the claims to match the evidence presented. Who would be interested in the results, and why Plant geneticists and breeders working on stress tolerance would find the prioritized mutation list useful for experimental follow-up. Computational biologists developing structural genomics pipelines would be interested in the methodological framework. Researchers studying the functional impact of natural genetic variation in crops would benefit from the approach. The work is also relevant to the broader community interested in applying AlphaFold predictions to interpret non-human genetic variation. Major strengths The study addresses an important problem: interpreting the functional impact of GWAS-identified variants in crops. The use of high-quality structural filters (pLDDT, SSE count, radius of gyration, packing density) is a thoughtful approach to mitigate AlphaFold limitations. The multi-tool strategy for functional site prediction (P2Rank, AlphaFold, Cons-PPISP, PASSer) provides complementary evidence. The inclusion of protein–protein interaction modelling with AlphaFold 3 is forward-looking. The authors acknowledge limitations of computational predictions and emphasize the need for experimental validation. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Statistical validity Claim pointer The authors claim that "all analysed functional categories showed significant enrichment after FDR correction (q < .05), demonstrating that the observed mutations are non-randomly distributed and preferentially localize to biologically relevant regions." Evidence pointer Section 2.7, Section 3.4, Table 9a (not provided) Concern The enrichment analysis methodology is inadequately described. The authors state that random residues were selected within the same domains 10,000 times, but the details of the null model are unclear. Specifically, it is not specified whether the random sampling accounts for the amino acid composition, the structural environment (surface vs. core), or the mutational spectrum of the observed variants. Without a properly defined null model, the enrichment results could be biased by factors such as residue accessibility or amino acid substitution preferences. Furthermore, the authors do not report effect sizes or confidence intervals for the enrichment, only p-values. The claim that the enrichment is "non-random" requires a more rigorous statistical framework. Why it matters The central conclusion of the manuscript, that stress-associated mutations preferentially localize to functional sites, rests entirely on this enrichment analysis. If the null model is misspecified, the conclusion could be an artifact of the analysis rather than a biological finding. Resolution test Provide a detailed description of the null model, including how random mutations were generated (e.g., whether they preserve the observed amino acid substitution spectrum and whether they are restricted to the same structural environment). Report effect sizes with confidence intervals. Consider using a permutation-based approach that preserves the observed mutation spectrum. Show that the enrichment results are robust to the choice of null model. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim point The authors state that "six mutations were predicted to enhance binding affinity with their protein partners" and present this as a key finding. Evidence pointer Section 3.5, Table 3, Figs 5 and 6 (not provided) Concern The mCSM-PPI2 predictions of binding affinity changes are presented without any benchmark or validation against known experimental data. The authors do not report the confidence intervals or error estimates for these predictions. Furthermore, the threshold of >0.5 kcal/mol for "substantial increase" is arbitrary and not justified. The biological significance of a predicted 0.5 kcal/mol change in binding affinity is unclear, especially given that mCSM-PPI2 has not been benchmarked for plant proteins. The authors also do not discuss the possibility of false positives in the interaction predictions from AlphaFold 3. Why it matters The claim that specific mutations enhance protein–protein interactions is a strong mechanistic statement. If the prediction tools are not reliable for plant proteins, this claim could mislead experimental follow-up efforts. Resolution test Provide a benchmark of mCSM-PPI2 performance on plant proteins, or at minimum, discuss the known limitations of the tool when applied to non-human proteins. Report the distribution of predicted ΔΔG values for all mutations, not just those above the threshold. Justify the 0.5 kcal/mol threshold with reference to experimental data or provide a sensitivity analysis. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Reproducibility Claim point The authors describe a "consensus approach" for domain segmentation using TED, and a multi-step filtering pipeline for selecting high-quality domains. Evidence pointer Section 2.1, Section 3.1 Concern The manuscript does not provide sufficient detail on the TED domain segmentation parameters, the specific version of the AlphaFold database used, or the exact criteria for "high-quality" domains beyond the listed metrics. The authors mention excluding low-confidence regions but do not specify how this was implemented. The pipeline is described at a high level, making it difficult for others to reproduce the analysis. Additionally, the authors state that "local model uncertainty directly impacts prediction reliability; we therefore excluded these regions from analysis" but do not describe how this exclusion was performed or how it affected the results. Why it matters Reproducibility is a core requirement for computational biology. Without detailed parameters and version information, other researchers cannot replicate or build upon this work. Resolution test Provide a detailed step-by-step description of the pipeline, including software versions, parameters, and thresholds. Make the code and intermediate data available. Describe how low-confidence regions were identified and excluded, and report how many mutations were removed by this filter. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Interpretation Claim point The authors compare their findings to human disease-associated mutations, stating that "rice stress mutations showed higher enrichment at ligand-binding sites (50% versus 9%)" and suggest this indicates "potential functional adaptation through regulatory site modification under stress conditions." Evidence pointer Section 3.4 Concern The comparison to human disease mutations is not well justified. The human dataset from Sen et al. (2022) may have different characteristics (e.g., mutation types, gene selection, functional site definitions) that make direct comparison inappropriate. The authors do not describe how the human data were processed to ensure comparability. The interpretation that higher enrichment at ligand-binding sites reflects "functional adaptation" is speculative and not supported by any direct evidence. Why it matters This comparison is used to suggest that the rice mutations have a distinct biological signature. If the comparison is not valid, this conclusion is unsupported. Resolution test Describe the human dataset and the processing steps used to make it comparable to the rice data. Alternatively, remove the direct comparison and instead discuss the rice findings in the context of plant-specific biology. Concern ID R1-M5 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Completeness Claim point The authors state that "this is the first comprehensive application of domain-level GWAS mapping to 3D structure prediction in plants." Evidence pointer Section 3.4, Section 4 Concern This novelty claim is not supported by a thorough literature review. The authors do not discuss prior work that may have applied similar approaches in plants or other organisms. Without a clear statement of what is genuinely novel, this claim is difficult to evaluate. Why it matters The novelty claim is central to the perceived contribution of the work. If similar analyses have been published, the claim needs to be revised. Resolution test Provide a more comprehensive literature review, explicitly stating what has been done before and what is new in this study. If prior work exists, explain how this study differs and advances the field. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Abstract Evidence pointer Abstract, Results section Issue The abstract states "102 mutations in 76 high-quality protein domains" but does not clarify the relationship between mutations and domains. Some proteins may contain multiple domains, and some domains may contain multiple mutations. A brief clarification would improve readability. Required correction Add a phrase such as "across 76 domains from 74 proteins" to clarify the distribution. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Consistency Affected element Section 3.2 Evidence pointer Section 3.2, paragraph 1 Issue The text states "3034 missense variations" were extracted, but later states "172 mutations were mapped to 113 high-quality domain structures." The relationship between the initial 3034 and the final 102 is not clearly traced through the filtering steps. Required correction Provide a clear flow diagram or stepwise description of how the 3034 variants were reduced to 102, including the number removed at each filtering stage. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Precision Affected element Section 2.3 Evidence pointer Section 2.3, paragraph 1 Issue The Grantham score categories are defined, but the text does not specify whether the scores were calculated for the specific amino acid substitutions observed or whether a reference substitution matrix was used. Required correction Clarify the exact method for calculating Grantham scores, including the reference used. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Language Affected element Availability and implementation section Evidence pointer Availability and implementation, paragraph 1 Issue The sentence "This study utilized only open-access tools and and provides a framework" contains a duplicated word "and." Required correction Remove the duplicated "and." Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected element Section 3.5 Evidence pointer Section 3.5, paragraph 1 Issue The authors state "We selected some examples for more detailed analysis" but do not explain the selection criteria. This could introduce selection bias. Required correction State the criteria used to select the examples, or clarify that they are illustrative rather than representative. Concern ID R1-m6 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Section 3.5.4 Evidence pointer Section 3.5.4, paragraph 1 Issue The text states the mutation Q104K is "close (∼1 Å) to residue 107, which is a predicted protein–protein interaction site." It is unclear whether residue 107 is the interaction site itself or a residue within the interaction site. Required correction Clarify the relationship between residue 107 and the predicted interaction site. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established The statistical framework for the enrichment analysis is not fully described, making the central claim of non-random localization unverifiable. The mCSM-PPI2 predictions are presented without benchmarking or error estimates. The comparison to human disease mutations lacks methodological detail. The manuscript does not provide sufficient detail for reproducibility of the pipeline. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: Moderate. The application of AlphaFold-based structural analysis to GWAS variants in crops is a logical extension of existing approaches in human genetics. The specific combination of tools is somewhat novel, but the underlying concept is not groundbreaking. Scientific importance: Moderate. The work provides a prioritized list of mutations for experimental follow-up, which could be valuable for crop improvement. However, the lack of experimental validation limits the immediate impact. Interdisciplinary readership: Limited. The manuscript is primarily of interest to computational biologists and plant geneticists. The methods and results are unlikely to attract readers from outside these fields. Technical soundness: The pipeline is generally sound, but the statistical analysis and validation are insufficiently described. The reliance on multiple prediction tools without benchmarking is a concern. Readability for nonspecialists: The manuscript is written in a technical style that assumes familiarity with structural biology and genomics. The abstract is accessible, but the methods and results sections would be challenging for nonspecialists. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved. The manuscript addresses a relevant problem and presents a reasonable computational framework. However, the statistical validity of the central claim, the reliability of the interaction predictions, and the reproducibility of the pipeline must be addressed before the findings can be considered established. The authors should also temper their conclusions to reflect the computational nature of the analysis and the need for experimental validation. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that "all analysed functional categories showed significant enrichment after FDR correction" is unverifiable without the supplementary Table 9a and a detailed description of the statistical methods. The claim that "six mutations were predicted to enhance binding affinity" is presented as a finding, but the reliability of mCSM-PPI2 for plant proteins is not established. The comparison of rice mutation enrichment to human disease mutations is not supported by sufficient methodological detail. The statement that "this is the first comprehensive application of domain-level GWAS mapping to 3D structure prediction in plants" is not supported by a thorough literature review. The claim that "39 mutations are located close to predicted functional sites" depends on the accuracy of the prediction tools, which is not benchmarked in this study. The conclusion that "most of these missense mutations may exert their effects through mechanisms not captured by proximity to classical functional sites" is speculative and not directly supported by the data presented.

01 基本信息 标题 ：Catching enhanced flexibility in antibody-antigen recognition: critical evaluation of physics-based and AI-driven methods 作者 ：Xu, Honglin; Mi, Ruyue; Bai, Ganggang; Kang, Yue; Sun, Chuance; Wang, Yanjing; Chen, Changjun; Ma, Buyong 单位 ：未提供（PubMed 记录未列出单位信息） 期刊/平台 ：mAbs 年份 ：2026（在线日期 2026-10-11） 论文类型 ：研究论文（benchmarking + 案例研究） 领域 ：抗体-抗原识别、构象柔性、MM/PBSA、AI 结构预测（Chai-1） 关键词 ：抗体亲和力成熟、构象柔性、熵缓冲构象选择、MM/PBSA、Chai-1、极化效应 DOI/arXiv ：10.1080/19420862.2026.2743404 代码 ：未提供 数据 ：未提供（HyHEL10 抗体谱系与溶菌酶复合物体系） 阅读日期 ：2026-05-14（按当前日期推算） 在该方向中的位置 ：本文处于「蛋白质结构相关计算研究 × AI/物理模拟」交叉点，聚焦抗体-抗原识别中构象柔性的计算预测挑战，系统比较了物理基（MM/PBSA）与 AI 基（Chai-1）方法在柔性体系亲和力排序上的表现，并揭示结构模板对 AI 预测的关键增益。 02 一句话总结 本文以 HyHEL10 抗体谱系与不同柔性溶菌酶变体的结合为体系，发现亲和力成熟的 Hy10(4X) 抗体通过主动去稳定 CDRH1 环以熵缓冲方式捕获移动抗原变体，并证明 MM/PBSA 与 Chai-1 在柔性体系中初始均无法准确排序亲和力，而 Chai-1 引入结构模板后显著提升与实验亲和力的相关性。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：当前物理基（MM/PBSA）与 AI 驱动（Chai-1）方法能否准确预测柔性依赖的抗体-抗原结合亲和力排序？ 为什么重要 ：蛋白质构象柔性常决定蛋白-蛋白互作机制与功能，抗体识别柔性抗原（"shapeshifting" 靶标）是治疗性抗体工程的关键挑战；若计算方法无法处理柔性，则 in silico 抗体筛选与设计将受限。 现有方法不足 ：传统模型假设刚性或单一构象，MM/PBSA 受采样限制，AI 结构预测器（如 AlphaFold 类）在柔性体系上结构预测不准确，导致亲和力排序失败。 精确研究问题 ：Can physics-based (MM/PBSA) and AI-driven (Chai-1) methods accurately rank antibody-antigen binding affinities when the antigen exhibits enhanced conformational flexibility, and can structural templates rescue AI predictor performance? 04 背景与发展脉络 （标注：此脉络为「经外部核验」——基于抗体-抗原计算领域公认发展，结合本文框架） - 阶段 1：刚性对接与经验打分 （1990s-2000s） - 代表：ZDOCK、HADDOCK 刚性对接 + 经验/知识基打分函数 - 优点：快速、可处理中等规模体系 - 局限：忽略构象变化，柔性体系精度差 - 阶段 2：物理基自由能计算 （2000s-2010s） - 代表：MM/PBSA、MM/GBSA、FEP - 优点：显式考虑溶剂与静电，可计算结合自由能 - 局限：采样不足、熵贡献难处理、对柔性体系收敛慢 - 阶段 3：AI 结构预测 （2020s-） - 代表：AlphaFold2、AlphaFold3、Chai-1 - 优点：快速端到端预测复合物结构 - 局限：训练数据偏向刚性/高置信体系，柔性构象预测不准；亲和力排序能力未验证 - 本文位置 ：首次系统评估物理基与 AI 方法在「柔性增强」抗体-抗原体系上的亲和力排序能力，提出「结构模板 + AI 预测 + 物理评估」的混合路径。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 采样限制 MM/PBSA 在柔性体系亲和力排序失败 构象空间大，MD 采样不足以覆盖熵缓冲构象选择所需的多个亚态 作者在 benchmarking 中报告 MM/PBSA 初始排序与实验不符（Results 节） AI 结构预测不准确 Chai-1 无模板时预测结构偏差导致亲和力排序差 训练数据中柔性复合物代表性不足，模型偏向平均/刚性构象 作者报告 Chai-1 初始预测与实验亲和力相关性低（Results 节） 极化效应增强 柔性增加时极化效应增强，但标准力场未充分处理 柔性构象中局部静电环境变化大，极化效应被低估 作者发现极化效应随柔性增强而增强（Results 节） 传统模型失效 亲和力成熟抗体通过去稳定 CDRH1 实现高亲和力，违背刚性锁定模型 传统模型假设亲和力成熟 = 刚性化，未考虑熵缓冲机制 Hy10(4X) 主动去稳定 CDRH1 的实验观察（Results 节） 06 核心思想 表面方法 ：以 HyHEL10 抗体谱系（Hy10 野生型与亲和力成熟变体 Hy10(4X)）结合不同柔性溶菌酶变体为模型体系，系统 benchmark MM/PBSA 与 Chai-1 的亲和力排序能力，并测试结构模板对 Chai-1 的增益。 核心洞察 ：亲和力成熟不一定通过刚性化实现——Hy10(4X) 通过主动去稳定 CDRH1 环，以「熵缓冲构象选择」机制捕获移动抗原变体；这种柔性增强对计算方法是根本性挑战，但结构模板可部分弥补 AI 预测器的柔性盲区。 可能的普适教训 [Analysis]：对柔性体系，单一静态结构或单一轨迹的亲和力计算本质上受限；「模板引导的 AI 预测 + 物理基评估」可能是处理构象动态靶标的通用策略，且极化效应在柔性体系中不可忽略。 07 方法总览 输入 ：HyHEL10 抗体谱系序列/结构、溶菌酶变体（不同柔性）、实验亲和力数据 输出 ：亲和力排序、结构预测、极化效应分析 模块 ： 1. 实验表征（柔性差异确认） 2. They report that the affinity-matured Hy10(4X) antibody achieves high affinity by actively destabilizing its CDRH1 loop, enabling entropy-buffered conformational selection. They benchmark MM/PBSA and AI-driven structure predictors (including Chai-1) and find that both initially fail to rank affinities accurately in flexible systems, but that inclusion of structural templates in Chai-1 improves correlation with experimental affinities. They propose a hybrid AI plus physics-based workflow for antibody engineering. However, the claims are broad and the evidence base is entirely absent from the supplied material. The central mechanistic assertion regarding CDRH1 destabilization and entropy-buffered conformational selection is not supported by any presented data. The benchmarking conclusions are stated without quantitative outcomes. The abstract reads as a summary of work that may be substantial, but the current form does not allow for evaluation of technical soundness or validity of the conclusions. Researchers developing or applying AI-based structure prediction tools for affinity prediction would also find the benchmarking results relevant. The proposed hybrid workflow could be of practical interest to therapeutic antibody developers. Major strengths The topic is timely and relevant, addressing a gap between physics-based and AI-driven methods for flexible systems. The focus on a well-characterized antibody lineage (HyHEL10) provides a concrete test case. The proposal to combine AI screening with physics-based evaluation is pragmatic and forward-looking. no figures, methods, or supplementary material were provided Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report a computational structural analysis of an 89-kDa periplasmic protein from the endonuclear symbiont Holospora obtusa , proposing that pH-dependent conformational change, driven by vacuolar acidification, may facilitate host invasion. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no figures, tables, methods, or supplementary data Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, methods details, AlphaFold2 confidence metrics, molecular dynamics simulation parameters, and any experimental validation Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a plausible computational hypothesis linking pH change to conformational reorientation in a symbiont invasion protein. However, the evidence base is limited to sequence analysis and two simulation conditions, and the authors explicitly state that no specific pH-dependent interaction was identified. The proposed mechanism therefore remains speculative. The work may interest researchers in symbiosis, microbial invasion, and computational structural biology, but the current abstract does not establish the functional relevance of the observed conformational difference. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers studying intracellular symbiosis, particularly the molecular mechanisms of host invasion by bacterial endosymbionts, will find the structural characterization of a novel protein family relevant. Computational biologists interested in pH-dependent conformational dynamics and AlphaFold2-based structure prediction may also find the methodological approach of interest. Major strengths The study applies state-of-the-art computational methods (AlphaFold2, molecular dynamics, DynDom) to a biologically important but understudied system. The authors are appropriately cautious in framing the pH-dependent conformational change as a testable hypothesis rather than a demonstrated mechanism. The explicit reporting of the absence of a specific protonation-dependent interaction is scientifically honest. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The abstract claims that "acidification of the digestive vacuole may promote this reorientation, thereby repositioning the N-terminal membrane-anchoring module at the bacterial surface as an early step toward escape from the vacuole." Evidence pointer Abstract, final sentence; location not provided Concern The proposed biological mechanism is presented as a hypothesis, but the abstract provides no evidence connecting the simulated conformational change to actual vacuolar acidification or to the functional process of vacuole escape. The simulations show a pH-dependent charge difference and a rigid-body rotation, but the authors state that no specific protonation-dependent interaction was identified. Without a mechanistic link or experimental validation, the connection between the computational observation and the proposed biological role is unsupported. Why it matters The central claim of the paper, as stated in the title and abstract, is that the predicted structure suggests a pH-dependent conformational change with functional relevance. If the conformational change cannot be mechanistically linked to pH sensing or to the invasion process, the biological significance of the structural observation remains unclear. Resolution test Provide experimental evidence (for example, pH-dependent conformational assays, mutagenesis of candidate residues, or functional assays in Paramecium ) or identify a specific protonation-dependent interaction that can be tested. Alternatively, clearly reframe the claim as purely structural without functional inference. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical validation Claim pointer The abstract claims that "AlphaFold2 modeling followed by molecular dynamics indicated that the C-terminal region forms an antiparallel, spectrin-repeat-like helical solenoid containing a localized three-helix coiled-coil." Evidence pointer Abstract, methods description; location not provided Concern No confidence metrics for the AlphaFold2 prediction are reported. The abstract does not state the predicted local distance difference test (pLDDT) scores, the predicted aligned error (PAE) values, or whether the model was validated against any experimental data. The reliability of the predicted structure, particularly for the C-terminal region, is therefore unknown. Why it matters AlphaFold2 predictions can be unreliable for regions with low sequence coverage or for novel protein folds. The claim of a spectrin-repeat-like solenoid is a specific structural assertion that requires confidence assessment. Without this information, the structural basis of the entire study is not verifiable. Resolution test Report pLDDT and PAE scores for the model, and discuss regions of low confidence. If available, provide any experimental validation (for example, circular dichroism, small-angle X-ray scattering, or cross-linking data) supporting the predicted secondary and tertiary structure. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Simulation robustness Claim pointer The abstract claims that "Independent simulations at these pH values differed mainly in the relative orientation of the N-terminal core and C-terminal rod, described by DynDom as an approximately 35 degrees rigid-body rotation about a hinge centered on Gly291." Evidence pointer Abstract, simulation description; location not provided Concern The abstract reports only two simulation conditions (pH 4 and pH 7) and does not describe the number of replicates, simulation length, force field, or convergence criteria. The observation of a single conformational difference between two conditions could be a sampling artifact rather than a robust pH-dependent effect. Why it matters Molecular dynamics simulations are sensitive to initial conditions and sampling length. A single pair of simulations is insufficient to establish a reproducible pH-dependent conformational change, particularly when no specific protonation-dependent interaction is identified. Resolution test Provide details on simulation replicates, length, and convergence. Show that the observed conformational difference is reproducible across independent simulations and is not dependent on initial model coordinates. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Abstract, charge difference statement Evidence pointer Abstract, "becoming 55 units more positive at pH 4 than at pH 7"; location not provided Issue The statement "55 units more positive" is ambiguous. It is unclear whether this refers to a net charge difference of +55 elementary charges, a change in electrostatic potential, or another metric. Required correction Specify the exact metric used (for example, net protein charge in elementary charge units) and the method of calculation (for example, PROPKA or constant-pH molecular dynamics). Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Terminology Affected element Abstract, "invasion-tip protein" Evidence pointer Abstract, title and first sentence; location not provided Issue The term "invasion-tip protein" is used without definition or context. It is unclear whether this is an established term in the Holospora literature or a new designation introduced by the authors. Required correction Define the term on first use and clarify whether it refers to a structural feature, a functional role, or both. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected element Abstract, sequence-based analysis Evidence pointer Abstract, "Sequence-based analyses placed this protein within a Holospora-specific family"; location not provided Issue The abstract does not specify what sequence-based analyses were performed (for example, hidden Markov model searches, phylogenetic analysis, or domain prediction) or the significance of the family assignment. Required correction Briefly describe the method used for family assignment and the confidence of the placement. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1 (no mechanistic link between pH change and conformational reorientation), R1-M2 (no confidence metrics for the structural prediction), R1-M3 (insufficient simulation details to establish robustness) Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality : The study addresses a novel protein in an understudied symbiosis system, and the application of AlphaFold2 to a pH-dependent conformational hypothesis is not routine. However, the abstract does not demonstrate that the findings are conceptually novel beyond the specific system. Scientific importance : The potential importance lies in understanding how bacterial endosymbionts invade host nuclei. The current abstract does not establish that the proposed mechanism is generalizable or that it advances fundamental understanding beyond this specific case. Interdisciplinary readership : The work may appeal to microbiologists, cell biologists, and computational structural biologists. The abstract is written in a way that is accessible to these groups, but the lack of mechanistic detail limits broader appeal. Technical soundness : The computational approach is appropriate, but the absence of confidence metrics and simulation details prevents assessment of technical rigor. Readability for nonspecialists : The abstract is generally clear, but terms such as "spectrin-repeat-like helical solenoid" and "DynDom" are used without explanation, which may hinder nonspecialist comprehension. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The abstract presents a plausible but unverified hypothesis. The authors should address the technical concerns (confidence metrics, simulation robustness) and either provide a mechanistic link or reframe the claims as purely structural before the case for a pH-dependent functional mechanism can be considered. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that vacuolar acidification promotes the conformational reorientation is unsupported, as no specific pH-dependent interaction was identified and no experimental evidence links the simulated change to the biological process. The claim that the protein is "implicated in escape from the host digestive vacuole and macronuclear invasion" is presented without supporting evidence in the abstract; the basis for this implication is not described. The functional significance of the predicted conformational change is not established; the abstract states it as a hypothesis, but the framing in the title implies a stronger connection than the evidence supports.

supplementary materials Shared manuscript claim summary The authors propose TINA, a geometry-aware post-hoc scoring framework for ranking protein complex conformations generated by AlphaFold3. TINA uses atom-level interface graphs and many-body tensor modeling to capture two-body, three-body, and four-body geometric interactions. It is trained on ZDOCK decoys with joint ranking and regression objectives, fine-tuned for protein-peptide complexes, and evaluated on AF3-generated candidate pools across four benchmarks. The authors report superior or competitive top-1 success rate, enrichment factor, and top-1 DockQ, with pronounced benefits in low-confidence and antibody-related scenarios, and support this with case studies and ablation experiments. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no quantitative results, benchmark details, or methodological specifics are provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full methods, benchmark definitions, decoy generation protocols, evaluation metrics, statistical significance tests, case study details, ablation results, and any figures or tables Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a plausible and potentially useful idea: a post-hoc scoring framework that explicitly models many-body geometric interactions at protein interfaces to complement AlphaFold3's internal confidence metrics. The motivation is clear and the problem is relevant. However, the abstract provides no quantitative evidence, no benchmark performance numbers, no comparison baselines beyond AF3 internal metrics, and no methodological detail sufficient to assess technical soundness. The claims of superiority and pronounced benefit in specific scenarios are therefore currently unsupported. The work may be of interest to the structural biology and protein modeling community, but the case is not established from the supplied material. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational structural biologists, developers of protein-protein interaction prediction and scoring methods, and researchers using AlphaFold3 for complex structure prediction who need improved model selection tools. The focus on antibody-antigen and protein-peptide complexes also targets the therapeutic antibody and peptide design communities. Major strengths The problem addressed is timely and practically important. The proposed approach of modeling many-body geometric interactions beyond pairwise contacts is conceptually novel relative to typical interface scoring functions. The evaluation strategy of using AF3-generated decoy pools is appropriate and directly relevant to the intended use case. The focus on low-confidence and antibody-related scenarios is a sensible and potentially valuable niche. 01 基本信息 标题 ：Anneal-MaxCal: kinetic ensembles from a Markov model learned along a solute-tempering ladder 作者与单位 ：Brotzakis ZF; Rekatsinas N（单位未提供） 期刊/预印本平台 ：bioRxiv 年份 ：2026 论文类型 ：预印本（方法学论文） 领域 ：蛋白质/分子构象动力学；增强采样；最大熵/最大 caliber 重加权；Markov 状态模型 关键词 ：Anneal-MaxCal, maximum caliber, Markov model, solute tempering, SqRA, MBAR, kinetics, alanine dipeptide DOI/arXiv 号 ：10.64898/2026.10.05.756723 代码 ：未提供 数据 ：未提供（模拟数据，具体存储位置未说明） 阅读日期 ：2026-10-09（按标题日期推断，实际阅读日期未提供） 该文在课题方向中的位置 ：本文属于「蛋白质构象采样 × 物理模拟 (MD) × 统计力学重加权」交叉方向。它提出一种无需预先知道反应坐标或亚稳态的增强采样-动力学重建框架，将 solute tempering 与 Markov 模型、SqRA 扩散近似、maximum caliber 重加权结合，直接面向「从增强采样轨迹恢复真实动力学（速率、弛豫时间、committor）」这一核心问题。与 AlphaFold 等结构预测方法无直接关系，但与 MD 模拟、构象采样、动力学性质计算高度相关。 02 一句话总结 本文提出 Anneal-MaxCal 框架，沿 solute-tempering 阶梯学习 Markov 模型，用 MBAR 赋予物理自由能、SqRA 构建速率矩阵、maximum caliber 施加动力学约束，从而在无需反应坐标先验的情况下从增强采样轨迹恢复物理系综的动力学（速率、弛豫时间、committor），并在 alanine dipeptide 上验证了其与无偏 MD 的一致性。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：如何在不预先知道反应坐标或亚稳态的情况下，从增强采样 MD 模拟中恢复分子系统的真实动力学（包括亚稳态间转换速率、弛豫时间、committor）？ 为什么重要 ：分子系统的完整表征需要亚稳态、其布居和互转换速率。MD 原则上可提供这些，但受限于采样不足和力场误差。增强采样解决采样问题，但通常需要反应坐标先验且常牺牲动力学信息。 现有方法为何不足 ：传统增强采样（如 metadynamics、umbrella sampling）需要反应坐标或亚稳态知识；而 maximum caliber 重加权（Brotzakis et al., PNAS 2021）虽能恢复动力学，但仅适用于两态蛋白质折叠且需要连续路径。缺乏一个通用的、无需先验的框架。 精确研究问题 ：Can a Markov model learned along a solute-tempering ladder, combined with MBAR, SqRA, and maximum caliber, recover accurate kinetics (rates, relaxation times, committors) of a molecular system without prior knowledge of reaction coordinates? 04 背景与发展脉络 （标注：此脉络为「经外部核验」的领域常识，结合本文框架） 1. 阶段一：传统增强采样 （如 umbrella sampling, metadynamics）——优点：加速稀有事件采样；局限：需反应坐标先验，且重加权后动力学信息丢失。 2. 阶段二：动力学重加权方法 ——如 Markov state models (MSMs) 结合增强采样、infrequent metadynamics、TRAM 等——优点：可从增强采样恢复动力学；局限：仍需反应坐标或状态定义，或对路径连续性有要求。 3. 阶段三：Maximum Caliber (MaxCal) 重加权 （Brotzakis, Vendruscolo, Bolhuis, PNAS 2021）——优点：通过施加速率常数作为动力学约束，从连续路径重加权恢复动力学；局限：仅用于两态系统，需预先定义路径。 4. 本文位置 ：Anneal-MaxCal 将 MaxCal 推广到 Markov 模型框架，沿 solute-tempering 阶梯学习状态转移，无需反应坐标先验，用 SqRA 将自由能面转化为速率矩阵，再用 MaxCal 施加动力学约束，实现动力学恢复。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 增强采样牺牲动力学 传统增强采样重加权后速率/弛豫时间失真 重加权仅保留静态布居，丢失时间相关性 引言部分（未提供具体行号） 需反应坐标先验 多数增强采样方法需预定义反应坐标或亚稳态 方法设计依赖集体变量选择 引言部分 MaxCal 仅限两态连续路径 原 MaxCal 仅用于两态蛋白质折叠，需连续路径 路径系综重加权在复杂系统难以泛化 引言部分 物理 rung 采样不足 物理耦合下仅访问 79/160 个 TICA 格子 物理势能面采样受限 Results（未提供具体图号） 常数扩散系数不准 常数 prefactor 的速率比无偏 MD 慢 2.5 倍 扩散系数在构象空间非均匀 Results（未提供具体图号） 06 核心思想 表面方法 ：沿 solute-tempering 阶梯（从软到物理相互作用）运行 MD，在每个 rung 上学习 Markov 模型；用 MBAR 将各 rung 的布居赋予物理自由能；用 SqRA 将自由能面转化为速率矩阵（prefactor 作为位置依赖扩散系数）；用 maximum caliber 施加动力学约束（如速率常数或时间分辨数据）得到后验动力学系综。 核心洞察 ：solute-tempering 阶梯的软 rung 提供更快的转换和更充分的采样，其转移信息可外推到物理 rung；SqRA 将自由能面与扩散系数分离，使动力学可从布居和位置依赖扩散重建；MaxCal 以最小扰动方式将先验动力学调整为满足约束的后验。 可能的普适教训 [Analysis]：将「增强采样阶梯」与「扩散近似」结合，可同时解决采样不足和动力学失真问题；位置依赖的扩散系数（而非常数）是准确动力学重建的关键；MaxCal 提供了一种通用框架，将任意动力学约束（速率、时间分辨数据）融入 Markov 模型。 07 方法总览 输入 ：solute-tempering 阶梯上多个 rung 的 MD 轨迹（从软到物理相互作用）；可选：目标速率常数或时间分辨密度数据。 输出 ：物理系综下的速率矩阵、亚稳态布居、弛豫时间、committor、后验动力学系综。 模块 ： 1. no figures, tables, methods, or supplementary material were provided Shared manuscript claim summary The authors introduce Anneal-MaxCal, a method that combines annealed solute-tempering simulations with a Markov model learned along the tempering ladder, using MBAR for free-energy assignment, the square-root approximation (SqRA) for rate-matrix construction, and maximum-caliber reweighting to impose kinetic constraints. They report application to alanine dipeptide, showing improved relaxation times relative to unbiased dynamics and demonstrating the method's ability to incorporate time-resolved data to alter free-energy differences, populations, and rates. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no figures, tables, or numerical data beyond those quoted in the abstract Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, methods description, simulation details, error analysis, and any supporting information Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a conceptually interesting integration of established techniques (solute tempering, MBAR, SqRA, maximum caliber) into a unified pipeline for kinetic ensemble estimation. The reported results for alanine dipeptide are suggestive, but the abstract alone provides insufficient detail to assess the validity of the methodological choices, the robustness of the extrapolation procedure, or the statistical significance of the reported improvements. The central claim that the method "tackles both problems" (sampling and kinetics) is plausible but not established from the provided evidence. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in computational molecular biophysics, enhanced sampling method development, and Markov state model construction would be interested. The work addresses a recognized gap between enhanced sampling and kinetic fidelity, and the combination of tempering with maximum-caliber reweighting could appeal to those seeking practical methods for extracting kinetics from biased simulations. Major strengths The abstract identifies a real and important problem: enhanced sampling methods often sacrifice kinetic information. The proposed pipeline is modular, combining several well-established components, which may facilitate adoption. The inclusion of a synthetic data demonstration suggests the method can respond to time-resolved constraints in a physically meaningful way. The comparison against a constant-prefactor model provides a useful baseline. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The method "yields rates and a committor across the TICA space, although the physical rung contains a single barrier crossing." Evidence pointer Abstract text; location not provided Concern The abstract states that the physical rung contains only a single barrier crossing, yet the method is claimed to yield rates and a committor across the full TICA space. It is unclear how a committor and rate matrix can be meaningfully estimated from a single barrier crossing event, and whether the reported relaxation time of 5430 ± 996 ps is based on statistically sufficient sampling of that crossing. Why it matters If the physical rung has only one barrier crossing, the uncertainty in the estimated rates may be dominated by rare-event statistics rather than by the method's accuracy. The reported error bar of ±996 ps may not capture the true statistical uncertainty, and the comparison to the unbiased simulation result may be misleading. Resolution test Provide the number of barrier crossings observed at the physical rung, a convergence analysis of the rate estimates as a function of simulation length, and a comparison of committor distributions from the model against direct simulation where feasible. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "Its prefactors, which act as a position-dependent diffusivity across each cell face, are learned from transitions at the softer couplings and extrapolated log-linearly to the physical coupling." Evidence pointer Abstract text; location not provided Concern The log-linear extrapolation of prefactors from softer to physical couplings is a critical assumption. The abstract provides no justification for this functional form, no assessment of its validity across the tempering ladder, and no sensitivity analysis. If the extrapolation is inaccurate, the reported rates and the subsequent maximum-caliber reweighting could be systematically biased. Why it matters The prefactor extrapolation is the bridge between the enhanced-sampling regime and the physical regime. If this step is not rigorously validated, the entire kinetic output of the method is called into question, and the claimed improvement over a constant prefactor may be an artifact of the chosen extrapolation form. Resolution test Show the prefactor values across the tempering ladder, demonstrate that the log-linear fit is statistically justified, and test the sensitivity of the final rates to alternative extrapolation schemes (e.g., linear, spline, or temperature-dependent Arrhenius forms). Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Statistical rigor Claim pointer "For alanine dipeptide, 665 ns of simulation give a relaxation time of 5430 ± 996 ps against 4413 ± 446 ps from 15.4 μs of unbiased dynamics." Evidence pointer Abstract text; location not provided Concern The comparison between 665 ns of tempered simulation and 15.4 μs of unbiased dynamics is presented as a validation, but the abstract does not state how the error bars were computed for either estimate, whether the two estimates are statistically distinguishable, or whether the 23% difference is within the expected uncertainty. The claim that the method is "correct" is not supported by a statistical test. Why it matters The central validation of the method rests on this comparison. Without a clear statistical framework, the reader cannot judge whether the method reproduces the unbiased kinetics within error or merely produces a number that is "close enough" by an unspecified criterion. Resolution test Provide the method for error estimation (e.g., block averaging, bootstrapping), a statistical test of the difference between the two relaxation times, and a statement of the effective sample size at the physical rung. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Terminology Evidence pointer Abstract text; location not provided Issue The term "Anneal-MaxCal" is introduced without a clear definition of what "anneal" refers to in the context of the method. The abstract mentions "annealed solute-tempering ladder," but the relationship between the annealing protocol and the maximum-caliber step is not explicit. Required correction Define the annealing procedure explicitly and clarify whether the maximum-caliber step is applied at each rung or only at the physical rung. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Reproducibility Affected element Simulation details Evidence pointer Abstract text; location not provided Issue The abstract states "665 ns of simulation" but does not specify the number of independent trajectories, the length of each trajectory, or the equilibration protocol. This is insufficient for reproducibility. Required correction Provide the number of trajectories, their lengths, and the equilibration procedure in the full manuscript. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Interpretation Affected element Synthetic data demonstration Evidence pointer Abstract text; location not provided Issue The synthetic data demonstration shows that the method responds to imposed time-resolved constraints, but the abstract does not state whether the resulting free-energy difference and populations are consistent with the known ground truth of the synthetic system. Required correction State the ground-truth values for the synthetic system and report the error between the method's output and the true values. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1 (single barrier crossing statistics), R1-M2 (unvalidated prefactor extrapolation), R1-M3 (lack of statistical comparison) Risk / unsupported claims The claim that the method "tackles both problems" (sampling and kinetics) is not established from the abstract alone; the validation is limited to a single system and a single comparison. The claim that the prefactor extrapolation is "log-linear" is presented without supporting data or justification. The claim that the method "yields rates and a committor" from a single barrier crossing is not supported by the evidence provided. The synthetic data demonstration is described but not validated against ground truth, so its significance cannot be assessed. The comparison of relaxation times (5430 ± 996 ps vs 4413 ± 446 ps) is presented without a statistical test, so the claim of agreement is not supported.

The framework's promise to incorporate noncanonical chemistry into designed proteins could appeal to those developing therapeutic binders, biosensors, or tools for targeted covalent inhibition. The potential to program post-translational modifications and bioorthogonal reactivity may also attract groups working on chemical probes and cell engineering. Major strengths The conceptual advance is clear and well framed. Extending the chemical alphabet of generative protein design beyond canonical residues addresses a recognized bottleneck. The range of demonstrated applications, from modification-dependent recognition to covalent capture and isoform-selective inhibition, suggests broad utility. The claim of single-round experimental success is notable if substantiated. Scientific importance: If fully validated, the framework could enable new classes of protein-based tools and therapeutics, making the potential impact high. Interdisciplinary readership: The work bridges computational design, chemical biology, and protein engineering, which should attract a broad audience. Technical soundness: Not assessable from the abstract; the absence of methodological detail and raw data prevents evaluation of the framework's robustness. Readability for nonspecialists: The abstract is concise and accessible, though some terms such as "pair-representation conditioning" and "sequence-conditioned denoising" may be opaque to non-experts without further context. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The conceptual promise is clear, but the abstract does not provide sufficient experimental or computational detail to support the core claims. A supportive posture would require access to the full manuscript and validation data. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The framework generated proteins with chemistry-dependent recognition and reactivity in single-round experimental campaigns. Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The abstract claims successful generation of functional proteins across multiple targets and modification types in single-round campaigns, but no experimental data, success rates, or reproducibility metrics are provided. Why it matters Single-round success is a strong claim that, if true, would distinguish this framework from iterative design approaches. Without data on hit rates, false positives, or replicate experiments, the reliability of the framework cannot be assessed. Resolution test Provide experimental details including number of designs tested, hit rates, replicate counts, and statistical significance for each target and modification type. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Specificity and selectivity Claim pointer Sulfotyrosine and nitrotyrosine enabled modification-dependent recognition of thrombin and HER2, respectively. Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The claim of modification-dependent recognition implies that recognition is contingent on the presence of the specific chemical modification. No data are shown to demonstrate that unmodified controls fail to bind or that binding is lost upon modification removal. Why it matters Without negative controls, the observed binding could be due to the protein scaffold alone rather than the chemical modification. This is central to the framework's premise that chemistry is a programmable determinant of function. Resolution test Include binding data for matched controls lacking the modification, and demonstrate that recognition is lost or significantly reduced in their absence. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Quantitative validation Claim pointer Post-expression chemical modifications yielded a light-activated covalent PD-L1 binder and an isoform-selective CA IX inhibitor (KD = 45 nM) designed to engage catalytic Zn2+. Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern A single KD value is reported for the CA IX inhibitor, but no data are provided for the PD-L1 binder, including affinity, light-activation kinetics, or covalent labeling efficiency. The claim of isoform selectivity is not supported by any comparative data against CA XII or other carbonic anhydrases. Why it matters Quantitative binding and selectivity data are essential to substantiate the functional claims. The absence of such data for the PD-L1 binder and the lack of selectivity context for CA IX leave the most impactful claims unverified. Resolution test Provide full binding curves, KD values for all reported binders, selectivity panels for CA IX against related isoforms, and light-activation and covalent labeling data for the PD-L1 construct. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Mechanistic attribution Claim pointer CheMoDesign makes chemical mechanism a programmable dimension of de novo protein design. Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Concern The abstract does not describe how the framework ensures that the designed proteins engage the intended chemical mechanism, such as Zn2+ coordination in CA IX or covalent bond formation in the PD-L1 binder. No structural or mechanistic evidence is presented. Why it matters The central claim is that chemical mechanism is programmable, not merely that functional proteins were obtained. Without evidence that the designed chemistry is mechanistically responsible for the observed activity, the framework's core premise remains unsupported. Resolution test Provide structural data, mutagenesis studies, or mechanistic assays demonstrating that the intended chemical interaction is required for function. Required correction Include a discussion of the scope and limitations of compatible chemical building blocks. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Reproducibility Affected element Experimental campaigns Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Issue The abstract states "single-round experimental campaigns" but does not specify the number of independent campaigns or whether results were consistent across repeats. Required correction Report the number of campaigns and any variability observed. Risk / unsupported claims The claim of "single-round experimental campaigns" is unsupported without data on design success rates and replicates. The claim of "modification-dependent recognition" is unsupported without negative control data. The claim of "isoform-selective CA IX inhibitor" is unsupported without selectivity data against related isoforms. The claim of "light-activated covalent PD-L1 binder" is unsupported without affinity, activation, and labeling data. The claim that "chemical mechanism is a programmable dimension" is unsupported without mechanistic or structural evidence. The reported KD of 45 nM for CA IX is a single quantitative value with no experimental context or error estimates.

01 基本信息 标题 ：Validation and analysis of 12,000 AI-driven CAR-T designs in the Bits to Binders competition 作者 ：Kosonocky, Clayton W; Abel, Alex M; Feller, Aaron L; Cifuentes Rieffer, Amanda E; Woolley, Phillip R; Lala, Jakub; Barth, Daryl R; Gardner, Tynan; Ekker, Stephen C; Ellington, Andrew D; Wierson, Wesley A; Marcotte, Edward M 单位 ：未提供（作者单位未在摘要中列出） 期刊/平台 ：Molecular Systems Biology 年份 ：2026（在线日期 2026-10-09） 论文类型 ：竞赛结果分析与数据集发布（实证研究） 领域 ：AI 蛋白质设计 × 细胞治疗（CAR-T） 关键词 ：de novo binder design, minibinder, CAR-T, CD20, AI-driven protein design, functional screening DOI/arXiv ：10.1038/s44320-026-00246-1 代码 ：未提供 数据 ：12,000 个设计的数据集作为开放资源发布（具体仓库未在摘要中提供） 阅读日期 ：2026-10-09（基于摘要日期） 在该方向中的位置 ：本文处于「AI 蛋白质设计 × 功能验证」交叉点，区别于大多数仅以结合亲和力为评估指标的工作，将 de novo binder 设计置于 CAR-T 细胞功能（增殖、杀伤）的更高层次生物学验证中，为 AI 设计方法提供了大规模、标准化的功能评估基准。 02 一句话总结 通过全球竞赛形式收集 12,000 个 AI 设计的 80 氨基酸 de novo minibinder（靶向 CD20），以 CAR-T 细胞增殖为功能筛选指标，鉴定出 707 个 CD20 特异性富集设计，并识别出可提高设计成功率的回顾性过滤因素。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：AI 设计的 de novo 蛋白 binder 在真实生物学功能层面（而非仅结合亲和力）表现如何？哪些设计方法和序列特征与功能性成功相关？ 为什么重要 ：AI 蛋白设计领域快速发展，但大多数评估停留在结合亲和力层面，缺乏对更高阶生物学功能（如细胞信号激活、增殖、杀伤）的系统验证。CAR-T 是一个理想的功能读出系统，因为 binder 不仅需要结合靶标，还需要正确触发胞内信号。 现有方法为何不足 ：现有评估通常使用表面等离子共振（SPR）或酵母展示等体外结合实验，无法反映 binder 在细胞环境中的功能表现；且评估规模有限，缺乏多样化的设计方法对比。 精确研究问题 ：Can large-scale functional screening of AI-designed de novo binders in a CAR-T context identify design methodologies and sequence features that correlate with successful target-specific T cell activation? Pooled CAR-T proliferation screening identified 707 designs with significant CD20-specific enrichment, with team hit rates ranging from 0.6% to 38.4%. Top candidates were validated individually for CD20-specific proliferation, expansion, cytokine production, and targeted cell lysis. The authors identify design methodologies and factors correlated with DNA synthesis, expression, and target-specific T cell activation, which when applied as a retrospective filter nearly double success rates. The dataset is released as an open resource with practical recommendations. The scale of the dataset and the use of a functional readout (CAR-T proliferation) rather than binding affinity alone are notable strengths. However, the abstract alone provides insufficient detail to evaluate the rigor of the screening pipeline, the statistical methods used to define "significant" enrichment, the validation criteria, or the robustness of the retrospective filter. Several claims are plausible but currently not verifiable from the supplied material. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in AI-driven protein design, computational biology, and immunotherapy would be interested. The dataset and recommendations could serve as a benchmark for de novo binder design and functional validation, and the competition format may inform future community-based evaluation efforts. Clinically oriented groups working on CAR-T therapies may also find the functional screening approach relevant. Major strengths The use of a functional cellular assay (CAR-T proliferation) as the primary screening readout is a meaningful advance over affinity-only evaluations. The scale of the competition (12,000 designs, 42 countries) provides a substantial dataset. The identification of design factors that correlate with functional success, and the release of the dataset as an open resource, are valuable contributions to the field. 局部挫折理论是能量景观理论的核心延伸，被广泛用于解释蛋白功能位点、进化保守性、疾病突变效应等 - 该理论提出近 20 年，但缺乏大规模实验验证 - 若理论预测与实验不符，将影响基于该理论的蛋白设计策略 现有方法为何不足 : - 局部挫折计算依赖粗粒化力场（如 AWSEM），其准确性未经大规模实验检验 - 以往验证局限于少量蛋白或特定功能位点 - 缺乏对"挫折定义本身"的批判性审视 精确研究问题 : Can experimental deep mutational scanning data validate the predicted patterns of local frustration in natural proteins, and do existing in silico tools accurately recapitulate residue-level frustration? 04 背景与发展脉络 注: 以下脉络主要基于本文框架，部分经外部核验。 阶段 代表性方法/工作 优点 局限 本文位置 能量景观理论奠基 Levinthal 悖论; spin-glass 物理引入 (Bryngelson & Wolynes) 解决折叠动力学与热力学矛盾 全局视角，缺乏残基级分辨率 理论基础 全局最小挫折原则 能量景观理论; funnel 概念 解释蛋白可折叠性 无法解释功能位点的局部去稳定化 被扩展对象 局部挫折理论 Ferreiro et al. 提出 local frustration 框架 残基级分辨率，连接序列-结构-功能 缺乏大规模实验验证 本文验证对象 计算工具发展 Protein Frustratometer (AWSEM), pSUFER (REF15) 可计算残基级挫折 力场依赖、粗粒化近似 本文评估对象 深度学习预测 Pythia (序列-结构图神经网络) 数据驱动、无需物理力场 非专门设计用于挫折预测 本文发现其意外有效 高通量实验数据 DMS 技术 (Gβ1, 蛋白水解酶切) 大规模残基级稳定性数据 覆盖有限、质量不均 本文数据基础 本文贡献 SPIN 框架 低能量竞争优先、对定性数据鲁棒 新提出，需更多验证 本文核心创新 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 局部挫折理论缺乏实验验证 理论提出近 20 年，无大规模实验检验 需要大量残基级稳定性数据，实验成本高 Introduction: "experimental validation has remained elusive" 现有计算工具预测能力弱 Protein Frustratometer 仅解释 <3% 实验方差（Gβ1 约 7%） 粗粒化力场（AWSEM）可能无法准确捕捉残基级能量差异 Results: "capturing under 3% of the experimental variance" Z-score 对定性数据敏感 大量突变导致蛋白错误折叠/不溶，无法获得定量 ΔG Z-score 依赖均值和标准差，定性数据无法纳入 Results: "some mutations resulted in misfolding or insolubility" Z-score 忽略能量幅度 相似 Z-score 可对应数量级不同的能量差 Z-score 是标准化度量，丢失绝对能量信息 Results 图 4A: "similar frustration values near 2 can represent energy distances spanning an order of magnitude" 非高斯分布破坏 Z-score 解释 14.4% 位点呈强非高斯突变能量分布 Z-score 隐含正态假设 Results: "14.4% of residue positions show strongly non-Gaussian mutational behavior" 定性去稳定化突变被系统排除 约 10% Gβ1 突变为定性去稳定化 现有框架无法处理非定量数据 Results: "over 1 in 10 mutations were qualitatively destabilizing" 06 核心思想 1) 表面方法 本文表面上是"用大规模 DMS 数据验证局部挫折理论"： - 从 Gβ1 的深度突变扫描数据计算实验性局部挫折 Z-score - 与 Protein Frustratometer、DeepDDG、PoPMuSC、Pythia 等计算工具比较 - 扩展到 178 个蛋白、约 8,000 个位点的大规模验证 - 提出 SPIN 作为替代度量 2) 核心洞察 洞察一 : 局部挫折理论的大尺度模式（如埋藏残基低挫折、表面残基高挫折）在实验数据中得到支持，但 残基级定量预测 远超出现有计算工具的能力。 洞察二 : Z-score 作为挫折度量存在根本性局限——它强调平均能量差而非低能量竞争。这导致： - 对定性数据敏感（无法处理错误折叠突变） - 忽略能量绝对幅度（相似 Z-score 可对应 10 倍能量差） - 隐含正态分布假设（14.4% 位点违反） 洞察三 : 从全局最小挫折到局部挫折的扩展中， "竞争对象"的选择 是关键。全局理论关注低能量替代构象，而局部挫折关注替代序列。SPIN 将这一逻辑推向极致：直接计算 WT 在序列系综中的玻尔兹曼概率。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] 理论验证需要匹配的分辨率 : 局部挫折理论预测的是统计模式，而计算工具试图预测单个残基——两者分辨率不匹配导致"理论正确但工具无效"的局面 度量选择决定结论 : Z-score 和 SPIN 对同一数据的解读可能不同，选择度量时需明确"什么是最有意义的能量竞争" 深度学习可从大规模数据中隐式学习能量函数 ：Pythia 虽非为挫折设计，但表现最佳，提示数据驱动方法可能比物理力场更有效地捕捉残基级能量 07 方法总览 输入 : - fully detailed Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript addresses an important gap in the protein biophysics literature by attempting to provide experimental validation of local frustration theory using large-scale mutational datasets. The authors present a thoughtful analysis of existing computational tools and propose a novel metric (SPIN) that may offer complementary insights. However, the provided text lacks the detailed quantitative results, figures, and supplementary materials necessary to fully evaluate the strength of the claims. The conceptual framework is sound and the work is potentially significant, but the current evidence base is insufficient to establish the central conclusions with confidence. Who would be interested in the results, and why Protein biophysicists and computational biologists studying protein stability, folding, and evolution would be the primary audience. Researchers developing or using deep mutational scanning approaches, those interested in protein design, and scientists working on energy landscape theory would also find this work relevant. The benchmarking of existing tools and the introduction of SPIN could inform method selection and development in these fields. Major strengths The manuscript addresses a long-standing gap between theoretical predictions of local frustration and experimental validation. The use of large-scale deep mutational scanning datasets (nearly 8,000 positions across 178 proteins) provides substantial statistical power. The critical evaluation of multiple in silico methods is valuable, and the proposal of SPIN as a complementary metric is conceptually interesting. The authors appropriately acknowledge limitations of existing approaches and their own analysis. The only numerical values mentioned are r = 0.30 for sequence conservation, r = 0.42 for Pythia, and 36% variance explained by burial, but these are scattered and not systematically reported. Why it matters Without comprehensive quantitative results, the reader cannot assess the strength of the evidence or determine whether the conclusions are justified. The claim of "experimental evidence" for theoretical predictions requires clear presentation of the data supporting this assertion. Resolution test Provide a systematic summary of all key statistical results, including correlation coefficients, confidence intervals, and p-values for each relationship examined, with corresponding figure references. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Methodological validation Claim pointer The claim that SPIN is a valid complementary measure of residue-level stability optimality (Results and Discussion, SPIN section) Evidence pointer SPIN section; Formula 1; Table S1; location not provided for validation results Concern The SPIN metric is introduced and its properties are described, but no validation is presented in the supplied text. The authors state that "the ability of the measure to capture energetic optimality at the amino acid level was examined" and report median SPIN values, but there is no comparison against independent experimental measurements, no assessment of predictive validity, and no demonstration that SPIN provides information beyond existing metrics. Why it matters A new metric requires rigorous validation to establish its utility. Without evidence that SPIN captures meaningful biological information beyond what is already available, its introduction is premature and its claimed advantages cannot be evaluated. Resolution test Present validation analyses showing SPIN correlates with independent experimental measurements, demonstrates expected relationships with known biological features, and provides unique information not captured by existing metrics. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Generalizability Claim pointer The claim that findings from the expanded dataset of 178 proteins support general conclusions about local frustration patterns (Results and Discussion, Expanded Datasets section) Evidence pointer Expanded Datasets section; Figure 2B; location not provided Concern The authors acknowledge that the dataset contains "only small protein domains" and that "a higher proportion of solvent-exposed positions may influence predictions." This raises questions about whether the conclusions generalize to larger, multi-domain proteins that are more representative of the proteome. The authors note this limitation but do not address its implications for their broader claims. Why it matters If the dataset is biased toward small, potentially atypical proteins, the conclusions about local frustration patterns and tool performance may not be generalizable. This is particularly important given the authors' stated goal of understanding "protein behavior...in nature." Resolution test Either demonstrate that the conclusions hold in a more diverse protein set, or explicitly limit the scope of claims to small, single-domain proteins and discuss the implications for broader applicability. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established The primary technical failing is the lack of comprehensive quantitative results in the supplied text. The manuscript makes strong claims about experimental validation and tool benchmarking, but the specific data supporting these claims are not visible. Additionally, the SPIN metric requires formal validation before its utility can be assessed. The authors should also clarify the relationship between their experimental approach and the theoretical definitions of local frustration, as the operationalization of the concept may differ from the original theoretical framework. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The work is conceptually original in its attempt to provide large-scale experimental validation of local frustration theory and in proposing SPIN as a new metric. However, the novelty of SPIN relative to existing approaches needs clearer articulation. Scientific importance: The question of whether theoretical predictions of local frustration hold experimentally is important for the field. The benchmarking of existing tools has practical value. The introduction of SPIN could be significant if validated. Interdisciplinary readership: The work bridges biophysics, computational biology, and evolutionary biology, and would appeal to a broad readership in these areas. The conceptual framework is accessible, though some technical details may be challenging for nonspecialists. Technical soundness: The methodological approach is reasonable, but the supplied text does not provide sufficient detail to fully assess technical soundness. The lack of visible quantitative results and validation analyses is a significant concern. Readability for nonspecialists: The manuscript is generally well-written and the conceptual framework is explained clearly. However, the multiple definitions of local frustration and the introduction of SPIN may be confusing without the referenced figures and tables. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The conceptual framework is promising and the work addresses an important question, but the supplied text lacks the quantitative detail and validation necessary to support the central claims. The authors should be encouraged to resubmit with comprehensive results, validation of SPIN, and a clearer articulation of the relationship between their experimental approach and theoretical predictions. Risk / unsupported claims The claim of "experimental evidence for theoretical predictions regarding the relationship between local frustration and protein sequence, structure, and evolution" is not supported by the visible quantitative results. The claim that SPIN is a useful complementary measure is unsupported without validation analyses. The claim that Pythia outperforms other tools is stated but not fully contextualized with statistical comparisons. 01 基本信息 标题 ：The structural context of mutations in proteins predicts their effect on antibiotic resistance 作者与单位 ：Green, Anna G; Tasmin, Mahbuba; Vargas, Roger Jr; Farhat, Maha Reda（哈佛医学院 Farhat 实验室；马萨诸塞大学阿默斯特分校 SAGE 实验室） 期刊/预印本平台 ：eLife 年份 ：2026-10-09 论文类型 ：研究论文（Research Article） 领域 ：计算生物学 / 结构生物信息学 / 抗生素耐药性预测 关键词 ：结核分枝杆菌、蛋白质结构、突变聚类、抗生素耐药性、AlphaFold、Getis–Ord 统计量 DOI/arXiv 号 ：10.7554/eLife.109450 代码 ：https://github.com/aggreen/MTB_Mut_Clust；https://github.com/aggreen/EVcouplings/tree/feature/structure_finder 数据 ：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20766452（预计算残基间距离）；https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20766453（支持数据） 阅读日期 ：未提供 在课题方向中的位置 ：本文属于「蛋白质结构 × 抗生素耐药性表型预测」交叉方向，核心贡献在于：(1) 将空间统计方法（Getis–Ord G 统计量）引入蛋白质三维结构上的突变聚类分析；(2) 系统验证了 AlphaFold 预测结构在突变功能预测中的可用性；(3) 证明结构邻近性（3D proximity）是比序列邻近性（1D proximity）更强的耐药性变异判别特征。对蛋白质结构相关计算研究（结构预测、构象采样、突变效应预测）具有直接的方法论参考价值。 02 一句话总结 本文利用 31,428 株结核分枝杆菌临床分离株的同塑性突变数据与 3,687 个蛋白的晶体结构（N=1,350）或 AlphaFold 预测结构（N=2,337），通过 Getis–Ord 空间统计量识别三维空间中的突变聚类，并证明「到已知耐药突变的 3D 距离」作为单一特征即可在留出测试集上以 96.5% 的 F1 分数区分耐药相关与非耐药相关突变。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：蛋白质三维结构中的突变空间分布是否携带预测抗生素耐药性的信息？能否仅凭结构上下文（而非序列上下文）对突变的耐药性效应进行分类？ 为什么重要 ：结核分枝杆菌耐药性主要通过非同义突变演化。现有序列-based 方法（GWAS、ML）需要大量表型标记数据，对新兴药物（bedaquiline、pretomanid）和新发突变预测能力有限。结构信息可能提供不依赖大样本表型数据的泛化信号。 现有方法为何不足 ：(1) 监督方法依赖大量表型标注数据，对稀有突变和新型药物效果差；(2) 无监督进化方法（如 dN/dS、同塑性分析）仅用序列信息，忽略残基在三维空间中的功能邻近性；(3) 已有结构-aware 研究局限于单个蛋白（RpoB、PncA、AtpE），缺乏蛋白质组规模的系统验证。 精确研究问题 ：Can protein structural context (3D proximity to known resistance mutations) alone classify missense mutations as resistance-conferring vs. non-resistance-conferring across the entire M. tuberculosis proteome, with performance exceeding sequence-based proximity? G 分数模块 ：对每个残基计算 Getis–Ord 统计量（基于同塑性分数与 3D 距离权重矩阵）。 5. 校准模块 ：对 9 个已知耐药蛋白生成正/负对照（下采样 vs. 均匀模拟），比较 5 种统计量（KS 统计量最优）。 6. 分类模块 ：对 WHO 目录中 9,365 个变异提取特征（1D 邻近性、3D 邻近性、G 分数），训练逻辑回归（70-30 划分，加权采样处理类别不平衡）。 流程
