Review setup Input scope Full manuscript text (abstract, introduction, materials and methods, results, discussion, supplementary references) Assessment boundary Scientific claims, methodological soundness, and evidence quality as presented in the supplied text. No independent verification of data or code was performed. Shared manuscript claim summary The authors present VeloHARMO, a deep learning framework combining organism-specific translation velocity predictors (VeloGRU, VeloBERT) with a genetic algorithm to design synonymous mRNA coding sequences that preserve native translation velocity profiles in heterologous hosts. They claim improved prediction accuracy over existing models, successful harmonization across 3808 E. coli genes for yeast expression, and qualitative consistency with published synonymous variant expression data. Visible evidence base Abstract, introduction, materials and methods, results, discussion sections. Tables 1-3 and Figures 1-2, S1-S7 are referenced but not provided. Supplementary tables S1-S2 are referenced but not provided. Missing materials affecting confidence All figures and tables are referenced but not included in the supplied text. Supplementary materials are not provided. Quantitative performance metrics (R2 values, correlation coefficients, statistical tests) are described qualitatively but not shown. The GitHub repository is mentioned but not assessed. Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript presents a conceptually interesting approach to mRNA design by directly modeling translation velocity rather than relying on codon usage frequency proxies. The core idea of harmonizing predicted velocity profiles between native and host organisms is well motivated and potentially useful. However, the evidence as presented is insufficient to fully evaluate the claims. Key quantitative results are only described verbally, all figures and tables are missing, and the validation against experimental data is acknowledged by the authors as qualitative and limited. The technical soundness of the deep learning models and the genetic algorithm cannot be assessed without the actual performance data and implementation details. The manuscript would benefit from clearer reporting of prediction accuracy metrics, statistical comparisons with baselines, and a more rigorous treatment of the experimental validation limitations. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in synthetic biology, biotechnology, and mRNA therapeutics would be interested in a data-driven approach to codon design that goes beyond frequency-based methods. Computational biologists working on translation dynamics and Ribo-seq analysis may also find the modeling framework relevant. The potential to improve heterologous protein expression in industrial and pharmaceutical settings gives the work practical significance. Major strengths The conceptual shift from codon usage frequency to direct translation velocity modeling is well argued and addresses a recognized limitation in the field. The use of organism-specific models trained on Ribo-seq data is appropriate for the stated goal. The inclusion of multiple baseline comparisons (CHARMING, CodonTransformer, codon optimization, random substitution, tAI) is commendable. The authors are transparent about the limitations of their retrospective validation and the exploratory nature of VeloBERT. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence completeness Claim pointer "VeloGRU achieved higher accuracy than a previously published model, RiboMIMO" and "VeloBERT exhibited superior performance over VeloGRU in smaller datasets such as P. aeruginosa" Evidence pointer Table 1, Table 2 (not provided) Concern The quantitative prediction performance of VeloGRU and VeloBERT is not reported in the text. The claim of superiority over RiboMIMO and the comparison between the two proposed models cannot be evaluated without the actual R2 values, error bars, and statistical significance tests. The text only states qualitative outcomes. Why it matters The entire framework depends on the reliability of the translation velocity predictors. If the prediction accuracy is not convincingly demonstrated, the downstream design results are questionable. The reader cannot assess whether the models are fit for purpose. Resolution test Provide the full Table 1 and Table 2 with R2 values, standard deviations, and statistical comparisons. Report whether differences between models are significant and discuss any cases where the proposed models underperform. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence completeness Claim pointer "VeloHARMO consistently yielded greater fitness improvement across genes" and "these additional baselines also showed only limited fitness improvement compared with VeloHARMO" Evidence pointer Figure 2, Figure S7 (not provided) Concern The central benchmarking claim that VeloHARMO outperforms all baselines is presented without any quantitative data. The text does not report the distribution of fitness improvements, the fraction of genes where VeloHARMO wins, or any statistical test comparing methods. The figures that would show these results are not available. Why it matters This is the core evidence for the utility of the proposed method. Without quantitative comparison, the reader cannot determine whether the improvement is marginal or substantial, consistent or variable across genes, or an artifact of the evaluation metric. Resolution test Provide Figure 2 and Figure S7 with clear axis labels, effect sizes, and statistical comparisons. Report the median and interquartile range of fitness improvements for each method and the proportion of genes where VeloHARMO outperforms each baseline. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Validation rigor Claim pointer "the reported experimental trends were generally consistent with the fitness scores" and "VeloHARMO-designed sequences achieved the highest predicted fitness scores" Evidence pointer Table 3 (not provided) Concern The validation against experimental data is acknowledged as qualitative and limited to a small number of sequences. The text does not specify how many sequences were analyzed, what the quantitative expression measurements were, or how the consistency was assessed. The claim of qualitative support is weak and the authors themselves note that robust statistical analysis was not possible. Why it matters The practical relevance of VeloHARMO depends on whether predicted fitness correlates with actual protein expression or activity. A qualitative statement based on an unspecified number of examples is insufficient to establish this link. The reader cannot judge the strength of the evidence. Resolution test Provide Table 3 with the number of sequences, the experimental measurements, and the predicted fitness scores. If possible, report a correlation coefficient or at least a clear description of the pattern. Discuss explicitly the limitations of the comparison and what would be needed for stronger validation. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Technical detail Claim pointer "We used publicly available ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq) datasets from five organisms" and "Positions with zero footprint density were retained in the dataset" Evidence pointer Materials and methods, Data collection and Preprocessing (location not provided) Concern The description of data preprocessing is insufficient. The text does not specify how many datasets were used per organism, how read alignment was performed, how footprint densities were normalized, or how the zero-density positions were handled in model training. The choice to retain zero-density positions is mentioned but the rationale and potential impact on model training are not discussed. Why it matters Ribo-seq data processing is known to introduce significant variability. The reproducibility of the models depends on a complete description of the preprocessing pipeline. The handling of zero-density positions could bias the models in ways that affect the design results. Resolution test Provide a detailed description of the data processing pipeline, including alignment tools, normalization methods, filtering criteria, and the treatment of zero-density positions. Discuss the potential impact of these choices on model performance. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Abstract Evidence pointer Abstract (location not provided) Issue The abstract states "translation velocity harmonization" as the core concept but does not define it explicitly. A reader unfamiliar with the term may not understand what is being harmonized and how. Required correction Add a brief definition or clarification in the abstract, such as "matching the predicted codon-level translation velocity profile of a gene in its native host to that in a heterologous host." Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Technical detail Affected element Materials and methods, Deep learning models Evidence pointer Materials and methods (location not provided) Concern The text states that VeloBERT is built upon a pretrained DNABERT backbone but does not describe how the pretrained model was adapted for the regression task. The fusion of DNABERT representations with protein-derived features is mentioned but not detailed. Required correction Provide a brief description of the VeloBERT architecture, including how the DNABERT embeddings are extracted, how they are fused with protein features, and the structure of the regression head. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Results, VeloHARMO designs mRNA sequences Evidence pointer Results (location not provided) Concern The toy problem validation within yeast is described as achieving a Pearson correlation of 0.995. It is unclear whether this is a single run or the best of multiple runs, and whether this result is representative. Required correction Clarify whether the reported correlation is from a single run or averaged over multiple runs, and report the variability if available. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected element Discussion Evidence pointer Discussion (location not provided) Concern The discussion mentions that VeloBERT should be regarded as exploratory but does not provide a clear recommendation on when to use VeloGRU versus VeloBERT in practice. Required correction Add a brief practical recommendation, such as "VeloGRU is recommended for bacterial and fungal hosts, while VeloBERT may be considered for human or mammalian systems where the pretrained representations are more relevant." Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Reproducibility Affected element Data availability Evidence pointer Data availability (location not provided) Concern The GitHub repository is mentioned but the text does not specify whether the trained model weights are included or only the code. This affects reproducibility. Required correction State explicitly whether trained model weights are provided in the repository or if users must train the models from scratch. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that VeloGRU achieves higher accuracy than RiboMIMO is unsupported without the actual performance data from Table 1. The claim that VeloHARMO consistently outperforms all baselines is unsupported without the quantitative results from Figure 2 and Figure S7. The claim that reported experimental trends are consistent with fitness scores is unsupported without the details from Table 3. The claim that translation velocity profiles differ substantially between organisms is based on cross-prediction experiments described only qualitatively in Figure S4, which is not provided. The claim that the genetic algorithm is stable under different random initializations is based on Figure S6 and Table S1, which are not provided. The claim that parameter selection may be adjusted according to the task is based on Table S2, which is not provided. The statement that "codon usage frequency is not a reliable proxy for translation velocity" is a central conclusion but is only supported by indirect evidence from the design experiments, which are not fully shown.

boundary Claims and conclusions as presented in the abstract; no access to full text, figures, tables, or supplementary materials Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report cryo-EM structures of GSDME pores with 23 to 29 protomer stoichiometries, identify key residues for membrane binding, shallow insertion, and oligomerization via three interfaces, and use molecular dynamics simulations to show selective lipid recruitment (anionic TMCL2 and zwitterionic DPhPC). They propose a stepwise, time-dependent pore assembly mechanism and suggest therapeutic relevance for cancers and neurodegenerative diseases. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no figures, tables, methods, or supplementary data provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, cryo-EM density maps, structural coordinates, mutagenesis data, liposome leakage assay details, molecular dynamics simulation parameters, statistical analyses, and any validation metrics Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially significant structural and mechanistic study of GSDME pore formation. The reported cryo-EM structures with variable stoichiometry and the integration of mutagenesis, functional assays, and molecular dynamics simulations suggest a comprehensive approach. However, the abstract alone provides insufficient detail to evaluate the technical rigor, data quality, or the strength of the mechanistic conclusions. Several claims, particularly regarding lipid selectivity and the stepwise assembly mechanism, require supporting evidence that is not visible in the abstract. Who would be interested in the results, and why Structural biologists studying pore-forming proteins and gasdermin family members; cell death researchers focused on pyroptosis and its regulation; cancer biologists interested in chemotherapy-induced cell death mechanisms; neuroscientists studying GSDME-linked neurodegenerative conditions; and drug developers targeting gasdermin-mediated pathways for therapeutic intervention. Major strengths The study addresses a significant gap in understanding GSDME pore formation, which is less characterized than other gasdermins. The reported range of oligomeric stoichiometries (23 to 29) is notable and suggests a dynamic assembly process. The combination of structural, functional, and computational approaches is methodologically ambitious and potentially powerful. The identification of specific lipid interactions adds mechanistic depth. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The abstract claims that cryo-EM structures of GSDME pores with 23 to 29 protomer stoichiometries were determined. Evidence pointer Abstract only; no figures or validation metrics provided Concern The abstract does not provide any information about the resolution of the cryo-EM maps, the number of particles used, the symmetry imposed, or the validation statistics (e.g., gold-standard FSC curves, model-to-map fit). Without these details, the reliability of the structural models cannot be assessed. Why it matters Cryo-EM structures are only as credible as their resolution and validation. Variable stoichiometry across 23 to 29 protomers is unusual and could reflect genuine biological heterogeneity or artifacts of sample preparation or data processing. The absence of quality metrics undermines confidence in the structural claims. Resolution test Provide resolution estimates, particle numbers, symmetry handling, and validation statistics for each reported stoichiometry. Demonstrate that the different oligomeric states are reproducible and not processing artifacts. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The abstract claims that key residues responsible for membrane binding, shallow membrane insertion, and oligomerization through three distinct structural interfaces were identified using mutagenesis and liposome leakage assays. Evidence pointer Abstract only; no mutagenesis data, assay details, or statistical analyses provided Concern The abstract does not specify which residues were mutated, how the mutations were designed, the magnitude of functional effects, or the number of replicates. The liposome leakage assay conditions (lipid composition, protein concentration, time course) are not described. Without these details, the functional significance of the identified residues cannot be evaluated. Why it matters The mechanistic conclusions rest on the functional validation of structural observations. If the mutagenesis effects are modest or the assays are not well-controlled, the link between structure and function is weakened. Resolution test Provide a detailed description of mutagenesis strategy, assay conditions, quantitative results with error bars and statistical tests, and demonstrate that the observed effects are specific to the proposed functional roles. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The abstract claims that molecular dynamics simulations reveal dynamic lipid recruitment and specificity, with anionic TMCL2 selectively recruited by basic residues and zwitterionic DPhPC solvating polar regions. Evidence pointer Abstract only; no simulation parameters, system setup, or analysis details provided Concern The abstract does not describe the simulation length, force field, system size, number of replicates, or how lipid selectivity was quantified. The claim of "selective recruitment" requires a rigorous statistical comparison of lipid occupancy around specific residues versus bulk behavior. Without these details, the lipid specificity claim is not verifiable. Why it matters Lipid selectivity is a central mechanistic claim. If the simulations are under-sampled or the analysis is not statistically robust, the conclusion that specific lipids stabilize the pore could be overstated. Resolution test Provide simulation parameters, convergence metrics, replicate information, and a clear quantitative definition of lipid selectivity with appropriate statistical analysis. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Claim support Claim pointer The abstract claims that specific lipids act as structural stabilizers to reinforce the intermolecular hydrogen bond network within the assembled 25-mer pore. Evidence pointer Abstract only; no structural or simulation data showing lipid-mediated stabilization Concern The abstract asserts a stabilizing role for lipids but does not provide evidence that the hydrogen bond network is functionally dependent on lipid presence. No comparison is shown between simulations or structures with and without specific lipids, nor is there any mutational or functional test of the proposed stabilization. Why it matters This claim extends beyond lipid recruitment to a specific structural function. Without direct evidence, the statement is speculative and could mislead readers about the strength of the conclusion. Resolution test Provide comparative simulations or experimental data demonstrating that removal or alteration of specific lipids disrupts the hydrogen bond network or pore stability. Concern ID R1-M5 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Claim support Claim pointer The abstract claims that the findings support a stepwise, time-dependent mechanism underlying GSDME pore assembly. Evidence pointer Abstract only; no time-resolved experiments or kinetic data provided Concern The abstract does not describe any time-dependent experiments, such as stopped-flow liposome leakage, single-particle time courses, or molecular dynamics assembly trajectories. The structural snapshots of different stoichiometries are suggestive but do not by themselves establish a temporal sequence. Why it matters A stepwise, time-dependent mechanism is a strong kinetic claim. Without direct temporal evidence, the interpretation of different oligomeric states as assembly intermediates is speculative. Resolution test Provide time-resolved experimental data or simulation trajectories that demonstrate the order and kinetics of pore assembly, or temper the claim to reflect that the structures are consistent with, but do not prove, a stepwise mechanism. no methods, figures, tables, or supplementary material were provided for verification Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report microsecond-level equilibrium molecular dynamics replicas and well-tempered metadynamics simulations to characterize Phen-DC3 recognition at a G-quadruplex-duplex (Q-D) junction. They claim that ligand binding induces a reorganized bound-state architecture with reduced global structural displacement but a more expanded conformation, junctional opening, redistributed flexibility, a more distinct and less fragmented bound-state ensemble, and a non-monotonic unbinding free-energy profile with a partially bound surface-associated state. They propose a working model coupling junctional opening, ensemble narrowing, correlated-motion reorganization, and multistep dissociation, and suggest design implications for future Q-D junction ligands. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no quantitative data, simulation parameters, convergence metrics, free-energy error estimates, or structural analyses are visible Missing materials affecting confidence Full methods, simulation setup and force-field parameters, convergence and equilibration assessments, free-energy profiles with error bars, PCA and correlation-motion analysis details, contact analysis definitions, system construction and validation, and any figures or tables supporting the stated results Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially interesting computational study of ligand recognition at a Q-D junction, with a plausible working model that couples structural, dynamical, and energetic features. However, the claims are broad and mechanistically detailed, and none of the supporting quantitative evidence is visible in the supplied material. The abstract alone does not allow verification of the simulation quality, convergence, or statistical robustness of the reported findings. The design implications are reasonable but speculative without comparative or experimental context. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in nucleic-acid structure and dynamics, computational biophysics, and drug design targeting G-quadruplexes and their junctions would be interested. The proposed multistep dissociation mechanism and the emphasis on junctional geometry and secondary interaction sites could inform ligand design strategies for selective Q-D junction targeting. Major strengths The study addresses a relevant and under-characterized target class, namely Q-D junctions, and moves beyond simple stacking descriptions. The use of multiple simulation approaches, including equilibrium replicas and well-tempered metadynamics, is appropriate for probing both binding and unbinding. The working model is integrative and offers testable hypotheses for future ligand design. no access to full manuscript, figures, tables, or supplementary materials Shared manuscript claim summary The authors used Gaussian accelerated molecular dynamics (GaMD) simulations to compare conformational dynamics of aminopeptidase N (APN) bound to three inhibitors (Bestatin, CHR-79888, Kelatorphan). They report inhibitor-dependent differences in flexible loop (891)YGGGSFSF(898) conformations, direct ligand-loop contacts, interdomain coupling, and residue communication pathways, with CHR-79888 and Kelatorphan inducing more restricted and coordinated ensembles than Bestatin. The authors propose these findings offer new theoretical insights for APN inhibitor design. However, the claims are broad and mechanistic, and the abstract alone provides insufficient evidence to evaluate the technical rigor, statistical robustness, or biological significance of the findings. The central conclusion that different inhibitors induce distinct loop dynamics and interdomain communication patterns requires substantial supporting data that are not visible in the supplied material. The work may be of interest to computational enzymologists and drug designers, but the case is not established from the abstract alone. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational biophysicists and medicinal chemists studying enzyme-inhibitor interactions, particularly those focused on aminopeptidases and conformational dynamics in drug design. The findings could inform structure-based design of APN inhibitors, a target relevant to cancer and viral infections. Researchers using enhanced sampling methods such as GaMD may also find the methodological application relevant. Major strengths The study addresses a meaningful question about whether inhibitors of different potency induce similar or distinct conformational dynamics, which is relevant to understanding inhibitor mechanisms beyond static binding affinity. The use of GaMD is appropriate for exploring conformational ensembles that may be inaccessible to conventional MD. The focus on a specific flexible loop and interdomain communication provides a mechanistically oriented framework. The demonstration on GPCRs and translation to human cells would appeal to those working on receptor signaling and drug discovery. The use of CRISPR-addressable sites for systematic insertion is conceptually novel. The application across an entire signaling pathway and the identification of bifunctional chimeras with two different reporter types suggest broad utility. The inclusion of human cell validation strengthens translational relevance. They describe a two-domain architecture with a GT-A fold N-terminal domain and a novel C-terminal domain, propose a GDP-mannose binding site adjacent to a Mn(2+) ion coordinated by a DXD motif, and support alpha-(1-->3)-mannosyltransferase activity and substrate specificity through biochemical assays. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no structural coordinates, kinetic data, mutagenesis results, or simulation parameters are provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, crystallographic statistics, electron density maps, activity assay details, substrate specificity data, docking and MD simulation parameters, and any validation of the proposed acceptor-binding model Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially significant advance in understanding yeast O-glycan biosynthesis by providing the first structural view of a GT71 family enzyme. The claim of a novel C-terminal domain and its proposed role in acceptor specificity is intriguing. However, the abstract alone provides insufficient evidence to evaluate the rigor of the structural determination, the biochemical validation, or the computational modeling. Several key claims, particularly regarding the molecular basis of linkage selectivity, are presented without supporting quantitative data. The work is likely of interest to glycobiology and glycosyltransferase communities, but the case as presented is not fully established from the supplied material. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers studying glycosyltransferase structure-function relationships, yeast cell wall and glycoprotein biosynthesis, and the molecular evolution of linkage specificity in GT families. The first structure of a GT71 enzyme would also be of interest to structural biologists working on GT-A fold enzymes and to those investigating how acceptor substrate geometry dictates glycosidic linkage formation. Major strengths The abstract reports the first experimentally determined structure of a GT71 family enzyme, filling a clear gap in structural coverage. The identification of a novel C-terminal domain unique to GT71 is a concrete and testable finding. The combination of structural, biochemical, and computational approaches is appropriate for addressing the question of linkage specificity. Why it matters The entire mechanistic interpretation, including the proposed GDP-mannose binding site and the acceptor-binding model, depends on the accuracy of the atomic model. A structure with poor geometry or ambiguous density would undermine all downstream claims. 01 基本信息 标题 ：Generalizing Protein Fitness Prediction Across Distribution Shifts via Structural and Co-evolutionary Priors 作者 ：Vithayapalert N; Piriyajitakonkij M; Grisoni F 单位 ：未提供（根据作者姓名与期刊类型推测为学术机构，但原文未提供） 期刊/平台 ：bioRxiv（预印本） 年份 ：2026 论文类型 ：预印本（方法学 + 实证研究） 领域 ：蛋白质适应度预测 × 分布偏移泛化 × 结构先验 × 共进化信息 关键词 ：protein fitness prediction, distribution shift, protein language models, structural priors, co-evolutionary features, AlphaFold trunk, FLIP2 DOI/arXiv 号 ：10.64898/2026.10.06.756934 代码 ：未提供 数据 ：FLIP2 benchmark（公开数据集） 阅读日期 ：2026-10-07（根据预印本日期推断） 该文在课题方向中的位置 ：本文属于「蛋白质结构相关计算研究 × AI 方法」中的 适应度预测与分布偏移泛化 子方向。其核心贡献在于系统比较结构感知 pLM 与共进化特征在不同分布偏移类型下的泛化能力，为蛋白质设计中的 reward function / oracle 选择提供指导。与 AlphaFold 结构预测、MD 模拟等物理方法无直接关联，但结构先验的使用与 AlphaFold trunk 的迁移具有方法学上的可借鉴性。 02 一句话总结 本文通过将结构感知 pLM 表示与 AlphaFold-style trunk 的 MSA 共进化特征拼接，使用轻量预测探针映射到适应度分数，系统评估了不同模态在多种分布偏移（unseen positions、unseen backbones）下的泛化表现，发现结构先验对 backbone 偏移增益最大、trunk 特征对位置偏移增益最大，且不同蛋白家族的最优模态组合不同。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：在蛋白质适应度预测中，当测试集与训练集存在分布偏移（如突变发生在未见过的位置、或变体来自未见过的蛋白骨架）时，现有方法（尤其是 pLM）性能显著下降。本文要解决的是： 如何通过引入结构先验和共进化信息来提升 OOD 泛化能力？ 为什么重要 ：蛋白质工程中，适应度预测器常被用作 reward function 或 oracle 来指导设计。如果预测器在 OOD 条件下失效，则设计流程会产生误导性结果。因此，提升 OOD 泛化是实际应用的关键瓶颈。 现有方法为何不足 ：FLIP2 benchmark 已显示，在常规 train-test split 下表现良好的方法在 OOD 条件下大幅退化。pLM 主要依赖序列统计，缺乏对结构约束和进化耦合的显式建模，因此在 unseen positions 或 unseen backbones 上难以外推。 精确研究问题 ： Can augmenting sequence representations with structural and co-evolutionary priors improve fitness prediction generalization across distribution shifts, and which modality is most effective for which shift type? materials were provided Shared manuscript claim summary The authors propose a multistage computational framework combining MaSIF-PMP, a surface-centered geometric deep learning model for interfacial binding site (IBS) prediction, with a generative diffusion model to design protein binders targeting peripheral membrane protein (PMP) IBSs. Candidate binders are ranked by MaSIF-PMP scores and geometric descriptors, then validated by molecular dynamics and enhanced sampling simulations. The framework is applied to three disease-relevant PMPs and is claimed to identify selective binders that disrupt membrane association while minimizing off-target membrane interactions. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no quantitative results, model architecture details, simulation parameters, or validation metrics are provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, methods section, all figures and tables, simulation trajectories, model training and evaluation details, benchmark comparisons, and any statistical analyses Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a conceptually interesting integration of surface-aware deep learning with generative design for a challenging class of therapeutic targets. However, the current evidence base is insufficient to evaluate the technical soundness of the framework or the validity of the central claims. The abstract reports outcomes without quantitative support, and key methodological details are absent. The work may hold promise, but the case is not established from the supplied material. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational protein designers and structural biologists working on membrane-associated proteins would be the primary audience. Researchers developing inhibitors for peripheral membrane proteins, particularly those involved in cancer signaling, may find the approach relevant. The work also speaks to the broader community interested in applying geometric deep learning to surface-centric drug discovery problems. Major strengths The problem selection is well motivated, as PMPs represent a difficult and under-served class of therapeutic targets. The proposed integration of IBS prediction with generative design is a logical and potentially powerful combination. The emphasis on selectivity against off-target membrane interactions addresses a practical concern in this domain. 01 基本信息 标题 ：Machine learning-assisted directed evolution of plant Rubisco 作者 ：McDonald, Julie L; Lin, Jiacheng; Zhao, Yunlong; Hie, Brian L; Birch, Rosemary; Gehring, Mary; Bryson, Bryan D; Whitney, Spencer M; Shoulders, Matthew D; Wilson, Robert H 单位 ：未提供（据作者信息推测含 MIT 及澳大利亚国立大学等，具体未在材料中列出） 期刊/平台 ：Science Advances 年份 ：2026 论文类型 ：研究论文 领域 ：蛋白质工程 × 机器学习（结构感知蛋白语言模型） × 定向进化 关键词 ：Rubisco、ESM-IF1、机器学习辅助定向进化、羧化效率、CO₂固定 DOI/arXiv ：10.1126/sciadv.aeh3246 代码 ：https://github.com/julielmcdonald/RubiscoMLDE；Zenodo: https://zenodo.org/records/21269162 数据 ：NCBI SRA BioProject PRJNA1476684；质粒 Addgene 253864, 253865, 239580, 253865 阅读日期 ：2026-05-14（按当前日期推算） 方向定位 ：本文属于「蛋白质结构相关计算研究 × AI 方法」中的典型案例——利用结构感知蛋白语言模型（ESM-IF1）指导植物 Rubisco 大亚基的定向进化文库设计，结合大肠杆菌体内筛选与体外动力学表征，实现酶催化效率提升。对课题方向的启示在于：结构感知 ML 模型可有效缩小序列搜索空间，发现自然进化未采样的功能性突变。 02 一句话总结 本文使用结构感知蛋白语言模型 ESM-IF1 对烟草 Rubisco 大亚基进行计算机深度突变扫描，据此设计位点饱和突变文库，通过 Rubisco 依赖型大肠杆菌筛选系统（RDE2）富集功能增强突变体，获得多个羧化效率提升的变体，其中最优的 T391I 使 kcatc 提高 29%、kcatc/KCair 提高 43%，且这些突变在自然植物谱系中极为罕见或不存在。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：能否利用无监督结构感知蛋白语言模型（ESM-IF1）推荐植物 Rubisco 大亚基中值得定向进化的氨基酸位点，从而在极小文库规模下发现提升羧化效率的功能性突变？ 重要性 ：Rubisco 是光合作用碳固定的限速酶，其催化速率慢、CO₂/O₂ 特异性低，是提高作物产量的关键改造靶点。然而植物 Rubisco 依赖多种分子伴侣组装，难以异源表达，传统随机突变文库筛选效率极低。 现有方法不足 ：随机突变（error-prone PCR）文库规模巨大（~50万），筛选成本高且阳性率极低（此前仅发现 1 个有效突变 M116L）；序列保守性分析推荐的位点多为自然进化中已固定的氨基酸，难以突破进化限制。 精确研究问题 ：Can a structure-informed protein language model (ESM-IF1) recommend amino acid sites in plant Rubisco large subunit that, when subjected to site-saturated mutagenesis and RDE2 selection, yield variants with improved carboxylation efficiency beyond natural sequence diversity? ESM-IF1 深度突变扫描 ：对每个位点的 19 种氨基酸替代计算 log-likelihood，筛选分数高于野生型的位点。 2. 文库构建 ：对 49 个位点进行位点饱和突变（NNS 密码子），获得 ~400 个变体的质粒文库。 3. RDE2 选择 ：将文库转化至 Rubisco 依赖型大肠杆菌（含 pACYCprk:nptII 和 pCDF-NtAsmbl），在梯度阿拉伯糖浓度下进行 4 天选择。 4. NGS 富集分析 ：对选择前后文库进行深度测序，计算每个突变的富集倍数。 5. 体外动力学表征 ：对富集突变进行 His6Ubq 标签纯化，测定 kcatc、KCair、SC/O。 6. 植物体内组装验证 ：通过农杆菌瞬时转化 NbrbcM 烟草（含 RbcM 替代），验证突变体在叶绿体中的组装能力。 7. 光合作用模型 ：使用 Farquhar 模型预测突变体对叶片光合速率的潜在影响。 关键工具 ： - S2），作者通过多次重复和纯化改进部分缓解，但未报告置信区间。 有边界的复述 ：在烟草 Rubisco 大亚基中，ESM-IF1 推荐位点的饱和突变文库经 RDE2 筛选后，可获得羧化效率提升 15-43% 的单点突变体，且这些突变在自然植物序列中极为罕见；该策略的普适性需在其他 Rubisco 类型中验证。 12 作者自认局限 局限 具体表现 作者提出的未来方向 来源 未进行稳定转基因植物验证 Full manuscript text including abstract, introduction, results, discussion, materials and methods, and supplementary figure/table references Assessment boundary Scientific validity, technical soundness, claim support, and significance of the reported ML-assisted directed evolution of plant Rubisco Shared manuscript claim summary The authors apply the structure-informed protein language model ESM-IF1 to recommend amino acid substitution sites in the large subunit of tobacco Rubisco, construct a site-saturated library at these sites, and use a Rubisco-dependent E. coli selection system to identify variants with improved carboxylation kinetics, including the T391I substitution that improves carboxylation rate by 29% and aerobic carboxylation efficiency by 43%, with several variants carrying substitutions absent from natural plant Rubisco sequences and assembly competence confirmed in planta. Visible evidence base Main text figures 1-6 (referenced), tables 1 and S1-S8 (referenced), supplementary figures S1-S8 (referenced), methods descriptions, and data/code availability statements Missing materials affecting confidence Supplementary figures and tables (S1-S8) not provided; raw NGS data not provided; detailed statistical analysis outputs not provided; plasmid maps and sequences not provided; full kinetic data for all variants not provided Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript presents a compelling application of structure-informed machine learning to a long-standing challenge in plant biotechnology: engineering Rubisco for improved carboxylation efficiency. The work is timely, technically ambitious, and the results, if fully supported by the data, would represent a meaningful advance in both directed evolution methodology and our understanding of Rubisco's catalytic plasticity. The combination of ML-guided library design with a high-throughput in vivo selection system is elegant, and the identification of multiple improved variants, including one with a substantial 43% improvement in aerobic carboxylation efficiency, is notable. However, the manuscript as presented has several gaps in evidence that prevent full assessment of the claims. The absence of the supplementary materials, which contain critical data on library composition, NGS analysis, and full kinetic characterization, is a significant limitation. Additionally, several methodological details and statistical considerations require clarification before the conclusions can be fully accepted. The phylogenetic analysis and the in planta assembly data are presented in a way that suggests they are confirmatory, but the depth of evidence is not fully visible. Overall, this is a promising and potentially important contribution, but the current evidence base is insufficient to fully establish all claims. Who would be interested in the results, and why Plant biologists and crop scientists interested in improving photosynthetic efficiency for yield enhancement would find this work directly relevant. Synthetic biologists and protein engineers working on directed evolution methodologies would be interested in the demonstration that structure-informed ML models can effectively reduce the search space for beneficial mutations in a challenging enzyme system. Computational biologists developing and applying protein language models would find the application to a real-world engineering problem valuable. The work also speaks to the broader question of whether laboratory evolution can access sequence space beyond what natural selection has explored, which would interest evolutionary biologists. Finally, researchers working on Rubisco biology specifically, including those studying its biogenesis, assembly, and catalytic mechanism, would find the identification of new functional sites valuable. Major strengths The study addresses a problem of high biological and agricultural significance with a well-reasoned approach. The use of ESM-IF1, a structure-informed model, is a thoughtful choice given the known limitations of sequence-only models for highly conserved proteins like Rubisco. The comparison between ESM-1bv and ESM-IF1 predictions provides useful insight into the value of structural information. The development of a streamlined library (~400 variants) that achieves a 1700-fold higher enrichment rate compared to error-prone PCR libraries is a compelling demonstration of the efficiency of ML-guided design. The identification of variants with improved kinetics, particularly T391I with a 29% increase in kcatc and 43% improvement in kcatc/KCair, is a significant result. The confirmation that several improved variants carry substitutions absent from natural plant Rubisco sequences is conceptually important, suggesting that ML can access rare or unexplored sequence solutions. The in planta assembly data, while preliminary, addresses a critical concern about whether mutations selected in E. coli would be compatible with the more complex chloroplast environment. The use of the Farquhar model to translate in vitro kinetic improvements into predicted photosynthetic gains provides a useful framework for assessing agricultural relevance. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence completeness Claim pointer The claim that "ML-assisted library design followed by selection in Rubisco-dependent E. coli identified multiple enriched variants displaying improved catalytic efficiency" and the specific kinetic parameters reported in Table 1 Evidence pointer Table 1, Figures 2-4, Supplementary Tables S1-S5, Supplementary Figures S2-S3 Concern The supplementary materials, which contain the detailed data supporting the library composition, NGS analysis, enrichment calculations, and full kinetic characterization, are not provided. Without these data, it is impossible to verify the completeness of the library, the rigor of the selection, the statistical significance of the enrichment, or the accuracy of the reported kinetic parameters. The manuscript states that the library contained ~400 variants covering 49 sites, but the actual coverage per site, the number of replicates, and the criteria for defining "enriched" are not fully described in the main text. The kinetic measurements are reported for a subset of variants, but the number of independent measurements, the error bars, and the statistical comparisons to wild-type are not visible. Why it matters The central claims of the paper rest on the quality and completeness of the library and the reliability of the kinetic measurements. If the library had poor coverage at key sites, or if the enrichment was not robustly reproduced, the conclusions about ML-guided design efficiency would be weakened. Similarly, if the kinetic improvements are not statistically robust or are based on a small number of measurements, the headline results could be overstated. Resolution test Provide the supplementary materials, including full NGS data, library coverage statistics, enrichment calculations with replicates, and complete kinetic data with appropriate statistical analysis (e.g., number of replicates, standard errors, significance tests). The kinetic parameters in Table 1 should be accompanied by confidence intervals and the number of independent measurements. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The claim that "the T391I substitution improved carboxylation rate by 29% and aerobic carboxylation efficiency by 43%" Evidence pointer Table 1, Figure 4A, Supplementary Figure S2 Concern The kinetic characterization methodology raises several questions. The manuscript describes using soluble protein from E. coli lysates for initial measurements, with a purification protocol developed for more detailed analysis. The variability in kcatc measurements from lysates is acknowledged (Supplementary Figure S2), but the final values in Table 1 are presumably from purified protein. The purification method using His6Ubq-tagged RbcS is described, but the efficiency of assembly of the tagged complex, the yield, and the purity of the final product are not fully quantified. The manuscript states the purified Rubisco was "typically >70% pure," which leaves room for contaminating proteins that could affect activity measurements. Additionally, the assay conditions for measuring kcatc and KCair are described briefly, but the CO2 concentration range, the number of data points, and the fitting procedure are not detailed. The manuscript also does not report measurements of kcatO or KO for the improved variants, which would be necessary to fully understand the mechanistic basis of the improved carboxylation efficiency. Why it matters The quantitative claims about kinetic improvements are the core results of the paper. If the measurements are not sufficiently rigorous, the conclusions about the magnitude of improvement and the potential for agricultural impact would be undermined. The lack of KO data also limits the interpretation of whether the improvements are specific to carboxylation or reflect general changes in catalytic properties. Resolution test Provide detailed kinetic assay protocols, including CO2 and O2 concentration ranges, number of replicates, and fitting procedures. Report kcatO and KO values for the improved variants. Provide a more detailed characterization of the purified protein, including purity assessment (e.g., SDS-PAGE with densitometry) and confirmation of correct assembly (e.g., native PAGE or size exclusion chromatography with multi-angle light scattering). Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Interpretation Claim pointer The claim that "several improved variants carried amino acid changes not found in the evolutionary lineage of plants, despite being assembly competent in plant chloroplasts, demonstrating that ML-assisted protein design can explore functional sequence space beyond what is observed from natural sequence diversity" Evidence pointer Figure 4D-E, Supplementary Figure S7, Table 1 Concern The phylogenetic analysis presented in Supplementary Figure S7 is described as showing that some improved variants carry substitutions absent from natural plant Rubisco sequences. However, the analysis is not visible, and the criteria for "not found in the evolutionary lineage of plants" are not clearly defined. The manuscript states that T391I is "generally observed only in distantly related Rubisco from diatoms and bacteria," but the frequency of isoleucine at this position across the full diversity of Rubisco sequences is not quantified. The claim that these substitutions are "rare" or "absent" from plants needs to be supported by a clear description of the sequence database used, the search criteria, and the statistical significance of the rarity. Additionally, the in planta assembly data (Figure 5) is presented as evidence that these rare substitutions are compatible with chloroplast biogenesis, but the data appears to be from transient expression in N. benthamiana, which may not fully recapitulate stable transformation outcomes. Why it matters The claim that ML can access sequence space beyond natural diversity is conceptually important and distinguishes this work from more conventional directed evolution approaches. If the rarity analysis is not rigorous, this claim would be weakened. The in planta assembly data is also critical for establishing the practical relevance of the findings. Resolution test Provide the full phylogenetic analysis, including the sequence database used, the alignment methods, and the frequency of each improved substitution across major Rubisco lineages. Provide more detailed data on the in planta assembly experiments, including the number of biological replicates, the efficiency of assembly, and ideally, data from stable transformants. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer The claim that "ML-assisted library preparation is therefore effective for generating small, streamlined Rubisco libraries that successfully navigate the high degree of sequence conservation present in land plant isoforms" Evidence pointer Figure 3B, Supplementary Table S5 Concern The comparison between the ML-guided library and error-prone PCR libraries is presented as a 1700-fold higher enrichment rate, but the details of this comparison are not fully visible. The error-prone PCR library from prior work (reference 12) may have used different selection conditions, different starting templates, or different definitions of "enriched." The manuscript does not describe how the enrichment rates were normalized or whether the comparison is apples-to-apples. Additionally, the library construction method using gene fragments from Twist Biosciences and Golden Gate Assembly is described, but the efficiency of the assembly, the number of transformants obtained, and the representation of all 49 sites in the final library are not quantified. Why it matters The efficiency of the ML-guided library design is a key methodological contribution. If the comparison to error-prone PCR is not rigorous, the claim of superior efficiency would be overstated. The library quality also directly impacts the interpretation of the selection results. Resolution test Provide a detailed comparison of the ML-guided library and the error-prone PCR library, including the number of variants screened, the selection conditions, and the criteria for enrichment. Report the library coverage statistics, including the number of transformants, the representation of each target site, and the number of variants per site. Concern ID R1-M5 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Reproducibility Claim pointer The claim that "we further confirmed that ML-recommended, catalytically improved NtRbcL variants could assemble correctly in chloroplasts" Evidence pointer Figure 5, Supplementary Figure S8 Concern The in planta assembly experiments use a novel N. benthamiana line (NbrbcM) in which the native rbcL is replaced with R. rubrum rbcM. The manuscript describes the generation of this line but does not provide detailed characterization of its phenotype, growth characteristics, or the efficiency of the plastome transformation. The transient expression system using agroinfiltration is described, but the efficiency of transformation, the expression levels achieved, and the reproducibility of the assembly results are not quantified. The manuscript states that "detectable levels of assembled Rubisco" were observed at 5 days post-infiltration, but the sensitivity of the detection method and the quantification of assembly efficiency are not provided. Why it matters The in planta assembly data is important for establishing that the improved variants are not only functional in E. coli but also compatible with the chloroplast environment. If the assembly data is not robust, the translational potential of the findings would be less certain. Resolution test Provide detailed characterization of the NbrbcM line, including confirmation of rbcL replacement, growth phenotypes, and Rubisco content. Provide quantitative data on the transient expression experiments, including transformation efficiency, expression levels, and assembly efficiency. Ideally, include data from stable transformants. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1 (evidence completeness for library and kinetics), R1-M2 (kinetic characterization rigor), R1-M3 (phylogenetic analysis rigor), R1-M4 (library comparison methodology) Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The application of a structure-informed protein language model to guide directed evolution of Rubisco is novel. While ML-guided protein engineering is an emerging field, this specific application to a challenging plant enzyme with a streamlined library design represents an original contribution. The finding that ML can identify substitutions absent from natural plant sequences is conceptually interesting. Scientific importance: The work addresses a problem of fundamental importance in photosynthesis research and has potential implications for crop improvement. The demonstration that Rubisco's catalytic properties can be improved through targeted mutations is significant, though the magnitude of improvement and its translation to whole-plant photosynthesis remains to be established. Interdisciplinary readership: The work bridges machine learning, protein engineering, plant biology, and photosynthesis research. The methods and findings would be of interest to researchers in all these fields, though the presentation assumes familiarity with both ML concepts and Rubisco biology. Technical soundness: The overall approach is sound, but the current evidence base is incomplete. The lack of supplementary materials, the limited detail on kinetic characterization, and the absence of key control experiments prevent full assessment of technical rigor. The statistical treatment of the data is not fully visible. Readability for nonspecialists: The manuscript is generally well-written and accessible, but some sections assume significant background knowledge. The introduction and discussion are accessible to a broad scientific audience, but the results section may be challenging for readers not familiar with directed evolution or Rubisco kinetics. The use of abbreviations without always defining them clearly could be improved. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved. The core concept is promising and the preliminary results are encouraging, but the current evidence base is insufficient to fully establish the claims. The manuscript would benefit from providing the supplementary materials, more detailed kinetic characterization, and a more rigorous phylogenetic analysis. If these concerns are addressed, this could be a valuable contribution to the field. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that ML-assisted library design achieves a 1700-fold higher enrichment rate compared to error-prone PCR is not fully supported without detailed comparison data. The claim that improved variants carry substitutions "not found in the evolutionary lineage of plants" is not fully supported without the complete phylogenetic analysis. The claim that variants are "assembly competent in plant chloroplasts" is based on transient expression data and may not fully predict stable transformation outcomes. The predicted photosynthetic improvements from the Farquhar model are based on in vitro kinetic parameters and assume equivalent Rubisco content and activation state in planta, which may not hold. The statement that "ML-assisted protein design can explore functional sequence space beyond what is observed from natural sequence diversity" is an interpretation that requires more evidence to be fully established. The mechanistic explanation for how T391I improves kcatc is speculative and not directly tested. The claim that the approach "sidesteps" natural constraints on Rubisco evolution is not fully supported, as the long-term stability and fitness consequences of these mutations in plants are unknown.

04 背景与发展脉络 （标注：以下脉络为「经外部核验」——基于文中引用及领域共识） 经典自抑制模型（~2000s） ：ROCK 的 C 端区域（含 RBD 和 PHC1）与 N 端激酶域结合，维持自抑制构象；Rho-GTP 结合 RBD 后解除抑制。代表方法：生化 pull-down、激酶活性测定。局限：无法解释全长 ROCK 在细胞中的动态行为。 分子尺子模型（2015） ：Truebestein 等基于负染电镜提出 ROCK 始终呈延伸构象，~90-100 nm 卷曲螺旋作为分子尺子将激酶域定位在距膜约 120 nm 处。局限：未能确认 Rho 与 ROCK 的直接结合，留下激活机制空白。 Rho 活性成像与脉冲动力学（2017-2020） ：Graessl 等建立 TIRF 成像体系，揭示 Rho-GEF-H1 正反馈驱动的收缩脉冲；Kamps 等发展 Molecular Activity Painting 光化学遗传学工具。局限：ROCK1 在脉冲中的动态募集机制未知。 AlphaFold 辅助的界面预测（2021-2024） ：AlphaFold2/3 可高置信度预测蛋白复合物结构。本文首次将 AlphaFold 预测的 PHC1-Rho 界面与活细胞功能实验结合，填补结构预测与细胞信号传导之间的鸿沟。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 ROCK 激活机制争议 经典自抑制模型 vs. 延伸构象模型无法调和 生化实验与结构生物学方法观察的是不同构象状态；全长 ROCK 的构象动态难以在体外重构 Introduction 第 2-3 段 Rho-ROCK 直接相互作用未被确认 电镜研究未能重现 Rho 与 ROCK 的结合 可能由于 ROCK 的延伸构象使 RBD 远离膜，Rho 无法触及；或需要膜环境辅助 Introduction 第 3 段 ROCK1 动态募集机制未知 不清楚 ROCK1 如何在秒级时间尺度上被募集到 Rho 活性区 缺乏对 C 端结构域在活细胞中动态行为的系统研究 Results 第 1 节 PHC1 结构域功能被低估 此前仅被视为膜结合模块，未与 Rho 信号偶联 PHC1 的 Rho 结合能力未被探索；AlphaFold 预测提供了新线索 Results 第 3 节、Discussion 第 1 节 06 核心思想 表面方法 ：表达荧光标记的 ROCK1 截短体和点突变体，结合 TIRF 显微镜记录收缩脉冲中的动态募集；使用 AlphaFold3 预测 PHC1 与 Rho 家族 GTPase 的复合物结构；通过 Molecular Activity Painting 光化学遗传学手段进行局部扰动；pull-down 验证直接相互作用。 核心洞察 ：PHC1 结构域不仅是膜锚定模块，还包含一个 AlphaFold 可预测的 Rho 家族 GTPase 结合界面。该界面介导 ROCK1 向 Rho 活性区的快速募集，且与 RBD 协同——RBD 提供 Rho 结合特异性，PHC1 提供膜邻近性和额外的 Rho 接触。PHC1 的突变虽不影响膜募集，却显著降低肌球蛋白激活，说明该结构域在信号传导中具有催化/定位之外的功能。 可能的普适教训 [Analysis]：AlphaFold 预测的蛋白-蛋白界面即使亲和力不足以在体外 pull-down 中检测到，也可能在细胞膜环境中具有功能相关性。膜锚定和局部浓度效应可以显著增强弱相互作用的生物学功能。这提示结构预测课题应重视「弱但功能相关」的界面，并考虑膜环境对结合亲和力的贡献。 07 方法总览 输入 ：人 ROCK1 全长及截短体（RBD-PHC1、dPHC1、mPHC1、mPH、mC1）、点突变体（mutAPH、mutBPH、mutCPH、mutRBD）、GEF-H1 C53R 组成型活性突变体、肌球蛋白 IIa（MYH9） 输出 ：ROCK1 各结构域在收缩脉冲中的时空募集曲线、突变对募集和肌球蛋白激活的定量影响、AlphaFold 预测的复合物模型 模块 ： 1. 活细胞 TIRF 成像（U2OS 细胞，33°C，多激光激发） 2. 图像分析（ImageJ 自定义宏：标准差、脉冲频率、脉冲幅度） 3. The combination of live-cell imaging, structural prediction, and optogenetic perturbation is commendable. However, several technical concerns and interpretive gaps need to be addressed before the central claims are fully established. The evidence for direct PHC1-Rho interaction is indirect, and the functional significance of the PHC1 domain in myosin activation requires stronger experimental support. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers studying Rho GTPase signaling, actin cytoskeleton dynamics, cell contractility, and the molecular mechanisms of ROCK regulation. The findings may also be relevant to those interested in the structural basis of protein-membrane interactions and the application of AlphaFold predictions to guide experimental work. Major strengths The study addresses a significant gap in understanding ROCK1 recruitment mechanisms. The use of multiple complementary approaches, including live-cell imaging, AlphaFold predictions, and optogenetic perturbation, provides a multifaceted view. The identification of specific amino acid residues through structural prediction and their experimental validation is a notable strength. The temporal analysis of ROCK1 recruitment dynamics is carefully executed. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The authors claim that the PHC1 domain is sufficient for recruitment to Rho activity zones and that this recruitment is mediated by interaction with Rho-family GTPases. Evidence pointer Results section "The ROCK1 PHC1 domain is sufficient for recruitment of ROCK1 to Rho activity pulses", Figures 2 and 3 Concern The pull-down experiments (Figure S2D) do not demonstrate specific binding of the isolated PHC1 domain to active RhoA. The authors report that RhoA Q63L pulled down mCherry-mPHC1, but equally strong signals were detected with inactive RhoA T19N and with the mutant mPHC1 construct. This lack of specificity undermines the claim of a direct PHC1-RhoA interaction. Why it matters The central mechanistic claim of the manuscript is that PHC1 mediates recruitment through interaction with Rho-family GTPases. Without biochemical evidence for specific, activity-dependent binding, the interpretation of the cellular imaging data remains ambiguous. Alternative explanations, such as lipid-mediated recruitment or indirect association through other proteins, cannot be excluded. Resolution test The authors should perform quantitative pull-down assays with purified proteins, including dose-response experiments and competition with unlabeled Rho. Alternatively, surface plasmon resonance or isothermal titration calorimetry could provide definitive binding affinities and specificity. The experiments should include a panel of Rho-family GTPases in both active and inactive conformations. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Experimental design Claim pointer The authors claim that the PHC1 domain is critical for signal transduction to activate myosin at the plasma membrane, based on the failure of CA-ROCK1 to induce myosin recruitment in the optogenetic assay. Evidence pointer Results section "The PHC1 domain of ROCK1 is critical for signal transduction to activate myosin at the plasma membrane", Figure 5 Concern The CA-ROCK1 construct used in the optogenetic assay lacks the PHC1 domain but also lacks the RBD and most of the coiled-coil region. The failure of this construct to activate myosin could be due to the loss of any of these regions, not specifically the PHC1 domain. The authors do not test a construct that retains the PHC1 domain but lacks the RBD, or vice versa, to dissect the specific contribution of each domain. Why it matters The conclusion that the PHC1 domain is specifically required for myosin activation is not supported by the experimental design. The CA-ROCK1 construct is a minimal kinase domain construct, and its failure in the assay may reflect a general requirement for the C-terminal region in proper positioning or processivity, rather than a specific PHC1 function. Resolution test The authors should test additional constructs in the optogenetic assay, including: (1) CA-ROCK1 with the PHC1 domain appended, (2) CA-ROCK1 with the RBD appended, and (3) full-length ROCK1 with the PHC1 domain mutations. This would allow dissociation of the specific contributions of each domain to myosin activation. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Quantitative rigor Claim pointer The authors claim that ROCK1 is recruited to Rho activity zones within seconds, with a minimal temporal delay of approximately 3 seconds, and that this recruitment is significantly faster than myosin recruitment. Evidence pointer Results section "ROCK1 is dynamically recruited to cell contraction pulses in adherent mammalian cells", Figure 1 Concern The temporal analysis relies on cross-correlation of fluorescence signals from different proteins imaged in separate channels. The authors do not report the frame rate, the temporal resolution of their imaging system, or the potential for differential lag times between channels due to filter switching or acquisition order. The claim of a 3-second delay may be at the limit of their temporal resolution. Why it matters The temporal relationship between ROCK1 and myosin recruitment is used to support the model of sequential activation. If the temporal resolution is insufficient to resolve the true delay, the conclusions about the kinetics of the signaling cascade may be overstated. Resolution test The authors should report the imaging frame rate and the temporal resolution of their system. They should also perform control experiments with a dual-labeled construct to measure the cross-channel lag time and correct for it in their analysis. Alternatively, they could use simultaneous dual-color imaging with a beam splitter to eliminate sequential acquisition delays. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Interpretation Claim pointer The authors propose that the PHC1 domain and the RBD act synergistically to recruit ROCK1 to Rho activity zones, and that the PHC1 domain has additional functions beyond membrane targeting. Evidence pointer Discussion section "Potential synergistic role of the PHC1 domains and the RBDs in spatial positioning of ROCK1 in the cell cortex" Concern The model presented in Figure 6 is largely speculative and goes beyond the experimental data. The authors propose a specific conformational model involving a kink in the coiled coil and cooperative binding of RBD and PHC1 to membrane-associated Rho, but they do not provide direct structural or biophysical evidence for this model. Why it matters While speculative models can be useful for generating hypotheses, the authors present this model as a conclusion rather than a hypothesis. This could mislead readers into thinking that the conformational mechanism has been experimentally validated. Resolution test The authors should clearly distinguish between experimentally supported conclusions and speculative models. They should either provide additional experimental evidence for the proposed conformational changes (e.g., FRET-based assays, cross-linking, or hydrogen-deuterium exchange) or explicitly label the model as a hypothesis requiring further testing. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Abstract Evidence pointer Abstract Issue The abstract states that the PHC1 domain "mediates recruitment to Rho activity zones" but does not mention the caveats regarding the lack of direct biochemical evidence for PHC1-Rho interaction. Required correction The abstract should be tempered to reflect the indirect nature of the evidence, e.g., "consistent with a role in recruitment" rather than "mediates recruitment." Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Statistical reporting Affected element Figure legends Evidence pointer Figure legends throughout Issue The figure legends do not consistently report the number of independent experiments, the number of cells analyzed, or the statistical tests used for each comparison. Required correction Provide complete statistical details in each figure legend, including n values, statistical tests, and measures of dispersion. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Technical detail Affected element Materials and Methods, Microscopy Evidence pointer Materials and Methods section Issue The frame rate and acquisition parameters for TIRF imaging are not specified, making it difficult to assess the temporal resolution of the experiments. Required correction Report the frame rate, exposure time, and any binning or averaging used for image acquisition. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected element Supplementary figures Evidence pointer Supplementary Material section Issue Several supplementary figures are referenced in the text but not described in sufficient detail in the manuscript, making it difficult to evaluate the data. Required correction Provide complete legends and descriptions for all supplementary figures, or include the figures in the main text if they are essential for the claims. Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Interpretation Affected element Discussion Evidence pointer Discussion section Issue The discussion of the "molecular ruler" model and its extension is interesting but could be more balanced by acknowledging alternative models of ROCK regulation. Required correction Add a brief discussion of alternative models and how the current findings might distinguish between them. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1 (lack of specific biochemical evidence for PHC1-Rho interaction) and R1-M2 (inadequate construct design for dissecting domain-specific contributions to myosin activation) are the primary technical issues that must be resolved. The temporal resolution concern (R1-M3) also needs to be addressed to support the kinetic claims. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The study addresses a relevant question about ROCK1 recruitment mechanisms and proposes a novel role for the PHC1 domain. The application of AlphaFold predictions to guide experimental work is timely. However, the concept of PHC1 involvement in membrane recruitment is not entirely new, and the originality is moderate. Scientific importance: The findings could have implications for understanding ROCK1 regulation in cell contractility, which is relevant to various physiological and pathological processes. However, the importance is somewhat limited by the lack of definitive mechanistic evidence. Interdisciplinary readership: The work will primarily appeal to cell biologists and biophysicists studying cytoskeletal dynamics and Rho GTPase signaling. The structural prediction aspects may also interest computational biologists, but the overall interdisciplinary reach is moderate. Technical soundness: The imaging and optogenetic approaches are well-executed, but the biochemical validation is insufficient. The lack of quantitative binding data and the incomplete construct design undermine the technical soundness of the central claims. Readability for nonspecialists: The manuscript is generally well-written and accessible, with clear figures and logical flow. However, some sections, particularly the discussion of structural models, may be challenging for nonspecialists. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved. The manuscript addresses an interesting question and presents a plausible model, but the central claims regarding PHC1-Rho interaction and the specific role of PHC1 in myosin activation are not yet fully established from the provided evidence. The authors should strengthen the biochemical data and refine the construct design before the case is convincing. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that PHC1 directly interacts with Rho-family GTPases is not supported by the pull-down data, which show no specificity for active versus inactive RhoA. The claim that the PHC1 domain is specifically required for myosin activation is not supported by the construct design, as CA-ROCK1 lacks multiple domains. The proposed conformational model involving a kink in the coiled coil and cooperative binding is speculative and not directly tested. The claim of a 3-second temporal delay between ROCK1 and myosin recruitment may be at the limit of the imaging temporal resolution and requires verification. The statement that the PHC1 domain has "functions beyond membrane targeting" is not directly demonstrated by the experiments presented.

no methods, figures, tables, or supplementary materials were provided Shared manuscript claim summary The authors introduce Flock, a negative-enriched protein-protein interaction (PPI) dataset containing 26,934 positive and 377,643 negative pairs, assembled from PDB biological assemblies and literature-derived negatives curated via an agentic LLM workflow. They also present a Leakage-Free Set benchmark controlling for sequence and interface similarity and historical date cutoffs. Evaluations reportedly show ESMFold2 performance degradation on the Leakage-Free Set while ESMC generalises better. The authors claim Flock is the most comprehensive and challenging PPI benchmark to date. Visible evidence base Abstract text only. No dataset statistics beyond pair counts, no curation pipeline details, no benchmark construction methodology, no evaluation results, no figures or tables Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, methods section, dataset files, benchmark construction details, evaluation protocols, baseline model configurations, statistical analyses, and any supplementary information Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially valuable resource for the PPI prediction community, addressing a recognised gap in negative training data quality and scale. However, the evidence provided is insufficient to evaluate the core claims. The dataset construction methodology, the leakage control procedures, and the comparative model evaluations are all described at a level that prevents independent verification. The claim of being the "most comprehensive and challenging PPI benchmark to date" is not supportable from the abstract alone. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational biologists and machine learning researchers working on protein-protein interaction prediction, protein structure modelling, and protein language models. The dataset could serve as a training and evaluation resource for methods development. The leakage-free benchmark design addresses a recognised problem in the field and would interest researchers concerned with fair model evaluation. Major strengths The problem addressed is well recognised and important. The scale of negative data (377,643 pairs) substantially exceeds typical legacy datasets. The explicit focus on leakage control through sequence, interface, and temporal cutoffs is a thoughtful design element. The use of an agentic LLM workflow for literature mining is a novel methodological approach. graft-through polymerization and characterized them by circular dichroism spectroscopy, infrared spectroscopy, small-angle X-ray scattering, and molecular dynamics simulations. They report that the β-hairpin structure of the monomer is lost regardless of polymer composition, and that simulations indicate the polymer backbone destabilizes local secondary structure by restricting peptide motion and altering the free-energy landscape. The study is framed as providing design rules for synthetic polymer-based proteomimetics. However, the evidence base available for review is limited to the abstract, and several claims are stated without quantitative support or methodological detail. The central conclusion that the polymer backbone destabilizes secondary structure is plausible but cannot be rigorously evaluated from the supplied material. The work may be of interest to the biomaterials and proteomimetics communities, but the case as presented is not fully established. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in peptide-polymer conjugates, protein engineering, biomimetic materials, and drug delivery would be interested because the findings address whether brush polymer architectures can preserve peptide secondary structure, which is central to designing proteomimetic therapeutics and chemical biology tools. The negative result may guide future monomer and backbone design. Major strengths The study addresses a fundamental and under-explored question about the interplay between polymer backbone architecture and peptide secondary structure. The combination of multiple experimental techniques (CD, IR, SAXS) with molecular dynamics simulations is a rigorous approach. The use of trpzip2, a well-established model for β-hairpin folding, provides a clear benchmark for structural assessment. were provided Shared manuscript claim summary The authors introduce NuCaliby, a structure-conditioned model that jointly designs amino acid, mRNA, and DNA sequences at nucleotide resolution. The model predicts a Potts model over a nucleotide graph, trained with amino acid supervision via marginalization over synonymous codons. Claims include preserved residue-level designability comparable to the original Caliby model, composable inference-time guidance for sequence-level objectives, improved host tRNA adaptation beyond synonymous sequence space, direct embedding of RNA motifs into coding sequences, and wet lab validation showing expressible and soluble proteins on par with state of the art methods. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no figures, tables, methods sections, or supplementary data were supplied Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, methods details, model architecture specifications, training data description, benchmark definitions, wet lab protocols, quantitative results, and code repository contents Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a conceptually interesting extension of protein design to the nucleotide level, with a technically plausible training strategy based on marginalizing over synonymous codons. However, the evidence base is limited to the abstract, and several central claims, particularly regarding wet lab performance and the nature of the trade-off between tRNA adaptation and self-consistency, cannot be evaluated without the full manuscript. The work is likely to interest the protein design and synthetic biology communities, but the case for its significance and robustness is not established from the supplied material. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in computational protein design, mRNA therapeutics, synthetic biology, and codon optimization. The joint design of amino acid and nucleotide sequences addresses a practical bottleneck in gene synthesis and expression optimization, and the energy-based guidance framework may appeal to those working on constrained sequence design. Major strengths The conceptual advance of designing at nucleotide resolution while preserving amino acid-level designability is timely and relevant. The training strategy using amino acid supervision with marginalization over synonymous codons is elegant and likely to be technically sound. The composable inference-time guidance framework is a flexible and potentially powerful feature. The inclusion of wet lab validation, even if only summarized, strengthens the practical relevance. D等结构预测工具，在表达实验前对融合肽的二级结构倾向和电荷特征进行筛选，以理性设计针对革兰氏阴性菌的裂解酶融合变体。该文为「结构预测指导的蛋白质工程」提供了一个可迁移的案例，即计算预测与实验筛选结合，减少试错成本。 02 一句话总结 本文通过将7种不同肽段融合至裂解酶LysPd138的N端，结合AlphaFold2/PSIPRED结构预测与电荷分析，发现具有高α-螺旋倾向和较多正电荷残基的融合肽（Syn138、Pad138、CecA138）在150 mM NaCl及人/小鼠血清中保留增强的杀菌活性，并在另一裂解酶LysPd149上验证了该规律。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：如何理性选择或设计用于融合的肽段，以增强噬菌体裂解酶在生理条件（高盐、血清）下对革兰氏阴性菌（鲍曼不动杆菌）的杀菌活性？ 为什么重要 ：革兰氏阴性菌的外膜屏障使裂解酶难以接触肽聚糖；且裂解酶在高盐/血清等生理条件下活性显著下降，限制了其治疗应用。抗生素耐药问题日益严峻，需要新型抗菌策略。 现有方法为何不足 ：当前肽段融合策略主要依赖试错法（trial-and-error），需要大量筛选实验，成本高、耗时长，且缺乏对融合肽结构特征的理性指导。 精确研究问题 ：Can structure prediction (AlphaFold2/PSIPRED) and charge analysis identify peptide features (α-helicity, positive charge) that predict enhanced lysin activity under physiological conditions? 04 背景与发展脉络 阶段一：裂解酶作为抗菌剂的发现 （2000s–2010s）：裂解酶是噬菌体编码的肽聚糖降解酶，外源应用对革兰氏阳性菌有效（Schmelcher & Loessner, 2016; Ramos-Vivas et al., 2021）。 阶段二：针对革兰氏阴性菌的裂解酶工程 （2015–2025）：革兰氏阴性菌外膜阻碍裂解酶接触肽聚糖。策略包括：融合抗菌肽（AMP）、阳离子肽、去污剂样肽等以增强外膜穿透（Sui et al., 2023; Kim J. et al., 2025）。但高盐/血清条件下活性丧失问题未解决。 阶段三：AI结构预测辅助蛋白工程 （2020–至今）：AlphaFold2（Jumper et al., 2020）等工具使蛋白结构预测成为常规手段，为融合蛋白设计提供结构层面的指导。 本文位置 ：将AI结构预测（AlphaFold2/PSIPRED）与电荷分析引入裂解酶融合肽的筛选流程，提出「先计算筛选、后实验验证」的理性设计范式，属于阶段三在抗菌蛋白工程中的具体应用。 注：此脉络基于本文引言及参考文献构建，经外部核验（引用文献均为真实存在）。 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据
