No figures, tables, or supplementary files were provided for review. Assessment boundary Scientific content, structural logic, evidence quality, and internal consistency of the manuscript as submitted. Claims are assessed against the evidence presented within the text itself. No external literature verification was performed. Shared manuscript claim summary The manuscript is a review article that synthesizes structural biology knowledge of DEAD-box RNA helicases with multi-omics data from cold-stressed rubber tree (Hevea brasiliensis). It identifies nine differentially abundant DDX proteins under cold stress, highlights DDX39B as the most responsive, and uses AlphaFold2 predictions to argue for strong structural and evolutionary conservation of HbDDX39B. The authors propose that cold-induced downregulation of DDX39B may underlie cold sensitivity in tropical plants and suggest translational applications for crop improvement. Visible evidence base Text descriptions of Table 1 (structural data from PDB Europe), Table 2 (nine differentially abundant DDX proteins), Figure 1 (classification and domain architecture), Figures 2-5 (structural details of DDX3X, DDX21, DHX36, RIG-I-like receptors), Figure 6 (AlphaFold2 comparison of HbDDX39B with human ortholog), Figure 7 (conceptual framework), Supplementary Figures S1-S3, Supplementary Table S1. None of these figures, tables, or supplementary materials were actually provided to the reviewer. Missing materials affecting confidence All figures, tables, and supplementary files are referenced but not included. The multi-omics datasets (proteomics, transcriptomics) are cited via prior publications (Mao et al., 2022; Gao et al., 2025) but not described in sufficient detail to evaluate experimental design, statistical thresholds, or replication. The Ka/Ks analysis methodology is described only briefly. The AlphaFold2 prediction parameters, confidence metrics (pLDDT, PAE), and validation steps are not reported. Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript presents a potentially useful integrative review that connects structural biology of DEAD-box helicases with cold stress responses in a non-model crop species. The central observation, that DDX39B is strongly downregulated under cold stress in rubber tree and is highly conserved across tropical species, is interesting and could have translational relevance. However, the manuscript suffers from a fundamental mismatch between its stated scope and its actual content. The title and abstract promise "structural and functional perspectives," but the structural sections are largely a summary of previously published work on human and yeast systems, with no new structural data presented. The rubber tree-specific content is limited to a single AlphaFold2 prediction and a Ka/Ks analysis, both of which are described with insufficient methodological detail. The interpretive leap from sequence conservation to a mechanistic explanation of tropical plant cold sensitivity is not adequately supported. The manuscript reads more like a perspective or hypothesis paper than a comprehensive review, and the evidence base for its central claims is thin. Who would be interested in the results, and why Plant stress biologists studying cold tolerance mechanisms in tropical crops would find the identification of DDX39B as a candidate cold-responsive factor of interest. Researchers working on RNA metabolism in plants, particularly those studying splicing and mRNA export under abiotic stress, may find the conceptual framework useful. Structural biologists studying DEAD-box helicases might be interested in the comparative analysis, though they would find little new information. Agricultural biotechnologists focused on rubber tree improvement or engineering cold tolerance in tropical crops could see translational potential. The broader readership of a plant science journal would find the topic relevant, but the depth of analysis may not satisfy specialists in any single discipline. Major strengths The manuscript addresses a genuinely understudied area, namely DEAD-box helicase function in tropical crop stress responses. The integration of structural biology concepts with plant stress physiology is a worthwhile framing. The identification of DDX39B as a consistently cold-responsive helicase across multiple comparison groups is a concrete, useful observation. The Ka/Ks analysis, while briefly described, provides quantitative evidence for purifying selection. The authors are appropriately cautious in noting that their structural predictions require experimental validation. The writing is generally clear and accessible. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The manuscript claims that "nine differentially abundant DDX family proteins were identified" in cold-stressed rubber tree and that "DDX39B shows the most pronounced response." Evidence pointer Table 2, Section 4.1, location not provided Concern The multi-omics data underpinning the central claim of this review are not presented in sufficient detail. The manuscript refers to "a previous quantitative analysis" (Mao et al., 2022; Gao et al., 2025) but does not describe the experimental design, the cold stress treatment conditions, the time points sampled, the tissue types analyzed, the proteomics methodology, the statistical thresholds for differential abundance, or the number of biological replicates. Without this information, the reader cannot assess the robustness of the identification of these nine proteins or the claim that DDX39B is the most pronounced responder. The table itself is not provided. Why it matters The entire rubber tree-specific contribution of this review rests on these multi-omics data. If the underlying data are weak, underpowered, or derived from a single condition, the interpretive framework built on them collapses. A review article should either present the primary data with full methodological transparency or clearly direct readers to the original studies with a summary of key parameters. Resolution test Provide a detailed description of the experimental design, including cold stress conditions, time points, tissues, replication, statistical thresholds, and the magnitude of changes for each of the nine proteins. Include the full Table 2 with quantitative values and statistical measures. If the data are from published studies, summarize the key methodological parameters in the text or a supplementary table. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Claim-evidence alignment Claim pointer The manuscript claims that "AlphaFold2 predictions reveal near-identical core helicase folds" between rubber tree and human DDX39B, and that the RMSD across the core helicase domain is "only 0.299 Å." Evidence pointer Section 4.3, Figure 6, location not provided Concern The AlphaFold2 analysis is presented as a central piece of evidence, but the methodological details are almost entirely absent. The manuscript does not state which AlphaFold2 version was used, whether the predictions were run locally or obtained from the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database, what confidence metrics were obtained (pLDDT, PAE), how the structures were aligned, which residues were included in the RMSD calculation, or whether the comparison was performed on full-length proteins or isolated domains. The claim of "near-identical" folds based on a single RMSD value of 0.299 Å is difficult to evaluate without knowing the alignment procedure and the structural context. Furthermore, the comparison to the crystal structure of human DDX39B (PDB: 1XTI) is mentioned but not shown quantitatively. Why it matters The structural comparison is used to argue for strong functional constraint and to support the translational relevance of the findings. If the RMSD calculation is misleading, for example by excluding flexible regions or comparing only a small conserved core, the conclusion of "near-identical" folds would be overstated. The manuscript itself acknowledges that these are computational predictions, but the presentation still implies a level of precision that the described methods cannot support. Resolution test Report the AlphaFold2 version, the source of the models, the pLDDT and PAE scores for the regions compared, the exact residues included in the RMSD calculation, and the alignment method. Provide a figure showing the structural superposition with clearly labeled domains and confidence annotations. If possible, include a quantitative comparison of the rubber tree model to the human crystal structure using multiple metrics (e.g., TM-score, GDT-TS). Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Logical inference Claim pointer The manuscript proposes that "the cold sensitivity of tropical plants may be partially attributable to the inherent vulnerability of their RNA metabolic machinery to low temperatures" and that "reduced DDX39B abundance could lead to impaired splicing and nuclear export of cold-responsive transcripts." Evidence pointer Section 4.3, Section 5, location not provided Concern The causal chain from DDX39B downregulation to cold sensitivity is speculative and presented without adequate consideration of alternative explanations. The observation that DDX39B is downregulated under cold stress does not establish that this downregulation causes cold sensitivity. It could be a protective response, a downstream consequence of cellular damage, or unrelated to the cold sensitivity phenotype. The manuscript acknowledges this distinction in the concluding remarks but then proceeds to build a translational framework on the assumption that DDX39B modulation could enhance cold tolerance. The comparison to temperate plants with CBF/DREB-mediated cold acclimation is presented as if it were established that DDX39B is a limiting factor in tropical plants, which is not supported by the data shown. Why it matters The translational claims in Section 5.4, including the suggestion that DDX39B could be a target for marker-assisted selection or transgenic approaches, depend on the causal role of DDX39B in cold sensitivity. If the downregulation is a consequence rather than a cause, these applications would not be justified. The manuscript should clearly distinguish between hypothesis and established fact. Resolution test Reframe the discussion to explicitly label the causal model as a hypothesis requiring experimental testing. Describe the specific experiments needed to establish causality, such as overexpression or knockdown of HbDDX39B in rubber tree or a model system, followed by cold stress phenotyping. Alternatively, present additional evidence from the multi-omics data that supports a causal role, such as correlation with known cold tolerance regulators or enrichment of DDX39B targets among cold-responsive genes. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Scope coherence Claim pointer The title and abstract promise "structural and functional perspectives on DEAD-box RNA helicases in the rubber tree cold stress response," and the introduction states that the review will "synthesize current structural understanding of the DEAD-box helicase family, integrate recent proteomic evidence from cold-stressed rubber tree, and use AlphaFold2 structural prediction to examine the cold-responsive helicase DDX39B in detail." Evidence pointer Title, Abstract, Section 1, Sections 3.1-3.4, location not provided Concern The structural sections of the manuscript (Sections 3.1-3.4) review previously published structures of human and animal DEAD-box helicases (DDX3X, DDX21, DHX36, RIG-I-like receptors) in considerable detail, but these sections are not well integrated with the rubber tree focus. The connection between these structural examples and the cold stress response in rubber tree is asserted rather than demonstrated. The reader is left wondering why these particular helicases were chosen for detailed review, and how they inform the analysis of HbDDX39B. The manuscript would be stronger if the structural review were either substantially condensed or explicitly framed as a comparative basis for understanding the rubber tree protein. Why it matters A review should have a clear through-line that connects all sections. The current structure reads as two separate manuscripts, one on DEAD-box helicase structural biology and one on rubber tree cold stress, that have been combined. This weakens the coherence of the argument and may lose readers who are interested in one topic but not the other. Resolution test Revise the structural sections to explicitly link each example to the rubber tree context. For each helicase discussed, state what specific insight it provides for understanding HbDDX39B function or cold stress responses. Alternatively, condense Sections 3.1-3.4 into a single section that focuses on the structural principles most relevant to the rubber tree analysis. Concern ID R1-M5 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Novelty and contribution Claim pointer The manuscript claims to provide "a conceptual framework for dissecting DDX helicase roles in plant abiotic stress tolerance" and a "generalizable strategy for mechanistic investigations in non-model plant species." Evidence pointer Abstract, Section 5, Section 5.5, location not provided Concern The claimed novelty of the integrative approach is overstated. Combining multi-omics data with AlphaFold2 structure prediction is now a standard approach in plant biology and is not inherently novel. The manuscript does not demonstrate that this integration has produced insights that could not have been obtained by simpler analyses. The "conceptual framework" presented in Figure 7 is described only in text and appears to be a general schematic rather than a specific, testable model. The authors do not articulate what is genuinely new about their approach or what specific hypotheses it generates that would not arise from standard sequence analysis alone. Why it matters For a review article to be valuable, it must either synthesize existing knowledge in a way that generates new insights or identify specific gaps and opportunities for future research. The current manuscript does neither in a compelling way. The reader is left with a general sense that DEAD-box helicases are important in cold stress, but no clear agenda for future research. Resolution test Articulate specific, testable hypotheses that arise from the integration of structural and multi-omics data. For example, predict which specific residues in HbDDX39B might be responsible for cold sensitivity based on comparison with cold-tolerant orthologs, or identify specific RNA targets whose splicing or export might be affected by DDX39B downregulation. Describe how the proposed framework differs from existing approaches in the literature. The structural comparison between rubber tree and human DDX39B is presented with a single RMSD value but no methodological context. The causal link between DDX39B downregulation and cold sensitivity is asserted without experimental support. These issues must be resolved before the manuscript's central claims can be considered established. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: Moderate. The topic is relevant but the approach is not novel. Combining multi-omics with AlphaFold2 is now standard practice. Scientific importance: Moderate. The identification of DDX39B as a cold-responsive helicase in rubber tree is of interest to a specialized audience, but the broader significance is not clearly established. Interdisciplinary readership: Limited. The manuscript is unlikely to attract readers beyond plant stress biology and RNA metabolism. Technical soundness: Weak. The methodological details for the key analyses are insufficient to assess technical quality. Readability for nonspecialists: Acceptable. The writing is clear, but the structural sections assume familiarity with helicase biology that may not be universal. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The manuscript has a potentially interesting core observation, but the evidence base is too thin to support the claims made. Major revisions are required to provide adequate methodological detail, to reframe the causal claims as hypotheses, and to better integrate the structural and rubber tree-specific sections. If the authors can provide the missing data and revise the interpretive framework, the manuscript could become a useful contribution to the plant stress biology literature. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that nine differentially abundant DDX proteins were identified in cold-stressed rubber tree is not supported by the provided text, as the underlying data and methodology are not described. The claim that DDX39B shows the "most pronounced response" to cold stress is not supported by quantitative data. The claim that rubber tree DDX39B shares ">95% sequence identity" with orthologs from other tropical species and "~73% identity" with human DDX39B is presented without showing the alignment or specifying the sequences compared. The claim that AlphaFold2 predictions reveal "near-identical core helicase folds" with an RMSD of 0.299 Å is not supported by methodological detail or a figure. The claim that "the cold sensitivity of tropical plants may be partially attributable to the inherent vulnerability of their RNA metabolic machinery to low temperatures" is a hypothesis presented without direct evidence. The claim that DDX39B downregulation "could lead to impaired splicing and nuclear export of cold-responsive transcripts" is speculative and not supported by functional data. The claim that the predicted LysM and protein kinase domains in isoform A0A6A6KEA8 represent "a potentially novel domain architecture not previously reported" is not verifiable from the provided text. The translational claims regarding marker-assisted selection or transgenic approaches for cold tolerance are not supported by the evidence presented. The statement that "recent multi-omics investigations have identified multiple DDX family proteins that are differentially abundant under cold stress" is not verifiable without access to the cited primary studies.

01 基本信息 标题 ：DreamFold: A World Model to efficiently generate protein folding pathways in the latent space 作者 ：Ianeselli, Alan; Im, Jewon; Cavallin, Eddie; Gerstein, Mark B 单位 ：Yale University（由致谢与计算资源部分推断，具体作者单位未在摘要中提供） 期刊/平台 ：Protein Science（Protein Society 官方期刊） 年份 ：2026（在线日期 2026-09-30） 论文类型 ：方法学原创研究 领域 ：蛋白质折叠路径计算 × 生成式 AI（World Model）/ 隐空间建模 关键词 ：World Model、蛋白质折叠路径、隐空间、变分自编码器、进化策略、生成式 AI DOI/arXiv ：10.1002/pro.70794 代码 ：未提供（提及 GitHub 仓库存放 GROMACS 协议文件，但未给出具体地址） 数据 ：Zenodo，https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17369796 阅读日期 ：2026-05-14 在该方向中的位置 ：本文属于「AI 驱动的蛋白质构象采样/路径生成」子方向，首次将 World Model 范式（源自机器人/游戏领域）引入蛋白质折叠路径计算，在隐空间中完成折叠策略学习，实现比 MD 快 4 个数量级的折叠路径生成，并保持原子级分辨率输出。与 AlphaFold 等静态结构预测方法互补，聚焦动态过程；与基于物理的 MD 模拟相比，绕开了逐帧积分的高昂计算成本。 02 一句话总结 DreamFold 使用变分自编码器将蛋白质结构（Φ/Ψ 二面角 + Cα 距离）和动作（二面角旋转）压缩到 10 维隐空间，训练前馈神经网络作为隐空间动力学模型，再用 CMA 进化策略在"梦境环境"中学习折叠策略，以比 MD 快 3,800–30,000 倍的速度生成从展开态到天然态的折叠路径，并在 7 个测试蛋白上验证了折叠中间体和过渡态的原子级结构准确性。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：能否用 World Model 范式在隐空间中高效生成蛋白质折叠路径，避免 MD 模拟中逐帧积分的高昂计算成本？ 为什么重要 ：蛋白质折叠路径、中间体和过渡态结构是理解蛋白质功能、错误折叠疾病机制以及进行基于结构的药物设计（尤其是靶向隐蔽口袋）的关键信息。但 MD 模拟受限于时间尺度和计算资源，难以覆盖中等大小蛋白的完整折叠过程。 现有方法不足 ： MD 模拟计算成本高（O(NlogN)），且需要预先指定力场和长时间平衡； 增强采样方法（如 rMDBF、D&R）虽加速采样，但仍需大量 MD 计算； 现有 AI 方法多聚焦静态结构预测（如 AlphaFold）或构象集合生成，缺乏对折叠路径（时间有序的构象转变序列）的高效生成能力； 直接在高维原子坐标空间训练强化学习/进化策略不可行，需要降维。 精确研究问题 ：Can a World Model trained on limited Monte Carlo trajectory data build a latent spatio-temporal representation of protein dynamics that enables efficient generation of physically plausible folding pathways at atomistic resolution? 04 背景与发展脉络 （标注：以下脉络为「经外部核验」——基于摘要中引用的文献与领域常识，但具体细节以本文框架为主） 阶段 代表性方法 优点 局限 物理模拟时代 全原子 MD（Shaw et al., 2010） 高精度、物理严格 计算成本极高，难以跨越毫秒级折叠时间尺度 增强采样 rMDBF（Ianeselli et al., 2018）、D&R（Ianeselli et al., 2024） 加速路径采样 仍需大量 MD 计算，计算复杂度仍为 O(NlogN) 降维建模 VAE 用于蛋白质构象（Mansoor et al., 2024; VAE1（结构编码器） ：输入 S = [Φ, Ψ, Cα距离]，输出 10 维隐向量 ς。编码器和解码器均为神经网络。 3. VAE2（动作编码器） ：输入 A = [ΔΦ, ΔΨ]，输出 10 维隐向量 α。 4. FFN（未来状态预测器） ：输入 [ς(t), α(t)]，输出 ς(t+1) 的预测。这是 World Model 的"环境模拟器"。 5. 控制器（策略网络） ：输入 ς(t)，输出 α(t)。使用 CMA 进化策略训练，奖励 = 路径累积 Ramachandran 评分 + 终点隐空间距离。 6. 解码与验证模块 ：将隐空间轨迹解码回原子结构，与 DESRES MD 轨迹进行路径相似性比较。 训练流程 ： - Step 1: 生成随机 rollout 数据（50 轨迹 × 500 步） - Step 2: 训练 VAE1（结构压缩） - Step 3: 训练 VAE2（动作压缩） - Step 4: 训练 FFN（隐空间动力学） - Step 5: 固定 VAE1/VAE2/FFN，用 CMA 训练控制器 关键假设 ： - 隐空间中的欧氏距离近似反映构象相似性； - FFN 学到的隐空间动力学足以捕捉折叠的关键中间态； - 能量最小化步骤保证了训练数据的物理合理性。 08 核心模块拆解 模块 功能 为何需要 输入输出 支撑证据 移除后的已知或预期影响 VAE1（结构编码器） 将高维结构特征压缩为 10 维隐向量 降低策略学习维度，使 CMA 可行 输入：Φ/Ψ 二面角 + Cα 距离（~3N 维）；输出：ς ∈ R^10 方法节 Step 2；重建误差作为训练损失 移除后控制器需在高维空间学习，CMA 不可行 [预期] VAE2（动作编码器） 压缩动作空间 动作空间同样高维（2N 个二面角变化） 输入：ΔΦ/ΔΨ；输出：α ∈ R^10 方法节 Step 3 移除后 FFN 输入维度爆炸，训练数据需求剧增 [预期] FFN（未来状态预测器） 学习隐空间动力学 ς(t+1)|ς(t),α(t) 构建"梦境环境"，使控制器训练无需真实 MD 输入：[ς(t), α(t)]；输出：ς(t+1) 预测 方法节 Step 4；MAE 损失 移除后控制器无法在梦境中训练，需回到真实环境 [预期] 控制器（策略网络） 学习折叠策略 α(t)|ς(t) 生成从展开态到天然态的路径 输入：ς(t)；输出：α(t) 方法节 Step 5；CMA 训练 移除后无法生成路径 [预期] Ramachandran 正则化 惩罚不合理的 Φ/Ψ 组合 防止隐空间解码产生立体化学不合理构象 输入：解码后的 Φ/Ψ；输出：惩罚分数 Results 图 2a-d；正则化降低路径能量 移除后路径可能包含高能不合理构象 [预期] 解码器（VAE1 的 decoder） 将隐向量重建为原子结构 输出原子级分辨率路径 输入：ς；输出：S（Φ/Ψ + Cα 距离） 方法节 Step 2 移除后无法获得原子结构 [预期] 09 关键公式符号 1. ：需要已知目标天然态结构（PDB），因此无法用于预测未知蛋白的折叠路径；本质上是"条件路径生成"而非"折叠预测"。 输出性质 ：生成的路径是"物理合理的"（经 Ramachandran 正则化和能量最小化数据训练），但 不是 真实动力学轨迹——路径上的构象序列不等同于时间演化的 MD 轨迹，缺乏真实的时间尺度。 验证边界 ： - 路径相似性高 ≠ 动力学正确：DreamFold 路径在折叠顺序（哪些结构先形成）上与 MD 一致，但无法给出折叠速率或中间体寿命； - 中间体识别是"存在性"而非"群体性"：找到中间体构象 ≠ 知道其热力学稳定性或群体比例； - 速度优势（30,000×）是端到端路径生成 vs. MD 模拟的对比，不包括训练数据生成（MD/MC 采样）的一次性成本。 适用边界 ：测试蛋白 ≤133 aa（Ubiquitin 76 aa 用于 TS 分析，hCRBP2 133 aa 为最大折叠测试）；449 aa 的 α-tubulin 仅做了可行性演示，无验证。方法依赖训练数据的力场（Rosetta），继承了力场的系统误差。 正确表述 ：DreamFold 是一种高效的蛋白质折叠路径生成器，能在保持原子级分辨率的同时，以远低于 MD 的计算成本生成与 MD 在折叠顺序上一致的路径，可用于发现药物靶向的中间体构象；但它不提供热力学/动力学定量信息，且路径的物理真实性受限于训练力场。 12 作者自认局限 局限 具体表现 作者提出的未来方向 来源 无法直接计算热力学/动力学量 路径不满足细致平衡，不能提取自由能、速率常数等 结合短 MD 松弛 + MSM 重建热力学（已在本文演示） Limitations 节 路径非平衡态 No line numbers were provided; references to sections and figures are based on the manuscript structure. Shared manuscript claim summary The authors present DreamFold, a generative World Model framework that learns protein folding pathways in a latent space. The model encodes protein structures and dihedral angle moves into latent vectors using variational autoencoders, predicts future latent states with a feedforward neural network, and trains a controller via evolutionary strategies (CMA-ES) to drive folding toward a target native state. The authors claim speedups of up to ~30,000× over molecular dynamics, linear scaling O(N) with system size, and accurate identification of folding intermediates and transition states validated against MD simulations and experimental data. Visible evidence base Abstract, full methods description, results sections for regularization, folding pathway computation, performance benchmarks, path similarity analysis, thermodynamics reconstruction, and case studies for Fip35, TrpCage, Protein G, λ-repressor, PrP, Ubiquitin, and hCRBP2. Figures referenced but not provided. Supporting Information referenced but not provided. Missing materials affecting confidence Figures 1–9, all Supporting Information sections (including model architecture details, hyperparameters, training procedures, and additional validation), the Zenodo data repository contents, and the GitHub repository with protocol files. Without these, quantitative claims about performance, accuracy, and scaling cannot be independently verified. Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript presents a conceptually interesting application of World Models to protein folding, with a plausible pipeline combining VAEs, a forward dynamics model, and evolutionary policy optimization. The claimed computational speedups are striking and, if reproducible, would be of practical value. However, the evidence base as provided is insufficient to establish the central claims. Key validation metrics, benchmark details, and comparisons are described qualitatively or deferred to Supporting Information and figures that were not available for review. The thermodynamic reconstruction via MSM is acknowledged as approximate, but the limitations of this approach are understated. The manuscript would benefit from clearer reporting of error bars, statistical significance, and direct comparisons to baseline methods. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational biophysicists and structural biologists interested in fast generative approaches for conformational sampling; AI researchers working on World Models and latent-space dynamics; drug discovery scientists targeting cryptic pockets and folding intermediates. The promise of orders-of-magnitude speedup over MD would attract a broad interdisciplinary audience if the claims are substantiated. Major strengths 1. Novel application of World Models to protein folding, extending a successful AI paradigm from robotics/games to molecular simulations. 2. The pipeline is modular and clearly described, with each component (VAE, FFN, CMA-ES) justified. 3. The authors address a real bottleneck (computational cost of MD) and propose a principled alternative. 4. Validation against multiple reference datasets (DESRS, experimental data) is attempted, and the authors acknowledge the out-of-equilibrium nature of their trajectories. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer "DreamFold can compute protein folding pathways four orders of magnitude faster than molecular dynamics (MD), up to ~30,000×." Evidence pointer Results section "Performance"; Figure 4 (not provided); Supporting Information S1: section 5 (not provided) Concern The speedup claim is central to the paper's impact, but the provided text does not include the actual benchmark data, hardware specifications, or the MD baseline used for comparison. The scaling argument (O(N) vs O(N log N)) is presented theoretically, but no empirical scaling plots or wall-clock measurements are shown in the manuscript text. The comparison to MD is also complicated by the fact that DreamFold trajectories are not physical dynamics and lack a time axis, making "speedup" ambiguous. Why it matters Without reproducible benchmark details, the headline performance claim cannot be assessed. If the speedup is not robust across systems or is sensitive to hyperparameters, the practical utility of DreamFold is diminished. Resolution test Provide a table or figure with wall-clock times for DreamFold vs MD for all tested proteins, including hardware details, number of MD replicates, and statistical variability. Clarify what "speedup" means in the absence of a physical time scale. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Validation rigor Claim pointer "We have validated our results against established MD benchmarks and other available experimental data." Evidence pointer Results sections "Computation of folding pathways and validation", "Path similarity and structure formation analysis"; Figures 3, 4 (not provided) Concern The validation is described qualitatively. For Fip35, the authors report 94% pathway I prevalence, but no confidence intervals, number of replicates, or statistical test are given. For TrpCage, the two pathways are described as "almost equiprobable," but the 48/52 split is not tested for significance. The path similarity analysis is mentioned, but the actual similarity values, the choice of reference trajectories, and the interpretation of "indistinguishable" are not provided in the text. Why it matters The central claim of accuracy rests on these comparisons. Without quantitative metrics and statistical rigor, the reader cannot distinguish genuine agreement from chance or systematic bias. Resolution test Report mean and standard deviation (or confidence intervals) for pathway fractions, path similarity scores, and structural metrics across replicates. Include a statistical test (e.g., bootstrap or permutation test) for pathway preference. Provide the actual similarity values and the criteria for "indistinguishable." Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Reproducibility Claim pointer "DreamFold has been built via custom-made code written in Python using Keras and tensorflow." Evidence pointer Methods section; Data Availability Statement; GitHub repository (URL not provided in text) Concern The manuscript states that code and data are available, but the specific repository URLs and the Zenodo DOI are only mentioned in the Data Availability Statement. The Supporting Information is referenced extensively but was not provided for review. Key details such as VAE architecture (layer sizes, latent dimension), training hyperparameters (learning rate, batch size, epochs), and the exact reward function formulation are deferred to Supporting Information S1. Why it matters Reproducibility is a core requirement for computational papers. Without full architectural and training details, other groups cannot implement or benchmark DreamFold. Resolution test Include the full model architecture, hyperparameters, and training procedures in the main text or ensure the Supporting Information is accessible. Provide the GitHub and Zenodo links in the main text. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Conceptual clarity Claim pointer "DreamFold can be used to compute the folding pathway of biomolecules and obtain the atomistic structure of therapeutically relevant intermediate states." Evidence pointer Results sections "PrP folding intermediate", "Structural ensemble of hCRBP2"; Figures 6, 9 (not provided) Concern The identification of folding intermediates and cryptic pockets is presented as a key application, but the criteria for "identifying" an intermediate are not defined. For PrP, 7 out of 50 trajectories passed through the intermediate, but the authors do not explain why the other 43 did not, or whether this fraction is expected. For hCRBP2, the "open monomer" intermediate is described as "transient," but the frequency and structural variability of this state are not quantified. Why it matters The biological and therapeutic relevance of the method depends on the reliability and reproducibility of intermediate identification. Without clear criteria and statistics, the claim is anecdotal. Resolution test Define a quantitative criterion for intermediate detection (e.g., structural similarity threshold, residence time). Report the fraction of trajectories that populate each intermediate, with variability across independent runs. Compare the identified intermediates to experimental structures where available. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Abstract Evidence pointer Abstract, first sentence Issue The phrase "data regarding their folding mechanisms and dynamics is scarce" is grammatically incorrect ("data" is plural) and could be rephrased for clarity. Required correction Change to "data regarding folding mechanisms and dynamics are scarce" or "are limited." Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Terminology Affected element Results section "Ubiquitin's transition state" Evidence pointer Results, "Ubiquitin's transition state" paragraph Issue The authors use "Ψ and Φ analyses" to refer to phi-value analysis, which is standard, but the notation is confusing because Ψ and Φ are also used for dihedral angles earlier in the text. This dual use could confuse readers. Required correction Clarify the distinction, e.g., "phi-value analysis (Ψ-value analysis)" and avoid using Ψ/Φ for both dihedral angles and phi-values without explicit definition. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected element Methods section Evidence pointer Methods, "Molecular dynamics simulations" paragraph Issue The MD simulation protocol is described, but the temperature for each system is not specified in the text; it is only stated that "Temperature was chosen to match available MD data and is shown in Figure 5." Required correction State the temperatures explicitly in the text or in a table. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Statistical reporting Affected element Results section "Performance" Evidence pointer Results, "Performance" paragraph Issue The speedup factors (3800×, 8000×, 30,000×) are reported as single numbers without error bars or variability across runs. Required correction Report mean and standard deviation across multiple independent runs, or state that these are representative values. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1 (speedup claim without benchmark data), R1-M2 (validation without quantitative metrics), R1-M3 (reproducibility details missing), R1-M4 (intermediate identification criteria undefined). Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality The application of World Models to protein folding is novel and extends a successful AI paradigm to a new domain. This is a creative contribution. Scientific importance If the claims are substantiated, the method could significantly accelerate conformational sampling and enable studies of larger systems than currently feasible with MD. The identification of cryptic pockets has direct therapeutic relevance. Interdisciplinary readership The work bridges AI, biophysics, and drug discovery, and would appeal to readers across these fields. The conceptual framing is accessible. Technical soundness The pipeline is plausible, but the evidence provided is insufficient to assess technical soundness. Key benchmarks, statistical analyses, and implementation details are missing or deferred to Supporting Information. Readability for nonspecialists The manuscript is generally well-written and the World Model concept is explained clearly. However, some sections (e.g., the MSM reconstruction) assume familiarity with specialized methods. The dual use of Ψ/Φ notation is a minor readability issue. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved. The core idea is promising and the application is timely, but the current manuscript does not provide sufficient evidence to establish the central claims of speed, accuracy, and biological utility. The authors should provide the missing benchmark data, statistical rigor, and implementation details. Risk / unsupported claims The speedup claim (up to ~30,000×) is unsupported without benchmark data and a clear definition of "speedup" in the absence of a physical time scale. The claim of linear scaling O(N) is presented theoretically but not empirically demonstrated in the text. The validation against MD and experimental data is described qualitatively; no quantitative similarity metrics or statistical tests are provided. The identification of folding intermediates (PrP, hCRPB2) and the cryptic pocket is based on a small number of trajectories (7/50 for PrP) without defined criteria or statistical confidence. The MSM reconstruction is acknowledged as approximate, but the limitations of this approach for recovering true kinetics are understated. The claim that DreamFold is "the first application of generative World Models in the context of biomolecular simulations" is a strong priority claim that would require a thorough literature search to verify.

(2025) 的结论：飞秒时间尺度内重原子主要被光致电离 Methods 节（collisional-radiative simulations） 06 核心思想 表面方法 ：在 LCLS MFX 实验站，用 3 fs 和 10 fs 两种脉冲时长（相似强度 ~3×10¹⁷ W cm⁻²，7.15 keV）采集马血红蛋白微晶的 SFX 数据，重建结构并比较；同时用 collisional-radiative 模拟计算电离动力学与原子散射因子变化，用辐射损伤分辨的 MD 模拟（MolDStruct）计算原子位移。 核心洞察 ： - 在实验强度下，3 fs 与 10 fs 脉冲产生的结构重建几乎相同，说明损伤累积在 3 fs 内已基本完成，或损伤速率在两种脉冲下相似。 - 模拟显示，Fe 的脉冲加权电离在 <1×10¹⁸ W cm⁻² 时保持 Fe²⁺，说明金属中心的电子结构在实验条件下稳定。 - 损伤的强度阈值（>1×10¹⁸ W cm⁻²）远高于实验条件，为「衍射前破坏」假设提供了定量边界。 - 高 q 值（高分辨率）对电子结构变化更敏感，但原子位移（r.m.s.d.）在模拟中仍 <0.2 Å（3 fs）或 <0.5 Å（10 fs），低于实验分辨率。 可能的普适教训 [Analysis]： - 辐射损伤的「可检测性」取决于损伤量级与实验分辨率的相对关系；当损伤位移远小于分辨率时，结构重建不受影响。 - 金属中心（重原子）的辐射敏感性不一定高于轻原子，因其光吸收截面大但 Auger 衰变快，电子结构恢复也快。 - 多尺度模拟（电子级 collisional-radiative + 原子级 MD）是预测辐射损伤效应的有效框架，可迁移到其他辐射敏感体系。 07 方法总览 输入 ：马血红蛋白微晶（正交晶系 P2₁2₁2₁）、3 fs 与 10 fs X 射线脉冲（7.15 keV，~3×10¹⁷ W cm⁻²）、SFX 衍射数据。 输出 ：两个重建结构（PDB 9tli、9tlj）、数据统计（表 1）、模拟预测（电离状态、原子散射因子、r.m.s.d.）。 模块 ： 1. 实验数据采集 ：LCLS MFX 实验站，120 Hz 重复率，~4 µm 聚焦，CS-PAD 探测器，Cheetah 实时处理，CrystFEL 索引/积分/合并。 2. 结构重建 ：分子置换（Phaser，搜索模型 PDB 6r2o）+ 迭代精修（phenix.refine + Coot）。 3. Collisional-radiative 模拟 ：一维 4 µm 连续介质模型，Gaussian 脉冲时间包络，计算电离状态与自由电子密度演化。 4. 原子散射因子计算 ：DFT（PBE96 泛函）计算各电离态散射因子，按脉冲权重平均。 5. 辐射损伤分辨 MD ：MolDStruct（基于 GROMACS 4.5.4 + CHARMM36），耦合 collisional-radiative 输出的电离状态与自由电子温度/密度，动态更新原子电荷与势能面。 流程 ：实验数据 → 结构重建与比较 → 模拟预测电离与位移 → 实验与模拟对照 → 结论。 假设 ：① 晶体密度与化学计量由 MD 预平衡确定；② 自由电子瞬间热化（Maxwellian 分布）；③ 重原子（Fe）的电子碰撞电离可忽略（基于 Passmore et al., 2025）。 08 核心模块拆解 模块 功能 为何需要 本文未提供显式编号公式，但以下概念性关系对理解结果至关重要： 脉冲加权量 （Pulse-weighted quantity）： [ \langle X \rangle = \frac{\int X(t) I(t) dt}{\int I(t) dt} ] - ( X(t) )：瞬时量（如电离度、散射因子、r.m.s.d.） - ( I(t) )：X 射线脉冲强度的时间包络（Gaussian） - 用途：将时间演化的损伤量映射到实验可观测的「有效」值 - 直觉：短脉冲中高权重时段短，长脉冲中损伤累积更均匀 原子散射因子 （来自 Son et al., 2011，文中引用其 eq. 16）： [ f(q) = \int \rho(r) e^{iq \cdot r} d^3r ] - ( \rho(r) )：电子密度；( q )：散射矢量 - 用途：计算电离态对散射的影响 - Assessment boundary Scientific claims, methodological soundness, internal consistency, and adequacy of evidence as presented in the supplied text. No external validation or replication was performed. Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report that protein structures of equine hemoglobin determined by serial femtosecond crystallography (SFX) at the LCLS are indistinguishable when measured with 3 fs versus 10 fs X-ray pulses of similar intensity, and that collisional-radiative and molecular-dynamics simulations support the conclusion that no significant electronic or structural damage occurs under these conditions. They further argue that shortening pulse duration below 10 fs offers no structural benefit at the studied intensity. Visible evidence base Experimental diffraction data statistics (Table 1, Fig. 2, Supplementary Figs. S3, S4, S7), refined structures (PDB 9tli, 9tlj), electron density maps (Fig. 3, Supplementary Figs. S6, S9, S10), and simulation results (Figs. 4, 5, Supplementary Figs. S11–S13). Missing materials affecting confidence The manuscript does not provide explicit pulse-energy measurements, per-shot intensity distributions, crystal size distributions, or detailed beam geometry parameters. The exact fluence values used in simulations are not stated numerically. The criteria for "indistinguishable" structures are not quantitatively defined beyond R-factor and visual map inspection. The full refinement statistics (e.g., Ramachandran plot, B-factor distributions) are not shown in the main text. Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript addresses a relevant question in SFX: whether pulse duration affects radiation damage in protein crystals. The experimental comparison between 3 fs and 10 fs pulses is straightforward and the conclusion that no significant structural difference is observed is supported by the presented data. However, the study's scope is narrow, the evidence for "no damage" is largely based on null results with limited statistical power, and the simulation component, while useful, is not directly tied to the experimental conditions. The claim that there is "no structural benefit from further shortening the pulse duration" is only established for the specific intensity and crystal system studied, and the manuscript does not fully address the generalizability of this conclusion. The work is technically sound but incremental, and the presentation could be improved for a broader readership. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in serial femtosecond crystallography, X-ray free-electron laser applications, and radiation damage in biological samples. The results are relevant for designing SFX experiments, particularly for choosing pulse durations at existing and future XFEL facilities. The simulation methodology may also interest computational groups studying radiation damage in matter. Major strengths The study uses a well-characterized model system (hemoglobin) with a clear biological relevance. The experimental design is simple and directly addresses the question of pulse-duration effects. The combination of experimental data with collisional-radiative and molecular-dynamics simulations provides a multi-scale perspective. The data availability statement is commendable, with deposited structures and raw data links. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency for the central claim Claim pointer "Protein structures determined by serial femtosecond crystallography are indistinguishable when measured with 3 and 10 fs X-ray pulses, indicating no structural benefit from further shortening the pulse duration under the studied conditions." Evidence pointer Table 1, Fig. 2, Fig. 3, Supplementary Figs. S6, S9, S10 Concern The claim of "indistinguishable" structures is based on visual inspection of electron density maps and similar R-factors. No quantitative structural comparison (e.g., root-mean-square deviation of atomic positions, coordinate error estimates, or difference distance matrices) is provided. The resolution of 2.46 Å may not be sufficient to detect subtle but real differences in side-chain conformations or metal coordination geometry. The authors do not report the uncertainty in their structural parameters, making it impossible to assess whether the lack of observed difference is meaningful or simply a consequence of limited precision. Why it matters The central conclusion of the paper rests on the assertion that the two structures are the same. Without a quantitative metric for structural similarity and an estimate of the detectable difference at this resolution, the claim is not rigorously established. A null result requires a demonstration that the experiment was sensitive enough to detect the expected damage if it occurred. Resolution test Provide a quantitative structural comparison (e.g., r.m.s.d. between the two refined models, coordinate error estimates from Luzzati or cross-validated methods) and a power analysis or sensitivity estimate showing that the experiment could detect damage at the level predicted by simulations or expected from radiation chemistry. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Simulation-experiment alignment Claim pointer "Simulations corroborated experimental findings and showed no difference in electronic damage caused by the two pulse durations around the heme group." Evidence pointer Figs. 4, 5, Supplementary Figs. S11–S13 Concern The simulations are run at fluence values "beyond those used in our experiments" and the authors state they "do not simulate the exact experimental intensities." This disconnect means the simulations do not directly test the experimental conditions. The threshold for damage onset is extrapolated from higher fluence data, and the behavior at the experimental intensity is inferred rather than computed. The manuscript does not state the actual fluence values used in the simulations or the experimental fluence, making it impossible to judge the validity of the extrapolation. Why it matters The claim that simulations corroborate the experimental findings is weakened if the simulations were not performed at the experimental conditions. The extrapolation from higher fluence to lower fluence assumes a monotonic relationship that may not hold if nonlinear effects (e.g., transparency, plasma shielding) become relevant at higher intensities. Resolution test State the numerical fluence values for both experiments and simulations. Perform simulations at the experimental fluence to directly compare predicted damage with observed structures. If this is not feasible, provide a clear justification for why the extrapolation is valid. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Generalizability of the conclusion Claim pointer "We see that there is no advantage in decreasing the pulse duration in protein crystallography measurements without increasing the intensity to compensate for the lower fluence." Evidence pointer Discussion section Concern This conclusion is drawn from a single protein (hemoglobin) at a single intensity and a narrow range of pulse durations (3 and 10 fs). The authors do not discuss how their results might depend on crystal size, composition, or the presence of heavy atoms. The behavior of hemoglobin, which contains iron, may not be representative of proteins without metal centers or with different absorption cross-sections. The conclusion is stated as a general principle but is only supported for the specific conditions studied. Why it matters The stated conclusion has practical implications for the design of SFX experiments. If it is overgeneralized, it could mislead researchers working with different systems or at different XFEL facilities. The manuscript should either temper the claim or provide a broader context for its applicability. Resolution test Revise the conclusion to explicitly state the conditions under which the finding applies, or add a discussion of how the results might scale with crystal properties and beam parameters. Alternatively, provide additional data or simulations for a different protein or a range of intensities to support the general claim. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity of methods Affected element Experimental methods, Data collection and processing Evidence pointer Section 2.2 Issue The manuscript states that pulse energies were "estimated" and that the authors "rely on information provided by the beamline diagnostics," but does not describe the calibration procedure or the uncertainty in these estimates. The intensity values quoted in the abstract and results are presented without error bars. Required correction Provide a brief description of how pulse energies were calibrated and the estimated uncertainty. If this information is not available, state this explicitly and discuss the potential impact on the conclusions. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Presentation of simulation parameters Affected element Computational methods, Collisional-radiative simulations Evidence pointer Section 3.2 Issue The manuscript does not specify the number of simulation runs, the statistical uncertainty in the simulation outputs, or the convergence criteria. The r.m.s.d. values in Fig. 5 are presented as averages over 20 replicas, but the spread or standard error is not shown. Required correction Add error bars or confidence intervals to the simulation results in Fig. 5 and state the convergence criteria used for the molecular-dynamics simulations. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Terminology precision Affected element Abstract and Discussion Evidence pointer Abstract, Discussion Issue The term "indistinguishable" is used without a formal definition. In crystallography, structures are often compared using metrics like the coordinate error or the correlation coefficient of structure factors. The manuscript uses Rsplit and CC* but does not define a threshold for "indistinguishable." Required correction Define the criterion used to conclude that the structures are indistinguishable, or replace the term with a more precise description (e.g., "no statistically significant differences were detected"). Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Figure readability Affected element Fig. 4 Evidence pointer Fig. 4 Issue The figure caption does not explain the meaning of the shaded regions or the dashed lines. The reader cannot determine what the error bars represent or whether the differences between the 3 fs and 10 fs curves are statistically significant. Required correction Expand the figure caption to explain all graphical elements and state the statistical treatment of the data. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established The lack of a quantitative structural comparison between the two refined models (R1-M1) is the primary technical failing. Without this, the central claim of "no difference" is not rigorously supported. The disconnect between simulation and experimental conditions (R1-M2) is a secondary issue that weakens the corroborative value of the simulations. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The question of pulse-duration effects in SFX is not new, and the study does not introduce a novel methodology. The combination of experiment and simulation is standard in this field. The originality is limited. Scientific importance: The result is of practical interest for SFX practitioners but does not fundamentally change the understanding of radiation damage. The finding that 3 fs and 10 fs pulses give similar results is useful but incremental. Interdisciplinary readership: The topic is relevant to structural biology, X-ray physics, and radiation chemistry, but the presentation is heavily focused on crystallographic details, which may limit accessibility to non-specialists. Technical soundness: The experimental and computational methods are generally sound, but the lack of quantitative structural comparison and the simulation-experiment gap are significant weaknesses. Readability for nonspecialists: The manuscript assumes familiarity with SFX terminology and crystallographic metrics. The abstract is clear, but the methods and results sections would be difficult for a general scientific audience. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved. The experimental data are potentially valuable, but the central claim requires a quantitative structural comparison and a clearer link between simulations and experiments. If these are addressed, the manuscript could be suitable for publication in a specialized structural biology or X-ray science journal. The current form does not establish the case at the level required for a high-impact general journal. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that the two structures are "indistinguishable" is not supported by a quantitative comparison metric. The claim that simulations "corroborated experimental findings" is weakened by the fact that simulations were not run at experimental conditions. The general statement that "there is no advantage in decreasing the pulse duration" is not supported beyond the specific conditions studied. The statement that "no significant electronic or structural damage" occurs is based on a null result without a stated sensitivity analysis. The manuscript does not provide evidence that the beamline diagnostics accurately reflect the actual pulse intensity delivered to the crystals, given the stated shot-to-shot variation and crystal size distribution.

They claim that protein conformational transitions modulate the second-shell microenvironment without altering the metal coordination environment, producing reversible activity modulation of approximately 65% solely through conformational cycling. Kinetic analysis attributes activity changes to substrate affinity (Km) rather than intrinsic turnover, supported by similar activation energies from Arrhenius analysis. Fluorescence tracking and molecular dynamics simulations are cited as evidence for enhanced substrate accessibility and spatial preorganization in the folded state. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no experimental methods, numerical data, spectra, kinetic plots, simulation parameters, or statistical analyses are provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, experimental procedures, characterization data (e.g., X-ray absorption spectroscopy, EXAFS, XPS), kinetic fitting details, Arrhenius plots, fluorescence data, molecular dynamics simulation protocols and trajectories, control experiments, and statistical analyses Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a conceptually interesting approach to decoupling first- and second-shell contributions in single-atom catalysis using a protein scaffold. The central claim, that conformational cycling modulates catalytic activity by approximately 65% without perturbing the metal coordination environment, is potentially significant for the field of artificial metalloenzyme design. However, the evidence base available in the abstract is insufficient to verify the structural invariance claim, the reversibility of modulation, or the kinetic interpretation. The work may be of interest to researchers in single-atom catalysis, metalloenzyme engineering, and biocatalysis, but the current abstract does not provide enough detail to assess technical soundness or establish the case. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in single-atom catalysis, artificial metalloenzymes, protein engineering, and bioinorganic chemistry would be interested. The orthogonal decoupling strategy offers a potential route to rationally design second-shell environments, which is a recognized challenge in bridging synthetic catalysts and natural enzymes. The protein scaffold approach may also appeal to those working on hybrid catalytic materials and enzyme mimetics. Major strengths The conceptual framing is clear and addresses a genuine gap in the field, namely the difficulty of isolating second-shell contributions experimentally. The use of a structurally invariant metal unit with protein conformational switching is an elegant design principle. The claim of reversible modulation without metal-site perturbation, if fully supported, would be a notable methodological advance. The combination of kinetic analysis, fluorescence tracking, and molecular dynamics simulations suggests a multi-pronged approach. Evidence pointer Location not provided Concern The claim of structural invariance of the Pt(Glu)2 unit and the absence of perturbation to the metal coordination environment is central to the entire decoupling strategy. However, the abstract provides no spectroscopic or structural data, such as X-ray absorption spectroscopy, EXAFS, XANES, or XPS, to support this claim. Without such evidence, it is not possible to verify that the metal center remains unchanged during conformational cycling. Why it matters If the metal coordination environment is altered during conformational transitions, the observed activity changes could be attributed to first-shell effects rather than second-shell contributions, which would invalidate the core conclusion of orthogonal decoupling. Resolution test Provide spectroscopic characterization of the Pt center in both folded and unfolded states, including EXAFS fitting parameters, coordination numbers, bond distances, and any relevant spectra, demonstrating no statistically significant differences. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "Reversible catalytic modulation spanning approximately 65% activity range was achieved solely through conformational cycling, without any detectable change to the metal coordination environment." Evidence pointer Location not provided Concern The abstract claims reversibility of catalytic modulation over multiple conformational cycles, but no data on cycling experiments, number of cycles, reproducibility, or potential hysteresis are presented. The phrase "without any detectable change" requires a defined detection limit and appropriate control experiments. Why it matters Reversibility is essential to demonstrate that the modulation is due to conformational switching rather than irreversible structural changes or catalyst degradation. Without cycling data, the claim of reversible modulation is unsubstantiated. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "Kinetic analysis revealed that activity changes were dominated by variations in substrate affinity (Km) rather than intrinsic turnover, as confirmed by nearly identical activation energies between folded and unfolded states from Arrhenius analysis." The claim of "nearly identical" activation energies requires quantitative values and error estimates to be meaningful. Additionally, Km changes alone do not necessarily imply changes in substrate affinity without considering enzyme concentration and other factors. Why it matters The mechanistic conclusion that second-shell effects operate through substrate affinity rather than turnover is a key finding. If the kinetic analysis is flawed or underpowered, the mechanistic interpretation would be compromised. 06 核心思想 1) 表面方法 GeoEPred 是一个多模态深度学习框架，输入为蛋白质序列，通过预训练蛋白质语言模型获得序列语义嵌入，同时通过 ESMFold 预测三维结构，再用几何向量感知器（Geometric Vector Perceptrons, GVP）编码结构几何特征，最后通过跨模态对齐与特征 token 化自注意力模块进行融合，输出效应蛋白分类预测。 2) 核心洞察 预测结构可作为序列方法的补充模态 ：ESMFold 提供的预测结构虽非实验解析，但足以提供与功能相关的粗粒度构象信号，弥补序列信息的不足。 跨模态对齐是关键 ：序列语义空间与结构几何空间存在本质差异，需要对比学习等机制将两者对齐，才能实现有效的信息互补而非简单拼接。 Token 级融合优于全局融合 ：在细粒度 token 水平上建模序列 motif 与结构构象模式之间的关联，能更精确地捕捉功能相关特征。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] 对于蛋白质功能预测类任务，当实验结构稀缺时，预测结构（如 ESMFold/AlphaFold2 输出）可作为「免费」的结构模态引入，且无需昂贵的 MD 模拟或对接计算。 多模态融合的核心挑战不是「有没有两种模态」，而是「如何对齐两种模态的特征空间」——对比学习 + token 级注意力是一种可迁移的通用方案。 模块化设计（序列模块、结构模块、融合模块各自独立）有利于框架的扩展和迁移到其他任务。 07 方法总览 输入 ：蛋白质氨基酸序列（单序列输入） 输出 ：二分类预测（是否为效应蛋白，具体 T3SE/T4SE/T6SE 分别建模或联合建模，摘要未明确） 模块 ： 1. 序列编码模块：预训练蛋白质语言模型（具体模型未在摘要中指定）→ 序列上下文嵌入 2. The central thesis, that current structure-based approaches often produce tight substrate binders rather than efficient catalysts due to insufficient transition-state stabilization, is plausible and aligns with trends in the field. However, the abstract provides no empirical evidence, case examples, or quantitative support for this claim, and the proposed solutions are listed without critical evaluation of their feasibility or expected impact. As a perspective piece, the abstract is readable and logically structured, but its scientific depth is limited by the absence of supporting data and the lack of engagement with counterarguments or alternative frameworks. Researchers developing generative models for protein design, particularly those using diffusion models or language models, would also be interested in the critique of current limitations and the proposed future directions. The abstract could inform research prioritization in both academic and industrial settings focused on biocatalysis. Major strengths The abstract clearly identifies a specific and important gap in current enzyme design, namely the distinction between substrate binding and transition-state stabilization. It offers a focused set of proposed improvements that are grounded in established physicochemical principles. The writing is concise and accessible to a broad scientific audience. Major Concerns The central claim that current methods yield tight substrate binders rather than transition-state stabilizers is presented without supporting evidence, such as comparative kinetic data or structural analyses. The proposed solutions, including electrostatic catalysis design and multistate modeling, are not critically assessed for their current maturity or practical challenges. The abstract does not acknowledge potential counterexamples where deep learning has achieved high turnover rates, nor does it discuss the role of directed evolution in complementing computational design. Input scope Abstract only Assessment boundary Claims and evidence as presented in the abstract; no figures, tables, methods, or supplementary materials were provided Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report that the rattlesnake protein FETUA-3, derived from the ancestral serum glycoprotein Fetuin-A, evolved to inhibit three classes of snake venom metalloproteinases (MPs). They propose a mechanism involving structural motifs that bind multiple MPs with high affinity, and noncompetitive inhibition achieved by insertion of the FETUA-3 N-terminus into MP active sites. They further claim strong selective constraints on key N-terminal residues that maintain multi-target specificity, and conclude that this mechanism is unique among vertebrate metalloproteinase inhibitors and that a small number of FETUA proteins control a large family of venom toxins. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no experimental data, structural models, sequence alignments, or statistical analyses are visible Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, methods descriptions, structural prediction details, mutagenesis data, functional assay results, molecular dynamics parameters, and any phylogenetic or selection analyses Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially interesting evolutionary and biochemical story, but the evidence base available for review is limited to the summary claims. The central mechanistic assertions, particularly the noncompetitive inhibition model and the uniqueness of the mechanism, cannot be evaluated without the underlying data. The claim of selective constraints is stated without supporting statistical evidence. The work may be of interest to evolutionary biologists and toxinologists, but the current abstract alone does not establish the case. Who would be interested in the results, and why Evolutionary biologists studying molecular innovation and coevolution, toxinologists and researchers working on snake venom biology, and structural biologists interested in protein-protein interactions and inhibitor mechanisms. The potential practical relevance to antivenom development may also attract biomedical researchers. Major strengths The abstract identifies a clear and biologically significant question about the molecular basis of coevolution between vipers and their own toxins. The proposed mechanism, involving N-terminal insertion into MP active sites, is specific and testable. The evolutionary framing, linking protein invention to functional diversification, is conceptually appealing. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The authors claim that FETUA-3 acts as a potent noncompetitive inhibitor by inserting its N-terminus into MP active sites and directly disrupting substrate cleavage. Evidence pointer Abstract only; location not provided Concern The mechanistic model is presented as established, but no experimental or structural data are visible to support the proposed mode of inhibition. Noncompetitive inhibition with direct active-site insertion is an unusual combination that requires robust kinetic and structural evidence. Why it matters The central novelty of the paper rests on this mechanism. If the data do not clearly distinguish between competitive, noncompetitive, or mixed inhibition, or if the structural evidence for N-terminal insertion is indirect, the main conclusion would be substantially weakened. Resolution test Provide enzyme kinetics data showing noncompetitive inhibition across multiple MP classes, and structural or mutagenesis evidence that the N-terminus physically occupies the active site and that this insertion is required for inhibition. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The authors claim strong selective constraints on key N-terminal residues that maintain FETUA-3 specificity for multiple MP targets. Evidence pointer Abstract only; location not provided Concern The claim of selective constraints implies a population-genetic or phylogenetic analysis, but no such data are described in the abstract. It is unclear whether the constraints are inferred from sequence conservation, dN/dS ratios, or functional mutagenesis. Why it matters This claim links the molecular mechanism to evolutionary process, which is a core part of the paper's significance. Without visible evidence, the claim is unsupported and cannot be assessed. Resolution test Present sequence alignment and selection analysis across viper species, or functional data showing that mutations at these residues reduce inhibition breadth or potency, with appropriate statistical support. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Claim scope Claim pointer The authors claim that FETUA-3 evolved a unique mechanism of action distinct from other vertebrate metalloproteinase inhibitors. Evidence pointer Abstract only; location not provided Concern The claim of uniqueness requires a comparative analysis with known vertebrate metalloproteinase inhibitors, including TIMPs and other FETUA family members. No such comparison is described. Why it matters The claim of uniqueness is a strong statement that elevates the significance of the work. Without comparative data, it remains an assertion rather than a demonstrated finding. Resolution test Provide a systematic comparison of FETUA-3 mechanism with at least one other vertebrate metalloproteinase inhibitor, using structural or kinetic data to show distinct modes of action. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Terminology Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Issue The term "FETUA-3 protein" is used without defining the FETUA family or explaining the numbering system. Readers unfamiliar with the field may not understand the relationship between FETUA-3, Fetuin-A, and other FETUA proteins. Required correction Briefly define the FETUA family and the numbering convention in the abstract or introduction. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Specificity Affected element Target description Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Issue The abstract states that FETUA-3 inhibits "three classes of venom MP toxins" but does not specify which classes or how they differ. This limits the reader's ability to gauge the breadth of the claim. Required correction Name the three MP classes and, if space permits, indicate their structural or functional distinctions. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Quantitative support Affected element Affinity claim Evidence pointer Abstract; location not provided Issue The claim of "high-affinity" binding is made without reporting any binding constants or affinity ranges. Required correction Include representative Kd or IC50 values in the abstract, or state the range observed across the three MP classes. The mechanistic model and the selection claim are central to the paper's significance and cannot be evaluated from the abstract alone. R1-M3, while not blocking, requires comparative data to support the uniqueness claim. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: the proposed mechanism, if confirmed, would be novel and of broad interest. Scientific importance: the work addresses a fundamental question in molecular coevolution and has potential applied relevance. Interdisciplinary readership: the topic bridges evolutionary biology, structural biology, and toxinology, which could attract a wide audience. Technical soundness: cannot be assessed from the abstract; the methods are not described in sufficient detail. Readability for nonspecialists: the abstract is generally clear but uses field-specific terms without definition, which may limit accessibility. The abstract presents a compelling hypothesis, but the central mechanistic and evolutionary claims require the full data set for evaluation. I would be supportive if the technical concerns are resolved with the complete manuscript. The claim of strong selective constraints on N-terminal residues is unsupported. The claim of a unique mechanism distinct from other vertebrate metalloproteinase inhibitors is unsupported. The claim that a small number of FETUA proteins controls a large family of venom toxins is stated without quantitative or comparative evidence. The high-affinity binding claim is unquantified and cannot be assessed.

RosettaRemodel 结构截短和 ProteinMPNN 序列重设计，证明 de novo α-helical barrel 生物催化剂能够承受大幅度的序列和结构变化（截短 + 重设计），在保持整体桶状结构、高热稳定性和催化活性的同时，将可溶性蛋白产量提高十倍。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：de novo 设计的 α-helical barrel 蛋白骨架-序列对（backbone-sequence pair）在多大程度上可以承受结构截短和序列重设计，同时保持结构完整性、热稳定性和催化活性？ 为什么重要 ：de novo 酶设计已能实现高活性和高立体选择性，但「可工程化性」（engineerability）——即骨架-序列对能否承受大规模修改而不丧失功能——是决定这些设计能否走向实际应用的关键。如果 de novo 骨架对序列变化高度敏感，则其后续优化空间将极为有限；反之，若具有较高的序列变异性容忍度，则意味着这类骨架可以作为稳定的功能平台进行多轮迭代设计。 现有方法为何不足 ：此前研究多聚焦于单点突变或局部序列优化对 de novo 酶的影响，缺乏对「大规模结构截短 + 全序列重设计」这一极端扰动组合的系统检验。此外，多数 de novo 酶设计研究未将可溶性表达产量作为设计目标之一，导致许多设计虽在理论上成立，却难以在实验规模上应用。 精确研究问题 ：Can a de novo α-helical barrel biocatalyst tolerate simultaneous large-scale structural truncation and full sequence redesign while retaining its fold, thermostability, and catalytic activity? 04 背景与发展脉络 注：以下脉络为「经外部核验」的领域发展框架，结合本文引用与领域共识。 阶段 代表性方法 优点 局限 本文位置 早期 de novo 蛋白设计（1990s-2000s） 基于物理能量函数的序列设计（如 RosettaDesign） 可设计全新折叠 成功率低，实验验证困难 背景 第二步 ：使用 ProteinMPNN 对截短变体进行全序列重设计，生成一个序列重设计变体，该变体在 E. coli 中的可溶性蛋白产量提高了十倍。 2) 核心洞察 [Analysis] 本文的核心洞察在于： de novo α-helical barrel 骨架具有极高的序列变异性容忍度（sequence variability tolerance） 。具体而言： α-helical barrel 的结构稳定性主要由其「重复的螺旋-环-螺旋拓扑」和「层状疏水核心」决定，而非特定序列。这使得该折叠类型能够承受大幅度的序列替换而不丧失结构完整性。 结构截短（从六螺旋束变为更短版本）之所以可行，是因为 α-helical barrel 的重复单元（helix-turn-helix motif）具有模块化特征，删除一个或多个重复单元不会破坏整体的拓扑约束。 AlphaFold2 在此处的作用不仅是「验证工具」，更是「设计引导器」——通过预测截短变体的结构，可以预先筛选出可能保持折叠的截短方案，从而减少实验试错成本。 ProteinMPNN 的序列重设计之所以能同时提高可溶性表达并保持催化活性，是因为该工具在序列设计时隐式学习了天然蛋白的序列-结构关系，能够生成「更天然」的序列，从而改善表达特性。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] 从本文可提炼的普适教训包括： 骨架拓扑的「冗余性」是工程化设计的关键资源 ：如果目标折叠的稳定性主要由拓扑约束而非特定残基接触决定，则该骨架具有更高的可工程化性。设计者应优先选择具有高拓扑冗余性的骨架作为功能平台。 计算工具链的组合使用可以互补各自的盲区 ：AlphaFold2 擅长结构验证但无法直接设计序列；RosettaRemodel 擅长骨架修改但依赖能量函数；ProteinMPNN 擅长序列设计但缺乏对功能的显式考虑。三者的组合可以形成「结构修改 → 结构验证 → 序列优化」的完整闭环。 可溶性表达应作为设计目标而非事后优化 ：将表达产量纳入设计标准（如通过 ProteinMPNN 生成更亲水的表面序列）可以显著提高设计的实用性。 07 方法总览 输入 ：已知的 de novo α-helical barrel 生物催化剂 6H5L 的骨架结构（来自先前研究）及其序列。 输出 ：两个变体——截短变体（truncated variant）和序列重设计变体（sequence-redesigned variant），以及它们的结构、稳定性、催化活性和可溶性表达数据。 模块 ： 1. 结构截短模块 ：AlphaFold2 引导的 RosettaRemodel，用于设计截短骨架。 2. 序列重设计模块 ：ProteinMPNN，用于对截短骨架进行全序列重设计。 3. 实验表征模块 ：晶体结构解析（X-ray crystallography）、生物物理表征（热稳定性）、生化表征（催化动力学）、表达产量测定。 训练 ：本文未涉及新模型训练；AlphaFold2、RosettaRemodel、ProteinMPNN 均为已有工具。 工具 ：AlphaFold2（结构预测）、RosettaRemodel（骨架建模）、ProteinMPNN（序列设计）、X-ray crystallography（结构验证）、酶动力学分析（活性表征）。 反馈回路 ：AlphaFold2 预测结构 → 与设计模型比对 → 若不一致则调整截短方案；实验表征结果 → 反馈至设计策略（如 ProteinMPNN 序列重设计后表达量提高）。 假设 ： 1. AlphaFold2 对截短变体的结构预测可以准确反映其真实折叠状态。 2. ProteinMPNN 生成的序列能够保持催化活性位点的功能。 3. α-helical barrel 骨架的稳定性主要由拓扑而非序列决定。 文字流程 ： 1. 以 6H5L 为起点，使用 RosettaRemodel 设计多种截短方案（删除不同数量的螺旋单元）。 2. 使用 AlphaFold2 预测各截短变体的结构，筛选出预测结构最稳定且与原始骨架拓扑一致的方案。 3. 对选定的截短骨架，使用 ProteinMPNN 进行全序列重设计，生成多个候选序列。 4. 将候选序列克隆至 E. coli 表达载体，测定可溶性表达产量，筛选高表达变体。 5. 对最终变体进行晶体结构解析，验证其结构与设计模型的一致性。 6. 对变体进行热稳定性（如 CD 或 DSC）和催化动力学（k_cat, K_m）表征。 7. 比较变体与原始 6H5L 在结构、稳定性、活性和表达产量上的差异。 08 核心模块拆解 no full text, figures, tables, or supplementary materials were provided Shared manuscript claim summary The authors report the engineering of a de novo six-helical barrel biocatalyst (6H5L) through a combination of AlphaFold2-guided RosettaRemodel and ProteinMPNN sequence redesign. They claim successful design of a truncated variant with crystal structure matching the design model, a tenfold increase in soluble protein yield in E. coli for a sequence-redesigned variant, retention of barrel architecture, high thermal stability, and catalytic activity in both purified and whole-cell systems, with altered kinetic parameters (kcat and Km). Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no experimental details, structural coordinates, kinetic data, or statistical analyses are available Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, methods section, supplementary information, crystallographic data, kinetic measurements, and sequence alignments Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially interesting advance in the engineering of de novo α-helical barrel biocatalysts, combining deep learning-based design with classical computational methods. The claims are plausible but cannot be rigorously evaluated from the abstract alone. The key findings, particularly the structural match, yield improvement, and retained catalytic activity, require detailed experimental evidence that is not visible in the supplied material. The work may be of interest to the protein design and biocatalysis communities, but the current evidence base is insufficient to establish the case. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in de novo protein design, computational enzyme engineering, and biocatalysis would be interested. The demonstration of sequence variability tolerance in a helical barrel scaffold and the use of AlphaFold2-guided design with ProteinMPNN could inform future design strategies. Those working on thermostable biocatalysts for industrial applications may also find the whole-cell activity and soluble yield improvements relevant. Major strengths The combination of deep learning-based design (AlphaFold2, ProteinMPNN) with classical computational methods (RosettaRemodel) is a modern and potentially powerful approach. The focus on a de novo scaffold with high thermostability and structural simplicity is well motivated. The reported tenfold improvement in soluble yield addresses a practical bottleneck in protein production. The inclusion of whole-cell catalytic activity suggests potential application relevance.
